### Exact signatures, contexts, and ownership

Engine signatures:

```go
DamagePacketTo(DamageRecipientRef, ResolutionValue) DamagePacket
DealDamagePackets(DamageSourceRef, ...DamagePacket) ResolvingEffect
```

The packet stores typed immutable declarations. The action copies its input
slice, visits every packet in definition inspection, rejects empty/nil/unbound
declarations, and resolves one source and all positive recipient amounts before
submitting damage. Positive amounts for the same resolved recipient identity
are summed before replacement processing. Zero/negative packets do not create
an event or subtract another packet's amount. Stable first-recipient order is
retained. Existing `Game.DealSimultaneousDamage`, assignment constructors and
source/reference/value resolvers execute the instruction. No parallel damage
system, generic dispatch, scratch result slot or new replacement service exists.

RON private signatures:
`compileDamagePackets(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` and
`compileDamagePacketRecipient(Node, scope) (damageRecipientFactory, error)`.
Exact action shapes:

```ron
SpellDealsMultipleDamage(ThisSpell, [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient), ...])
PermanentDealsMultipleDamage(ThisPermanent, [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient), ...])
```

Both have arity two. The second operand is a nonempty list and each member is
exactly `DamageToRecipients/2`. The source must be the matching symbol in an
existing spell/permanent context. Amounts use `compileInstanceValue` unchanged.
Recipients are the in-scope symbol `Ref_AnyTarget`, `Player(ref)/1` using
`compilePlayerRef`, or `Permanent(ref)/1` using `compilePermanentRef`.
Existing scope, type, incarnation and binding requirements remain in force.
No plural recipient set, numbered/unbound target, opponent choice, malformed
wrapper or mismatched source is silently accepted. Each factory lowers fresh
packet effects against that action's `instanceBindings`. Existing spell,
activation, supported trigger and modal envelopes share this lowering; the slice
adds no envelope, target declaration, event binding, result or announcement rule.
Real cards cover spells and activations; synthetic RON covers player/permanent
wrappers in spells, activations and entry triggers. Modal envelope lowering is
reused without a new mode contract or additional real-card coverage claim.

Inventory now gives the action's packet operand role `damage_packet` and
`DamageToRecipients/2` children roles `value` and `recipient`. Existing wrappers
then provide player/permanent-reference roles. Descendants of still-rejected
records remain reported, with support explicitly unverified.

Reuse includes definition validation, per-factory targets, stack legality,
transactional casting/activation, stack copies and retargeting, clone isolation,
current source characteristics and retained incarnation LKI, phasing, damage
assignment/batches, protection/prevention/redirection, affected-player replacement
order, lifelink, planeswalker loyalty, and post-resolution state-based actions.
RON owns only spelling, shape/scope checks and lowering. No Go fallback,
card-name branch or partial production registry is introduced. Old callers stay
available. API and rules docs describe only this shape and inherited behavior.

### Established contracts and exact supported context

New engine signature:

```go
SourceTappedStateWithLKI(tapped bool) StateCondition
```

The immutable source-only declaration performs pure information checks.
Without a captured source incarnation it requires a live phased-in source.
With a captured incarnation it reads the matching present object, including
its retained state after phasing, or the ZoneSystem departure snapshot for
that incarnation. Unknown identities do not match. Return and a second
departure of the same physical card cannot overwrite the original state.
Existing retained incarnation snapshots survive transient LKI cleanup. This
adds no global last-action slot or new snapshot store. Live-only tapped-state
conditions keep their behavior and callers.

`RunStepWithPriority(Draw)` now detects beginning-of-step triggers before the
normal draw, runs the normal draw through replacements, then places pending
triggers through the shared APNAP path before priority. A normal-draw replacement
can no longer create a beginning-of-step trigger by untapping a source or erase
one by removing it. Skipped steps still emit no draw event. CR 603.2b, 603.4,
504.1, 608.2h, 400.7 and 702.26b/d establish these timing/information contracts.
Local `data/LEA.json` Oracle text confirms both complete records. Howling Mine's
published departure ruling also specifies last-known tapped state:
https://mtg.wtf/card/2ed/248/Howling-Mine . No source transcription defect was found.

Private compiler signature:
`compileDrawStepIntervening(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
Exact supported shape on permanent cards:

```ron
TriggerI(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersDrawStep(players),
    PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, state), actions)
```

`players` is the symbol `AnyPlayer` or `SinglePlayer(You)`; `state` is the
symbol `IsTapped` or `IsUntapped`. Other subjects, player declarations, condition
shapes, arities and spell contexts are rejected. Actions use the existing
`compileActions` grammar. Each factory creates a fresh `BindPlayer` and builds
its body with `instanceBindings.steps`. `Trigger_ThatPlayer` is scoped to this
body, remains a player reference, and is not a target. The adapter uses
`TurnStepBegins(EachDrawStep, binding)`, `WhenEvent`, `WithInterveningIf` and
`EventPlayerIsController` for the controller-only case. Source control at
detection filters the event; `You` at resolution uses the captured ability
controller. Copies can change that controller while keeping the event player.
The action sequence is fully inside the condition's resolution check.

The existing `compileTappedUpkeep` dispatcher retains its supported upkeep
shape and selects the draw-step helper for this event. Existing storage-land
regressions and invalid-shape tests remain active. Ordinary draw-step `TriggerA`
and other `TriggerI` events/conditions remain unsupported. Inventory assigns
`AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersDrawStep/1` a `player_filter` child role; nested
`SinglePlayer/1` supplies `player_reference`. Support is still marked unverified,
and aggregate engine-validation/gameplay counts remain null.

Reuse: ZoneSystem incarnation/LKI snapshots, trigger detection/placement,
resolution source/controller snapshots, typed player bindings, clone/copy paths,
normal draw and replacement pipelines, `PermanentDealsDamage`, prevention,
transactional casting/mana/payment and untap restrictions. RON owns spelling,
shape checks and binding scope; reusable timing and LKI rules stay in mage.
No fallback, partial production registry, name branch, skipped rule, Go-card
deletion, obsolete generator removal or unused DSL deletion is introduced.
No deletion caller audit or native startup completion claim is made.

### Exact supported declarations and reuse boundary

Private adapters in `graveyard_return.go`:

```go
compileCardRef(Node, scope) (cardReferencePlan, error)
compileGraveyardTarget(Node, scope) (targetFactory, string, error)
compileGraveyardTargetFilter(Node) ([]mage.CardFilter, bool, error)
compileGraveyardReturn(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)
```

`Targeted([TargetGraveyardCard(filter)], ActionList([...]))` declares one typed
card target. Supported filters are `IsCardtype(type)`, nonempty recursively
nested `And([filters])`, and `InAPlayersGraveyard(players)`. `players` is exactly
`SinglePlayer(You)` or the symbol `AnyPlayer`. A filter without a player
restriction selects from any graveyard. Any controller restriction in an
`And` remains in force, including when combined with an any-player operand.
Other player filters, `Or`, permanent filters, malformed tuples and empty
conjunctions fail declaration validation. These filters read cards in their
current graveyard zone, without permanent/LKI conversion or mutation.

The target body may read the symbol `Ref_TargetGraveyardCard` as a `CardRef`.
`scope.cardTarget`, `actionPlan.cardTarget` and `instanceBindings.cards` carry
its typed plan and instance declaration. Each factory call creates a separate
`CardTargetBinding`; each body builds its actions against that declaration.
The reference cannot escape to another mode or ability, or stand in for a
permanent, player or spell. Modal scopes clear card targets and use their own
target namespace. Supported shared contexts are spells, modal spell bodies,
activated abilities and ordinary triggered ability bodies.

Actions:

```ron
PutGraveyardCardIntoHand(Ref_TargetGraveyardCard)
PutGraveyardCardOntoBattlefield(Ref_TargetGraveyardCard, [EntersNormally])
```

The hand action goes to the card owner's hand. The battlefield shape requires
a target filter that includes `IsCardtype(Creature)`, including nested `And`.
Other card types, unrestricted battlefield targets, entry lists, or modifiers
remain rejected; the restriction has an explicit invalid-declaration test.
Normal entry uses the resolving controller and retains the shared entry path,
including tapped-entry operations and ETB triggers. A subsequent action cannot
use the old card reference after the first action moves it.

Engine reuse: `DeclareGraveyardCardTarget`, `GraveyardCardFilter`,
`InAnyGraveyard`, `CardTargetBinding`, `ReturnCardToHand`,
`ReturnCardToBattlefield`, `You`, target declaration preparation, announcement
and legality checks, graveyard-visit identity, transactional mana/tap/sacrifice
costs, shared zone movement, normal battlefield entry, trigger placement,
stack copying and game cloning. No engine rule or state store was added.
CR 400.7, 601.2c/f/h, 602.2b and 608.2b/c/h were read from the local rules.

### Exact signatures, ownership and contexts

New engine APIs:

```go
ControllerOfWithLKI(PermanentRef) PlayerRef
PowerOfWithLKI(PermanentRef) ResolutionValue
ManaValueOfWithLKI(PermanentRef) ResolutionValue
```

Supported engine subjects: `This`, `AttachedPermanent`, `From(PermanentBinding)`
and singular `PermanentTargetBinding`. A private typed information-reference
interface obtains identity from the existing source context, target declarations,
saved permanent bindings or attachment service. Current phased-in information
wins; otherwise retained information must match both UUID and incarnation.
Power uses the saved final layered value. Unknown subjects yield no player or
zero number. Reads are pure and do not make an action reference live.
The existing live-only queries and mutation references keep their behavior.

`ZoneSystem` retains ownership of snapshots. Departure information reuses
`LKIByIncarnation`; phase information uses the same snapshot builder with a
separate map and lifecycle, cloned independently. This separation preserves
existing damage-source and subtype-condition contracts. `Game.PhaseOut` saves
the whole direct/indirect group before any member becomes absent. Phase-in
removes those snapshots. Indirect phase-in now gets mutable attachment pointers
so a clone's phase status cannot change. No zone-change event is created.

RON spellings and scope remain in `ron`:

```ron
ControllerOfPermanent(permanentRef)
PowerOfPermanent(permanentRef)
ManaValueOfPermanent(permanentRef)
PlayerAction(ControllerOfPermanent(permanentRef), GainLife(value))
PlayerAction(ControllerOfPermanent(permanentRef), LoseLife(value))
Exile([Permanent(permanentRef)], [])
```

Permanent refs are the correctly bound source, Aura host, local target or
captured permanent event. `compilePlayerRef` builds `ControllerOfWithLKI`;
`compileInstanceValue` builds the numeric queries; permanent-controller life
contexts use the indicated player's `GainLifeFor` / `LoseLifeFor` service.
`compilePermanentExile(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` validates the exact
single-permanent, empty-modifier form and lowers it to `mage.Exile`. Bodies work
in spells, modes, activations and ordinary triggers. Other exile lists, subjects,
modifiers, linked results and replacement contexts remain rejected. Existing
player-target life support limits remain unchanged. There are no card-name
branches, Go fallbacks, declaration panics or global last-action slots.

Dependencies/reuse: typed per-instance target/event bindings; source and
attachment incarnation context; shared definition/dominance validation;
ZoneSystem snapshots and copy-on-write storage; target legality and native
announcement; transactional mana costs; destruction/regeneration/indestructible
rules; singular exile; life and damage actions; replacement rechecks and
recipient choices; stack copying, modal scopes and cloned resolution frames.
No new cost, event scheduler, replacement order or simultaneous zone operation
was added. API/rules documentation records only this established behavior.

### Exact signatures, dependencies and ownership

Private adapters:

```go
compilePermanentEntry(Node) (optionFactory, error)
compileFixedEntryCounters(Node) (optionFactory, error)
```

`compilePermanentEntry` replaces the private `compileTappedEntry` name in its
compiler caller and retains the existing single `EntersTapped` operation.
New supported context:

```ron
AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, [
    EntersWithNumberCounters(Integer(n), counter)
])
```

This is an ordinary permanent-card rule. `AsPermanentEnters/2` has the symbol
`ThisPermanent` and a one-element list. `EntersWithNumberCounters/2` has tuple
`Integer/1` containing an integer literal in 0–255, and an existing validated
permanent counter type. Named counter symbols and supported signed
`PTCounter/2` integer coordinates reuse `compilePermanentCounterType`.
Wrong kinds, roles, arities, sources, unknown counters, negative/oversized amounts,
computed/X values and combined operation lists remain positioned compiler errors.
Instant/sorcery entry rules keep their existing non-spell-rule rejection.
No runtime declaration panic or card-name branch is introduced.

RON owns spelling, declaration limits, diagnostics and lowering.
Each option creates a fresh `mage.EntersWithNCounters` ability through
`mage.WithAbility`. No mutable compiler state, global result slot, new binding,
Go-card fallback or production registry change exists. Inventory assigns
`entry_value` and `permanent_counter_type` to the two operands and
`integer_literal` to the fixed value; support remains unverified reporting.

Engine reuse: `prepareBattlefieldEntry`, transient entering-permanent visibility,
`AddCountersWithReplacement`, additional-entry-counter and doubling replacements,
entry event detection, counter P/T, typed any-target/source-incarnation damage,
transactional casting/activation, stack/card copies, `Game.Clone`, zone return and
phasing. No execution API or engine rules implementation changed. No new batch
operation, event binding, saved result, or LKI query is introduced.

A concrete engine limitation was found during adapter review: `Permanent.Counters`
is `[NumCounters]uint8` and `AddCounter` converts the count to `uint8`.
An added test first proved that a 256-counter declaration was accepted; the adapter
now rejects it before execution. Unbounded totals, including replacement-expanded
totals above 255, remain an engine contract gap. Collection entry counts 2–7 and
observed replacement totals 7–8 fit. This run does not widen shared counter storage.
No source-data defect was corrected; the recorded Avenger/Liege/Fastbond concerns
remain open. No environment failure occurred.

### Exact contract, ownership and dependencies

Changed private adapter:

```go
compilePlayerEffect(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)
```

Supported new shapes in resolving action lists:

```ron
Targeted([TargetPlayer(AnyPlayer)], ActionList([
    PlayerAction(Ref_TargetPlayer, GainLife(value)),
    PlayerAction(Ref_TargetPlayer, LoseLife(value)),
    PlayerAction(You, GainLife(value))
]))
```

`GainLife/1` and `LoseLife/1` take an existing validated resolution value,
including `Integer/1` and announced symbol `ValueX`. Target declarations are
singular, and references are symbols. Contexts: spell, activation, trigger and
selected spell mode. Each factory builds its own player-target declaration and
read. A sibling explicit `You` or bare life action keeps the resolving action
controller; it does not inherit another action's player scope.
The same common lowering now honors existing non-event spell-controller reads
(`ControllerOfTargetSpell`, `ControllerOfSpell(Ref_TargetSpell)`) instead of
silently using `You`. Permanent-controller LKI and step-event player behavior
remain supported. Spell-cast event life reads remain explicitly rejected.

Unbound, incompatible, tuple-shaped and mode-external references, wrong life
arities and unbound X are declaration errors. No runtime declaration panic,
new global scratch result, card-name branch, skipped rule, fallback or partial
production registry is introduced. Complete unsupported modal records still fail.

RON owns spelling, scope and lowering. The engine owns life execution.
Reuse: `playerReferencePlan.build`, `instanceBindings`, typed player/spell target
bindings, `compileInstanceValue`, `GainLifeFor`, `LoseLifeFor`, life replacement
and notification services, transactional payments, target resolution, stack
copies, `Game.Clone`, controller snapshots and modal target namespaces.
No engine API or engine behavior changed. No new simultaneous batch or
replacement-order contract is needed for this singular life adapter.
Player subjects do not have permanent incarnations or phase state. Source
phase/departure/control tests cover independence from the activation source;
existing permanent-controller LKI tests remain in the full suite.

### Exact supported signatures, contexts and dependencies

Private adapter contexts established:

```ron
Targeted([TargetPlayer(Opponent)], actions)
Targeted([TargetPermanent(ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent))], actions)
Targeted([TargetPermanent(And([filter, ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)]))], actions)
TriggerA(WhenAPlayerCastsASpell(Opponent, spellFilter), actions)
```

Opponent is a symbol, not a singular resolving player reference. Target forms
work in spells, activations, triggers, and selected spell modes. Permanent
controller restrictions compose in nested And lists with existing filters.
Source-dependent Or filters still reject. Spell filters/actions retain their
existing supported shapes. Cast matching uses source control at event time;
queued trigger control and captured caster/spell identities do not follow later
control changes. Targets use the stack controller at resolution, including
copies. Source departure does not change the ability controller.

Changed private functions: `compileTarget(Node, scope)`,
`compilePermanentTargetFilter(Node, scope)`, `compileTriggerRule(Node, scope)`.
Engine prerequisite: `(*Game).isTargetStillLegal(uuid.UUID, Card, uuid.UUID,
Zone, Target) bool` now applies the target specification to an existing player,
instead of returning true before checking it. A nil specification keeps the
existing player-existence behavior. All-illegal objects resolve no instruction,
including untargeted sibling effects. No public API changes.

RON owns syntax, arities, scopes, lowering and per-factory declarations. Reuse:
`DeclarePlayerTarget`, `TargetOpponentOnly`, `DeclarePermanentTarget`,
`TargetOpponentControls`, `SpellCast().ByOpponent().WithSpell().WithCaster()`,
existing spell card filters, player/permanent instance bindings, shared stack
legality and target snapshots, counter placement/replacement services, copying,
transactional payment and Game.Clone. No wrapper or second legality system was
added. No global result slot, game-time declaration panic, fallback, partial
production registry, skipped rule or card-name branch.

The initial working hypothesis that RON dropped an effect wrapper was disproved
by inspecting `Spell` and `ActionDefinition`. The actual defect was the shared
resolver's early player return. Existing typed drain-copy tests passed because
loss and gain to the same copied controller canceled. New tests isolate loss
and verify that an independent draw also cannot run. This is an engine contract
fix, not a source defect. No new LKI information read, simultaneous operation,
replacement ordering or optional payment contract is introduced. Permanent
identity, phase and control behavior use the existing target/counter services.

retaining the first pending trigger. Tests were not weakened. The former


Both constructors are tuples of arity 1. `ref` must pass the existing typed
permanent-reference compiler in the current action scope: source
`ThisPermanent`, attached Aura `HostPermanent`, declared `Ref_TargetPermanent`,
or event-bound `Trigger_ThatPermanent`. Source/host/event references remain
illegal outside their scopes. This form works in spell actions, activations,
trigger bodies, and selected spell modes. Target filters and costs retain their
existing supported shapes. A bare `TapOrUntapPermanent`, other optional bodies,
lists, malformed tuples, numbered/unbound references, and sibling-scope reads
remain rejected at compile time.

Private signature:
`compileOptionalTapChoice(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)`.
`compileEffect` dispatches MayAction to this adapter. It lowers to
`mage.MayTapOrUntap(subject.build(bindings))`, constructing fresh effects with
per-instance typed bindings. Inventory assigns an optional action's child the
action role and the tap/untap subject the permanent-reference role, including
unsupported optional parents. Reporting still marks syntax support unverified.

The engine already implements the full rule, so there is no engine change or
new public API. Reused services: `compilePermanentRef`, `instanceBindings`,
`MayTapOrUntap`, target announcement/revalidation and incarnation capture,
`TapPermanent`, `UntapPermanent`, stun replacement and tap/untap events,
transactional cast/activation payment, stack copies and `Game.Clone`.
The resolving controller chooses whether to change the subject's current state;
this choice occurs after costs and target announcement. Decline does not stop
later instructions or refund costs. A source departure/control change does not
transfer its activation's chooser. Target leave/return invalidates its old
incarnation; phasing makes it absent and a phase cycle preserves identity.
Copies have their own controller and target. Clone SearchPlayer defaults decline
independently of live scripted choices. Replacement and event execution use the
shared engine operations. No LKI information read, replacement ordering,
finite-prevention, or simultaneous-operation contract was added.

RON owns spelling, shape validation, scope, diagnostics and lowering. No game
state or choice was moved into the compiler. No card-name branch, fallback,
partial production registry, skipped rule, global last-action slot, or game-time
declaration panic was introduced. No source defect or environment failure was
needed to implement the slice. Avenger/Liege/Fastbond concerns remain open.

### Exact supported shapes and reuse boundary

```ron
TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter)
Twice(value)
ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(player))
```

The value constructors and controller wrappers are tuples of arity 1. `filter`
accepts existing source-independent permanent filters. Nested `And([...])`
can include at most one controller clause. Without it, `MatchingPermanents`
selects the global current collection. With it, `PermanentsControlledBy` uses a
player compiled by `compilePlayerRef`, including the current `You`, declared
`Ref_TargetPlayer`, event-bound `Trigger_ThatPlayer`, and existing typed controller
reads in their valid scopes. Collection players, controller clauses inside `Or`,
multiple controller clauses, numbered/unbound refs and sibling scope leaks remain
compile-time errors. Source/host/event reference restrictions remain unchanged.

`Twice` recursively compiles its operand with `compileInstanceValue` and lowers
to `MultiplyValues(Fixed(2), operand)`. Signed intermediates remain signed;
nonpositive final life/damage amounts use existing engine behavior. These values
work only in action consumers of `compileInstanceValue`, including resolving
spells, activations, triggers and selected spell modes. They do not establish
static/CDA/entry/cost values, temporary P/T values, recipient-loop bindings,
beginning-of-turn history or damage history.

Private signatures:
- `compileBattlefieldCount(Node, scope) (valueFactory, error)`.
- `compileCountFilter(Node, scope, **playerReferencePlan) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)`.

The count-filter helper extracts one immutable typed controller plan and combines
pure filters. It performs no runtime query. Factory construction supplies fresh
instance bindings. The resulting value uses shared `CountPermanents`,
`MatchingPermanents`, `PermanentsControlledBy`, and typed `PlayerRef` services.
No engine/public API change. Membership, characteristics and control are read
when each instruction uses the value; ownership does not select membership.
Phased permanents are absent. Tokens and returned objects can join the current
collection. Prior zone actions change the count for later instructions.

Shared target legality/payment rollback, event-player snapshots, source LKI,
stack-copy/retargeting, clone isolation, native damage/prevention/lifelink and
zone operations remain in the engine. RON owns spelling, shape/scope validation,
diagnostics and lowering. No fallback, card-name branch, game-time declaration
panic, skipped rule, global last-action slot or partial production registry.
No new replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation contract was needed.

Inventory assigns `Twice`'s child the value role and the battlefield count's child
the permanent-filter role, including descendants of rejected records. Existing
controller/player role reporting then exposes the typed player reference.
Reporting support remains unverified; this does not claim support for unknown
nested parents.

### Supported shapes, contexts and reuse

```ron
TriggerA(WhenAPlayerTapsAPermanentForMana(AnyPlayer, IsCardtype(Land)), body)
TriggerA(WhenAPlayerTapsAPermanentForMana(AnyPlayer, IsCardtype(Land)),
  ActionList([PlayerAction(Trigger_ThatPlayer,
    AddMana(Trigger_AnyManaTypeProduced))]))
TriggerA(WhenAPermanentIsTappedForMana(SinglePermanent(HostPermanent)),
  ActionList([PlayerAction(ControllerOfPermanent(Trigger_ThatPermanent),
    AddMana(ManaProduceG))]))
```

The general any-player land event permits existing non-mana action bodies. It
introduces typed, per-factory/per-trigger `Trigger_ThatPlayer` and
`Trigger_ThatPermanent` bindings. The first saves the activating player; the
second saves the exact event land incarnation. The body is a lexical scope;
neither reference escapes into sibling abilities. Current controller reads use
existing `ControllerOfWithLKI`, including departure LKI and phase information.
Targets keep existing declaration, legality and instance rules.

Mana-producing bodies are supported only in the two exact single-instruction
bonus shapes. The attached form needs an Aura scope. It accepts one concrete
white/blue/black/red/green/colorless production, including `And` of exactly one
production. The produced-type symbol is a declared event value, not a fixed
color or arbitrary choice. Other bodies, recipients, multiple instructions,
multiple productions, `AnyManaColor`, wrong arities/kinds, nonland filters,
numbered/unbound references, source/target mana events and sibling leaks fail
compilation. Attached non-mana actions remain unsupported. General explicit
player mana actions outside this event context remain unsupported.

Private signatures:
- `compileLandManaTrigger(Node, Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
- `compileLandManaBonus(Node, bool) (optionFactory, bool)`.
- `compilePlayerMana(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)`.
- `usesManaAction(Node) bool`.

RON owns spelling, structural/scope checks, immutable event plans, fresh binding
construction, diagnostics and lowering. `LandTappedForMana().WithLand().WithPlayer()`
provides ordinary event capture. The compiler validates the typed action plan
before selecting the exact mana-bonus lowering. The mana bonuses use stateless
`NewManaFlareAbility(IsLand)` and `NewAttachedManaBonusAbility(color)` declarations;
there is no runtime chosen binding state to share in these declarations. The
shared service handles both solver metadata and production, so no bonus can be
counted twice. It adds one mana immediately to the activating player. Multiple
instances each add one; the produced-type choice reads only the original mana
ability's types and does not multiply its amount. Manabarbs remains an ordinary
trigger using native damage, prevention and lifelink.

A native payment probe showed that the first generic mana-trigger lowering
resolved correctly but supplied no solver bonus metadata. It failed both real
mana-bonus payment cases. This was a missing adapter to an existing engine
service, resolved by exact bonus lowering. The engine contract tests then
exposed real shared-service defects: phased bonus sources were counted, and
attached bonuses followed a returned card ID. `ManaSystem.ManaBonuses` now skips
phased sources and checks the attached incarnation. Existing callers remain.
This is the only engine change; there is no new public API, parallel event or
mana subsystem, global last-action slot, card-name branch, fallback or partial
production registry. No new simultaneous-operation or replacement-ordering rule
was needed. No production card definitions, generators or DSL exports were
removed because the cutover gate remains unmet.

Inventory gives the two event constructors' children player/permanent-filter
roles and explicit-player `AddMana`'s child the mana-production role. Reporting
still says support is unverified; syntax alone does not establish gameplay.

### Exact supported contract and reuse

`SetPower(Integer(n))`, with any signed integer literal, is supported only as a
modification in existing `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3` action lists.
Existing spell, activation and trigger contexts, typed subjects and durations
apply. The new helper is
`compileTemporaryPower(Node, permanentReferencePlan) (func(instanceBindings) mage.ContinuousModification, error)`.
It lowers to `mage.SetBasePower(subject.build(bindings), mage.Fixed(n))`.
No public API or engine behavior changed. One shared `Until` installation still
handles all modifications in the action. Layer 7b sets base power; base toughness
is preserved and layer 7c bonuses/counters still apply. Later layer 7b setters
use timestamp order. The value and subject are constructed per factory call.

Island targets a flying creature; Tree targets an attacking creature controlled
by either player. Existing legality checks run at announcement and resolution.
A creature phased out and in, or with a changed controller, leaves combat and
is no longer a legal Tree target. Once installed, the effect persists through
combat removal, control changes and phase cycles until cleanup. Source departure
does not cancel the queued ability or installed modification. Returned targets
have new incarnations and do not inherit it. Clones and copies retain their
own resolution state. Invalid activation leaves costs and stack unchanged.

Symbol/empty/multiple-argument `SetPower`, bare values, malformed `Integer`,

Existing invalid reference and duration checks remain in the shared compiler.
No card-name branch, fallback, global action slot, declaration panic, partial
production registry, parallel rules system or mutable shared binding was added.
Semantic inventory now reports the temporary value child, including descendants
of unsupported parents; it does not claim gameplay support from syntax.

### Exact contract, dependencies and engine reuse

Supported context:
`TriggerA(WhenAPermanentIsPutIntoAPlayersGraveyard(filter, AnyPlayer), actions)`.
`filter` is `IsCardtype(Land)` or `IsCardtype(Artifact)`, or
`And([IsCardtype(type), ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))])` in either
order, with exactly those two restrictions. Other filters, other types,
singular source selectors and restricted destination players
are not added by this contract. `TriggerI` remains rejected for this event.

New private signatures:
- `compileGraveyardTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
- `compileGraveyardEventFilter(Node) (core.CardType, bool, error)`.

The event lowers to `mage.PermanentDies().OfType(type).WithOwner(owner)` with
`WithController(controller)`, and optionally `YouControlled()`. Types and
controller restrictions use the pre-death object. `Trigger_ThatPlayer` reads
the destination graveyard owner; `ControllerOfDeadPermanent` reads the last
battlefield controller. The separate typed player bindings are created per
factory. Every pending trigger keeps its own captures, so later source/land
control changes, departure, return, phasing, copying or cloned games cannot
redirect either player. Source damage uses the existing original-incarnation
LKI service. Optional mana payment remains an adjacent `IfPaid` continuation.

### Supported shapes, reuse and dependencies

On permanent cards, support:
`TriggerI(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersEndStep(players), condition, actions)`.
`players` is symbol `AnyPlayer` or `SinglePlayer(You)`. Conditions are:

- `NoPermanentsPassFilter(filter, OnTheBattlefield)`, with the existing supported
  permanent-filter grammar. This reads both players' current battlefield.
- `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent,
  DealtDamageToAnyPlayerThisTurn(Opponent))`, with exactly that source and player.

New private signatures:
`compileEndStepIntervening(Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)`;
`compileEndStepCondition(Node) (mage.StateCondition, error)`;
`compileBoundStepTriggerWithCondition(event, body Node, ctx scope,
  each, your mage.TurnStepPattern, label string,
  condition mage.StateCondition) (optionFactory, error)`.
The existing bound-step compiler calls the last function with no condition.
All existing callers retain their behavior. The existing TriggerI dispatcher
validates three arguments before the new adapter can read them.

RON owns spelling, arity, scope and lowering. The engine retains
`BattlefieldHasNone`, `SourceDamagedOpponentThisTurnCondition`,
`TurnStepBegins`, `EachEndStep`, `YourEndStep`, `BindPlayer`, `WhenEvent`,
`WithInterveningIf`, APNAP, source incarnations, damage history, sacrifice,
protection, batch damage and transactional payments. No engine API changed.
The event-player binding is built with the effects per factory; pending events
and copies keep their own values. Conditions contain no chosen mutable state.
No fallback, card-name branch, partial production registry, new declaration
panic, global last-action slot or parallel rules executor was added.

Source phasing prevents detection; phased creatures do not count for absence.
Both conditions are checked again at resolution. A source phase cycle keeps
history, while departure/return makes a new incarnation. A pending Dervish
trigger keeps its original controller for the opponent check. A copy uses its
own controller. A pending Pestilence trigger cannot sacrifice its source after
another player gains control of it (CR 701.21a). Removing the source ability
after detection does not remove the pending trigger. No new LKI contract is
claimed; absent-source actions use the existing exact incarnation services.

### Exact contract and engine reuse

In existing spell, activation and trigger action sequences:
`MayCost(SacrificeAPermanent(filter))/1` and
`PlayerMayCost(player, SacrificeAPermanent(filter))/2` require an adjacent
`If(condition, [actions])/2` or `Unless(condition, [actions])/2` with a nonempty
body. The player uses existing typed references. MayCost retains the resolving
controller. The filter uses the existing activation-sacrifice grammar through
`compileSacrificeCostFilter`, including nonempty recursive `And/Or`.
Conditions are symbols `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid`.
If/Paid and Unless/NotPaid run on successful payment; Unless/Paid and
If/NotPaid run on failed or declined payment. Both polarities also apply to the
existing fixed `PayMana` shape. Other optional costs remain rejected.

The unchanged private signature is
`compileOptionalPayment(payment, continuation Node, ctx scope) (effectFactory, error)`.
RON owns syntax, arity, branch polarity and adjacency. It lowers the complete
pair to `IfPaid` or `UnlessPaid`, using fresh cost/effect objects per factory.
`compileCosts` reuses `SacrificeMatchingIncludingSourceCost`, so one current,
unphased matching permanent controlled by the payer can pay, including the
source. Costs are prepared and committed through the engine transaction;
invalid/stale selections consume no payment object. The card goes to its owner.
Regeneration does not replace sacrifice. Each pair has a local result, with
no new global last-action state or saved-result reader.

Existing engine services retain controller capture, source incarnation/LKI,
phasing, copying/cloning, ordered source sacrifice and damage, prevention and
combat rules. A copied Elder Spawn trigger cannot sacrifice a source its new
controller does not control; its independent damage still affects that copy's
controller. A returned source does not receive old tap/sacrifice instructions.
No new simultaneous-operation or replacement-order contract is introduced.
No engine prerequisite or source defect was hidden behind the adapter.

### Exact supported signatures and ownership

`compileArtifactTapTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`:
inside `TriggerA/2`, `WhenAPermanentBecomesTapped/1` accepts
`IsCardtype(Artifact)/1`, or `And/1` containing exactly that filter and
`ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)/1`, in either order.

`compileArtifactActivationTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`:
inside `TriggerA/2`, `WhenAPlayerActivatesAnAbility/2` accepts symbol `AnyPlayer`
or `Opponent`, and `And/1` with exactly one source filter plus symbol
`DoesntHaveTapSelfInCost`. Source is `AbilityOfAPermanent(IsCardtype(Artifact))/1`
or `AbilityOfPermanent(HostPermanent)/1` in an Aura scope. The two members may
occur in either order. Other activation contexts remain rejected.

`compileArtifactEventBody` gives the action plan a lexical `permanentEventPlan`
and builds a fresh `PermanentBinding` for each factory/rule. Symbol
`Trigger_ThatPermanent` uses existing typed reads; no event player or activated
ability binding is invented. Arity, literal kinds, duplicate/missing filters,
wrong host scopes and unrelated event reads are compilation errors.

RON owns syntax, context and lexical identity. Engine reuse:
`ArtifactBecomesTapped().WithArtifact` with optional `ByOpponent`,
`ArtifactAbilityActivatedWithoutTapCost().WithArtifact` with optional
`AttachedToSource`, `EventPlayerIsOpponent`, `WhenEvent`, `ControllerOfWithLKI`,
existing source damage/life actions, APNAP pending triggers, payment events,
stack copy and game clone services. No global last-action state or fallback.

to use `activatedSourceIsArtifact` and exact `SourceIncarnation` capture.

### Exact signatures, dependencies and ownership

`compileCosts(Node) ([]costFactory, bool, error)` accepts bare symbol
`DiscardACardAtRandom` as a cost in `Activated/2` and
`ActivatedWithModifiers/3`, including nested `And([costs])/1` lists. Each
factory produces `mage.DiscardRandomCost(1)`. Tuple forms of the singular cost,
random-number costs and optional random-payment declarations stay rejected.
Resolving random actions keep their existing explicit player scope.

RON owns spelling and declaration validation. The engine owns reusable
`DiscardRandomCost(n int) Cost`, negative-count definition checks, random
selection, hand-visit locking, deterministic-before-random payment ordering,
replacement processing and simultaneous discard events. Existing public callers
remain supported. The current caller audit found the two Go definitions and DSL
alias still using the service; none is removed. This is not a DSL removal audit.

Dependencies and reuse: `costPaymentTransaction`, `lockPaymentCosts`, isolated
payment clones, `RandomSource`, `capturedCard` hand visits, locked `discardCost`,
`newCostDiscardAction`, `discardActionsTogetherWithEvents`, engine target plans,
`Until/ModifyPT`, regeneration shields, stack copies and game clones.
Random costs are moved after deterministic costs, preserving each group's
order. Selection takes place on the validation game after prior payments;
validation no longer substitutes a player-selected discard. The transaction
saves the complete candidate hand visits, selected visits and random state.
Commit uses the locked selection and repeats the total payment on an isolated
game before live spending, so changed visits, random queues or replacement
outcomes fail before other costs are spent. Direct `Pay` uses the same path.
No hand-choice interface, global last-action slot, card-name branch, skipped
rule, registry fallback or game-time declaration panic is introduced.

The random service retains its existing unscripted process RNG fallback; this
slice does not add a seeded game generator. Scripted queues stay independent
and advance once on successful live payment. Copies do not pay costs again.
Source/target identity, phasing, boost duration and regeneration reuse existing
engine behavior. No new LKI, replacement-order or phasing service is claimed.

### Exact signatures and reuse boundary

`compileDefendingLandRule(Node, Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)` lowers:

```ron
PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent, [
  CantAttackUnlessDefendingPlayer(
    PlayerPassesFilter(DefendingPlayer, ControlsA(IsLandType(Island))))
])
```

Only one operation, the typed source permanent, bare `DefendingPlayer`, and
`ControlsA/1` are accepted. It reuses
`mage.Static(mage.CanAttackOnlyIfDefendingPlayerControls(filter))`. Current
control/subtype and phased absence affect attack legality. The nonactive player
is the defending player in this engine. Ability removal stops the restriction;
later rule changes do not remove an already declared attacker.

`compileNoLandTrigger(Node, Node, scope) (optionFactory, error)` lowers
`TriggerA(WhenAPlayerControlsNoPermanents(SinglePlayer(You),
IsLandType(Island)), actions)` to `mage.WhenState(mage.ControlsNone(filter),
sequence)`, with targets from the existing action plan. `SinglePlayer/1` must
contain bare `You`. The current controller supplies the state condition. The
pending instance keeps its source incarnation and trigger controller. There is
no event-player/permanent binding and no intervening-if resolution check.
A later matching permanent does not cancel the queued sacrifice. Pending/stack
instances suppress repeated state triggers; a countered instance can rearm.

Both adapters use `compileLandDependenceFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter,
error)`: `IsLandType/1` with bare Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest or
Desert. Other predicates, subtype names, tuple operands, Aura hosts, chosen
players, opponent state conditions, inverse attack conditions, multi-operation
lists and unbound event reads remain rejected in these contexts. Other existing
compiler filter contexts keep their behavior.

RON owns spelling, arity, context validation, inventory roles and lowering.
The engine owns legality, continuous layers, phasing, current control, state
arming/APNAP, transactional payment, source identity, sacrifice, pending/stack
copying and clones. Existing `compilePermanentRef`, `compileFilter`,
`compileActions`, per-factory `plan.build`, `TriggerA`, and engine source capture
are reused. Factories build separate abilities and targets. No game-time
panics, global last-action state, card-name branches, skipped rules or Go
fallback are introduced. No engine prerequisite was missing. No new LKI,
replacement-order or simultaneous-zone service is claimed.

### Supported signatures, contexts and dependencies

`compileSourceAttackTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`
lowers these exact event declarations under `TriggerA/2`:

```ron
WhenACreatureAttacks(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))
WhenACreatureAttacksAndIsntBlocked(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))
```

They use `mage.WhenEvent(mage.Attacks(mage.This), ...)` and
`mage.WhenEvent(mage.AttacksUnblocked(mage.This), ...)`. The action body uses the
existing `compileActions` and `actionPlan.build`, so every factory gets fresh
abilities, targets and effects. The compiler's `scope.sourceAttack` enables
bare `Trigger_ThatCreature` only inside this body. `compilePermanentRef` returns
the typed `permanentSource` reference, whose engine value is `mage.This`.
This is an exact alias for this source-only event context: the engine already
captures the original source incarnation separately for each pending/stack
instance. There is no shared mutable event slot. A host or arbitrary creature
would need a separate event binding; it is not lowered to the source.

`PermanentDealsDamage/3` now validates its source through the typed permanent
reference compiler. It accepts `Trigger_ThatCreature` in this context and keeps
rejecting target/host/unbound damage sources. This preserves the existing damage
pipeline, source LKI and prevention. Existing spell source validation is retained.

`compileTemporaryDuration` accepts bare `UntilEndOfCombat` in source attack
bodies and uses `mage.Until(core.EndOfCombat, modifications...)`. Existing
end-of-turn/source-tapped behavior is unchanged. Other contexts still reject
this new duration. The full supported action-body shape includes existing
source/target temporary layer modifications, payment continuations and actions;
unsupported body declarations still fail the entire card.

Inventory now assigns `permanent_filter` and `permanent_reference` roles below
both combat event constructors, including rejected parents' descendants. Roles
are syntax evidence, not support claims. Host events, combined events, blocking
events, `Trigger_DefendingPlayer`, non-mana optional payments, delayed events,
coin flips and band filters remain rejected. No rules are skipped.

RON owns spelling, kinds/arity, lexical context and lowering. The engine owns
attack/block legality and timing, APNAP, source/controller capture, clones,
stack copies, source LKI, damage/prevention, continuous effects/expiry and
transactional costs. All required contracts already exist. No new engine
replacement-order or simultaneous-operation contract is claimed. No Go fallback,
card-name branch, game-time declaration panic or partial production registry is
introduced. Existing callers remain intact.

engine reuse and a bounded implementation. First-error frequency did not imply

existing `YourUpkeep` engine pattern.

### Exact supported shapes and reuse boundary

`compileDelayedStep(n Node, ctx scope) (effectFactory, error)` implements:

```ron
CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfTheNextEndStep, ActionList([...]))
CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheNextEndOfCombat, ActionList([...]))
CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfPlayersNextUpkeep(You), ActionList([...]))
```

The two bare events require symbols; upkeep requires exactly one bare `You`.
The body must be a nonempty `ActionList/1`. Existing action shapes in spell,
activation or supported trigger resolution can be used in that body, including
nested schedules and existing optional-payment continuations. New targets and
modes inside the delayed body remain errors. Inherited declarations retain their
per-factory typed identities; `compileActionSequence` builds fresh body effects
with that factory's `instanceBindings`. No declaration is constructed at game
time, and no global last-action slot is used.

RON owns syntax, arity, lexical binding checks and lowering. `mage.AtNext` owns
scheduling and capture with `EachEndStep`, `EachEndOfCombat` or `YourUpkeep`.
The shared engine saves source incarnation, controller, permanent/player/number
bindings, created-token bindings, typed target frames and X per scheduling
resolution. Nested schedules capture their current frame. Actions read captured
incarnations; information reads keep their existing LKI semantics. An inherited
target is not a new target of the delayed ability. The original target filter is
not checked again by a later untargeted action. An all-illegal original spell
never schedules its body. Source departure, control changes and ability removal
do not remove the schedule. Sacrifice still requires the resolving controller
to control the source; independent damage still resolves through prevention/LKI.

A tested capture limit was found: `AtNext` does not save event spell bindings.
The new `scope.delayedStep` flag makes `compileSpellRef` reject those reads in
this body. Captured event players remain available with their existing supported
actions. This is an explicit unsupported context, not a new engine contract.
Other players' next upkeeps, next main phase, `AtNextEndOfCombatThisTurn`, departure
and combined events, new delayed targets, histories, choices and links remain
unsupported. No card rule is skipped. No replacement ordering or simultaneous
operation contract is changed; damage and payments still use their shared services.

Semantic reporting assigns `delayed_step_event` and `actions` to descendants of
`CreateFutureTrigger/2`, and `player_reference` beneath next upkeep, even when
the enclosing record is rejected. Syntax roles and counts are not support claims.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

`compileCombatPairTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`
and `compileCombatPairFilter(n Node) (string, error)` support:

```ron
TriggerA(WhenACreatureBlocksACreature(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), filter), actions)
TriggerA(WhenACreatureBecomesBlockedByACreature(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), filter), actions)
```

`filter` is `IsCardtype(Creature)`, a one-element `And` containing that filter,
or `And` containing exactly one creature type and one `IsNonCreatureType`
with a validated creature subtype, in either order. No other event subject,
filter combination, tuple/symbol substitution or duplicate is accepted.
Existing action-body and target declaration support is reused unchanged.

The blocking event exposes only `Trigger_ThatOtherCreature`; the blocked-by
event exposes only `Trigger_TheBlockingCreature`. `scope.combatOpponent` holds
a typed `permanentEventPlan`. `compilePermanentRef` requires that plan's exact
name. It builds `From` using the existing per-instance permanent binding map.
Each card factory constructs a fresh binding and body. `BlocksCreature(This)`
with `WithOpponent`, or `BecomesBlockedBy(This)` with `WithBlocker`, performs
engine event detection and incarnation capture. `WithoutSubtype` performs the
optional exclusion at detection; `ValidateSubtypeFamily` checks declarations.
No RON game state, runtime declaration construction or global action slot is
introduced. `AtNext` saves these bindings for each delayed schedule.

Dependencies: typed permanent scopes, instance action factories, existing
per-creature combat events, event captures, delayed-step capture and shared
destruction. Events are per opposing creature, not the once-per-combat
`WhenACreatureBlocks` shape. Exclusion does not recur at resolution. Control or
characteristic changes cannot redirect the saved subject. A returned incarnation
is distinct; an absent phased subject cannot be destroyed. Source departure
does not cancel an independent pending ability. Destruction permits regeneration.
Targets, costs, replacement ordering and simultaneous operations remain owned
by their existing services. No new general LKI contract is established.

Inventory now gives both event arguments the `permanent_filter` role and reads
`SinglePermanent` descendants as references even below a rejected parent.
Support remains tracked by shape/context, not the existence of an event name.

### Exact shapes, scope and reuse

`compileIndefiniteType(n Node, ctx scope) (effectFactory, error)` accepts:

```ron
CreatePermanentLayerEffect(reference, [AddCardtype(type)])
CreatePermanentLayerEffect(reference, [SetLandType(type)])
```

Exactly one operation is supported. `AddCardtype` accepts Creature, Artifact,
Enchantment or Land; `SetLandType` accepts Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain or
Forest as symbols. Empty/combined modifications, malformed symbols, unsupported
types and other modification families fail compilation with positioned errors.
This is a resolving action, not a static rule or entry replacement. The subject
uses the existing `compilePermanentRef` lexical contract: source, Aura host,
singular declared target or matching event binding, only where bound. No new
reference aliases or scope lifetimes are invented.

Dependencies are already present: instance-bound action factories, permanent
references and target declarations, activation/casting payment transactions,
sacrifice costs, counter replacements and the engine's continuous layer services.
`AddCardtype` reuses `compileTemporaryType` validation/lowering. Each factory
builds `AddCardType` or `SetSubtypeFamily(..., SubtypeLand, type)` with its own
bindings and installs it through `Until(Indefinite)` at resolution.

Engine reuse is exact: captured incarnation identity, source-independent lifetime,
clone isolation, shared layer ordering, target legality and cleanup are unchanged.
Basic land subtype replacement already calls the CR 305.7 service: remove printed
rules/land types, grant intrinsic mana, preserve other families/types/supertypes
and abilities granted by other effects. There is no missing engine prerequisite.
No RON runtime state or last-action slot is added. LKI is not used to act on absent
objects. No simultaneous operation is introduced; Transmogrant's counter and
artifact instructions remain ordered and use existing replacement services.

Inventory assigns `CreatePermanentLayerEffect` arguments the
`permanent_reference` and `resolving_modification` roles. Descendants retain
`card_type` and `land_subtype` roles even when another modification is rejected.
Inventory support remains unverified by default; known syntax is not proof of
engine or gameplay support.

### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse

`compileAttachmentTargetFilter(n Node) (mage.PermanentFilter,
[]mage.PermanentTargetOption, error)` handles the one-argument
`AttachedToAPermanent(hostFilter)` in a `TargetPermanent` declaration, including
conjunctive target filters. `compileAttachmentHostFilter(n Node,
allowController bool) (mage.PermanentFilter, bool, error)` accepts existing pure
permanent-filter leaves and nonempty nested `And([filters])` / `Or([filters])`.
A host `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` can occur once, on a conjunctive
path. It can be the complete host filter. Controller restrictions inside `Or`,
Opponent/event/target players, source exclusions, empty/malformed lists and
nested attachment queries fail with positioned compilation errors. This is a
target context, not a general static/collection filter or movement adapter.

`compilePermanentTargetFilter` integrates the adapter for existing spell,
activation and trigger target declarations. Host queries use `IsAttachedTo`;
controller restrictions use `TargetAttachedToYouControl`. No target restriction
is lifted from the host to the Aura. The engine reads the current host at
announcement and resolution; the captured target is the Aura incarnation.
Factory-local declarations and existing instance bindings isolate activations,
copies and clones. The resolving stack controller supplies You, so source
control/departure cannot redirect the restriction. Copies use their own
controller. The adapter neither captures mutable game state nor adds a global
last-action slot. No new scope aliases are added.

Dependencies are already present: typed singular targets, target legality,
attachment queries, transactional payments, incarnation tracking, copy/clone
services, destruction/regeneration/indestructible and owner-zone execution.
LKI does not permit actions on an absent target. No simultaneous operation or
replacement-order contract is introduced. Inventory assigns the attachment
operand `permanent_filter`, including under a recognized but rejected record;
syntax support stays unverified by default.

### Exact supported signatures, contexts and reuse

`compileCombatPairTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`
supports both two-argument directional events in `TriggerA`. Subjects are
`SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)` and, in Aura scope,
`SinglePermanent(HostPermanent)`. The body uses existing resolving actions and
supported delayed actions; complete-card tests use `ActionList`.

`compileCombatPairFilter(n Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)` accepts bare
`IsCardtype(Creature)` or `And([conditions...])` with exactly one such creature
condition. Optional conditions are one `IsNonCreatureType(creatureSubtype)` and
one `IsColor(color)` or nonempty `Or([IsColor(color), ...])`. Subtypes and colors
are validated. Top-level condition order is unrestricted. Other types, numeric,
history, controller and nested-conjunction forms stay unsupported.

The event-level `Or([blockingEvent, blockedByEvent])` accepts exactly one of each
direction in either order. Both branches must have identical position-free
subject/filter declarations. Arbitrary or unequal unions are rejected. The
union has only `Trigger_ThatOtherCreature`; separate blocking and blocked-by
rules retain `Trigger_ThatOtherCreature` and `Trigger_TheBlockingCreature`.
Each is a typed `permanentEventPlan` local to its body, built as a fresh
`PermanentBinding` in each factory call. No game state is held in the plan.

Engine signatures:

- `BlocksCreatureMatching(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter) filteredCombatPairPattern`
- `BecomesBlockedByCreatureMatching(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter) filteredCombatPairPattern`
- `BlocksOrBecomesBlockedByCreatureMatching(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter) filteredCombatPairPattern`
- `(filteredCombatPairPattern).WithOpponent(*PermanentBinding) filteredCombatPairPattern`

These use existing `EvtDeclaredBlocker`, `EvtCreatureBlockedBy`, `EvtCombatPair`,
`PermanentRef`, immutable filters, definition producers, `eventPermanentCapture`,
trigger stacking, delayed frames and `Destroy`. Existing source-only APIs and
callers remain available. Engine subjects are restricted to `This` and
`AttachedPermanent`; invalid subjects and captures fail definition validation.
The existing zero-value filter means match all, but both event creatures must
still be present and phased in. Explicit supplied event incarnations are checked.

Event filters run only at detection. Current attachment lookup checks the host
incarnation; later attachment/color/subtype/control changes do not redirect the
opponent or recheck the filter. Bindings survive source departure, pending
clones and copied triggers. Actions cannot follow a returned opponent or act on
a phased-out opponent. Regeneration and indestructibility use ordinary engine
destruction. These are untargeted events; shroud does not stop them. No new LKI
read, payment, replacement ordering, simultaneous-operation or event-generation
contract is introduced. Existing transactional casting and scheduling services
remain responsible for those rules.

Inventory now preserves the `event` role under `Or/1`, including unsupported
parent/body forms. Descendant subjects, colors and references keep their roles.

### Exact supported contexts and engine reuse

Engine signature:
`NewConditionalManaAbility(condition StateCondition, whenTrue, whenFalse []ManaProduction) *ManaAbility`.
Both branches contain nonempty, fixed-color, positive-amount productions with
no restrictions or choices. Definition metadata validates the condition and
branches. Input and result slices are copied. The condition must remain unchanged
by the tap cost because payment queries precede it. It reads current source
controller and battlefield membership, with no LKI, saved result or game state
in the declaration. Missing/phased sources produce nothing.

RON signature/context:
`Activated(TapPermanent(ThisPermanent), ActionList([IfElse(condition, [AddMana(production)], [AddMana(production)])]))`.
`condition` is `PlayerPassesFilter(You, ControlsA(filter))` or nonempty, nested
`And` combinations of those `ControlsA` checks under the same player wrapper.
`filter` permits `AnyPermanent`, card types, positive/negative land or creature
subtypes, enchantment subtype, positive/negative colors or supertypes, and
nonempty `And`/`Or` combinations. Tap/combat status filters are rejected.
Subtype validation follows the existing engine family contract: custom unknown
subtypes are allowed, known mismatched families are rejected. `production` is
one concrete `ManaProduce*` symbol or a nonempty `And` of them. Repeated colors
and multiple fixed colors work. Empty branches, extra actions/costs, modifiers,
choice/dynamic production, undeclared players and other conditions are rejected.

Private compiler boundaries: `conditionalManaBody(Node) bool`,
`compileConditionalMana(Node) (optionFactory, error)`,
`compileManaCondition(Node) (mage.StateCondition, error)`,
`compileManaControlCondition(Node) (mage.StateCondition, error)`,
`compileManaControlFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)`, and
`compileManaBranch(Node) ([]mage.ManaProduction, error)`.
Factories create separate mana abilities and copied branch slices. Immutable
condition plans have no binding producers or mutable chosen state. Existing
`PlayerControls`, `AllConditions`, `PermanentFilter`, `ManaAbility`, `ManaSystem`,
solver, tap events, mana bonuses and transactional casting handle execution.
No card-name branches, fallback registry or alternate mana system was added.

Queries and activation read the same production service. Mana resolves without
a stack object (CR 605.1a/605.3b). Subtypes, not names, identify prerequisite
lands. Control changes and phasing update membership immediately; a returned
prerequisite can match the current collection. Clones keep separate battlefield,
tap and pool state. Bonus mana applies once per tap. Ability removal suppresses
activation. These rules introduce no target, delayed identity, LKI, replacement
ordering or simultaneous damage contract. Existing engine services retain those
contracts; there is no new reference or global action-result slot.

Inventory now preserves roles for `IfElse/3` branches, resolving
`PlayerPassesFilter/2`, and nested static-player `And/1`, even below rejected
bodies. Reporting does not imply general `IfElse` gameplay support.

### Supported signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine signature:
`UntilNextUpkeep(player PlayerRef, modifications ...ContinuousModification) ResolvingEffect`.
The typed player reference is validated with the modifications. At resolution the
engine saves its UUID and captures the existing subject incarnations and values.
Absent players start no effect. Nil/empty modifications, unbound player or subject
references, and control modifications outside the established end-of-turn policy
remain invalid. Direct `Until(UntilYourNextTurn, ...)` remains invalid.

RON signature/context:
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, modifications, UntilNextUpkeep(You))`.
`You` must be a bare symbol. Existing singular permanent references and supported
temporary modifications are reused in resolving spell, activation, supported
trigger, and supported delayed-action bodies. Collection operations, static
contexts, cost operations, other duration players, new modification forms, and
end-of-upkeep durations gain no support. `compileTemporaryDuration` owns spelling
and validation. Its immutable factory uses `mage.You`; each resolution captures
its own player and modification data. No mutable scope or global action slot is
added. Inventory preserves the operand's player-reference role even below a
rejected modification or earlier unsupported action.

The existing `untilEffect`, `composedLayerEffect`, layer capture/application,
`EffectManager.Remove`, `RemoveUntilYourNextTurn`, and turn scheduling supply
execution. Composed effects carry the saved player UUID. Both explicit removal
and layer pruning honor the existing source-independence contract. Legacy
noncomposed duration callers retain the current source-controller policy.

CR 109.5 fixes `You` to the resolving ability controller. Source control changes,
departure, return, ability removal and phasing do not change this duration.
Recipient control changes preserve it; departure breaks incarnation identity.
Recipient phasing suspends application but cannot postpone expiry. Effects end
before the captured player's next actual upkeep event detection and priority
(CR 500.4/500.6); layers are applied again before that event. Cleanup, untap and
other players' upkeeps do not expire them. Skipped upkeeps do not run the expiry
hook; an extra upkeep can expire them in the same turn. No delayed trigger or
stack object is added. Existing targeting, copy, transactional costs and layers
remain responsible for their contracts. No new LKI read, replacement ordering,
simultaneous operation or optional payment result is introduced.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine: `PermanentMatchesFilter(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter)
StateCondition`. Supported references are `This` and `AttachedPermanent`.
Definition validation rejects nil, target and saved references. The zero filter
matches a live subject. The declaration is immutable and has no chosen state.
Execution checks the current source and any supplied source incarnation, then
the current attachment and its saved incarnation. Shared `FilterBattlefield`
queries evaluate the filter on the same live subject. Absent, phased and returned
objects fail; departure never uses LKI. Attachment changes select the new host;
control changes preserve identity. Source/host phase cycles restore a qualifying
condition without creating a new object (CR 400.7, 702.26b).

RON: `If(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, filter), [supported-static-body...])`.
The subject must be bare `ThisPermanent` in a permanent rule or bare
`HostPermanent` in an Aura rule. Bare `IsUntapped` retains its existing adapter.
All other supported filters lower through `compileStaticConditionFilter` and the
new engine service. The reused grammar accepts nonempty nested `And`/`Or`,
`IsNonToken`, permanent type/subtype, color/supertype, tapped-state and combat
membership predicates with existing exact shapes. Ability/P/T queries remain
rejected to keep conditions independent of the characteristics their body changes.
Target, event, saved and malformed references remain compile errors. Existing
layer-6 keyword or layer-7c P/T conditional bodies are unchanged. Resolving
branches, entry/cost contexts and other conditional body forms gain no support.

`While`, `Static`, typed references, `FilterBattlefield`, static permanent sets,
`ModifyEachPT`, definition validation and the shared layer service provide
execution. Static conditions and recipient membership remain live on each pass
(CR 611.3a–c). Layer-4 subtype and layer-5 color changes precede layer-7c bonuses;
layer-6 source ability removal disables the static rule (CR 613.1d–g, 613.4c).
Factories and cloned games hold no shared mutable condition state. Aura casting,
target legality and cost rollback reuse existing services. No new replacement,
event-player, APNAP, simultaneous-operation, decision or LKI service is introduced.

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

Engine API:

- `PreventDamageThisTurn(recipient DamageRecipientRef, from PermanentFilter)
  ResolvingEffect`. A zero filter means any source. Definition validation checks
  the typed recipient, including nil and unbound target reads. Resolution uses
  the existing reference service; absent/phased recipients install no rule.
  Players keep their resolved identity. Permanents keep ID and incarnation.
  Control changes and phase cycles preserve installed rules; returned objects
  do not inherit them. Each replacement has end-of-turn duration and survives
  the source's departure, phasing and ability removal.
- `DamageSourceIsAttacking() PermanentFilter`. Live queries check the source's
  current combat incarnation. Departed or phased sources use the attacking state
  captured by `snapshotPermanentInformation` in `PermanentLKI.Attacking`.
  Existing departure and phase maps supply separate immutable information.
  Phase-in restores live queries and does not restore attacking status. A
  returned card cannot replace the original source's combat information.

RON resolving actions:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(DamageWouldBeDealtToRecipient(recipient),
[PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)` and
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(DamageWouldBeDealtByAPermanentToRecipient(filter,
recipient), [PreventThatDamage], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
Recipients reuse `compileDamagePacketRecipient`: `Permanent(typed-reference)`,
`Player(typed-reference)`, or bound bare `Ref_AnyTarget`. Existing resolving
spell/mode/activation/trigger/delayed scopes retain their own bindings. No static,
entry, cost or replacement-operation context is added. No target declaration is
created by the action itself. Source filters reuse exact supported type/subtype,
supertype/color/keyword/token/tapped predicates and nonempty nested `And`/`Or`.
Bare `IsAttacking` lowers to the new retained-state query. `IsBlocking` and
`PowerIs` remain explicitly rejected in this source context. Wrong arity,
malformed or unbound recipients, extra operations, tuple operations, empty
logical filters, and other durations remain compile errors.

`damagePreventionRuleReplacement`, `damageFilterSource`, typed target references,
`instanceBindings`, the replacement choice/recheck pipeline, simultaneous damage,
source LKI, transaction payment, stack copying and native cleanup are reused.
No parallel prevention, zone, targeting, timing or damage service is introduced.
Unlimited rules do not consume finite amounts and need no CR 615.7 allocation.
They apply to combat and noncombat packets, with affected-player ordering and
recipient rechecks after redirection. Existing unpreventable damage bypasses
prevention. The normal battlefield `IsAttacking` filter is unchanged.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

Supported resolving actions:

- `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, DiscardHand)/2`: both operands are bare symbols.
- `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, DrawNumberCards(Integer(n)))/2`: exact one-argument
  tuples for the action and number, with a nonnegative integer literal.

Lowering: `mage.DiscardEach(mage.EachPlayer)` and
`mage.DrawEach(mage.EachPlayer, mage.Fixed(n))`. The compiler entry point is
`compileEachPlayerAction(Node) ([]effectFactory, error)`.
The shared resolving-action dispatcher permits these in supported spell/mode,
activation, trigger and delayed action lists. No static, cost, entry,
replacement-operation or nested `PlayerAction` body support is added.

Existing engine services select players and current hands at resolution.
Discard prepares replacements, moves the complete batch, then sends events.
Draw performs individual actions, active player's draws first (CR 121.2/121.2c).
Separate instructions remain sequential (CR 608.2c). Empty hands and zero draws
permit continuation. Spell disposal follows CR 608.2n. Relevant local API and
rules contracts, draw rules and resolution rules were read.

No typed target, event reference, result binding or loop-local player reference
is created by these actions. Surrounding bindings retain their identity. Fresh
effect factories build each operation; no mutable chosen state is captured.
Source departure, control change or phasing cannot change the all-player set.
Existing transactional casting, stack copying, clones, draw/discard replacements,
graveyard visits, trackers and event ordering remain in use. No engine changes,
parallel rules services or LKI queries are required.

Wrong arity/kind, tuple `AnyPlayer` or `DiscardHand`, player filters other than
bare `AnyPlayer`, action-list bodies, negative/noninteger/malformed counts,
X/result-dependent amounts, shuffle and other player actions are rejected.
`ActionPlayer` remains unbound after this operation. Inventory now assigns
`EachPlayerAction/2` arguments `player_filter` and `player_action`; amount
children use the established value role. Inventory roles do not prove support.

### Supported signatures, contexts and reuse

Engine APIs:

- `RevealHandFor(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`: resolve the player, copy the
  current hand through `Game.RevealHand`, record each card through
  `recordPublicReveal`. No moves or choices; repeat reveals remain legal.
- `DiscardMatchingHand(player PlayerRef, filter CardFilter) ResolvingEffect`:
  select all matching current hand cards, construct effect-caused
  `DiscardAction`s, use `discardActionsTogetherWithEvents(actions, false)`. Replacements
  see the original hand; events see all moves. Prevented or redirected discards
  do not stop the other cards. No payment, random selection or discard choices.
- `CountMatchingHand(player PlayerRef, filter CardFilter) ResolutionValue`:
  pure current-player/current-hand count; no history, snapshot, LKI or RNG read.
  Each matching multicolor card counts once. Zero engine filters match all cards.

Nil and unbound player refs are declaration errors; unresolved or absent players
supply no reveal/discard and zero count. Existing typed player bindings,
resolution frames, casting transactions, copied targets, clone services, hand
membership, public reveal snapshots, discard replacements/events/trackers and
spell damage/prevention are reused. No parallel zone or replacement system is
introduced. Source departure, return, phasing or control change cannot redirect
an ability's resolving controller. These operations read current hands; no
permanent LKI or saved card visit is required. Selection does not follow a
previous reveal history entry. No result binding is produced or overwritten.

RON forms:
`PlayerAction(player, RevealHand)` (bare symbol only),
`PlayerAction(player, DiscardCards(filter))`, and
`TheNumberOfCardsOfTypeInPlayersHand(filter, player)` in existing resolution-value
contexts. Hand card filters: `IsCardtype(type)`, `IsNonCardtype(type)`,
`IsColor(color)`, `IsNonColor(color)`, nonempty nested `And([...])` / `Or([...])`.
RON owns spelling, filter validation and lexical reference checks. Engine owns
hand execution. This does not add bare reveal/discard actions, EachPlayerAction
bodies, cost, entry, static or replacement-operation contexts. Existing spell,
mode, activation, trigger and delayed resolving scopes use per-factory typed
references. Inventory assigns hand count operands card-filter/player-reference
roles and filtered-discard operands card-filter roles; all nested nodes remain
visible even under unsupported parents.

### Exact supported contract and reuse

RON event:
`TriggerA(WhenAPermanentDealsDamageToAPlayer(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent),
Opponent), body)`. Both arguments have exact kind/arity checks. Only source
permanents and bare Opponent are supported. Host/target subjects, collections,
AnyPlayer and SinglePlayer filters remain rejected. This shape produces only
bare `Trigger_ThatPlayer` in its resolving body; it does not produce an amount
or permanent binding. Cost, entry, static and replacement contexts are not added.

`damagePlayerPlan` has lexical identity. Each factory call creates its own
`PlayerBinding`, stored in `instanceBindings.damagePlayers` and read with
`FromPlayer`. RON owns validation, spelling, lexical scope, lowering and nested
inventory roles. Engine reuse: `DealsDamageToOpponent(This, binding)`,
`WhenEvent`, `Sequence`, typed reference/target services, event capture,
resolution frames, pending-trigger clone and stack-copy services, actual damage,
prevention and combat. No new event system, game-time declaration panic,
card-name branch, global last-action slot or fallback registry.

The engine checks the opponent of the source controller at event time. Combat
and noncombat actual damage trigger; zero and fully prevented damage do not.
Each event keeps its own player. Source departure, return, phasing, control
changes and copied-trigger controller changes cannot redirect that player.
No permanent LKI read is needed by this adapter: facts are already captured.

`PlayerAction(player, DiscardHand)` requires a bare action symbol and an existing
typed player reference. It is supported in existing resolving player-action
scopes, using `DiscardMatchingHand(player, CardFilter{})`. Select the current
hand at resolution. The existing simultaneous discard service prepares all
replacements before moves and sends events after all moves. This is not a
bare action or EachPlayerAction adapter and does not add a cost context.
Random discard reuses existing `DiscardAtRandom` without a new random service.

Selection: the three poison cards offer the strongest credible gain for the
