### Exact supported shapes and reuse

Engine API: `AddPoisonFor(subject PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue)
ResolvingEffect`. Resolve the player, then read the amount in the current
resolution frame. Positive amounts use `Player.AddPoisonCounters`; absent
references and nonpositive amounts make no change. Definition validation checks
nil and unbound declarations. This instruction does not deal damage, lose life
or run state-based actions. Existing checks cause loss at ten poison counters.
Dynamic engine values are supported and tested with event-local `FromNumber`.
No new generic player-counter replacement contract is claimed.

RON resolving `PutCounters/1` accepts a one-element list containing
`ACounterOfTypeOnPlayer(PoisonCounter, player)` or
`NumberCountersOfTypeOnPlayer(Integer(n), PoisonCounter, player)`, where n is a
nonnegative integer literal. Existing typed player references are supported.
Other counter types, dynamic RON amounts, plural lists, costs and entry contexts
remain rejected. Permanent-counter placement keeps its existing behavior.

RON event: `TriggerA(WhenAPermanentDealsDamageToAPlayer(
SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), AnyPlayer), body)`. Bare AnyPlayer extends the
existing bare Opponent shape. Reuse `DealsDamageToPlayer(This, binding)` and
`DealsDamageToOpponent(This, binding)` respectively. Only the source permanent
is supported. The body gains bare player reference `Trigger_ThatPlayer`; no
amount/permanent binding is fabricated. The private lexical plan creates a
fresh `PlayerBinding` per ability factory and uses existing `instanceBindings`.

Token context: the ability list of `TokenWithPT/6` or `NamedTokenWithPT/7` accepts
this source damage-player `TriggerA/2` with bare AnyPlayer or Opponent, together
with existing keywords. Compile each body in a fresh permanent scope. The
creator's targets, X, payments and event bindings cannot enter that scope.
Supported body actions reuse the existing resolving compiler. Each card/effect
factory builds a fresh immutable `DefineToken` declaration with `TokenAbilities`;
engine token cloning supplies distinct runtime IDs and sources. Other token
trigger families and token supertypes remain rejected.

RON owns spelling, positioned errors, lexical scope, typed lowering and nested
inventory roles. Engine reuse: player resolution frames, number values,
actual-damage events, prevention pipeline, LKI event facts, deferred/APNAP
triggers, stack copies, token batches, token ability cloning, payment rollback,
phasing and game/player cloning. No card-name executor, global last-action slot,
Go fallback, partial production registry or new reflection dispatch is added.
No permanent information read needs LKI: the damaged player is already saved
at event time. Prevented events produce no trigger; partial damage produces
one fixed poison instruction regardless of the amount dealt.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine APIs:
`WithCastingCondition(condition StateCondition) ActionOption` for `ActionSpell`;
`IsDuringSteps(steps ...PhaseStep) StateCondition`;
`AfterFirstUpkeep() StateCondition`. TurnReader now exposes `GetStep() PhaseStep`
and `UpkeepHasEnded() bool`; all repository callers build. This is an added
interface requirement for outside implementations. Conditions run with the
casting card ID and caster ID before choices and payment. Definition validation
rejects nil/invalid trees, unavailable target/payment bindings, battlefield-source
reads and casting conditions on activations. Multiple conditions are conjunctive.
Input step slices are copied. Queries are pure and grant no priority or sorcery
permission. Conditions do not run again when copying or resolving a stack spell;
casting a card copy does run them.

TurnSystem owns first-upkeep completion and the stored step's turn identity.
Native upkeep completion and direct same-turn SetStep departure record it.
Later upkeep steps remain permitted (CR 503.2). Turn changes clear history;
clone state is independent. A skipped upkeep does not produce completion.
A late extra upkeep can become the first actual upkeep. New turns cannot inherit
history from an old turn ending during upkeep. The first step-index prototype
failed the new real Reset second-upkeep test; it was replaced by this history
contract before acceptance. The external rules check agrees with local CR 503.2:
[Wizards Comprehensive Rules](https://media.wizards.com/2024/downloads/MagicCompRules%2004102024.pdf).
The skipped-upkeep behavior follows CR 500.11 and the actual-completion contract.

RON supports one top-level `CastEffect(CantBeCastUnless(condition))/1` on a
nonmodal instant/sorcery, independent of its order beside SpellActions.
Conditions: nonempty nested `And/1` lists; `IsAPlayersTurn/1` or `IsPlayersTurn/1`
with bare You or Opponent; bare IsDuringUpkeep, IsDuringDeclareAttackersStep,
IsDuringDeclareBlockersStep, IsAfterUpkeep. The last uses AfterFirstUpkeep,
not a numeric step comparison. RON owns spelling, arity, scope and diagnostics.
Other predicates/operations, duplicates, permanents, modal spells and nested
CastEffect actions remain rejected. No synthetic targets or event values exist.

Resolving `UntapEachPermanent(filter)/1` uses existing pure permanent filters,
And composition, and at most one
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(typed-player-reference))/1` restriction.
Reuse compileCountFilter, typed instanceBindings, MatchingPermanents,
PermanentsControlledBy and UntapEach. Selection occurs at resolution, excluding
phased objects. Plural-target and chosen-payment collections remain rejected.
Complete other consumers read: Candelabra of Tawnos (PayManaX and targeted
collection blockers), Magnetic Mountain and Thelon's Curse (payment-choice
collections); none is an estimated unlock.

Existing services retain casting transactions, target identity/legality,
copy retargeting, native priority, duration/cleanup, simultaneous untap batches,
stun replacements and clone behavior. The shared gate covers hand, free and
alternate-cost zone casting, cast copies and castability queries. No card-name
branch, Go fallback, game-time declaration panic, mutable global result slot,
partial production registry or second rule system was added.

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `TargetToughnessLessThanSourcePower() PermanentTargetOption`, used
with typed singular/plural permanent target declarations. Strict comparison
reads current target toughness and current source power at announcement and
resolution. Missing source information permits no targets. Departure uses
retained incarnation power; return cannot substitute another source. Phasing
uses the existing phase-information snapshot's power; phase-in restores live
queries. Retained power includes continuous bonuses and counters. Copies keep
the source and independently use the copy controller's other restrictions.
The option adds no mutable binding or chosen state.

RON supported forms:

- `PowerAndToughnessIsEqualTo(PT(p,t))/1`, with two signed integer literals.
  Uses HasPowerEqual and HasToughnessEqual on current characteristics in
  existing permanent-filter contexts.
- `ToughnessIs(EqualTo(Integer(n)))/1`, `LessThanOrEqualTo`, or
  `GreaterThanOrEqualTo`, with a signed fixed integer. Uses engine equality/GTE,
  Or and Not, without arithmetic overflow or a parallel characteristic query.
- In permanent target contexts only:
  `ToughnessIs(LessThan(PowerOfPermanent(ThisPermanent)))/1`.
  The permanent source must be available in that lexical scope. Nested And
  composes with existing controller/type restrictions. Source comparisons under
  disjunctions and non-target contexts remain rejected. Unsupported comparisons,
  X, host/target references, bad shapes, and unbound spell sources are rejected.

Reuse: DeclarePermanentTarget(s), per-instance target declarations, target
announcement/resolution validation, transactional activation/casting, current
P/T filters, resolutionTargetSource, incarnation/phase LKI, stack copies,
Game.Clone, continuous modifications, AtNext and captured delayed references.
RON owns spelling and scopes; the engine owns source-relative target legality.
No card-name branch, Go fallback, skipped rule, partial production registry,
global last-action slot, or game-time declaration panic was added.
Delayed destruction does not repeat target filters. Return makes a new object;
phasing at the next end step can consume the one-shot delay without destruction.
Indestructible retains existing destroy semantics. Simultaneous operations and
replacement ordering are unchanged; this slice introduces no batches or costs.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Private adapter: compileCoinBranch(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error).
Supported resolving forms: FlipACoin_OnLose([actions])/1 and
FlipACoin_OnWinAndLose([win-actions], [loss-actions])/2. Each supplied list is
nonempty. Both branches are compiled and validated. Nested branches are allowed.
Existing spell/mode, activation, trigger and delayed resolving contexts use the
same dispatcher. No cost/static/entry/replacement/PlayerAction body context,
new target declaration, heads/tails result binding or repeat procedure is added.

Each branch receives the surrounding scope by value and builds its effects
with the same per-instance typed instanceBindings. Target, event, X and paid
cost reads keep their lexical producer and identity. Optional payment and its
adjacent continuation stay together inside a branch; results cannot escape to
another branch or later action. Malformed kinds/arities, empty lists, unbound
or incompatible refs, nested target declarations and unsupported children are
positioned compile errors, even when they are in an unselected branch.

RON owns spelling, declaration validation, lexical scope and inventory roles.
Engine reuse: FlipCoin(You), OnWin, OnLoss, Sequence, RandomSource and its Clone,
typed target declarations/resolution frames, transactional casting/activation,
AtNext captured delayed references, source LKI, token creation, damage prevention,
sacrifice and temporary layer modifications. There is one flip at resolution;
only the selected branch runs. Loss-only wins consume a flip with no action.
Stack copies flip separately with their resolving controller. Failed casting,
activation and all-illegal resolution do not consume live random outcomes.

Goblin Kites installs its flying effect and delay before any flip. The next
end-step trigger keeps the controller and target incarnation and has no new
target. Return cannot substitute a new creature. Phasing can prevent sacrifice;
a phase cycle retains identity. Shroud and toughness changes after installation
do not repeat targeting. Losing control prevents the original controller's
sacrifice. The one-shot trigger still flips once and is consumed when its
sacrifice cannot happen. Bottle's source sacrifice is a cost; later damage uses
the shared prevention/source services. Its token uses the resolving controller.
No engine API, replacement order or simultaneous-operation contract is added.
No global result slot, Go fallback, card-name executor, declaration panic,
parallel rules service or partial production registry is introduced.

### Exact shapes, engine contracts and reuse boundary

RON resolving actions: `RemoveCreatureFromCombat(ref)/1` and
`RemoveCreatureFromCombatAndUnblockBlockers(ref)/1`, using `compilePermanentRef`
and per-factory `instanceBindings` in existing spell/mode/activation/trigger
bodies and coin branches. They declare no targets. The former lowers to existing
`RemovePermanentFromCombat`; the latter to new
`RemovePermanentFromCombatAndUnblock(PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`.
Unbound/incompatible refs, wrong kind/arity and cost/static uses remain errors.

`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(ref, [CantBlock], UntilEndOfTurn)/3` accepts the
existing source or singular target scope, exactly one symbol operation and the
symbol duration. It lowers to `Until(EndOfTurn, CantBlock(ref))`.
`CantBlock(PermanentRef) ContinuousModification` uses `AddCanBlockOnly` with
`Not(AnyPermanent)`, preserving native legality, cumulative restrictions,
incarnation capture, duration, layers and clone behavior. It survives ability
removal, source departure, control changes and phase cycles after installation;
returned objects are distinct. Later combats are restricted; existing blocks
are not removed by the restriction. Absent/phased refs install no rule.

Combat groups retain a per-attacker set of blocker ID/incarnation pairs added
this combat. Explicit unblocking requires that the resolved incarnation is still
blocking the attacker and is its sole historical blocker. A different blocker's
departure does not make it historically sole. Multiple groups are independent;
clones copy the history maps and combat reset discards them. Ordinary removal
continues to leave attackers blocked. Existing legacy unblocking callers retain
their behavior. No new unblocked-attack event is fired by this action.

Required departure prerequisite: `RemoveFromBattlefield` removes live combat
membership after `captureLKI`. The snapshot keeps attacking status and exact
current combat-opponent incarnations. Existing `ForEachCombatOpponent` uses the
source's captured incarnation to read departure information, then acts only on
still-present, unphased matching opponents. This preserves its death-effect
caller without retaining stale live combat membership or following returned
objects. Snapshot lists are private immutable values; clone queries reuse the
existing incarnation-keyed LKI service. The legacy live-only typed
`BlockingOrBlockedBy` contract is unchanged.

RON owns spelling/validation/lowering. Combat, LKI, references, definition
validation, native triggers/APNAP, costs, coin/RNG, copied stack objects,
continuous rules and cleanup remain engine services. There is no card-name
executor, fallback, global last-action slot, production subset registry or
parallel subsystem. The inventory assigns permanent-reference roles to the
new action operands; reporting is not support proof.

### TDD and card-to-test mappings

New engine tests failed for missing typed unblocking and `CantBlock` constructors.
New RON gameplay failed for both unsupported removal actions. After lowering,
focused tests exposed missing live combat removal on departure; a synthetic
engine regression then failed for a departed object that still blocked. A test
used an incorrect LKI getter; it was corrected to `LKI` before confirming that
behavior failure. The native casting fixture needed its precombat-main setup.

The short suite exposed an older regression that expected the departed
incarnation to remain in live combat. Its assertion now requires both old and
returned incarnations to be absent from combat, and separately requires the
old pair in retained history. This is a contract correction under CR 506.4,

`ExecuteBlockers` resolves triggers, so a subsequent loss can remove a legally
declared blocker. A deterministic win now isolates the declaration restriction;
no assertion is weakened and no production rule is changed for the fixture.

### Exact signatures, contexts and ownership

Engine API:
`DeclareSpellTargetTargetingControlledPermanent(name string, filters ...CardFilter)
*SpellTargetBinding`. It declares one spell target with optional intrinsic card
filters. A selected spell must currently target at least one permanent controlled
by the player who chooses this spell target. The normal target service checks
this at announcement and resolution. Stack abilities and nil-card objects are
excluded. Each factory gets a fresh declaration.

RON intrinsic filter `IsEnchantmentType(Aura)/1` requires the enchantment card
type and Aura subtype. Only the symbol `Aura` is supported. It composes with
existing card-type/color filters and recursive nonempty intrinsic `And`/`Or`.

RON target filter:
`TargetsAPermanent(ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You)))/1`, alone or once in
a top-level `And([spellFilters])/1` for `TargetSpell(filter)/1`. Other conjuncts
can use recursive intrinsic spell filters. The selected shape works in existing
spell, mode, activation and trigger target declarations. `Ref_TargetSpell`
retains its existing per-instance binding. Duplicate history predicates,
history predicates below nested logical operators, other permanent predicates,
other players, malformed constructors and unbound/incompatible references are
compile errors. Inventory follows the operand into permanent-filter,
player-filter and player-reference roles; inspection is not proof of support.

RON owns spelling, shape checks and lowering. The engine reads each selected
stack object's target zones and captured permanent incarnations, and checks
current battlefield presence and control. CR 115.9b permits a target that gained
shroud to qualify even though it became illegal for the original spell.
Departure information is not used. Returned and phased-out objects do not
qualify; a phase cycle retains identity. Multiple targets need only one matching
permanent. Copies keep distinct stack identity and use their own current target
lists and controllers. Source departure, phasing and control changes do not
change a pending ability's controller.

Existing definition validation, typed target binding, cost transactions, stack
copying, clone isolation, target rechecks, native casting/activation, cleanup and
`Counter` execute the behavior. Uncounterable spells can be selected, but remain
on the stack after countering is attempted. No new damage, simultaneous-action,
replacement-order, LKI or payment service is needed. No card-name branch,
global last-action slot, fallback or partial production registry was added.
Existing `DeclareSpellTarget` callers keep their behavior.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

RON activation cost: `PayManaX(manaSymbols, ValueX)/2`, directly or within
nested `And([costs])/1` in `Activated/2` or `ActivatedWithModifiers/3`.
`manaSymbols` is the existing validated list grammar, with at least one bare
`ManaCostX`; fixed generic and colored symbols can share the list. The second
operand must be bare `ValueX`. Multiple X symbols or separate X cost components
use the same announced value (CR 107.3i). No new engine constructor is needed.
The adapter returns fresh `mage.ManaCostPayment` costs and declares X in that
activation's copied scope. Unbound action and target values, wrong arity,
malformed mana, a list without X, tuple bindings, defined-X expressions and
optional resolution payments are compile errors. X cannot leak between abilities.

`NumberTargetPermanents(ValueX, permanentFilter)/2` now checks that scope's X
declaration. Fixed counts retain their behavior. Resolving
`UntapEachPermanent(Ref_TargetPermanents)/1` uses the bound typed collection,
including fixed-count declarations, in existing spell/mode/activation/trigger
contexts. It lowers to `mage.UntapEach` and preserves each chosen incarnation.
Undeclared, malformed, singular and delayed collection reads remain errors;
existing filter-based untap forms are unchanged. Inventory walks PayManaX's
mana list as metadata and its amount as an announcement value, even below a
rejected parent. Reporting does not imply support for those parent contexts.

Engine prerequisite: `prepareActionPaymentTransaction` materializes each
`ManaCostPayment`'s announced X before applying the existing activation reduction.
`prepareActionCosts` already aggregates ordinary mana components. The saved
stack X remains unchanged by reductions or subsequent announcements. The existing
minimum-total-mana restriction is retained; colored costs remain colored.
Existing legacy `XManaCost` callers are preserved. Cost validation/planning and
commit remain on the shared isolated transaction. No new payment, target, zone,
untap, replacement or simultaneous-operation service is introduced.

`instanceBindings`, `DeclareXPermanentTargets`, `UntapEach`, stack X capture,
source/target incarnations, legality rechecks, mana planning, copying and cloning
supply execution. Target return creates a new object; phase cycles keep identity
(CR 400.7, 702.26b/d). Illegal targets are excluded at resolution, and all-illegal
abilities do not resolve (CR 608.2b). Source departure, control or phasing does
not redirect the saved targets. Untapping does not act on absent-object LKI.
Activation at instant timing and zero X use existing permissions (CR 107.3a,
601.2b/f, 602.2b). No new replacement-order or simultaneous-batch contract applies.

### Exact signatures, context, dependencies and reuse

Permanent rule `ActivatedWithModifiers(cost, actions, modifier)/3` accepts
`ActivateOnlyIf(condition)/1` where `condition` is one of these bare symbols:

- `IsDuringCombat`: BeginCombat, DeclareAttackers, DeclareBlockers,
  FirstStrikeDamage, CombatDamage or EndCombat.
- `IsDuringEndOfCombatStep`: EndCombat only.
- `IsDuringDeclareBlockersStep`: DeclareBlockers only.
- `IsDuringUpkeep`: Upkeep only, in either player's turn.

Each lowers to `mage.WithActivationCondition` with an immutable allowed-step
list. Existing modifier `And([modifiers])/1` combines predicates, turn restrictions
and use limits. Conditions do not set or replace the action's timing field.
They supply neither controller permission nor priority. The shared activation
query, mana solver and transactional announcement path check them before
payment. Resolution and copied stack abilities do not repeat the check.
Malformed tuples, unknown predicates, conditions with arguments and an inner

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API:
`DealDamageEachPlayer(source DamageSourceRef, subjects PlayerSet,
member *PlayerBinding, amount ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`.

Select current player membership once, in the set's order. Ignore duplicate and
absent IDs. Bind each player only while reading its amount. Evaluate all amounts
before any replacement or damage processing. Restore outer saved-player state
before the batch and callbacks. Nonpositive amounts create no assignment.
Definition validation treats the member as a local producer for the amount;
it cannot authorize reads in the set, before the operation or afterward. Nil
inputs, empty binding names and unbound reads fail validation.

RON resolving actions `SpellDealsDamage(ThisSpell, amount, recipient)/3` and
`PermanentDealsDamage(ThisPermanent, amount, recipient)/3` now accept:

- Existing `Player(player-reference)/1`, with bare `DealsDamage_ThatPlayer`
  bound only inside `amount` to that existing typed reference.
- `EachPlayer(AnyPlayer)/1` and `EachPlayer(Opponent)/1`, with a fresh typed
  amount-member declaration for each operation and factory instance.

Existing resolution values can read the local reference, including
`TheNumberOfCardsInPlayersHand(player)/1` and
`TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter)/1` with
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(player))`. Existing value grammar is retained.
Recipient declarations compile outside the local scope. Other actions, modes,
permanent/mixed amounts and delayed bodies cannot inherit the local reference.
General player filters, payment results and per-player discard results remain
unsupported. Bare player-target damage and other accepted recipients retain
their existing lowering. Both spell and permanent action contexts are covered.

`ron` owns spelling, lexical scope and typed plans. The engine owns the local
runtime frame and batch execution. Reuse: `DealDamageFrom`, `PlayerBinding`,
`HandSizeOf`, `CountPermanents`, `PermanentsControlledBy`, `EachPlayer`,
`OpponentsOf(You)`, shared definition validation, `DamageSourceRef`,
`PlayerDamageAssignment`, `DealSimultaneousDamage`, replacement choice/rechecks,
transactional casting/activation, target declarations, stack copies and game
cloning. No card-name branch, fallback, game-time declaration panic, partial
production registry or global last-action slot is added.

The native source service retains departure incarnation and LKI. A pending
activation keeps its controller; lifelink uses the live or retained source
controller. Return cannot substitute a new source incarnation. Phasing keeps
identity. Copies read their own target and controller. Prevention/redirection
change the proposed damage; they do not change the player used to compute the
original amount. Amounts are read at resolution, not announcement.

Semantic inventory now assigns the argument of recipient `EachPlayer/1` the
player-filter role even below an earlier unsupported action. Inventory remains
report-only and cannot authorize compilation of unsupported bodies.

### Established signatures, contexts and reuse

Public signatures remain unchanged:

- `Game.AddPreventionShield(id uuid.UUID, amount int)`.
- `PreventNextDamage(recipient DamageRecipientRef, amount ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`.
- `Game.DealSimultaneousDamage(assignments ...DamageAssignment)`.
- `Combat.ResolveDamage(g *Game, isFirstStrikeStep bool)`.

The supported engine context is the ordinary finite recipient shield over
explicit player/permanent damage packets. Current recipient control determines
the chooser. With distinct source identities and insufficient capacity,
`ChooseNumber` supplies legally bounded amounts, including zero for a packet.
Capacity sums are bounded by the shield amount to avoid overflow. A focused
maximum-integer test confirmed this failure before its fix. Bounds ensure all
applicable capacity is spent. Invalid answers use the legal
maximum. Forced amounts, enough capacity and a single source require no prompt.
Nonpositive or absent/phased/returned recipient packets are excluded. Saved
source ID and incarnation distinguish sources; a returned card cannot replace
retained source/controller/lifelink information. Prompts identify packet,
amount and retained source controller.

The batch replacement path reuses the existing matching service, priority tiers,
affected-player lookup, replacement labels and `ChooseMode`. It offers
replacement choices for later packets, not only the first assignment. Each
packet keeps its own applied-effect set, local to this invocation. Self
replacements run before ordinary shield choices; matching and priority are
checked again after changes. Prevention and redirection can be selected in
either order. A redirected packet can join a recipient shield group. Shield
consumption remains in `preventionShieldReplacement`; no state is held in RON,
no global last-action slot is added, and clone/captured-incarnation/expiry
ownership stays in the existing engine services. Unpreventable/unredirectable
packets do not consume the ordinary shield.

Native combat now collects assignments and uses the same batch, separately for
first-strike and normal steps. Both blocked and unblocked paths, including
existing band paths, feed that collection. Existing combat assignment and band
source-attribution behavior is preserved, rather than claimed as a new contract.
In particular, aggregate band source attribution remains a separate audit item
before claiming complete finite-card gameplay across all combat interactions.
Damage and lifelink execute before damage events and notifications. Single-damage
callers retain their existing replacement path. Shared candidate/label helpers
avoid duplicating matching, priority and replacement-label policy.

`ron` still owns spelling, lexical scope and declaration plans. No new RON
signature or context is authorized. The downstream shape remains rejected:
`CreateFuturePreventDamage(NextAmountOfDamageThatWouldBeDealtThisTurnToRecipient(amount, recipient), [PreventThatDamage])/2`.
Fixed/X values, typed any-target/permanent/player recipients, spell modes,
activations, delayed return and additional operations require subsequent adapter
and complete-card gameplay evidence. Source-specific prevention is outside this
ordinary recipient-shield contract.

Selection rationale: the incoming band defect is concrete and independently
reproducible, blocks a ten-card capability, and can be closed through a small
shared engine service. Complete finite records and the fresh ledger evidence
showed why an adapter alone would be premature. The contract, reuse boundary,
acceptance cases and zero immediate gain were stated before edits. The
`implement-engine` skill supplied the workflow; no removed card skill or Go card
requirements were used. No subagents were used.

### Exact service and contexts

New optional player interface:

```go
type BandingDamageAssigner interface {
    GetBandingDamageAssignment(g *Game, source *Permanent,
        recipients []*Permanent, amount int) map[uuid.UUID]int
}
```

Context: each positive blocking source assigning incoming damage to the current
members of an ordinary attacking band, separately in each damage step. Current
banding gives the choice to the attacking player; after its loss, the blocking
source's controller chooses. A result must use only eligible recipient IDs,
nonnegative amounts and the source's exact total. Nil/invalid maps use bounded
`Player.ChooseNumber`; invalid number answers use the legal maximum. No mutable
assignment state survives this invocation. Zero/negative sources are excluded
individually; `combatDamageValue` retains the toughness-assignment service.

The old `BandingDamageDistributor.GetBandingDamageDistribution([]*Permanent)`
signature is retained. Without a source-aware hook, one valid aggregate map
sets the recipient totals. Bounded per-source choices preserve those totals
and leave the caller's map unchanged. Invalid totals and an overflowing
aggregate total use independent source choices. Assignment validation subtracts
from the source budget, rather than adding untrusted amounts.

`Combat.AddBlockerIncarnation` now saves each blocker link for every attacking
band member, without duplicates. Removing the named member does not remove the
survivors' links. `SnapshotBlockedAlone` counts distinct blockers rather than
links. Current attack incarnations limit recipients. Native departure/phasing
removes combat membership; returned and phased-in objects do not regain it.

Reuse: `combatDamageValue`, `DealsDamageInStep`, `CaptureDamageSource`,
`PermanentDamageAssignment`, the existing `combatDamagePlan`,
`DealSimultaneousDamage`, finite shield allocation, replacement ordering/rechecks,
source/recipient incarnations, damage histories, lifelink, state checks and game
cloning. Source packets retain their own amount, ID, incarnation, controller,
owner, characteristics and keywords before replacements run. No RON spelling,
scope, binding or production-registry change is added. No parallel damage or
zone service, global last-action slot, fallback Go factory or card-name branch
is introduced.

Outgoing attacking-band aggregation and its shared trample/deathtouch decisions,
blocking-band assignment, "bands with other", and the old lethal-order policy
in other combat paths are excluded and remain open. This slice does not certify
complete banding gameplay. The finite RON shape remains rejected:
`CreateFuturePreventDamage(NextAmountOfDamageThatWouldBeDealtThisTurnToRecipient(amount, recipient), [PreventThatDamage])/2`.

### Exact shapes, contexts and dependencies

New resolving action:
`CreateFuturePreventDamage(NextAmountOfDamageThatWouldBeDealtThisTurnToRecipient(amount, recipient), [PreventThatDamage])/2`.
The event is an exact two-argument tuple. `amount` is exact `Integer(n)/1` with a
nonnegative integer literal, or bound bare `ValueX`. Zero is legal. Values are
read once at resolution through `mage.ValueAtResolution`. Other values remain
rejected in this shape.

Recipients reuse `compileDamagePacketRecipient`: `Permanent(typed-reference)`,
`Player(typed-reference)`, or bound bare `Ref_AnyTarget`. The enclosing scope must
supply each reference. Actions do not create targets. Permanent/player/any-target
bindings are built per factory instance. Spells, separate spell modes,
activations, triggers and delayed resolving bodies use their existing scopes.
Static rules, costs, entry operations and replacement operations gain no new
context. Activated modes, extra operations, source-specific events, malformed
arity, tuple `PreventThatDamage()`, incompatible/unbound references and negative
literals remain compile errors.

Lowering uses `mage.PreventNextDamage`, existing typed references and
`instanceBindings`. The engine owns captured recipient incarnations, control
and phasing, shield installation/consumption, amount capture, replacement
ordering/rechecks, simultaneous source allocation, source LKI, lifelink, cost
transactions, copied stack objects, pending clones and native cleanup. Rakalite
reuses `CreateFutureTrigger` -> `mage.AtNext` and the existing owner-return action.
No engine behavior or public signature changes. No duplicate prevention service.

Inventory now identifies the event's value and recipient roles and the action's
prevention event/operation roles, including children of rejected records. The
syntax snapshot remains unchanged because no RON source changed.

`AddType`). After that correction, the new complete-card tests failed for
`unsupported action (CreateFuturePreventDamage)`. The adapter then passed the

retarget choices belong to the copy controller, replacement labels use generic
engine labels (the fixture selects the installed redirect by index), and a
creature-type removal cannot test marked damage on a noncreature. The final
type-recheck case instead removes artifact identity from a still-creature target.
The retained-source case returns the same physical card under a new controller.

Existing damage-scope rejection coverage now tests malformed `Ref_AnyTarget()`
in the supported action. Existing life-mode tests now compile and execute the
complete modal records for all seven reprints, rather than extracting only the
life branch and requiring complete-record rejection. Exact inventory assertions

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Resolving actions:

- `SearchLibrary([FindAGenericCard, PutFoundCardsIntoHand, Shuffle])/1`.
- `SearchLibrary([FindACardOfType(And([IsSupertype(Basic), IsCardtype(Land)])),
  PutFoundCardsOntoBattlefield([EntersNormally]), Shuffle])/1`.

`And` accepts the two basic/land operands in either order, each once. These are
complete supported instruction sequences, not arbitrary search pipelines.
Wrong arity, extra/missing/reordered instructions, tuple spellings for bare
symbols, other destinations, modifiers, filters and plural searches are rejected.
Existing resolving spell, activation, trigger and delayed bodies can use the
actions. Static rules, costs, entry instructions and explicit player actions gain
no new context. No target, saved object, result or loop binding is produced.
The resolution controller is retained; the action does not follow the source's
later control, departure, phasing or returned incarnation.

The RON adapter owns spelling and shape checks. It lowers to existing
`mage.SearchLibraryToHand` and `mage.SearchLibraryToBattlefield`. The engine owns
choices, candidate legality, hidden zones, destination movement, normal entry,
shuffling and clones. Factories create fresh effects with no mutable choice
state. No Go-card fallback, name branch, global result slot, partial production
registry, declaration panic or alternate zone/entry service is added.

The `implement-engine` skill was used for shared engine repairs. Existing public
signatures and callers remain. Unqualified searches require a canonical candidate
when the library is nonempty; nil/foreign decisions use the first candidate.
Qualified searches may find no card. Candidates are validated by ID and the
canonical object is used. Empty searches do not prompt. Both services shuffle
once after destination movement, including empty/declined searches. A failed
normal entry restores the card to its library before shuffle. The existing
`PutOnBattlefieldBy` pipeline retains tapped entry and counter replacements.
No new search-restriction or general zone-replacement contract is claimed.

Inventory roles now describe search instructions, library card filters and
normal entry operations, even below rejected parents. Reporting does not change
strict loading. The source snapshot is unchanged, so no vocabulary refresh is
needed. No DSL function or Go definition is removed: complete loading, gameplay
and startup remain below the removal gates, and no caller audit authorizes deletion.

### Exact contract, contexts and engine reuse

No compiler adapter or RON shape is added. Existing ordinary `Banding` rules
and keyword grants use the repaired engine attacking-band outgoing path.
`CombatDamageAssigner.GetCombatDamageAssignment(g *Game, attacker *Permanent,
blockers []*Permanent, totalPower int) map[uuid.UUID]int` keeps its signature
and now receives each attacking source and its own positive damage amount.
Assignments have no lethal order. A current ordinary banding blocker changes
the chooser to the defender (CR 702.22j). That chooser uses the existing
`BandingDamageAssigner.GetBandingDamageAssignment(g *Game, source *Permanent,
recipients []*Permanent, amount int) map[uuid.UUID]int`, then the existing
`BandingDamageDistributor.GetBandingDamageDistribution(members []*Permanent)
map[uuid.UUID]int`, once per outgoing source. Incoming legacy aggregate requests
keep their prior behavior. No signature or unrelated combat path changes.

Source maps must use eligible blocker IDs, nonnegative amounts and at most the
source amount. Nontrample sources assign the complete amount. Only a trampling
source can leave a remainder for the defender. The complete band's assignments
must supply lethal damage to every blocker before that remainder is legal;
marked damage, other band members' assignments and assigned deathtouch damage
count (CR 702.19b). Caller maps are copied. Validation subtracts available
amounts to avoid overflow. Missing/invalid nontrample defending-band decisions
use the existing bounded number service. Other invalid complete plans use a
legal default plan, assigning nontrample sources before trampling sources and
retaining shared lethal damage. Decisions make no payments or live damage.

Each source keeps its captured ID, incarnation, controller, characteristics and
keywords. Phasing, departure, return, removal and control changes cannot restore
old combat membership. Zero/negative sources do not reduce another member's
damage. First/double strike use `DealsDamageInStep`. A blocked band with no
blockers deals only its trampling members' own damage to the defender. The
existing `DamageSource`, `PermanentDamageAssignment`, `PlayerDamageAssignment`,
`DealSimultaneousDamage`, finite shield allocation, replacement priority/rechecks,
histories, lifelink and game cloning execute the result. All assignments precede
one batch, and notifications follow that batch. No parallel damage system,
global result slot, name branch, factory fallback or partial registry is added.

The `implement-engine` skill supplied the shared-engine workflow. Compiler
spelling and scope logic remain in `ron`; there is no new binding, cost or target
plan. No DSL export is removed. The old private band-aggregate validator is
removed after its only caller is replaced; a repository search found no other
caller. Complete loading, gameplay/test migration and startup gates remain
unsatisfied, so Go definitions and generators remain in place.

### Exact signatures, context and reuse boundary

`Activated(cost, Modal_ChooseOne([body, body, ...]))` and
`ActivatedWithModifiers(cost, Modal_ChooseOne([body, body, ...]), modifiers)`
accept two or more supported `ActionList`/`Targeted` bodies. Every body must
compile. Unsupported nested modes, unbound/incompatible/cross-mode targets,
wrong arity and short mode lists reject the record. Supported activation costs
and modifiers retain their existing contracts. Costs apply to the complete
ability; chosen payment values are available in each mode, with distinct
per-instance bindings. The RON spelling and lexical scope remain in `ron`.

`compileChooseOneModes` and `buildChooseOneModes` are private shared compiler
helpers for spells and activations. Each mode resets target scope and uses its
own namespace. Each factory builds fresh targets and effects; payment bindings
are shared only within that ability instance. `compileActivatedRule` lowers to
`mage.NewModalActivated`. An empty supported cost declaration uses an explicit
zero cost. There are no game-time declaration panics or global action-result
slots. Existing nonmodal callers keep their signatures and behavior.

Reuse: engine mode legality/announcement, activation transaction, saved payment
numbers, target bindings/incarnations, source information, stack copies,
resolution legality, finite prevention/allocation, simultaneous damage and
cleanup. Mode choice and chosen-mode targets precede payment. Resolution and
copies retain that mode. Source sacrifice does not stop its effect; returned
and phased targets still fail legality as appropriate. No new engine rule,
parallel execution service, fallback or partial production registry is added.

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

Engine APIs:

- `ShuffleHandsAndGraveyardsIntoLibraries(subjects PlayerSet) ResolvingEffect`.
  Selects current hands and graveyards and moves them into their own libraries.
  All selected players' moves finish before per-card zone events and one
  graveyard-departure batch per player. All shuffles finish before a later
  instruction. Empty hands/libraries still shuffle. The typed collection is
  checked by definition validation; nil declarations reject before execution.
- `ShuffleHandsIntoLibrariesAndDraw(subjects PlayerSet) ResolvingEffect`.
  Moves hands only, then draws each player's moved count. The UUID-keyed count
  map is private to one invocation. Counts are captured before draws, survive
  later hand changes, and are separate across invocations, copies and clones.
  No general result binding or shared mutable declaration is introduced.

RON resolving action-list shapes:

- `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, ShuffleHandAndGraveyardIntoLibrary)`.
  Lowers to the first API with `mage.EachPlayer`. Later fixed draw instructions
  remain separate and use the existing `DrawEach` service.
- The adjacent pair `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, ShuffleHandIntoLibrary)`,
  `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, DrawNumberCards(NumCardsShuffledIntoLibraryThisWay))`.
  Lowers to the second API. The result is scoped to this pair and is not
  available to another mode, branch, or action. Missing/nonadjacent consumers,
  other player collections, tuple symbols, wrong arity, incompatible producers
  and standalone result reads reject the declaration. Other result consumers
  remain unsupported. Existing activation/modal action lists use this shape.

`ron` owns spelling, exact pair validation, producer dominance and lowering.
The fused engine action owns per-player execution and local counts. Each
factory builds fresh immutable effects and ability instances. The shared
service reuses `PlayerSet`, player zone mutations/ownership checks, clone-safe
`ShuffleLibrary`, existing zone/graveyard event types, and `DrawCards`/`DrawEach`
with the native draw replacement pipeline. It delays events until all moves
finish; the older per-player graveyard helper sends events too early for this
simultaneous operation. Movement is not discard, so discard replacements do
not apply. No parallel zone store, RNG, targeting or replacement system exists.
Draws use active-player order; source departure, return, control changes and
phasing do not change an all-player instruction already on the stack.

The retained `ShuffleHandAndGraveyardIntoLibraryAndDraw(n)` signature now uses
the same shuffle service and `DrawEach`. Its previous implementation let the
first seated player draw before the other player shuffled. A failing test
confirmed both the sequencing and draw-order defect before this fix. Existing
callers remain. No Go card definitions or DSL functions were removed because
complete loading, gameplay, runtime wiring and removal gates remain unmet.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Engine APIs:

- `UnlessManaPaid(player PlayerRef, cost ManaCost, amount ResolutionValue,
  body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` and `IfManaPaid`.
- `ManaValueOfSpellWithLKI(spell StackObjectRef) ResolutionValue`.

The mana template must contain X and nonnegative components. Each X uses the
same amount, read once before choices or mana production; nonpositive dynamic
amounts count as zero. Declaration validation rejects nil operands, invalid
mana templates and undeclared typed bindings. Hybrid symbol storage is copied.
The wrapper lowers to existing `unlessPaidEffect` with a fixed `ManaCostPayment`.
Its shared affordability check now excludes activation reductions, matching the
existing transaction's locked resolution cost. Zero payment needs acceptance;
unavailable payment offers no choice; decline or failed payment spends no cost
resources. Each call keeps its own conditional outcome. Existing fixed optional
payments retain their APIs and pass regression tests.

`ManaValueOfSpellWithLKI` reads current mana cost plus announced X while live.
The stack saves departure mana value by stack object ID on pop, removal by ID
or source, and stack-to-ante removal. Clone copies the value map. A returned
physical card uses a new stack ID and cannot replace old information. Saved
information does not restore membership or permit countering a departed spell.
The old `ManaValueOfSpell` keeps its live-only, zero-on-departure contract. No
saved spell controller, general spell LKI or delayed event-spell support is added.

RON resolving pairs:
`MayCost(PayManaX(mana-list, amount))/1` or
`PlayerMayCost(player-reference, PayManaX(mana-list, amount))/2`, followed by
`If(condition, [nonempty-actions])/2` or `Unless(condition, [nonempty-actions])/2`.
`condition` is bare `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid`. `mana-list` uses the existing
mana grammar, requires X, and permits fixed generic/colored symbols and repeated
X. `amount` is `Integer(n)` with n >= 0, a bound bare `ValueX`, or
`ManaValueOfSpell(spell-reference)/1`. Spell references use the scope's typed
`Ref_TargetSpell` or cast-event `Trigger_ThatSpell`. Player references reuse
`compilePlayerRef`; omitted payer uses resolving `You`. Factory-local bindings
are built with the actions and their declarations.

Supported contexts are existing spell/mode, activation, trigger and delayed
resolving lists. No casting/activation additional-cost, static, entry or
replacement-operation shape is added. Existing delayed event-spell reads remain
errors. Missing/nonadjacent continuation, malformed arity/symbols, negative
literal, X-free template and unbound/incompatible refs remain errors. Inventory
now distinguishes `resolution_cost` from announcement costs and classifies
nested spell-value reads even inside rejected records.

Existing typed references, `instanceBindings`, `SpellCast` captures, stack and
turn resolution, `IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`, mana solver and total-cost transaction own
execution. The slice introduces no zone, target, damage, replacement, APNAP or
simultaneous-operation system. Source changes do not redirect the captured
caster. Cleanup is not a payment lifetime; each pair runs once on resolution.

### Established signatures, contexts and ownership

Engine APIs:

- `LoseUnspentManaFor(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`: clears one current
  pool through `ManaPool.Clear`, including restricted mana, without life loss,
  production, payment or loss of production history. Nil/unbound/incompatible
  declarations fail engine validation.
- `HasManaAbility PermanentFilter`: current runtime classification through
  `IsActivatedManaAbility` and the shared triggered classifier. Tap state,
  unavailable costs and empty current output do not remove the ability.
  Ability loss and grants change membership. Immediate tapped-for-mana trigger
  resolution reuses the extracted classifier.
- `ControllerOfSpellWithLKI(spell StackObjectRef) PlayerRef`: current controller
  while present; exact stack-object departure controller otherwise. Stack pop,
  ID/source removal and ante removal save information. Clones own their maps.
  A recast cannot replace an earlier stack object's information. The old
  live-only `ControllerOfSpell` and spell-mana-value callers retain behavior.

RON resolving actions:

- `PlayerActions(player-reference, [actions])` saves the player once, then runs
  an ordered sequence. Its bare `ActionPlayer` read is body-local. Supported
  body actions are nested PlayerActions, explicit PlayerAction, TapEachPermanent,
  LoseUnspentMana and the existing draw/life/discard/hand-reveal player forms.
  Unsupported actions remain declaration errors. Nested scopes preserve outer
  bindings; siblings cannot use a finished body's ActionPlayer. Factory calls
  allocate fresh engine bindings. RON owns lexical plans and spelling; engine
  SnapshotPlayer/Sequence own state and execution.
- `LoseUnspentMana` is a symbol in a resolving list, explicit PlayerAction or
  scoped body. Tuple spelling is rejected. Implicit player actions use the
  selected body's player; You remains the resolving controller.
- `TapEachPermanent(filter)` uses one
  `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(typed-player-reference))`, directly or in
  nested And. Existing filters compose with that restriction. Duplicate
  controllers, controller predicates inside Or and unbound refs are rejected.
  Existing target-group tapping stays supported. `HasAbility(ManaAbility)` and
  `DoesntHaveAbility(ManaAbility)` use the new runtime query.
- Spells, activations, triggers and delayed resolving lists use these adapters.
  No cost, entry or static PlayerActions context is introduced. RON player
  information reads use the retained spell-controller query; that does not
  permit actions on departed spells or make illegal targets legal.

Reused engine services: instanceBindings, player/stack target declarations,
SnapshotPlayer, Sequence, PermanentsControlledBy, MatchingPermanents, TapEach,
optional resolution payments and their transaction, stack identity/information,
copy/retarget, cloning, phasing and target legality. Taps remain simultaneous;
tapping an effect-selected land does not activate its mana ability. Power Sink
continues unpaid instructions if countering fails, but all-illegal targets stop
resolution. No parallel zone/cost/target/replacement system, last-action slot,
card-name branch, fallback or partial production registry is introduced.

### Established shapes, contexts and dependencies

Engine:

- `PreventCombatDamageFrom(subject PermanentRef) StaticRule` prevents repeated
  outgoing combat damage to any recipient.
- `PreventCombatDamageTo(subject PermanentRef, from PermanentFilter) StaticRule`
  prevents repeated matching incoming combat damage. A zero filter permits all
  sources. Both read the current subject in the static source context.
- `DamageSourceIsEnchanted() PermanentFilter` reads current Aura status while
  live and retained `PermanentLKI.Enchanted` after departure/phasing. Capture
  reuses the same pure Aura query as the unchanged live IsEnchanted filter.
  Later casts/incarnations cannot replace saved information. Clones retain it.
- `CantAttack(subject PermanentRef) StaticRule` reuses CantAttackEach and the
  existing singleton reference set. It remains separate from host abilities.

The engine installs per-ability cycle replacements. Each proposed event checks
current source presence/incarnation and current subject identity. This is needed
because phasing need not start another layer cycle. RON owns spelling, scope,
arity, reference compatibility and lowering. It does not own parallel damage,
zone, replacement, cost or layer execution.

Permanent top-level `PreventDamage(event, [PreventThatDamage])` now accepts:
`CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByCreature(reference)`,
`CombatDamageWouldBeDealtToRecipient(Permanent(reference))`,
`CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByACreatureToRecipient(filter, Permanent(reference))`,
and `Or([incoming-event, outgoing-event])` in either order for the same subject.
References are ThisPermanent, or HostPermanent on an Aura. The union has exactly
one event of each direction. Its shared parser is reused from timed prevention.
Source filters accept And/Or, type/subtype, color/supertype, AnyPermanent,
IsTapped/IsUntapped, IsEnchanted/IsntEnchanted and IsAttacking. Enchanted and
attacking damage filters retain departure/phasing information. IsBlocking,
other relational/numeric filters, target/event refs, players, finite amounts,
mismatched unions and extra operations remain declaration errors in this context.
`PermanentRuleEffect(reference, [CantAttack])` uses the same reference boundary.

Reuse: StaticAbilityHolder and printed-ability lifecycle, definition validation,
PermanentRef/AttachedPermanent, damage-source incarnation/LKI, shared replacement
matching/order/rechecks, simultaneous damage, cloning, phasing, CantAttackEach,
source combat prevention union and current permanent filters. No card-name

### Exact contracts, signatures and reuse boundary

Permanent top-level rule:
`PlayerEffect(You, [DecreaseSpellCost(filter, [CostReduceGeneric(n)])])`.
Both operation lists contain exactly one item; n is a nonnegative integer
literal. Filters accept symbol `AnySpell`, `IsCardtype` with Creature, Artifact,
Enchantment, Instant or Sorcery, and nonempty recursively nested `And([filters])`
and `Or([filters])`. A union applies once when multiple types match. Zero is
accepted. Unsupported players, dynamic/colored reductions, mixed operations,
other filters, arities, kinds and action/cost/instant/sorcery contexts remain
compile errors. This does not claim support for the full PlayerEffect family.

RON owns declaration spelling, diagnostics, context checks, and lowering.
`compilePlayerCostReduction(Node) (optionFactory, error)` and
`compileCostSpellFilter(Node) (mage.SpellPredicate, error)` are private adapters.
They reuse ReduceSpellCostStatic, FixedAmount, SpellAny, SpellHasType, SpellsAnd,
SpellsOr, StaticAbilityHolder, definition validation, controller registration,
shared layer passes and the existing locked spell-payment transaction. Each
factory builds fresh source/ability/effect identities. Predicates are immutable;
there is no chosen state, target declaration, global result slot or new payment
pipeline. Costs apply to casting, not damage, life, activation or resolution.

Engine prerequisite: ReduceSpellCostStatic and its Labeled variant capture a
private sourceIncarnation on SpellCostReducer. `applies` checks current presence,
incarnation and controller before the existing player/filter/condition checks.
Phase-out suppresses the registered reduction without another layer pass;
phase-in restores the same source. Absent or returned sources cannot revive old
entries. Clone copies already copy the reducer value, including incarnation.
Explicit AddSpellCostReducer entries without the captured identity retain their
previous contract. No new public engine API. Whole-repository constructor search
found only the updated internal SpellCostReducer literal.

The source's current controller receives the reduction, independent of owner.
Ability removal and source/control changes use normal layer registration.
Independent sources add their reductions. Generic portions of printed, X and
additional mana costs are reduced after cost increases and never below zero.
Colored and nonmana costs remain required. Total costs lock before payments,
including sacrifice of the reducer itself. Source LKI must not keep a static
reduction active after departure. No new replacement, batch or APNAP operation
is established by this slice; the existing cost service remains responsible.

Inventory adds PlayerEffect player/operation roles and the cost_spell_filter,
spell_cost_reduction and integer_literal descendants. Reporting stays unverified
and cannot publish a production subset registry. Other unsupported player
operations retain unknown descendants rather than fabricated contracts.

### Exact shapes, contexts and engine contracts

RON `SacrificeNumberPermanents(Integer(n), filter)/2` accepts positive integer
literals. Existing sacrifice filters and nonempty recursive `And`/`Or` apply.
Supported in activation costs, including cost `And`, and resolution
`MayCost`/`PlayerMayCost` paired with an adjacent `If`/`Unless` payment condition.
The payer controls the distinct phased-in matching permanents; the source can
pay if it matches. Dynamic/zero/negative counts, malformed lists/arity/kinds,
unbound permanent references, and unsupported action/static contexts fail
compilation. No sacrifice-result binding, any-number or alternative cost shape
is added. Each factory constructs separate cost objects. RON owns spelling,
context checking, diagnostics and semantic roles.

Engine API:
`SacrificeNMatchingIncludingSourceCost(n int, filter PermanentFilter, text string)
Cost`. Existing `SacrificeNMatchingCost` keeps its source exclusion. Ordinary
matching sacrifice costs now participate in definition validation, with positive
count checks. No old export is removed. A caller audit found only positive
existing fixed-count uses; no compatibility caller depends on an invalid count.

All matching sacrifice costs select every distinct permanent before any removal,
then validate all choices together by current control, filter, presence and
incarnation. The shared total-cost transaction retains those choices and never
asks again on commit. Its existing cloned preflight now also runs for matching
sacrifice costs, including count one, so stale choices fail before mana or other
live resources are spent. One matching count cost uses `withZoneChangeBatch`;
separate cost objects stay separate payments. Sacrifice and zone-change events
use completed departures with prior-battlefield trigger detection, including
observers that leave in the same batch. The existing sacrifice/LKI path retains
ownership, indestructible/regeneration bypass and per-source departure facts.
No new replacement operation or global result slot is introduced.

Dependency: bare `ThatEnteringPermanent` is supported only inside the body of
`WhenAPermanentEntersTheBattlefield(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))`. It lowers
to the typed original source reference. Returned objects cannot replace it.
Other triggers, activation bodies and tuple spellings reject it. This completes
Mold Demon's unpaid branch and also unlocks Electric Eel's entry damage.

Reuse: `compileSacrificeCostFilter`, `compileCosts`, `compileOptionalPayment`,
`IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`, per-instance action/source bindings, cost transaction and
cloning, `sacrificeMatchingCost`, `withZoneChangeBatch`, LKI, trigger capture,
`CreateTokenCopies`/`DefineToken`, source damage and temporary layer services.
No registry fallback, subset production registry, Go stub, card executor or
new payment/departure pipeline is introduced.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine contract

Engine: `LimitUntapsDuringStep(PermanentFilter, int) StaticRule`. Nonnegative
fixed maximum, including zero; zero filter matches all. Negative declarations
fail definition validation. Effects clone their mutable source metadata. Printed
source departure, phasing and ability suppression use existing lifecycle checks;
recipient ability removal does not remove a static restriction. A returned source
is a new active instance. No departed-source LKI applies.

RON: `EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer,
[CantUntapMoreThanNumberPermanentsDuringTheirUntapStep(Integer(n), filter)])`
in permanent rules only. Exactly one operation, bare `AnyPlayer`, nonnegative
integer literal and existing permanent-filter grammar. Dynamic values, bound
references, other player filters and operations remain rejected. Other roles
(cost, entry, resolving action, spell rules) gain no support. Inventory reports
player filter, player rule operation, value and permanent filter descendants,
even when another parent remains unsupported. Factories produce fresh static
abilities and effects; no chosen state is captured in the compiler plan.

At the untap decision, final filters and quotas are saved after phase-in and
layer evaluation. Current control, phasing, tapped status, skip-next-untap,
captured prohibitions and existing optional-source choices determine eligibility.
Unrestricted eligible objects are selected automatically. For limited objects,
`ChooseMayAbility` permits stopping below the maximum, then `ChoosePermanent`
selects one remaining legal object. Nil stops; invalid choices use a legal
fallback. A selected artifact creature or artifact land consumes every matching
quota. Separate limits combine; duplicate limits cannot add allowances.

All choices finish before the shared `untapPermanentsTogether` batch (CR 502.3).
Stun replacement consumes a counter without backfilling that choice. Untap events
see the completed operation. A later decision uses fresh membership; explicit
untap effects remain legal. Existing land/artifact/creature limit fields remain
supported and now use the same selection. Native AI and search accept the exact
new optional untap prompt, preserving their ability to use these existing limits.
The old private `untapPermanentDuringUntapStep` helper had zero whole-repository
callers after integration and was removed from the modified engine file.

Reuse: static definition validation, effect source/layer lifecycle and cloning,
`FilterBattlefield`, player decision interfaces, captured/next-untap services,
source-tap-maintained decisions, stun handling and simultaneous untap. No separate
RON game state, global result slot, card-name branch, production subset registry
or Go fallback. No new cost, damage-replacement or APNAP contract is established.

### Exact signatures, scope and dependencies

RON resolving actions:

- `LookAtTheTopNumberCardsOfPlayersLibrary(player, Integer(n), operations)/3`,
  with a nonnegative integer literal and exactly one bare ordering symbol:
  `LeaveRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInSameOrder` or
  `PutTheRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInAnyOrder`.
- `MayHavePlayerAction(player, Shuffle)/2`, with bare `Shuffle` only.

Player arguments use existing typed reference plans and per-factory bindings.
These actions declare no target. Supported resolving spell, activation, mode,
trigger and delayed-action lists use the same lowering. Rules, static effects,
costs, entry operations and restricted scoped-player action lists gain no new
support. Dynamic counts, malformed/negative literals, multiple ordering
operations, unknown operations, other optional actions, and unbound or
incompatible references remain compile errors. Inventory descendants report
`player_reference`, `value`, `library_ordering_operation` and
`optional_library_action`, including under unsupported outer contexts.

Engine APIs:
`LookAtLibraryTop(viewer, library PlayerRef, count int, reorder bool)
ResolvingEffect`, `MayShuffleLibrary(chooser, library PlayerRef)
ResolvingEffect`, and `Game.LibraryLooks(viewerID) []PublicCardReveal`.
Optional `LibraryLookObserver.ObserveLibraryLook([]Card, GameReader)` and
`LibraryTopOrderChooser.ChooseLibraryTopOrder([]Card, GameReader) []uuid.UUID`
provide private display and ordering without changing the Player interface.

Inspection reads current library cards at resolution and records copied private
observations before choices. It does not publish public reveals or move cards.
History is past information, not permission to read current library order.
Getters and Game.Clone copy maps, slices, card definitions and types.
Only the viewer receives copied inspection notifications. The viewer chooses
a complete permutation of inspected cards; the uninspected suffix remains
unchanged. Invalid/missing/duplicate/extra IDs preserve original order.
Existing scry callers can supply an order with both partitions kept on top.
Empty inspection makes no order choice. Missing resolved players do nothing;
nil/unbound references and negative counts fail definition validation.

Optional shuffle uses the resolving chooser, separately from the library owner,
and calls the existing Player.ShuffleLibrary on acceptance, even for empty or
one-card libraries. HumanPlayer displays private cards on its own choice channel
and chooses successive top cards. Base/AI/search callers retain their existing
choice interfaces. This slice adds no shuffle event, RNG, replacement, cost,
simultaneous-operation, or permanent-LKI service. Source departure, phasing or
control change cannot redirect an already queued library instruction.

Reuse: typed player/target resolution and definition validation, fresh instance
bindings, RevealTopN, card snapshots, clone isolation, existing shuffle and scry
choices, native stack/copy/retarget and transactional casting/activation services.
RON owns spelling, shapes and scope; library state and player decisions stay in
the engine. No card-name branch, fallback, global last-result slot or partial
production registry was added.

### Shapes, contracts and engine reuse

Supported resolving shape: `MillNumberCards(Integer(n))`, with nonnegative fixed
`n`, in action lists, `PlayerAction(player, ...)`, or `PlayerActions` lists.
The existing typed player scope supplies the subject. Bare actions use the
ability controller; nested `ActionPlayer` reads use the existing local snapshot.

Supported payment shape: `MayCost(MillNumberCards(Integer(n)))` or
`PlayerMayCost(player, MillNumberCards(Integer(n)))`, with positive fixed `n`
and an adjacent `If`/`Unless` on `CostWasPaid`/`CostWasntPaid`. Each factory
constructs separate costs, effects and typed target bindings. Dynamic counts,
zero declared costs, malformed declarations, unbound/incompatible references,
all-player milling and activation-cost milling remain rejected.

RON owns spelling, shapes, contexts, diagnostics and lowering. Engine reuse:
`Mill`, `MillCost`, `Fixed`, typed player/target bindings, `SnapshotPlayer`,
`IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`, payment transactions, source-incarnation and clone services,
native step execution, `Until`, `GrantKeywordModification`, `SkipNextUntap`, and
mill modifiers. No new public engine API or last-action slot is introduced.

Shared `millCards` now offers the library owner the existing
`ChooseCardFromLibrary` choice with a graveyard-order reason. Candidate cards
are copies with retained IDs. All choices precede moves; then the complete batch
leaves the library and enters the graveyard in the chosen order. Invalid choices
use the first remaining card. Prior graveyard cards retain order. Zero/one-card
batches need no choice. `BasePlayer` keeps library order; native human players
can select another order. Queries and payment validation do not call the live
chooser. Commit affordability checks precede resources and choices.

An action mills as many cards as available. A cost requires the complete adjusted
count; modified zero can be accepted. Optional results stay with their own
continuation. Legacy mill modifiers retain their existing registration order;
this slice does not establish CR 616 replacement-choice semantics or a new
zone-event/replacement subsystem. Source incarnation, phasing and sacrifice
control checks use existing services, including LKI where those services require it.

The scope must supply announced X from the spell mana cost or activation cost.
Existing target scope/instance factories remain responsible for declarations.
The slice does not add resolution reads, static predicates, result bindings,
fixed amounts, disjunctions or other comparisons. Malformed tuples, callable X,
unbound/incompatible operands and no-X scopes are rejected. Duplicate spell
mana-value restrictions and combined spell mana-value/current-permanent-target
restrictions are rejected. Existing accepted contexts retain their behavior.

New engine APIs:

- `TargetManaValueEqualX() PermanentTargetOption`: compare a current permanent's
  mana value with the action's announced X. X in that permanent's cost is zero.
- `DeclareSpellTargetManaValueX(name string, filters ...CardFilter)
  *SpellTargetBinding`: compare current stack mana value, including each X in
  the target spell's cost and that spell's own `XValue`, with the action's X.

These options use existing target declarations and contain no chosen state.
Definition inspection exposes the restriction. Targets are constructed per
factory; copies keep their own stack identities, controller, targets and X.
`possibleTargetsWithX` uses a separate game view with its own X field for pure
candidate queries. Announcement validation, variable-target validation, prompts,
random choices and copy retargeting supply their explicit action X. Resolution
legality now supplies the resolving object's X before effects begin, rather
than reading a previous resolution's X. Existing direct callers of
`isTargetStillLegal` retain their current-frame interface.

Reuse: `PermanentTarget`, `typedSpellTarget`, `stackSpellManaValue`,
`ResolutionState`, `TargetBounds`, typed target references, existing incarnation
and zone checks, stack-copy/group services, transactional mana payment,
`DestroyWithoutRegeneration`, `ControllerOfWithLKI`, damage and `Counter`.
Target restrictions use current information, not target LKI. Detonate's later
controller read uses existing LKI even after destruction; indestructibility
does not suppress its independent damage. No parallel target, payment, zone,
replacement or simultaneous-operation service is introduced. No global
last-action binding, game-time declaration panic, fallback or partial production
registry is added.

### Supported signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine API: `ExileGraveyardCard(card CardRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It moves only a card in a graveyard whose typed reference remains valid.
It preserves the owner, puts the card in face-up exile, and attributes
`ExiledBy` to the resolving source. Nil/unbound references fail declaration
validation. A stale visit or reference to a card in hand/exile causes no move.

RON action: `Exile([CardInGraveyards(ref)], [])`, exactly one subject, no
modifiers. `ref` is a declared `Ref_TargetGraveyardCard` or the symbol
`Trigger_ThatGraveyardCard` inside
`WhenAPermanentDies(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))`.
The existing action-list contexts can lower the target form; real activation
and death-trigger gameplay and engine targeted spell gameplay are tested.
Malformed arity, callable/unbound/incompatible references, plural subjects and
face-down modifiers reject at compilation.

A typed `deathCardPlan` enters the source-death body only. Factories create fresh
`CardBinding` instances; `PermanentDies().WithCard` and `EventSourceIsSelf`
save the first graveyard visit before trigger placement. Existing
`PutGraveyardCardIntoHand` can use the same typed reference, with a synthetic
integration test. Battlefield return still requires a creature card target.
Entry, host-death and general filtered death bodies do not receive this binding.

Reuse: `CardRef`, `CardTargetBinding`, `FromCard`, graveyard visit identity,
`PermanentDies.WithCard`, departure ability/controller snapshots,
`MoveFromAnyGraveyard`, `Game.ExileCard`, zone/departure events, target
legality, stack copying, clone isolation and transactional activation costs.
RON owns syntax, role validation and per-instance plans. The engine owns zone
moves and references. No new replacement ordering or simultaneous move
contract is claimed; simultaneous deaths use the existing destruction service.
No card-name branch, fallback, skipped rule, declaration panic, global result
slot or partial production registry is added.

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `DeclareOpponentOrPlaneswalkerTarget(name string)
*DamageTargetBinding`. It reuses `PlayerOrPlaneswalkerTarget` with a private
player-only opponent restriction. Both controllers' planeswalkers remain legal.
Existing `DeclarePlayerOrPlaneswalkerTarget` and all its callers keep their
behavior. Candidate enumeration, announcement and resolution use the same engine
legality path. A copied spell uses its controller for player legality and
retargeting. Empty labels and undeclared bindings fail definition validation.

IsCardtype(Planeswalker))`, with `Ref_TargetPlayerOrPermanent` in existing
single-target spell, mode, activation and trigger contexts. Existing `AnyPlayer`
is retained. Arbitrary player filters, other permanent filters, callable symbols
and incompatible reference roles remain rejected. Each factory builds a fresh
target binding; no compiled declaration stores chosen targets.

RON value shapes: `HalfRoundedDown(value)` and `HalfRoundedUp(value)` each take
exactly one recursively supported `compileInstanceValue` expression. They lower
to `DivideRoundDown(value, Fixed(2))` and `DivideRoundUp(value, Fixed(2))`.
Supported resolving consumers include damage packets and existing instance-value
consumers. Nested X, battlefield count, characteristic, captured-result and
arithmetic reads retain their existing scope contracts. No static, entry, cost
or replacement value context gains support. Invalid or unbound inner reads
remain errors. Inventory classifies each half expression's argument as `value`,
including nested forms, without accepting unsupported parents.

RON owns spelling, arity, roles, scope and lowering. The engine owns division,
announced X, typed identity, LKI, target rechecks, transactions, cloning/copies,
resolution-time counts, simultaneous `DealDamagePackets` and replacement
execution. All packet amounts and recipients are read before one damage batch;
replacement effects do not recalculate the Mountain count. A sole illegal target
suppresses both targeted and self damage. Source return cannot substitute a new
incarnation or controller for retained LKI. No card-name branch, Go fallback,
skipped rule, declaration panic, global result slot or partial registry is added.

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `GainControlWhileSourceControlled(subject PermanentRef,
requireTapped bool) ResolvingEffect`. Definition validation requires a permanent
source and a bound non-nil subject. Resolution uses typed source/subject references
and the resolving controller. No LKI or returned source can start a duration.
Installed effects save both source and target incarnations and controller. Private
capture fields extend `controlContinuousEffect`; existing `ControlEffectSpec`,
`GainControl` and legacy tap-maintained callers retain their behavior.

RON action: `GainControlOfPermanentUntil(subject,
UntilPermanentChangesControl(You, ThisPermanent))`, or the same action with
`Or([UntilPermanentChangesControl(You, ThisPermanent),
ForAsLongAsPermanentRemainsTapped(ThisPermanent)])`. The ordered two-element
`Or` gives duration endpoints: either ending condition terminates the effect.
Other players, sources, endpoints, arities and incompatible references remain
errors. Subjects use existing typed permanent references in resolving permanent
scopes. Spell-source, static, entry, cost and replacement contexts gain no support.
Factories build fresh declarations; each stack frame keeps its own target.
Inventory reports the target as `permanent_reference`, duration terms as
`source_control_duration`, and their typed player/source arguments, including
expressions after an unsupported sibling without accepting the record.

The engine owns Layer 2 conditions, reconciliation/timestamps, control-change
sickness, prohibition on changing control, transactional costs, legality rechecks,
copy frames and cloning. Source departure, phasing or loss of control ends both
forms permanently. Actual untapping also ends the tapped form; stun replacement
preserves it. Source phasing and untap hooks expire captured durations before
phase-in/retap or untap notifications, including simultaneous untaps. Target
phasing preserves a valid source duration; target return cannot inherit control.
Cleanup and source ability removal do not erase installed durations. Separate
printed optional untap permissions remain choices after target departure.

No parallel zone/layer system, card-name branch, game-time declaration panic,
global result slot, Go fallback, skipped rule or production subset registry is
introduced. This slice adds no replacement ordering or APNAP contract.

### Exact signatures, contexts, state ownership and reuse

Engine declarations:

- `BeforeCombatStep(point PhaseStep, during bool) StateCondition`: points are
  DeclareAttackers, DeclareBlockers or CombatDamage; other points fail definition
  validation. False uses the first combat of the turn. True requires a current
  combat and uses that phase's boundary. The first actual damage step, including
  first strike, closes the damage window.
- `TurnReader.CombatWindowOpen(PhaseStep, bool) bool` is a pure query. TurnSystem
  owns value-only history, clones copy it,
  and both turn mutation paths reset it. No action-result slot is introduced.

Native step execution closes blockers/damage windows when an empty attackers
step ends. Skipped blockers, damage and absent first-strike steps do not become
current steps. Current layers are applied before first-strike existence is read.
TurnSchedule retains full-phase skip consumption at build/pop time so a skipped
first combat closes windows at the precombat-main boundary even when an extra
combat follows. Skipping only the beginning step retains the remaining combat.
EndCombat completion and transitions out of combat retain the first boundary.
Current-combat windows can reopen in extra combats, including a skipped beginning
step; first-combat windows cannot. Schedule and history clones stay independent.

RON casting context: one nonmodal instant/sorcery
`CastEffect(CantBeCastUnless(condition))` beside SpellActions gains the four bare
symbols `IsDuringCombat`, `IsBeforeAttackersDeclared`, `IsBeforeBlockersDeclared`,
and `IsBeforeCombatDamageStep`. `IsAfterCombat` remains unsupported. Existing
nonempty nested And
conditions and player-turn conditions remain valid. An explicit IsDuringCombat
anywhere in the And tree makes its before predicates current-combat predicates;
operand order does not change that context. Tuple forms, wrong arities, empty
And, unsupported predicates, modal/permanent casting contexts and duplicate
CastEffect declarations remain rejected. Existing casting gates apply the
condition before choices and payment and do not recheck it on stack copies or
resolution. No casting permission is granted.

RON activation context adds only
`ActivatedWithModifiers(cost, body, ActivateOnlyIf(IsBeforeCombatDamageStep))`.
The shared activation gate reads first-combat history before cost payment.
Other before/after activation predicates are not added. Existing mana/tap costs,
source legality, ownership/control, stack frames and transactional rollback are
reused. Angus reuses global combat prevention, shared damage replacements,
source departure behavior and native cleanup. No engine damage or replacement
ordering contract is changed. RON spelling/context stays in ron; reusable timing
state stays in mage. No card-name branch, Go fallback, skipped card rule, global
last-action slot, game-time declaration panic or partial production registry is
introduced.
