### Exact supported shapes, ownership and dependencies

Engine additions:

- `DeclareSpellOrPermanentTarget(name string) *SpellOrPermanentTargetBinding`:
  one shared target category across stack and battlefield. Stack candidates use
  stack object IDs, not physical card IDs; abilities and players are excluded.
  Each factory constructs a fresh declaration. It contains no choices.
- `SetObjectColor(object *SpellOrPermanentTargetBinding, color core.Color)
  ResolvingEffect`: reads the frame-local target capture. Definition validation
  rejects nil/undeclared bindings, empty declaration names and nonactual colors.
  Application checks the captured incarnation for permanents and the exact stack
  ID for spells, then reuses `Game.ChangeObjectColor`. Missing objects produce
  no action; a later cast or returned permanent cannot replace the old object.

RON supports only `SpellActions(Targeted_Modal([spellBranch, permanentBranch]))`
on an instant or sorcery without casting modifiers. Branch order is free.
Each branch must be `Targeted([target], ActionList([action]))` with exactly one
unfiltered `TargetSpell(AnySpell)` / `TargetPermanent(AnyPermanent)` target.
Actions are respectively `CreateSpellEffect(Ref_TargetSpell, [SetColor(colors)])`
and `CreatePermanentLayerEffect(Ref_TargetPermanent, [SetColor(colors)])`.
`colors` is `SimpleColorList([color])` with the same single White, Blue, Black,
Red or Green in both branches. Other target filters, actions, contexts, counts,
colors, references and modifications remain rejected. General Targeted_Modal,
CreateSpellEffect and indefinite color families remain partial.

The compiler validates each lexical branch, then builds one typed target and
one reusable engine action together per factory. The final engine action has
no RON spelling. The alternatives are not actual modes; copies can retarget in
either direction. Existing source-independent color services own duration,
layer-5 timestamps, effective-color/protection queries, copy characteristics,
spell-to-permanent carry, phasing and clone isolation. Native target services
own announcement/resolution legality, captured incarnation, frame bindings and
copy retargeting. Native casting payments own rollback. Color replaces the
current colors and preserves mana symbols. Cleanup, control changes and phasing
retain the installed effect; later zone changes end it. No new LKI, replacement
ordering, simultaneous-operation or cost service is needed for this one-object
characteristic action.

Reporting now assigns nested Targeted_Modal bodies, CreateSpellEffect references
and resolving SetColor arguments their correct semantic roles, even for rejected
text-changing records. It does not claim family-wide support. Production loading
still rejects the entire unsupported collection and installs no partial registry.
No Go fallback, card-name branch, skipped rule, global last-action slot or
runtime declaration panic is introduced.

### Source defect and correction

All nine records for these four names used
`TimesThisAbilityHasResolvedThisTurnIs`. Oracle counts activations, including
countered activations, and reads that count when the conditional instruction
resolves. Several waiting abilities can therefore see the same later count.
Copies read the count without adding an activation. Local `data/LEA.json`,
`data/4ED.json`, `data/4th_edition.json` and `data/FEM.json` confirm the three local
names. [Gatherer Nalathni Dragon](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=97050)
confirms the fourth. A direct Scryfall API attempt returned HTTP 400; Gatherer's
primary Oracle page supplied the needed evidence, so this did not block work.

Corrected all identical consumers together to
`TimesThisAbilityHasBeenActivatedThisTurnIs`: Dragon Whelp in LEA, LEB, 2ED, 3ED,
CED and CEI; Nalathni Dragon in PROMOS; both mana creatures in FEM. The obsolete
resolution-count spelling stays rejected. The two FEM records remain rejected
with `activation history mana bodies require mana-conversion planning`.
The parser rebuilt the vocabulary snapshot, including all source positions,
constructor signatures, counts and hashes. Fresh loader diagnostics replace its
old baseline. No other source defect was changed.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine API:

- `BindActivationHistory(name string) *ActivationHistoryBinding` declares one
  ability's history; it contains no chosen or mutable game state.
- `WithActivationHistory(binding *ActivationHistoryBinding) ActionOption` opts
  one `NewAction(ActionActivated, ...)` declaration into tracking.
- `IfActivationsAtLeast(binding *ActivationHistoryBinding, minimum int,
  body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` reads the count during resolution.

`TurnTrackers` owns the map keyed by immutable binding and saved incarnation,
clone copying and final-cleanup reset. The successful activation payment path
records once before stack placement; failed target/payment paths do not record.
The caller supplies the original incarnation, including when a cost sacrifices
the source. Existing activation-limit callers retain their behavior. A copied
stack object shares the immutable declaration, reads original-incarnation history
and does not add an activation. Control/phasing retain the count; return does
not. Definition validation rejects nil/empty/undeclared bindings, negative
thresholds, duplicate options, spell declarations and sharing a binding between
different abilities on one card.

RON supports resolving
`If(TimesThisAbilityHasBeenActivatedThisTurnIs(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n))),
[actions])`, with nonnegative literal `n` and a nonempty supported action list,
in nonmodal `Activated` and `ActivatedWithModifiers` stack bodies. Each factory
constructs a fresh binding and action together. Branch bodies keep their lexical
scope and instruction order. Other comparisons, malformed forms, delayed reads,
spell/static/trigger/modal and mana contexts stay rejected. Generic resolving
`If` remains partial. Inventory assigns history conditions/comparisons their
proper roles, including nested rejected mana records.

Native `AtNext` supplies delayed timing, controller and source capture. Native
`Until` and `ModifyPT` supply stacking bonuses, cleanup, identity and phasing.
Native casting/activation services supply costs and rollback. Native sacrifice
requires the effect controller to control the permanent: losing control before
the delay resolves prevents sacrifice. A phased source cannot be sacrificed;
the one-shot delay is consumed. A returned source cannot replace the old one.
No new LKI, replacement-ordering or simultaneous-operation rule is required.

### TDD and card-to-test mapping

The first engine tests failed for the missing typed API. The first real RON tests
failed at resolving `If` on both dragons. A separate declaration test exposed a
shared history binding between two abilities; validation was added after that
failure. A final audit added a failing duplicate-action declaration test and
closed that case before rerunning validation. The failed-payment case also
resolves older pending activations before another successful activation, so it
detects a count added by a failed payment through observable gameplay. Invalid-context tests failed for the missing valid compiler shape before
implementation. During implementation, a duplicate inventory switch case caused
a build failure and was corrected. Timing fixture failures were corrected:
end-step execution empties mana, and another player cannot sacrifice a creature
that the original delay controller no longer controls. No test was weakened.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

- `IfRequiredPaid(player PlayerRef, costs CostGroup, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `UnlessRequiredPaid(player PlayerRef, costs CostGroup, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- Each engine group must be nonempty and contain matching sacrifice costs only.
  Existing definition validation rejects captured payment results. Other cost
  families are rejected, including mandatory mana, preserving CR 118.3c.
- `SacrificePermanentAction.PermanentID()`, `.Destination()` and
  `.WithExile(sourceID uuid.UUID) *SacrificePermanentAction` expose the proposed
  sacrifice to the existing replacement pipeline. The action saves incarnation.
- RON action sequences support adjacent
  `MustCost(SacrificeAPermanent(filter))` and `If`/`Unless` with symbol
  `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` and a nonempty action list. Spell, activated,
  and triggered sequences use the same adapter. Result reads cannot escape the
  adjacent pair. Nested and independent pairs keep separate continuations.
- The existing sacrifice-filter grammar applies. `Other(ThisPermanent)` at the
  root or under conjunctions excludes the original source incarnation. An
  exclusion under a disjunction, a target/host exclusion, or an unavailable
  source scope remains rejected. No new general resolving If support is claimed.

The engine reuses `CostGroup`, matching sacrifice costs,
`prepareActionPaymentTransaction`, clone/preflight validation, typed controller
references, definition validation, source incarnation, shared damage/prevention,
trigger LKI and zone batches. Each factory builds its own costs and effects.
The success predicate is local; it does not read a global last-action slot.
Original optional-payment callers keep their choices and signatures.

Mandatory payment starts only after legal full-cost preparation. A changed exile
destination or prevented move still takes the paid branch (CR 118.12).
Sacrifice checks current control and phase status; failed/stale selections do
not consume a different object. Source control changes do not change a queued
trigger's payer. Copies use their own controller. A returned source can pay the
old trigger because it is a different object (CR 400.7).

`DoSacrifice` now uses the shared replacement pipeline. Regeneration does not
apply. The existing exile-instead service also handles sacrifice. Exile keeps
sacrifice and zone events, including source LKI, but causes no death event or
death-history increment. Matching multi-permanent sacrifice costs choose every
replacement before any move. The shared batch preserves the pre-move battlefield
for leave-event detection and defers trigger processing until all moves finish.
No new APNAP, mana-planning or general zone-replacement compiler contract is
claimed. Rule evidence: local CR 118.3c, 118.12, 400.7, 701.21a and 616.1.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

RON static rules now accept exactly one operation:

- `PermanentLayerEffect(subject, [AdjustPTXY(PlusX, PlusY, x, y)])`.
- `PermanentLayerEffect(subject, [AdjustPTForEach(power, toughness, count)])`,
  where the multipliers are signed integer literals.
- `subject` is `ThisPermanent` or `HostPermanent` with an Aura declaration.
  Targets, event refs, loop refs and absent host declarations are rejected.
- Static values accept `Integer(integer)`, recursive `Twice(value)`,
  `HalfRoundedDown(value)`, `HalfRoundedUp(value)`, and
  `TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter)`.
- Counts reuse nonempty conjunctions, existing type/subtype/color/supertype and
  tap/combat filters, and `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` in conjunctions.
  Controller reads use the current source controller, not its owner or host.
- The exact two-member conjunction of `IsEnchantmentType(Aura)` and
  `AttachedToPermanent(source-or-host)` lowers to `CountPermanents(AttachedAuras(...))`.
  Either member order is accepted. Extra conditions, duplicate/missing members
  and incompatible refs remain errors.
- Announced X, P/T characteristic reads, event/payment results, combined operation
  lists and collection subjects remain rejected in this context. Resolving and
  temporary value adapters retain their existing signatures and behavior.

The compiler uses existing `Static`, `While`, `ModifyPT`, `CountPermanents`,
`MatchingPermanents`, `PermanentsControlledBy`, `AttachedAuras`, `MultiplyValues`,
`DivideRoundDown` and `DivideRoundUp`. It does not use `ValueAtResolution` for
these live values. Each factory creates its own ability/effect state. Static
queries read current objects, with no LKI or mutation. Bonuses use layer 7c;
base values, counters, switching and layer-6 ability removal use the existing
layer service. No parallel count, attachment or layer implementation was added.

The Aura spell copy acceptance case exposed native engine gaps. The
`implement-engine` skill was used for this prerequisite without card wiring or
removed card skills. `CopySpellOnStack` now retargets nonmodal casting targets
through `Card.CastTargets()` and the existing target-group service. Copies of
permanent spells use the normal entry path and become token permanents under
CR 608.3f/707.10f. A token-card wrapper preserves the stack definition and makes
token status visible to entry replacements/events. Each resolution clones token
abilities and static effect source state, using existing token ability and
stateful effect cloning services; otherwise stateless effect structs get a
separate source identity. Copies use zero entry colors spent to cast, while
original cast facts stay intact. This does not invoke token creation.
No new public constructor is added. Instant/sorcery/ability copies and current
callers retain their behavior. No new replacement ordering, simultaneous batch,
APNAP or mana-payment service is introduced.

### Established shapes, context and reuse boundary

Engine APIs:

- `HasCounter(core.CounterType) PermanentFilter`: one or more counters of one
  kind on a supplied nonnil permanent.
- `CounterCountEquals(core.CounterType, int) PermanentFilter`: exact live count.
  The stored count is widened to int. Negative and above-storage-range counts
  cannot wrap into a match. Nil does not match exact zero.

RON static condition filters:

- `HasACounterOfType(counter)`.
- `HasNumberCountersOfType(EqualTo(Integer(n)), counter)`, where `n` is a
  nonnegative integer literal. All existing permanent-counter types and supported
  P/T pairs reuse `compilePermanentCounterType`.
- These filters compose with existing nonempty `And`/`Or`. They work in
  `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, filter)` and Aura `HostPermanent`, plus
  the existing static player `ControlsA`/`ControlsNo` contexts.
- Wrong arities/kinds, unknown/player counter types, unsupported P/T pairs,
  negative/dynamic thresholds, other comparisons and unbound/incompatible
  references remain errors. Resolving conditions, entry operations, replacement
  predicates, activation timing and counter-dependent durations are not added.
  Conditional bodies retain their existing restrictions; `PermanentRuleEffect`
  bodies still reject.

`PermanentMatchesFilter`, `PlayerControls`, `OpponentControls`, `ControlsNone`,
`FilterBattlefield`, `Static`, `While`, typed source/attachment references and
the existing layer service supply execution. Each factory owns its ability and
effect state; filters capture only immutable counter kind/count. No choice,
saved-action slot, new replacement, cost or simultaneous-operation service is
introduced. Presence/incarnation/phasing checks belong to the shared selectors,
not the raw counter filter. There is no LKI fallback for live static queries.
The `implement-engine` skill was applied to the reusable filters. No removed
card/set skill, Go card requirements, fallback or production subset registry was
used.

### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse boundary

- Trigger rule: `TriggerA(WhenAPermanentHasNumberCountersOfType(
  SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent), GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)), counter),
  body)`, with a nonnegative literal `n` and a validated permanent counter kind.
  Bare `ThisPermanent` must be in permanent scope. Host subjects, collections,
  other comparisons and dynamic thresholds reject at declaration time.
- The trigger body alone binds `Trigger_ThatPermanent` to the typed original
  source reference. `counterStateSource` records this lexical source-only
  context; it stores no game state. `This` reads the engine's saved trigger
  source incarnation, including on copies. No mutable event binding is needed
  because this supported event can only name its source.
- Resolving action: `RemoveCounters([AllCountersOfTypeFromPermanent(counter,
  subject)])`, exactly one instruction. `compilePermanentRef` validates source,
  Aura host, declared target and existing permanent-event references. The action
  reads the count at resolution. Other removal shapes remain unsupported in
  actions; existing cost forms remain unchanged.
- Engine reuse: `WhenState`, `SourceHasCounters`, `RemoveAllCounters`, `This`,
  `AttachedPermanent`, typed target/event bindings, `TriggerA`, `Sequence`,
  native trigger arming and source capture, entry/counter replacement services,
  transactional casting and native copy/clone services. Factories create fresh
  abilities and effects. No engine API or new execution system is introduced.
- Arming is per source/ability/incarnation. Threshold checks are state-trigger
  checks, not intervening-if checks. A changed count does not cancel an already
  queued reset. Missing/phased subjects are not changed; no LKI counter fallback
  applies. Zone return cannot redirect old triggers. Phase cycles keep identity.
- Inventory classifies nested event, comparison, literal, counter and removal
  reference roles even in rejected records. Classification is not support
  evidence for other contexts.

their event player and controller. Source phasing prevents detection. Departure,
return, later phasing and trigger copies do not redirect the saved drawer.

copy's controller. Factories, pending instances and clones reuse existing typed
reference isolation. No mutable chosen state is added to the compiler.

### Exact supported shapes and engine boundary

In supported spell, activation and trigger action lists, `MayCost(cost)` and
`PlayerMayCost(player, cost)` accept `PayLife(Integer(n))` with a nonnegative
integer literal, and `Or([cost, cost, ...])` with at least two alternatives.
Every alternative is fixed `PayMana([...])`, fixed `PayLife(Integer(n))`, or
another such `Or`. X, dynamic values, `And`, sacrifice/tap and other alternative
cost leaves remain rejected. Activation/additional casting costs do not gain
this RON grammar. Each payment still requires one adjacent nonempty `If` or
`Unless` body and symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid`.

RON owns spelling, shape validation, scope and fresh factory construction.
It lowers alternatives to `EitherCost`, life to `LifePayCost`, and the pair
to existing `IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`. Outcomes remain local to each pair. Typed
host-controller, spell-controller, source and attachment identities remain in
their existing plans and engine services. Nested `Or` descendants are now
inventoried as `resolution_cost`; labels remain unverified.

The engine prerequisite fixes recursive alternative affordability and option
locking to use the action transaction's mana policy. Resolution payments check
raw mana costs, including inside nested alternatives. Activation transactions
retain reductions; casting and legacy locking callers retain their policies.
Choices occur only after acceptance. One payable option needs no mode choice.
Mana abilities supply resolution mana through the shared service. Total-cost
validation and commit remain atomic. A failed selected payment does not spend
live mana or life. No global last-payment slot or new exported authoring API
is added. Replacement ordering and simultaneous operations have no new
contract in this slice; damage, destruction, regeneration, phasing, LKI,
countering and copy behavior reuse existing services.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

New engine APIs:

- `IfSacrificePaid(PlayerRef, PermanentRef, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `UnlessSacrificePaid(PlayerRef, PermanentRef, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

These resolve one typed subject before offering payment and build a fresh
identity-restricted `SacrificeMatchingIncludingSourceCost`. The existing optional
payment service checks payer control and affordability, takes the player's
choice, and runs the action transaction. A captured incarnation restricts both
validation and commit. Missing, uncontrolled and phased subjects cannot pay;
phase cycles preserve identity; leave/return does not. A source can pay its own
cost. Graveyard/exile destinations use the existing sacrifice action and zone
replacement pipeline. Regeneration and indestructibility do not prevent
sacrifice. Failed or declined payments take the unpaid branch. An absent payer
runs no branch, as with existing resolution payments.

RON action-list contexts accept `MayCost(SacrificePermanent(ref))` and
`PlayerMayCost(player, SacrificePermanent(ref))`. `ref` uses the existing bound
singular permanent grammar: source, Aura host, target, or an available event
reference. `player` uses the existing typed player grammar. Each declaration
requires one adjacent nonempty `If` or `Unless` list and symbol `CostWasPaid` or
`CostWasntPaid`; all four polarities work. Nested/consecutive pairs keep local
results. `MustCost`, composite/alternative sacrifice payments, collections,
new activation/casting costs and linked results remain unsupported.

`AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(HostController))` now exposes
`Trigger_ThatPermanent`, backed by the existing `AttachedControllerUpkeep`
host snapshot. Its existing `Trigger_ThatPlayer` retains the upkeep player.
These are event-local, fresh per factory and retained per pending trigger or
copy. Other step contexts do not gain a permanent binding. RON owns spelling,
validation and lowering; mage owns identities, choices, transactions and rules.
No parallel cost, zone, event or replacement service is introduced. No new
simultaneous-operation or replacement-ordering rule is claimed.

artifact.” The old DRK record instead read HostController and HostPermanent
again at resolution. This redirected payment/damage after control changes or
reattachment. CR 608.2c requires the written instructions; CR 701.21a prevents
a player from sacrificing an artifact they no longer control. Corrected only
Curse Artifact's payer, subject and damage recipient to captured event bindings.
The collection contains one record of this card, so there are no reprints to
update. Existing exact engine host/player snapshots supply this behavior.

made the new host-control and reattachment assertions fail; the corrected
record was restored. Initial test fixtures needed a creature's CardPT and an

SearchPlayer declining this optional sacrifice independently of live scripted
players. No gameplay assertions were removed to pass these checks. The old
Curse Artifact rejection assertion now requires full definition validation;
its prior damage-clause test retains its interactions with corrected identity.

### Supported signatures and reuse boundary

New engine API: `TargetControlledBy(PlayerRef) PermanentTargetOption`.
Supported references are `You` and `FromPlayer` of a saved event binding.
Definition validation rejects nil, missing and unsupported references and
visits event producers before target restrictions. The shared target query
reads current permanent control against the saved player. Existing event
capture instructions supply player values without executing effects or costs.
Each stack object retains its own player map for legality and retargeting;
copies and game clones copy this map. Separate pending events do not overwrite
one another. Candidate queries use a private game query frame. Random target
selection still consumes the live random stream after enumeration.

`WhenACreatureAttacksAndIsntBlocked/1`, with

action bodies. Both lower to existing source combat event patterns with a
fresh `PlayerBinding` per factory. Blocks, other events and independent
abilities do not gain this reference. Existing `Trigger_ThatCreature` keeps
source incarnation identity.

`Trigger_DefendingPlayer` or `You`, alone or inside nested `And/1` lists with
existing target restrictions. Other player expressions, disjunctions and plural
contexts remain rejected. Target factories now receive `instanceBindings` so
restrictions and actions share the same fresh declarations. RON owns spelling,
lexical scope and lowering; mage owns queries, player snapshots, stack state,
legality, choices, costs and zones.

### Contract, exact shapes and dependencies

Engine APIs:

- `TargetBlocksSource() PermanentTargetOption`.
- `TargetBlockedBySource() PermanentTargetOption`.
- `TargetInCombatWithSource() PermanentTargetOption`, a union of the two directions.
- `(*Combat).BlocksIncarnations(blockerID, blockerIncarnation, attackerID,
  attackerIncarnation uuid.UUID) bool` for live combat pairs.

The options compose conjunctively with other permanent target restrictions.
Engine definition validation requires a battlefield source. Both target
selection and resolution use the existing combat groups and incarnation maps.
Blocks of an attacking band and multiple blockers retain their pair identity.
The source passed to resolution target queries retains its original incarnation,
including live, absent, returned and phased cases. LKI supplies no live relation.
A blocked attacker remains blocked when a blocker leaves, but that departed
blocker is no longer a member of the pair (CR 509.1g/h). Departure, control
change, phasing, regeneration and explicit combat exit use the existing removal
contract (CR 506.4). Tapping does not remove a pair (CR 506.4b). Phase-in does
not restore combat membership. Removing source abilities does not cancel a
pending ability. Existing target legality, stack copies, clone isolation, cost
transactions and simultaneous/event/replacement pipelines retain their services.
This slice adds no new replacement or simultaneous-operation contract.

RON supports `IsBlockingAttacker(ThisPermanent)` and
`IsBlockedByDefender(ThisPermanent)` as permanent target filters, alone or
nested in `And`, and the exact two-direction `Or` in either order. Arguments
must be the bare `ThisPermanent` symbol in permanent scope. Other disjunctions,
duplicate directions, malformed declarations and host/event/target references
are rejected. Empty target disjunctions are rejected. Non-target collection,
static prevention and loop contexts remain unsupported. The spelling and
scope checks stay in `ron`; live pair behavior stays in `mage`. Factories
construct fresh typed target bindings; compiled plans retain no chosen state.
Semantic inventory classifies relation arguments as permanent references even
under unsupported parents, without implying those contexts are executable.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine API:
`IfPermanentMatches(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter,
body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`. It reuses `readPermanentInformation`,
including exact incarnation identity and phase/departure snapshots. It evaluates
at the instruction's position in the resolving sequence. Absent information is
false even for the zero filter. The predicate receives the current permanent or
its retained snapshot and the current game; this is a property query, not a
historical query of unrelated game state. Information reads cannot make an
absent/phased/returned object available for an action. Definition validation
rejects nil/unsupported references, unbound targets and nil bodies. Properties
and definition children propagate for the existing copy/validation services.
`PermanentMatchesFilter` remains unchanged as a static condition.

RON resolving actions support exactly
`If(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, filter), [nonempty actions])`.
`subject` uses the existing `compilePermanentRef` scope: bare `ThisPermanent`,
Aura `HostPermanent`, declared `Ref_TargetPermanent`, or the event reference
supplied by that event context. Factory-local bindings retain each declaration's
identity. Spell/mode/activation/trigger/delayed bodies use their existing scope;
the branch does not declare targets or make an unbound reference valid.

Pure property filters accept bare `AnyPermanent`, `IsTapped`, `IsUntapped`;
existing `IsSupertype`/`IsNonSupertype`, card-type, creature/land/enchantment
subtype, color and keyword predicates supported by `compileFilter`;
`PowerIs` and `ToughnessIs` with `EqualTo`, `LessThanOrEqualTo` or
`GreaterThanOrEqualTo` applied to `Integer(integer literal)`;
`PowerAndToughnessIsEqualTo(PT(integer, integer))`; and nonempty nested
`And([filters])` / `Or([filters])`. Existing supertype/color/keyword validation
remains in force. Unknown keywords and parameterized rampage are still errors.
Controller, counter, attachment, enchantment-status, historical and combat-pair
predicates are not added to property filters.

Bare `IsAttacking` and `IsBlocking` are supported as the entire filter through
`IfPermanentAttacking` and `IfPermanentBlocking`. They check current combat
membership and never restore it from LKI; property conjunctions/disjunctions
cannot contain them. Static `If`, intervening-if, activation restrictions,
`IfElse` and non-payment `Unless` do not gain support. Malformed arities,
wrong-role/unbound refs, empty logical filters and empty bodies are rejected.
The body reuses `compileActionSequence`, including nested branches and adjacent
payment continuations, with the same instance environment. Conditional mana production in activation
branches is rejected until classification and solver planning support the same
condition; spell and trigger mana actions keep their existing execution context.

Reusable rules stay in `mage`; spelling, shape and scope validation stay in
`ron`. The information service, existing filters, live combat branches, stack
legality/copy traversal, cost transactions, native layer/counter/zone actions,
cloning and cleanup remain their shared services. No new simultaneous-operation,
replacement, cost, event or static-state service is introduced. Bodies retain
those services' existing contracts. Inventory now classifies condition children
as permanent references/filters even under unsupported parents; this does not
claim those parent contexts are executable.

### Exact support, dependencies and reuse boundary

Engine addition:
`PreventCombatDamageByEachThisTurn(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`.
It uses `combatSourcePreventionInstallation` with `EndOfTurn`. Definition
validation checks its collection/ref declarations. Selection happens once at
resolution; duplicates within a set install one rule. Existing replacement
instances save each source incarnation, survive combat exit/control/phasing,
match captured departure damage, exclude returned incarnations and noncombat
damage, and expire in native cleanup. No new ordering or simultaneous-damage
service is introduced.

RON resolving collection:
`And([IsCardtype(Creature), IsBlockingAttacker(permanent-ref)])` lowers to
`BlockersOf`; `IsBlockedByDefender(permanent-ref)` lowers to `BlockedAttackersOf`.
Exactly two operands are required; either order is accepted. `TapEachPermanent`
uses this shape through the shared `TapEach` executor. Arbitrary extra filters,
controller constraints, bare relation filters and generic unions remain errors
in this new collection context.

RON resolving prevention:
`CreatePreventDamageUntil(CombatDamageWouldBeDealtByACreature(Or([
SinglePermanent(permanent-ref), relation-collection])), [PreventThatDamage],
UntilEndOfCombat|UntilEndOfTurn)`.
Exactly one singular reference and one relation collection are required, in
either order. Existing typed permanent references and scopes apply to each
reference independently. Factories build refs/targets from `instanceBindings`;
no chosen state is shared. Combat duration uses `PreventCombatDamageBy` and
`PreventCombatDamageByEach`; turn duration uses the corresponding turn
constructors. Each sequence captures its selected identities during resolution.
The constructor only installs rules, so the two selections have no intervening
battlefield mutation. Conditional bodies retain their resolution-time checks.
No static prevention, entry operation, cost, target declaration or arbitrary
permanent-filter context gains support.

Reuse: `BlockersOf`, `BlockedAttackersOf`, `TapEach`, typed targets/references,
`IfPermanentAttacking`/`IfPermanentBlocking`, `CantBeBlocked`, declaration
validation, source LKI/incarnations, stack copy/clone services, cost transactions,
combat packets, replacement ordering and native combat/cleanup boundaries.
RON spelling/shape/scope stays in `ron`; the constructor stays in `mage`.
Inventory classifies the nested collection as a permanent filter, including
under rejected parents, without claiming those contexts execute.
Rules read: CR 506.4, 509.1b/g/h, 615 and 616; existing identity/source contracts
supply CR 400.7 and 609.7 behavior. Local `data/LEG.json` agrees with Feint.
Sewers' complete source agrees with the Scryfall named-card API:
https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=Sewers%20of%20Estark . No source defect
was found in the selected records and no RON source was changed.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

Engine additions:

- `FilterPermanentSet(subjects PermanentSet, filter PermanentFilter)
  PermanentSet`: reads one typed set per operation, retaining its order and
  current matching, unphased members. It preserves the original set's legality
  and incarnation checks. It declares no targets and captures no absent object.
  A zero engine filter keeps all members. Definition inspection traverses the
  original set, so nil sets and undeclared target reads fail before gameplay.
  The wrapper has no mutable state.
- `PermanentDamageRecipients(subjects PermanentSet) DamageRecipientSet`: uses
  a private empty player set with the existing `DamageRecipients` service.
  Existing mixed-set nil validation is unchanged. `DealDamageEach` executes
  the same simultaneous damage batch, replacements and notifications.

RON resolving action support for `SpellDealsDamage(source, amount, recipient)`
and `PermanentDealsDamage(source, amount, recipient)`:

- `EachPermanent(filter)` uses live battlefield membership with the existing
  supported permanent filters. Nested `And`/`Or` must be nonempty. Attacking and
  blocking status are current, not departure information.
- `EachPermanent(Ref_TargetPermanents)` reads the local plural target binding.
- `EachPermanent(And([Ref_TargetPermanents, property-filter]))` requires exactly
  one plural reference and one supported resolving property filter, in either
  order. Nested property logic is supported; nested/duplicate references,
  singular/player references, extra operands and unsupported properties fail.

Existing spell, mode, activation and trigger action scopes and source/amount
validation remain in force. Live collections need no target declaration.
Plural reads require their local declaration and retain the existing rejection
of delayed plural target collections. Damage packet and replacement-operation
contexts do not gain collection support. Per-factory `instanceBindings` supply
plural targets; no game-time declaration, card-name executor or global result
slot is added. Inventory classifies the filter and collection reference roles,
including descendants, without claiming gameplay support for other contexts.

Reuse: `MatchingPermanents`, `PermanentTargetsBinding`, target announcement and
resolution validation, incarnation checks, current characteristic filters,
`TapEach`, `DamageRecipients`, `DealDamageEach`, simultaneous damage outcomes,
source LKI, lifelink, prevention/replacement rechecks, cost transactions, stack
copies, clone isolation and state-based actions. No separate damage, targeting,
cost, zone or replacement system is introduced. Rules read: CR 120.4/120.8,
400.7, 608.2b/c/h, 702.26b/d; existing damage/replacement contracts supply
CR 615 and 616 ordering.

Engine APIs:

- `ToughnessOfWithLKI(PermanentRef) ResolutionValue`: current layered toughness,
  or the exact incarnation's retained final departure/phase toughness. Unknown
  identity returns zero. It uses the same validation and information reader as
  power and cannot make an absent object available for actions.
- `UntilEndOfNextUpkeep(PlayerRef, ...ContinuousModification) ResolvingEffect`:
  captures player, subjects and values through the existing layer service. The
  next actual upkeep marks existing effects; they expire after priority, before
  final SBAs. New effects created during that upkeep wait for a later one.
  Skipped upkeeps do not mark effects; extra upkeeps can. The existing composed
  effect clone copies saved-player and marking state. No new duration enum,
  delayed trigger, zone, replacement, payment or global result service is added.

RON owns spelling, validation, value composition and inventory roles. The engine
owns retained information, incarnation checks, captured layer values and expiry.
Per-factory instanceBindings connect every value to its own target/event object.
Reuse includes `PowerOfWithLKI`, `readPermanentInformation`, phase/departure
snapshots, `SubtractValues`, `SetBasePowerToughness`, `ModifyPT`, `Until`, existing
7b/7c layer order, continuous-effect clone hooks, transactional casting, target
announcement/resolution checks and source-incarnation capture. Old callers stay.

### Exact shapes, contexts and engine reuse

RON top-level static shape:
`PermanentRuleEffect(subject, [CantBeTheTargetOfSpells(filter)])`, with exactly
one operation. `subject` is bare `ThisPermanent`, or bare `HostPermanent` on an
Aura. `filter` reuses the spell-filter compiler: bare `AnySpell`,
`IsEnchantmentType(Aura)`, `IsCardtype(type)`, `IsColor(color)`, and nonempty
nested `And([...])`/`Or([...])`. Malformed arity/constructors, non-Aura host reads,
unbound or wrong-role references, unsupported filters, empty logical lists and
combined operation lists fail compilation. No conditional, resolving, entry,
cost, ability-targeting or enchantment-attachment rule context gains support.
The semantic inventory assigns the nested operand `spell_filter`.

Engine APIs:

- `CantBeTargetedBySpells(PermanentRef, CardFilter) StaticRule`: live subject and
  filter checks through the current source, attachment incarnation and existing
  continuous-effect active/printed-suppression lifecycle. Nil/unbound references
  and zero filters fail definition validation. A source must be present and
  retain its ability. Both players' matching spells are prohibited. Source
  control changes do not remove the rule. Source departure, phasing and ability
  removal deactivate it; returned sources supply their new rule. A moving Aura
  follows its current host; returned hosts do not retain the old attachment.
  Host ability removal does not remove its separate Aura's restriction.
- `SpellTargetSource(Card) Card`: immutable pre-stack information view with
  explicit spell identity and the same card UUID. The existing `targetSourceLKI`
  also records spell identity for popped and copied spells. Ability views remain
  separate after source departure. `cardColors` reads the retained view so
  `CardFilter` color checks use current spell colors after stack removal.

RON owns grammar and reference validation; mage owns rules, current information
and targeting identity. Existing caller signatures stay. Spell-only casting,
grouped/modal choice, alternate-zone casting, castability queries, prompting,
interactive/AI choices and gametest validation now pass the explicit spell view.
Copies already query `resolutionTargetSource`, which supplies their own identity,
controller and colors. Existing ability queries keep their original source view.

Reuse: `StaticRule`, `FuncContinuousEffect`, printed-ability suppression,
`PermanentRef` and attachment/incarnation resolution, active effect removal and
clone hooks, `compilePermanentRef`, `compileSpellFilter`, instanceBindings,
transactional costs, target declarations/bounds, original-incarnation target
checks, resolution legality and copy retargeting. No new zone, targeting registry,
resolution slot, event, payment-result or replacement system is introduced.
Nontargeted Aura attachment stays legal. This service introduces no replacement
ordering, APNAP trigger or simultaneous-operation changes; those existing tests
remain in the full suites.

### Exact shape, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine API: `UntapWithManaPayment(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter,
cost core.ManaCost) ResolvingEffect`. It selects distinct controlled, tapped,
unphased matching permanents at resolution. The player can choose a subset or
zero. All selection precedes one total mana transaction. Failed total payment
spends nothing and untaps nothing. The operation saves `capturedPermanent`
identities locally; no global result, last-action slot or mutable declaration
state is used. Incarnations are checked before payment and again for the action.
A chosen object can leave during a mana ability; LKI does not restore it.
The total is fixed before payment; integer overflow fails before resources change.
Stun replacements and all untap events use the existing simultaneous batch.

RON shape in `compileActionSequence`:

```text
PlayerAction(player, ChooseAnyNumberPermanentsAndPayManaForEach(
  And([filter, ControlledByPlayer(PlayerAction_ThatPlayer)]), mana)),
PlayerAction(player, UntapEachPermanent(TheChosenPermanents))
```

The pair must be adjacent in one resolving `ActionList`; both player expressions
must be structurally identical and valid in that typed scope. Spell, activation,
trigger and conditional branch action lists use the same compiler path.
`filter` must require bare `IsTapped` through an `And` conjunction and otherwise
uses supported permanent filters. The outer `And` has exactly one filter and
one action-player controller clause, in either order. `mana` uses the existing
nonnegative fixed symbol list; X is rejected. The result is a bare symbol and
only its adjacent untap consumer is supported. This establishes a complete
choice/payment/result context, not arbitrary saved collections. Malformed,
unbound, wrong-player, wrong-controller, non-tapped and separated declarations
remain compile errors. RON owns spelling, scope, validation and lowering.

Reuse: `compilePlayerRef`, per-factory `instanceBindings`, saved upkeep players,
`PermanentsControlledBy`, existing permanent filters, `capturedPermanent`,
`prepareActionPaymentTransaction`, `ManaCostPayment`, mana solver and
`untapPermanentsTogether`. Source departure/control changes do not change a saved
upkeep player. Copies and cloned pending triggers use their own resolving choices
and payments. Choices are not targets and shroud does not exclude them.
Activation reductions do not change these resolution payments. No alternate
payment, zone, event or untap subsystem is introduced.

Local Oracle evidence: `data/ARN.json` for Magnetic Mountain and `data/FEM.json`
for Thelon's Curse explicitly require choosing tapped blue creatures controlled
by the upkeep player, paying for each chosen creature, then untapping them.
CR 118.3/118.12, 400.7, 502.3, 608.2d/g/h, 701.26b and 702.26b supply the
payment, identity, timing, legality and phasing contracts. No source defect was
found or corrected. All RON files/hashes are unchanged; no vocabulary source
refresh is needed. The semantic inventory now assigns roles to the choice's
filter/mana and the chosen collection reference.

### Exact shapes, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

In `Activated` and `ActivatedWithModifiers`, including modal bodies:

- `Exile([Permanent(ThisPermanent)], [])`: source exile during activation payment.
- `Exile([ACardInGraveyards(And([cardFilter,
  InAPlayersGraveyard(SinglePlayer(You))]))], [])`: one selected matching card
  in the activator's graveyard. Exactly one graveyard exile payment is permitted
  per activation. The owner clause occurs once at the outer conjunction;
  other operands reuse nonempty intrinsic card type/color logical filters.
- `ManaValueOfExiled(TheCardExiledThisWay)`: a saved numeric payment result in
  that activation's body, including its existing mode and branch scopes.
  `NumberCountersOfTypeOnPermanent(value, counter, subject)` accepts this value;
  other counter-amount contexts retain their previous support.

Object lists must contain one entry, and operation lists must be empty. Wrong
arity, tuple symbols, absent/duplicate/foreign graveyard controller clauses,
unbound results, source-exile result reads, cross-activation reads, multiple
matching graveyard payments, plural payments and controlled-permanent choices
remain compile errors. Exile payment forms are not resolving actions, casting
cost adapters, optional resolution costs, static operations or entry operations.

RON owns spelling, scope and diagnostics. `exilePaymentPlan` and each factory's
`instanceBindings.exiles` associate the cost and numeric consumer. Each activation
factory allocates its own `NumberBinding`; pending resolutions, copies and clones
use the existing saved-number frame. No new global last-action result is read.
Engine reuse: `ExileSourceCost`, `ExileMatchingCardFromGraveyardCostInto`, the
shared payment transaction and locked graveyard visits, `FromNumber`, existing
modal activation/copy services, `AddCountersTo`, typed permanent references and
incarnation validation. Payment consumes cards at announcement and never places
counters then. Failed total payment spends no live life, tap state or exile
objects. Card selection is not targeting. Paid-card departure does not erase the
saved value. A returned or phased-out source cannot receive counters via LKI;
a phase cycle preserves the original incarnation. Source control changes do not
change the saved payment.

Bare resolving action `ShuffleGraveyardIntoLibrary` lowers to the new reusable
`ShuffleGraveyardFor(PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`, with `You`. The shared library
recycler gains a graveyard-only mode. It moves the complete graveyard before zone
and aggregate graveyard-departure events, then shuffles once, including when empty.
The hand and other players' zones remain intact. The legacy effect delegates to
the same service, retaining current callers. Nil/unbound player declarations are
invalid, and an absent player has no effect. Copies resolve for their own
controllers. No separate zone, shuffle, counter or payment subsystem is added.

Local Oracle data in `data/ATQ.json` and `data/DRK.json` confirms the complete

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine API: `ChooseOpponentAsEnters() AsEntersBattlefieldAbility`. It runs through
the existing `prepareBattlefieldEntry` hook before battlefield registration and
entry observers. In this two-player engine, the entry controller has one eligible
opponent. The choice is saved on that entering permanent's `ChosenPlayer`, without
targeting, a stack object, payment, or an optional choice. The owner is irrelevant.
Definition metadata rejects the ability on instants and sorceries. New factory
calls make new abilities; copied permanent spells choose for their own entry
controllers. Control changes and phase cycles preserve the choice. New entries
choose again. Clones keep separate permanent state.

The existing `ETBChooseOpponent` helper sets the choice after registration. That
timing did not satisfy CR 614.12a, so it is not used by the new adapter. The
implement-engine skill supplied the prerequisite workflow. Legacy helpers and
their callers retain their behavior. The new primitive adds no parallel entry,
replacement, zone or choice subsystem and no general replacement ordering policy.

RON accepts exactly:

- `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,[ChooseAPlayer(Opponent)])`: one operation,
  one choice declaration per permanent card.
- `TriggerA(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(TheChosenPlayer)),body)`
  when that entry declaration exists. The declaration is checked before the
  other static card rules, so textual rule order does not change its scope.

RON owns spelling, arity, source/context validation, duplicate/unbound errors and
the private `opponentEntryChoicePlan`. The saved value lives in each permanent,
not in that compilation plan or a global last-action slot. Wrong arity, tuple
symbols, alternate player filters, combined entry operations, duplicate producers,
nonpermanent entry declarations, resolving player choices, chosen-player action
reads and chosen-player end-step filters remain errors. Cursed Rack reaches its
next unsupported static player operation; Jihad's combined entry remains rejected.

The upkeep adapter reuses `TurnStepBegins(EachUpkeep,playerBinding)`,
`EventIsChosenPlayerUpkeep`, each factory's existing step-event binding and the
standard pending-trigger frame. It checks the chosen player at event time and
captures that event's player before stack placement. It is not an intervening-if
check. Later control/choice changes, departure, return, phasing and ability removal
cannot redirect a pending trigger. Inactive sources cannot create new triggers.
Copies retain the event player even with another controller. The hand amount is
read at resolution; damage uses existing prevention, source LKI and lifelink.
CR 113.7a, 400.7, 603.6, 608.2h, 614.12a and 702.26 support these contracts.

### Exact supported signatures and reuse boundary

- `TriggerA(AtTheEndOfCombat, body)` with the bare event symbol and an existing
  supported action list/target context.
- `TriggerI(AtTheEndOfCombat,
  ACombatPermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent,
  Or([AttackedThisCombat, BlockedThisCombat])), body)`. The two distinct symbols
  may appear in either order, once each. No other history predicate or subject
  is accepted by this slice.

RON owns shape, arity, source and scope validation. The event supplies no player
or permanent event binding; unbound reads remain errors. Each factory builds
fresh abilities and action declarations. Engine reuse: `At`, `EachEndOfCombat`,
`WithInterveningIf`, `SourceAttackedOrBlockedThisCombatCondition`, the existing
incarnation-aware tracker, entry counters, removal actions and stack frames.
No engine change or new engine API was needed. No new state lives in RON.

The event fires at the beginning of each end-of-combat step, on either player's
turn. The intervening condition checks at detection and resolution. Declared
attacking/blocking history remains after removal from combat and control change,
but cannot follow a returned incarnation. Phasing blocks a check; a phase cycle
preserves history. Native resolution precedes the history reset; a later combat
starts fresh. Entering attacking never counts as having attacked (CR 508.4).
A plain pending trigger survives departure. Copies retain source identity and
use their own controller; clones keep independent history and counters.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

Engine: `AddCountersUpTo(subject PermanentRef, counter CounterType,
amount ResolutionValue, limit int) ResolvingEffect`. At resolution, the effect
controller chooses zero through `min(amount, max(limit-current, 0))`. Nonpositive
amounts, full/overfull or absent/phased subjects require no choice. Invalid
responses place nothing. Definition validation rejects nil/unbound references,
nil values, invalid counters and limits outside 0–255. This range follows the
existing counter storage; larger limits remain explicit unsupported declarations.

RON resolving action:
`PutCountersWithRestriction([UptoNumberCountersOfTypeOnPermanent(amount,
counter, subject)], CantCauseTheNumberOfCountersOfTypeOnPermanentToBeGreaterThan(
counter, subject, Integer(limit)))`. Exactly one placement and matching counter
and typed subject are required. Amounts reuse `compileInstanceCounterAmount`,
including correctly scoped announced X; counter types and references reuse the
existing validators. Fixed limits use 0–255. Malformed arity/lists, multiple
instructions, other instructions/restrictions, mismatched counter/subject,
unbound or wrong-category references and cost/static/entry contexts reject.
This action declares no new target or binding. Existing resolving spell, mode,
activation and trigger scopes continue to govern its references and values.

RON owns shape/scope/lowering and inventory roles. The engine owns the numeric
choice, incarnation checks and optional action limit. Each factory uses its own
existing typed declarations; each resolution reads its own stack X/controller.
No mutable choice is captured in a factory. Reuse: typed reference resolution,
`ChooseNumber`, `AddCountersAction`, the existing affected-player replacement
pipeline, X mana transactions, tap costs, upkeep restrictions, counter layers,
stack copies and clones. Existing counter placement callers keep their behavior.

The final amount for the restricted counter on the original subject is capped
after replacements using current room. Replacements retain normal ordering,
rechecks and cancellation. Original-destination placement requires the original
incarnation; a changed destination/counter does not inherit its restriction.
The action does not remove excess counters from other effects and establishes
no static maximum under CR 122.4. Control changes and phase cycles preserve the
subject; departure/return and unresolved phasing prevent placement. A pending
activation survives ability removal. Copies choose with their controller and
keep their own announced X. Clones have independent counters and frames; native
cloned simulation players choose their default amount. No new simultaneous
collection placement, LKI information read or payment contract is introduced.

### Exact signatures and contracts

Engine: `PreventDamageFromCardType(subject PermanentRef, kind core.CardType)
StaticRule`. Compose with `Static`. Valid card types are the engine enum;
nil/undeclared subjects and invalid types fail definition validation. The source
must be an active original battlefield incarnation. `This` protects that source;
`AttachedPermanent` follows the current host. The shared rule checks these
identities on every proposed damage event, including after another replacement.

RON static declaration:
`PreventDamage(DamageWouldBeDealtByASourceToRecipient(IsCardtype(type),
Permanent(subject)), [PreventThatDamage])`. Exactly two event arguments, one
valid type symbol, one typed subject and one symbol operation are required.
Subjects are `ThisPermanent` or a declared Aura's `HostPermanent`. Targets,
event refs, unbound hosts, player recipients, malformed arities, other filter
shapes, alternate operations and resolving/cost contexts reject. Source-type
syntax has a separate inventory role, `damage_source_filter`; its operand has
role `card_type`. This does not claim other source-filter shapes.

RON owns spelling, shape/scope validation, diagnostics and lowering. The engine
owns live subject resolution, exact damage-source type matching, static lifecycle
and replacement execution. Existing static combat prevention now shares private
`staticDamagePrevention*` types with this rule. Its public API and combat-only
behavior stay unchanged. No mutable choice or game state enters the factory.

Damage filters read current types while the original source permanent is live,
retained types after departure/phasing, and the captured card for spell sources.
Unknown captured permanent incarnations cannot fall back to another UUID visit.
Legacy UUID-only actions retain live lookup. Both combat and noncombat packets
can be prevented repeatedly; other recipients and nonmatching types receive
damage. Source-type changes and redirection are rechecked. The affected recipient
chooses the replacement order. Unpreventable damage still uses the shared rule.
Source ability removal ends prevention; removing a host's abilities does not
remove an Aura's separate rule. Attachment/control changes, phasing/phase cycles,
source departure/return, copies and game clones use existing identity services.

No new targeting, source choice, next-event consumption, spell-entry link,
allocation, timing, cost, LKI storage or simultaneous-operation service is added.
The existing shared services provide those applicable contracts. Accepted
permanent-only prevention still excludes captured spell sources.

### Exact supported signatures and reuse boundary

Engine: `PreventDamageFromBlockedCreatures(subject PermanentRef) StaticRule`,
composed with `Static`. `This` and `AttachedPermanent` use the existing live
subject service. Nil and undeclared references fail definition validation.
The rule extends the private static prevention implementation; existing public
combat-only and source-card-type services keep their contracts.

RON permanent static rule:
`PreventDamage(DamageWouldBeDealtByAPermanentToRecipient(And([IsCardtype(Creature), IsBlockedByDefender(ThisPermanent)]), Permanent(ThisPermanent)), [PreventThatDamage])`.
The two filter operands may occur in either order. Both permanent references
must resolve to the permanent source. Exactly one symbol operation is required.
Other source types, filter shapes, references, recipients, operations, malformed
arities, and resolving/cost contexts reject. Existing target and collection
uses of `IsBlockedByDefender` retain their independent contexts. Inventory already
assigns the nested filter and reference roles; no reporting adapter is needed.

RON owns spelling, declaration/scope checks and lowering. The engine owns
`Combat.BlocksIncarnations`, current damage-source identity/type matching,
static source/host lifecycle and the shared replacement pipeline. Factories
build separate abilities without mutable choice state. No new timing, target,
cost, LKI storage, damage batch or global result slot is added.

Prevention applies repeatedly to both combat and noncombat damage from a live
creature that the current subject blocks, only to that subject. A captured
source must still have the original incarnation. LKI cannot restore a departed,
returned, phased or removed combat pair. Phasing preserves permanent identity
but removes it from combat, including across a phase cycle. Control changes
also remove the pair. Tapping does not remove it. Current creature-type loss
stops matching. A returned attacker that enters a new pair cannot supply the
old captured source. Source ability removal ends the rule; a separate Aura's
rule survives host ability removal and follows its current attachment.
Replacement rechecks see pair changes and redirected recipients. The existing
pipeline retains affected-player ordering, simultaneous packets, unpreventable
damage and clone isolation. There is no shield consumption.

options. `WithYourTurnOnly` writes the same timing field, so ordinary option
order would erase sorcery timing in a conjunction. Applying `WithSorcerySpeed`
last preserves both main-phase and empty-stack restrictions. Independent
activation conditions and limits remain in effect. No game state or new
bindings are captured by the plan. Factory abilities and existing cost/target
bindings remain per instance.

announcement and transactional payment. No engine behavior or API is changed.

required. The priority loop owns priority; this adapter grants none. Timing is
checked before choices/payment and is not repeated during later resolution or
copy resolution. Mana planning and explicit mana activation agree. LKI,
replacement ordering and simultaneous-operation rules gain no new contracts.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine APIs:

- `SetBaseToughness(PermanentRef, ResolutionValue) ContinuousModification`:
  layer 7b, preserving printed/CDA power and earlier base-power settings;
  shared `Until` captures the value and incarnation. Shared `While` evaluates
  live values. Bonuses/counters and switches retain layer 7c/7d ordering.
- `AddValues(ResolutionValue, ResolutionValue) ResolutionValue`: extend the
  existing typed arithmetic service, with definition validation of operands.
- `CountGraveyardCards(PlayerRef, CardFilter) ResolutionValue`: pure current
  selected-player matching-card count; zero filter means all cards, absent
  player means zero. Reuse player identity and existing card filters/zone state.
  This does not establish all-zone CDAs or change card-characteristic queries.

RON supported shape:
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(typedPermanentRef, [SetToughness(value)])`, only in
resolving action contexts. Keep the existing single-modification boundary.
Values accept `Integer(integer)`, nested binary `Plus(left, right)` and
`Minus(left, right)`, `PowerOfPermanent(typedRef)` and
`ToughnessOfPermanent(typedRef)` through current/LKI queries, and
`TheNumberOfGraveyardCards(And([cardFilter,
InAPlayersGraveyard(SinglePlayer(typedPlayerRef))]))`. The latter accepts either
operand order and exactly one card filter and one graveyard player. Reuse the
existing nonempty type/color `And`/`Or` card-filter grammar and enclosing typed
player scope. No binding is fabricated. Unsupported static/temporary contexts,
chosen numbers, undeclared X, invalid arities, duplicate zones, unbound reads
and mixed modifications still reject at declaration time.

RON owns spelling, scope, validated factories and semantic inventory roles.
The engine owns layers, arithmetic, current graveyard queries and execution.
No mutable state is retained by a compiler plan. Factory targets and abilities
remain separate. The setting captures its subject and number at resolution;
control changes, source departure and cleanup cannot change the installed
number. Phasing preserves an installed setting. A returned permanent cannot
receive an old setting. Source/target departures cannot restore a combat pair
through LKI. Payment, APNAP, copies, retargeting and game clones use shared
services; no replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation rule changes.

### Established signatures and contexts

Engine: `MayPutFromHandOntoBattlefield(PlayerRef, CardFilter) ResolvingEffect`.
Typed player references participate in definition validation. Offered candidates,
hand visits and choices are local to each execution. No binding or last-action
slot is introduced. Selection occurs during resolution, with no source-presence
requirement or LKI read. Invalid choices and returned hand visits move nothing.
Instants/sorceries cannot enter. Empty candidate sets make no decisions. Decline
makes no card selection. Ownership is unchanged; the selected player controls
and puts the card onto the battlefield. This does not cast or play a land.

Reuse `Player` hand visits/decision methods and `prepareBattlefieldEntry`,
`registerBattlefieldEntry`, `completeBattlefieldEntry`; Aura legality uses
`canAttach`, `auraHostIsLegal` and `Attach`. A land-entry prohibition retains the
original hand visit. Permanent-host Auras choose a legal host before entry;
shroud permits this untargeted choice, protection and phasing restrict it.
No legal host keeps the Aura in hand. A missing or invalid mandatory host response
uses a legal offered host; its identity and legality are checked again. Attachment
precedes entry events.
This does not establish player-enchanting Auras, repeated player entry or a new
replacement pipeline. Existing Go callers and the legacy hand-entry action are
preserved. No DSL deletion is attempted before its caller/removal gates.

RON: `MayAction(PutACardFromHandOnBattlefield(filter, [EntersNormally]))` in
supported resolving action lists (spell/activation/trigger bodies and their
supported branches). Exactly one bare EntersNormally is required. Filters:
bare IsPermanent; IsSupertype with Basic/Legendary/Snow/World; validated
IsLandType/IsCreatureType; existing IsCardtype/IsNonCardtype/IsColor/IsNonColor;
nonempty recursive And/Or lists. RON owns spelling, filter context and errors.
PlayerAction/PlayerActions loops, repeated procedures, other entry operations,
resolution-cost positions and result consumers remain separate unsupported
contexts. Semantic reporting now labels hand_entry_filter and entry_operation
children even below rejected parents. Plans contain no selected runtime state.

### Exact shapes, engine contract and reuse

Engine: `CantBeEnchantedExceptBy(subject, exception PermanentRef) StaticRule`.
Both typed references require valid declaration scope. The rule reads current
source/subject/exception incarnations without LKI. Source ability removal,
departure and phasing disable its rule. Phase cycles keep the attachment; control
changes leave the prohibition intact. Current attachment movement moves the
restriction. A returned host cannot inherit the old attachment. Removing host
abilities does not remove the Aura's rule. Separate factory instances and copied
Aura spells have separate identities and cannot share the original exception.
Clones copy effect state and read their own source, attachment and suppression.

Reuse the existing printed continuous-effect lifecycle, typed references,
SpellTargetSource/retained spell views, targeting/payment/copy pipeline,
auraHostIsLegal, canAttach, optional hand entry and withZoneChangeBatch.
Aura spell queries reject illegal targets before payment and recheck at
resolution. Ability targets, non-Aura spells under this rule alone, Equipment
and shroud during untargeted entry remain separate. Spell-only restrictions
still do not forbid direct attachment.

Engine prerequisite correction: CR 303.4c/704.5m puts illegal attached Auras
into their owners' graveyards; the former implementation destroyed them.
Selected illegal Auras now move through one existing zone batch, bypassing
indestructibility and regeneration. Trigger checks receive the former
battlefield and events occur after all selected moves. No new replacement,
choice, APNAP, damage or cost service is introduced. Existing zone-move APIs
retain their contracts; this slice does not establish a new zone replacement API.

RON: top-level `PermanentRuleEffect(subject,
[CantBeEnchantedByAnEnchantment(And([Other(ThisPermanent),
IsEnchantmentType(Aura)]))])`. Operand order can be reversed. Subjects are bare
ThisPermanent, or bare HostPermanent on an Aura. Exactly those two filter
operands are supported. A two-operation list can pair this operation with one
existing `CantBeTheTargetOfSpells(filter)` in either order. Other exceptions,
extra conditions, duplicates, malformed references/arity, unknown operations,
conditional contexts and resolving durations remain explicit compile errors.
No spelling or scope logic is placed in the engine.
Semantic inventory labels the restriction filter, exception reference and
subtype even beneath rejected parents. No selected runtime state is captured
in compiler plans or shared between factories.

`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` or `ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)`,
alone or in a nonempty nested `And` with existing property filters, in either
operand order. Property-only `Or` retains the existing filter grammar.
Controller restrictions inside `Or`, duplicate/conflicting restrictions, other
player references, malformed arity/kinds and non-Aura enchant declarations are
errors. Cost, static-count and ordinary targeting filters keep their separate
contexts. The compiler uses a typed controller selector and constructs a fresh
cast target on every factory call. No runtime choice state enters the plan.
Existing inventory roles already describe the full selected syntax, including
beneath rejected parents; no new reporting role is required.

Engine API: `TargetPermanentYouControl(...PermanentFilter) Target`, the raw
counterpart of the existing typed `TargetYouControl` option. Opponent control
reuses `TargetPermanentOpponentControls` and `TargetOpponentControls`.
`auraHostIsLegalForController` keeps the supplied current/prospective controller
separate from card ownership and unwraps typed declarations before checking
their property filters and these controller flags. Existing `auraHostIsLegal`
callers retain their signature; it derives the current controller for live Auras.
Attachment and state actions pass the known source controller explicitly.
Optional hand entry supplies its prospective source through `canAttach`.

Casting and resolving targets read the spell controller; copies read their own
controller. Current attachment legality reads the Aura controller, not a saved
caster or owner. Changing either host or Aura control can end legality. Direct
illegal attachment retains the former attachment. Shroud prevents casting but
permits untargeted entry and existing attachment. Legal phase cycles retain
attachment identity. Returned or unavailable spell targets cannot receive an
Aura through an old target reference. This slice adds no LKI information read;
existing identity and departure services retain their contracts.

Reuse: permanent target flags/query services, casting/payment rollback,
resolution target checks, spell copies, current attachment lists/incarnations,
optional hand-entry visits and host choices, clone isolation, state-action
zone batching and former-battlefield event information. Illegal Auras move to
their owners' graveyards in the existing simultaneous batch, bypassing
indestructibility/regeneration. No new replacement-order, APNAP, damage, zone,
player-binding or global action-result service is introduced.

### Exact signatures, context and reuse

Resolving actions support:

- `If(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, filter), [actions...])` with
  `HasACounterOfType(counter)` or `HasNoCountersOfType(counter)`.
- `HasNumberCountersOfType(EqualTo(Integer(n)), counter)` and
  `HasNumberCountersOfType(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)), counter)`.
- Nonempty nested `And([filters...])` / `Or([filters...])` in the existing
  resolving property filter grammar. Each filter reads one counter kind.

`n` is a nonnegative integer literal. Counter names and supported PTCounter
coordinates use compilePermanentCounterType. Subjects use compilePermanentRef
and the existing typed, lexical scope. Malformed kinds/arity, unknown counters,
negative/dynamic thresholds, other comparisons and unbound references reject
at compilation. Static conditions retain their prior equality-only grammar;
activation and exiled-card conditions remain separate contexts. Conditional
mana activation remains an error until solver planning supports its body.

Engine API: `CounterCountAtLeast(counter core.CounterType, minimum int)
PermanentFilter`. Pure comparison promotes the stored count to int. Nil does
not match; zero, negative and above-255 engine thresholds use ordinary integer
comparison. No new game-time declaration panic or mutable query state.
Presence and exact/zero count reuse HasCounter and CounterCountEquals.

Execution reuses IfPermanentMatches and its current-or-LKI information service,
per-instance target factories, incarnation captures, counter add/remove actions,
existing destruction/sacrifice, control/phasing, stack copies, clones and casting
transactions. Preceding instructions complete before condition evaluation.
Old LKI may supply a count, but cannot permit an action on a departed, returned
or phased-out subject. No new binding producer, replacement ordering, batch,
APNAP, cost payment or simultaneous-operation contract is introduced.
Inventory now classifies HasNoCountersOfType's child as permanent_counter_type
and follows GreaterThanOrEqualTo's literal through the existing counter
comparison/value roles; expression context still distinguishes resolving use
from static use. Inventory support remains unverified, not a gameplay claim.

RON activation modifiers now accept:

`ActivateOnlyIf(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, filter))`

within `ActivatedWithModifiers`, including ordinary and Modal_ChooseOne bodies
and nonempty nested modifier And lists. Subject is a bare ThisPermanent on a
permanent or HostPermanent on an Aura. Targets, event results, players, malformed
references and non-Aura host reads reject at compilation. Conditions are
compiled in the declaration scope before the body introduces targets or modes.

Filter grammar reuses compileResolvingPropertyFilter: supported current types,
subtypes, supertypes, colors, tapped state, keywords and P/T comparisons;
nonempty nested And/Or; HasACounterOfType, HasNoCountersOfType and
HasNumberCountersOfType(EqualTo(Integer(n))|GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n)),
counter). Counter thresholds are nonnegative literals. Unknown counters,
dynamic/negative thresholds, unsupported comparisons and malformed declarations
remain errors. Static conditions retain their distinct grammar; resolving
branches retain their separate current-or-LKI behavior. Conditional mana bodies
with modifiers remain explicitly rejected by their existing compiler context.

children. Nil conditions fail definition validation and check false without a

zone, cost, target, replacement, event or simultaneous-action system is added.

PermanentMatchesFilter with This/AttachedPermanent reads live source/attachment
identity, with no LKI fallback. Absent, phased and stale hosts cannot qualify;

### Exact shapes, dependencies and engine reuse

RON static condition:
`PermanentPassesFilter(subject, AttackedDuringLastPlayersTurn(player))`.
Subject is bare ThisPermanent on a permanent or HostPermanent in Aura scope.
Player is bare You or ItsController; the latter reads the current subject
controller, which can differ from the Aura controller. The predicate is a direct
static property condition, not a general permanent filter. Nested And/Or property
filters, resolving branches, activation conditions, costs and targets do not
receive this history form. Wrong arity, tuple references/players, unsupported
players and unbound/incompatible subjects reject at compilation.

RON static body:
`If(condition,[PermanentRuleEffect(subject,[CantAttack])])`.
The body has one rule and one bare operation. Subject uses the existing live
source/Aura-host grammar. All existing supported static conditions are reused,
including counter conditions; mixed bodies and extra operations remain rejected.
Conditional untap bodies retain their existing grammar and execution service.

Engine APIs:

- `AttackedDuringLastTurnIncarnation(player, permanent, incarnation uuid.UUID)
  bool` reads the specified player's most recent completed turn. Final cleanup
  archives exact incarnations beside the existing ID-only history. Native and
  explicit attack declarations already supply these identities. Current-turn
  attacks and combat resets do not overwrite prior history. Another player's
  cleanup preserves it; a later empty completed turn clears it. Nested maps are
  copied independently by TrackerSystem.Clone. Existing ID-only callers remain.
- `PermanentAttackedDuringLastTurn(PermanentRef, PlayerRef) StateCondition`
  accepts This or AttachedPermanent and You or ControllerOf a live source/host.
  It shares resolveStatePermanent with PermanentMatchesFilter. Queries are pure,
  read current control/attachment and exact live incarnation, and use no LKI.
  Absent/phased subjects check false; a phase cycle keeps history; returned
  objects cannot inherit it. Invalid/nil declarations fail definition validation.
- `CantAttackIf(PermanentRef, StateCondition) StaticRule` adds a condition to the
  existing matchingAttackRestriction service. Conditional and unconditional
  callers use the same attack checks and printed static source lifecycle.
  Conditions check before declaration and cannot remove declared attackers.
  Removing host abilities cannot remove a separate Aura rule. Source removal,
  phasing and ability removal use the existing printed-effect wrappers.

Reuse: TrackerSystem archive/clone, typed source/host/controller references,
printed continuous effects, attack legality, PreventUntapDuringStep and its
simultaneous decision snapshot, land dependence, Aura targeting/attachment,
entry events, native cleanup and cost rollback. No parallel zone, event, target,
payment, damage or replacement subsystem. No global result slot, card-name
executor, Go fallback or partial production registry. No new replacement or
simultaneous-operation rule is needed; existing services retain their contracts.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Top-level permanent `TriggerA(event, actions)` supports these exact events:

- `WhenAPermanentIsDealtDamage(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))`.
- `WhenAPlayerIsDealtDamage(SinglePlayer(You))`.

Event and filter envelopes must be tuples with one argument. References must
be bare symbols. Other subjects, Aura hosts, collections, target/event refs,
additional arguments and malformed declarations remain rejected. These events
observe all damage, including combat damage; they are not combat-only.

Private adapter: `compileDamageReceivedTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope)
(optionFactory, error)`. RON owns spelling, lexical scope, validation and lowering.
The permanent event gives a typed source reference for bare
`Trigger_ThatCreatureOrPlaneswalker` only in its body. It resolves through `This`
and the engine's saved source incarnation, with no target or global result slot.
The player event matches the source controller at detection and does not declare
`Trigger_ThatPlayer` or a permanent recipient. Sibling abilities do not inherit
these bindings. Both events give an immutable per-event `damageAmountPlan` and a fresh
per-factory `NumberBinding` for bare `Trigger_AmountOfDamageDealt`.

`compileInstanceCounterAmount` now permits that saved event number in the existing
`NumberCountersOfTypeOnPermanent(amount, counter, subject)` resolving action.
Unbound or tuple-spelled damage numbers fail compilation. Other existing amount
forms retain their previous grammar. No general value or cost support is implied.

Engine reuse: `ReceivesDamage(This, amount)`, `ControllerIsDealtDamage(amount)`,
`BindNumber`, `FromNumber`, `WhenEvent`, `Sequence`, `This`, `AddCountersTo`, native
trigger snapshots/APNAP/stack placement, source incarnations, state-based actions,
shared damage batches, replacement/prevention pipeline, transactional casting,
phasing, trigger copies and game cloning. No new engine contract or public API.
Amounts are the final positive damage for each packet. Life loss and prevented
or zero damage do not trigger. An absent, phased or returned source cannot receive
an old action; a phase cycle retains identity. Damage amounts stay saved after
control changes, source departure and copies. LKI cannot make an absent subject
available for counter placement. No new replacement-order, simultaneous-damage
or cost-payment mechanism is added.
