### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse boundary

Top-level permanent `TriggerA(event, body)` now accepts:

- `WhenAPermanentEntersTheBattlefield(IsCardtype(Land))`.
- `WhenAPlayerPutsAPermanentOnTheBattlefield(AnyPlayer, IsLandType(type))`,
  where type is one bare Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain or Forest symbol.

Event/filter envelopes must be tuples of the declared arity. Other types,
collections, restricted actors, unknown/nonbasic subtypes, tuple-spelled references
and malformed declarations remain rejected. Existing source-entry adapters keep
their behavior. No general TriggerI, entry replacement or counter-payment support.

Private compiler signature:
`compileLandEntryTrigger(event, body Node, ctx scope) (optionFactory, error)`.
Both forms provide a typed `Trigger_ThatPermanent` only in their body. The actor
form additionally provides typed `Trigger_ThatPlayer`; a plain land-entry event
does not invent an actor. Sibling abilities cannot read either declaration.
`landEntryEventPlan{playerName string}` keeps declaration identity nonzero-sized;
`instanceBindings.entryActors` builds a fresh PlayerBinding for each factory.
Existing permanent-event plans build fresh PermanentBindings. No global result
slot or chosen state is stored in a compiler plan.

Engine API: `LandEnters().WithPermanent(binding *PermanentBinding)` returns the
existing landEntersPattern builder. It captures the exact entering incarnation
before trigger placement and composes with WithActor and WithController. Nil,
empty-name, duplicate and unbound declarations fail definition validation.
The typed capture uses existing eventPermanentCapture/capturedPermanent,
WhenEvent, trigger snapshots, retention, stack copies and clone services.

RON spelling/scope stay in ron. Reusable event identity stays in mage.
Existing LandEnters type/subtype matching, known-actor check and native zone
entry dispatcher are reused. Source lifecycle, APNAP placement, current/LKI
information reads, phasing, source-aware damage and prevention, transactional
casting and native land-play legality remain engine-owned. Ankh reads the land's
current controller at resolution, or its exact incarnation's retained controller
when absent; actor capture does not freeze that read. Return cannot replace old
information. Actions need the original present incarnation. A phase cycle retains
identity and does not create entry events. Chants save the actual entry actor,
which can differ from owner/controller and can differ from a copied trigger's
controller. Unknown setup actors do not trigger the actor form.

registry or runtime declaration panic. No existing caller changes or DSL removal.

### Exact shapes, contracts and dependencies

Engine API: `PutCounterOnMatchingCost(core.CounterType, PermanentFilter) Cost`.
It places one counter on a matching permanent currently controlled by the payer.
Zero filter accepts any permanent; the source can pay. Queries are pure.
Preparation copies the cost and locks a candidate's ID and incarnation. Commit
rechecks live presence, control and filter membership before resources are spent.
Departure/return invalidates the saved choice; phasing suspends it; a phase cycle
preserves it. Invalid/stale chooser objects fail. Selection is not targeting;
shroud and summoning sickness do not prohibit payment. The source need not remain
present when another object pays. Nested alternatives preserve the locked choice.

RON resolving action-sequence envelope:
`PlayerMayCost(payer, PutCounters([ACounterOfTypeOnAPermanent(counter,
And([IsCardtype(Creature), ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(payer))]))]))`.
Implicit `MayCost` uses `You`. The two filter parts can appear in either order;
there must be exactly one creature type and one controller clause. The same
bound player expression must supply the payer and control clause. Existing
permanent counter types are accepted. One adjacent nonempty `If`/`Unless` body
with `CostWasPaid`/`CostWasntPaid` stays with its payment. Existing spell,
activation, mode and trigger action-list contexts apply. No announcement cost,
static, replacement-operation or entry-operation context is added. Plural
instructions, other filters/counts/controllers and escaping result reads reject
at compilation. The complete FEM records need only the explicit event-player form.

Reuse: `IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`, `playerReferencePlan`/`instanceBindings`, saved
land-entry actors, `capturedPermanent`, payment preparation and full-cost
preflight, definition validation, `AddCountersWithReplacement`, affected-player
replacement selection, stack copying and game cloning. A modified type, doubled
amount or prevented placement still counts as payment (CR 118.11–12). No new
counter, target, damage, event, zone, timing or replacement dispatcher exists.
Each branch keeps its own result; no global last-action slot is introduced.
The single-object placement shape introduces no simultaneous collection action.

### Exact shapes, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `EachBeginCombat` and `YourBeginCombat`, both `stepPattern` values
that implement `TurnStepPattern`. They match `EvtBeginCombat`; the latter adds
`EventPlayerIsController` at detection. Existing `At`, `TurnStepBegins` and
`AtNext` work through the shared service. Delayed patterns retain their original
controller and trigger once. Native scheduling supplies the event; skipped
combats emit none, and extra combats emit separate events.

RON permanent-source rule:
`TriggerA(AtTheBeginningOfCombatDuringAPlayersTurn(players), actions)`, with
exactly bare `AnyPlayer` or `SinglePlayer(You)`. Existing action-list and target
contexts apply. `Trigger_ThatPlayer` is a local typed step-player reference,
separate from `You`. Factory calls build fresh `PlayerBinding` objects; each
pending event saves its own player. Controller-only matching uses control at
detection. Departure, return, phasing, control change and ability removal after
detection cannot change saved players/controllers. Copies retain event players
and use their own controller; clones retain independent pending state.

Immediate temporary permanent layer effects in this body can use bare
`UntilEndOfCombat`. Nested delayed-step bodies do not inherit the permission.
Effects use the original source incarnation; absent or phased objects cannot
receive a bonus. A phase cycle preserves identity. Control changes do not end a
resolved bonus. The existing end-combat endpoint removes the bonus. Malformed
arity/kinds, other player filters, unbound or escaping step players and unsupported
durations reject at compilation. No `TriggerI`, RON delayed combat-start spelling,
static/entry/cost/replacement context or installed temporary trigger is added.

Reuse: `compileBoundStepTrigger`, `stepEventPlan`, `instanceBindings`,
`TurnStepBegins`, `WhenEvent`, `BindPlayer`/`FromPlayer`, `stepPattern`,
`EventPlayerIsController`, pending-event captures, APNAP placement, typed source
references, continuous modifications, end-combat cleanup, stack copying and
`Game.Clone`. No new event dispatcher, scratch slot or game-state subsystem exists.
No payment or replacement behavior changes; cost rollback, damage replacement
ordering and simultaneous damage are not new contracts in this slice.

### Exact supported shapes and reuse

`compileCombatPairFilter` accepts bare `IsCreatureType(subtype)` or a one-argument
`And` list with one required creature subtype. An explicit
`IsCardtype(Creature)` can also occur once. The positive subtype adds `IsCreature`
as well as `HasSubType`; a noncreature cannot match it. Subtype declarations use
`ValidateSubtypeFamily(SubtypeCreature, ...)`. Known subtypes from another family
are rejected; the existing engine permits unlisted creature subtype names.
One excluded creature subtype and one established color condition remain legal.

A conjunction also accepts one `ToughnessIs(comparison(Integer(n)))`, where
comparison is exactly `EqualTo`, `LessThanOrEqualTo`, or `GreaterThanOrEqualTo`.
It must contain the explicit creature type or a positive creature subtype.
`compileFixedToughnessFilter` supplies the established pure current-toughness
queries. Duplicate predicate kinds, wrong arity/kinds, wrong subtype families,
X/dynamic values, other comparisons, empty conjunctions and unsupported nested
forms remain compilation errors. No other filter context is broadened.

`WhenACreatureBlocksACreature(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent|HostPermanent), filter)`
and `WhenACreatureBecomesBlockedByACreature(...)`, plus their existing exact
same-subject/filter two-direction `Or` union. Host references require an Aura.
Existing typed opponent names and lexical scopes are unchanged. Grouped
one-or-more events remain rejected, so Soldier is not lowered to per-pair triggers.

Filters read final current characteristics at event detection (CR 509.3f).
Later subtype/toughness/attachment/control changes cannot recheck the condition

trigger. Returned opponents are new objects; phased opponents cannot receive
actions. No reusable engine behavior was missing, so engine code is unchanged.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine APIs:

- `GrantTriggeredAbility(PermanentRef, *GenericTriggered) StaticRule`.
- `GrantEachTriggeredAbility(PermanentSet, *GenericTriggered) StaticRule`.

The donor context selects live recipients in layer 6. The granted prototype must
have a declared event or turn-step pattern and function on the battlefield.
Definition validation checks its entire expression graph in a fresh binding
scope, including body, event captures and target declarations. Nil subjects,
sets, triggers or effects; unbound reads; undeclared targets; opaque legacy
patterns; and zone-source declarations are rejected. Definitions follow the
existing immutable-declaration convention.

Each recipient gets a separate ability object. Its UUID derives from the grant
identity and both donor/recipient incarnations. Layer passes and control changes
keep the UUID; returned objects receive new identities. Phasing suspends the
grant and preserves its identity. A host grant follows the live attachment.
Source suppression and recipient ability removal use normal layer order.
Pending triggers keep the recipient incarnation and controller from detection
and survive grant removal. Clones retain separate resolution frames and effects.

RON supported shapes:

- `PermanentLayerEffect(HostPermanent,
  [AddAbility([TriggerA(event, body)])])`, in an Aura declaration.
- `EachPermanentLayerEffect(filter,
  [AddAbility([TriggerA(event, body)])])`, using the existing static permanent
  filter contract, including controller conjunctions and source exclusion.
- `event` is exactly
  `AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(SinglePlayer(You))`.

There must be one modification and one granted ability. Other events, selectors,
source/target subjects and combined modifications remain rejected. The body uses
existing resolving actions and adjacent payments in a fresh recipient permanent
scope. `You` means the trigger controller; `ThisPermanent` means the recipient.
`Trigger_ThatPlayer` is produced by its own upkeep event. Targets declared inside
the body are local. Donor attachment, X, choices, targets and event/payment
results cannot cross into this scope.

`compileBoundStepAbility` extracts the existing step builder; old callers keep
`compileBoundStepTriggerWithCondition` and unchanged behavior. Engine reuse:
`grantRecipientSet`, typed `PermanentSet`/`PermanentRef`, `Static`, printed
ability lifecycle, `WhenEvent`/`At`, event capture, APNAP placement, target and
source incarnation capture, `IfPaid`/`UnlessPaid`, payment transactions,
destruction/regeneration, sacrifice, stack copying and `Game.Clone`.
No replacement, zone, payment or parallel trigger subsystem is introduced.

Energy Flux uses sacrifice, which ignores regeneration/indestructibility but
requires its resolving controller to control the subject. Tabernacle uses
destruction, which permits regeneration and indestructibility. A copied trigger
with another controller can destroy the original recipient but cannot sacrifice
it without control. Farmstead's independent life action still occurs after
recipient departure when its payment succeeds. Separate upkeep triggers are
separate operations; no simultaneous destruction/sacrifice batch is invented.
No new LKI information read or replacement ordering is established.

### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse boundary

RON permanent-rule declarations support exactly:

- `EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer, [PlaysWithHandRevealed])`
- `EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer, [PlaysWithTopOfLibraryRevealed])`

Both selectors and operations must be symbols, and the list must contain one
operation. Other selectors, operation tuples, extra arguments, combined
operations, `PlayerEffect`, resolving actions, costs, and instant/sorcery static
rules remain rejected. `compileAllPlayerRule` dispatches these two operations;
existing all-player untap limits retain `compilePlayerUntapLimit`. Existing
inventory roles already classify these descendants as `player_rule_operation`.

Engine signatures:

- `RevealAllHands() StaticRule`
- `RevealAllLibraryTops() StaticRule`
- `(*Game).IsHandRevealed(uuid.UUID) bool`
- `(*GameRules).IsHandRevealed(uuid.UUID) bool`
- `(*GameRules).AddRevealedHand(uuid.UUID)` registers one per-cycle flag.

Library rules reuse `RevealTopCardsOfAllLibraries()` and existing
`IsTopCardRevealed` / `RevealTopN`. Hand state belongs to `GameRules` and resets
with each layer pass. Both static rules use `mage.Static`, battlefield source
checks and the printed-ability lifecycle. Every factory creates its own ability
and effect state; there are no target/choice/result bindings in these shapes.
The global selector refers to all players, independent of source control.
Phasing/departure and source ability removal suspend the rule. Phase-in/new
entry or expired suppression restores it. Multiple sources preserve the rule
when one leaves. World state checks can remove an older source.

`cloneGameRules` copies both visibility maps. `maps.Clone` preserves nil maps,
so inactive visibility adds no clone allocation. Active maps remain independent
before and after subsequent layer passes. `snapshotPlayer` reads the public-hand
flag and shows current contents; the debug display option is unchanged. Public
visibility does not move cards, grant casting/playing permission, create reveal
history, or change library order. Library announcement timing and object-visit
services are unchanged; no intermediate library announcement display or
library-target binding is added by this slice. LKI, target legality, APNAP,
replacement ordering and simultaneous actions do not add contracts here because
these declarations perform no such operations. Casting continues to use normal
transactional payment and stack resolution.

### Exact supported shapes, scope and reuse

`PermanentDealsDamage(source, amount, recipient)` now lowers singular typed
recipients through `compileReferencedPermanentDamage`:

- `source`: a bound `compilePermanentRef` source, Aura host, singular target or
  event reference. Each reference retains its existing declaration scope.
- `recipient`: `Permanent(typed-ref)`, `Player(typed-ref)`, or a bound bare
  `Ref_AnyTarget` / `Ref_TargetPlayerOrPermanent`.
- `amount`: existing `compileInstanceValue` forms. Explicit player recipients
  retain the existing damage-recipient value scope.

Lowering is `DealDamageFrom(DamageSourceOf(source), recipient, amount)`.
The existing collection and legacy bare target contexts retain their adapters;
this slice does not broaden plural or multiple-packet damage sources. Spells,
modes, activations and event bodies use existing local reference validation;
source reads require the corresponding permanent context. Invalid arity,
malformed declarations and unbound/incompatible references remain errors.

`WhenAPermanentBecomesTapped(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent))` lowers to
`BecomesTapped(This)`. A body-local `sourceTapped` scope makes
`Trigger_ThatPermanent` read that source. It uses the engine's captured source
incarnation instead of introducing another mutable binding. The existing
`SinglePermanent(HostPermanent)` path retains its own captured host binding.
Factories create separate action targets and event declarations. Engine stack
frames preserve copied/retargeted targets and cloned pending effects.

The engine owns damage-source characteristics/controller, source LKI, recipient
legality, power reads, prevention/replacement processing, mana production,
transactional costs, trigger placement and state-based actions. Tracker's two
actions are sequential; each reads power when it runs, and state-based actions
wait until resolution completes. They are not a simultaneous batch. The target
is the second damage source, so its lifelink uses its current controller. Source
departure/return and phasing use existing exact source information; absent
recipients receive no damage. Collection replacement ordering is unchanged.

City's tap transition can come from its mana ability or another tap action.
Mana is immediate; damage waits for trigger resolution. Repeated tapping of an
already tapped object and land entry do not create a transition. Pending triggers
retain their detection controller and original source after control changes,
phasing or return. Copies use their copy controller as usual. No global
last-action slot, parallel damage system or runtime declaration panic is added.

### Contract, exact signatures, and reuse

`MustCost(DestroyPermanent(ref))/1` followed immediately by `If/2` or `Unless/2`
with symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` and a nonempty action list is
supported in existing resolving spell, activation, trigger and delayed action
sequences. `ref` must already bind a permanent in that lexical context. All four
branch polarities are supported. Invalid arity, unbound or incompatible refs,
unbound results, separated producers/continuations, optional destruction costs,
activation destruction costs and `IfElse` remain rejected.

The RON spelling here means "destroyed this way", as the actual Oracle records
require; it does not add a destruction cost to the mandatory-sacrifice engine
contract. `ron` owns grammar, lexical validation and lowering. The engine owns
incarnation-aware destruction, replacement application, LKI, damage, targets,
delayed reference capture, copies, clones and definition validation.

Reuse: `DestroyWithResult`, `DestroyedThisWayInto`, `BindNumber`, `FromNumber`,
`IfPositive`, `SubtractValues`, `Sequence`, and the existing typed permanent
reference plans. Each build creates a fresh result binding; its source-position
name distinguishes nested declarations. A zero result reverses branch polarity
through `1 - result`. Each pair is closed over its own producer and consumer;
there is no global result slot. The existing engine writes zero when destruction
fails and one when it destroys the original object. Regeneration,
indestructibility, phasing, departure and return cannot produce stale success.

Local `data/LEG.json` and `data/4ED.json` confirm Cosmic Horror's actual
"destroyed this way" text. LEG data confirms Infinite Authority's two delays and
original enchanted creature counter recipient. Relevant rules read: CR 118.12,
603.7a/c/e, 608.2b/c, 701.8a-c and 701.19a-c. No source defect is corrected;
existing unrelated source concerns remain. All twelve RON hashes are unchanged,
so no vocabulary source snapshot refresh is needed.

### Supported signatures, contexts and reuse

Engine API: `ChooseAtResolution(player PlayerRef, options ...ResolutionOption)
ResolvingEffect`; each option has `Label string`, `Body ResolvingEffect`, optional
`When StateCondition`. Options are copied at construction. Conditions supply
choice legality and are read at resolution with source incarnation/controller.
Zero available options or an absent player do nothing; one option needs no
prompt; multiple options use `Player.ChooseMode`. Invalid answers select the
first available option. The selected body receives the existing EffectContext.
Every body and condition is validated. Branch results cannot validate reads in
another branch or after the choice. No selected index is stored in a declaration.

RON `ChooseAnAction/1` accepts at least two alternatives, each a one-action list:
`PutCounters([ACounterOfTypeOnPermanent(PTCounter(p,t), Ref_TargetPermanent)])`.
The target is declared outside the choice and uses the existing typed target
binding. Coordinates must name a supported counter. Other actions, subjects,
plural instructions, target declarations and replacement-operation contexts are
not added. This is a complete counter-choice shape, not general action choice.

RON `ChooseAnAbility/1` accepts at least two distinct existing temporary keywords
and an adjacent `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3` continuation. That list must
contain `AddAbilityVariable(TheChosenAbility)/1`. The reference must be bare and
is bound only in that continuation. Existing supported modifications can share
the list. Subjects and durations keep their existing contracts. Each fixed
branch lowers one typed keyword; there is no game-time choice binding or global
last-action slot. Missing/separated continuations, escaped/incompatible reads,
duplicate options, malformed keywords and parameterized rampage reject.

Both forms operate in supported resolving sequences. Ordinary spell, activation,
trigger and modal target bindings have definition evidence; real activations and
an ordinary upkeep trigger have gameplay evidence. No new static, entry, cost or
replacement-operation context is accepted. Modal spell/ability announcement
selection remains with its current service. Resolution copies choose separately.

Reused services: typed PermanentRef/PlayerRef, per-factory instanceBindings,
EffectContext and target group captures, Sequence, AddCountersTo, current P/T
counter types, DiscardCost(1), total-payment transaction and hand visits,
GrantKeywordModification, ModifyPT, existing durations, layered ability removal,
stack copies, clone frames, replacement pipelines and native cleanup. The engine
adds only typed resolution dispatch. No LKI, combat, simultaneous-operation or
replacement-order policy is changed.

- `IntersectPermanents(sets ...PermanentSet) PermanentSet`
- `AttachmentsOn(hosts PermanentSet) PermanentSet`
- `PermanentsControlledByPlayers(players PlayerSet, filter PermanentFilter) PermanentSet`

Union/intersection copy the operand slice, resolve typed children in the current
EffectContext and select each live incarnation once in battlefield order.
Attachments use current host membership and the attachment's saved host
incarnation. Host control is independent of attachment control. Player-set
controllers use existing `OpponentsOf(You)`. No selected state is stored in any
declaration. Empty compositions, nil operands and unbound nested player reads
fail definition validation. Queries make no choices or resource changes.

RON `PutEachPermanentIntoItsOwnersHand/1`, `DestroyEachPermanent/1` and
`DestroyEachPermanentNoRegen/1` now share recursive contextual collection lowering:
nonempty `And([filters])/1`, `Or([filters])/1`, characteristic leaves from the
existing permanent-filter grammar, `OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(ref))/1`,
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(ref))/1`, `ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)/1`,
and `AttachedToAPermanent(host-filter)/1`. Player references must be bound in
the current resolving scope. Ownership and control stay local to Boolean operands;
repeated operands are valid and cannot repeat members. Each instruction reads its
own current membership. New incarnations can enter untargeted collections; LKI
cannot restore absent members. Targets retain existing identity/legality rules.
This establishes resolving spell and activation gameplay; existing return tests
retain typed player target reads. It adds no static, entry, cost or replacement
operation context. Other action families retain their existing filter adapters.

Permanent target `OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))/1` uses `TargetYouOwn` and
existing conjunction options, including `TargetYouControl`. Other target owner
references and contextual owner disjunctions reject. Copies use their own stack
controller. No new target service or retargeting policy is introduced.

Reused: per-factory instanceBindings and typed player/target references;
PermanentsOwnedBy, PermanentsControlledBy, MatchingPermanents, OpponentsOf;
ReturnEachToHand, DestroyEach, DestroyEachWithoutRegeneration; shared zone and
batch pipelines, target legality, payment transactions, attachment incarnation,
phasing, combat state, stack copies and Game.Clone. There are no RON executors
for reusable rules. Replacement ordering and regeneration policy are unchanged.

### Exact contract, context and reuse boundary

Engine type: `ManaActivationPayment [AnyColor + 1]int`. New optional fields:
`ManaTap.ActivationPayment *ManaActivationPayment` and
`ManaTap.SourceIncarnation uuid.UUID`. Internal source discovery records the
incarnation; every solver-produced action saves its payment colors by value.

`SolveMana(ManaSolverInputs) (*ManaSolution, error)` and `CanSolveMana` now search
all legal color allocations for each supported source's activation cost, rather
than paying the first legal allocation. Generic, colored and supported hybrid
pips and current mana conversions use the existing pool candidate and legality
services. Equivalent allocations are deduplicated. Spell-restricted mana cannot
pay ability costs. Zero costs have one empty allocation. Queries do not spend
mana, activate sources, consume RNG or ask for choices.

`ManaSystem.ActivatePlannedManaSource` rechecks source incarnation, current
controller, tap legality, ability, productions, reduced cost and saved payment.
An invalid payment fails before spending or tapping. It executes the selected
colors and retains the existing production, event, bonus and activation-history
services. A departed/returned source cannot execute its prior discovered plan;
a phased source is unavailable, and a phase cycle retains incarnation. Clones
can execute a plan independently. Nil payment and zero incarnation preserve
legacy caller behavior. Existing sequential direct `ApplyManaSolution` behavior
and the casting/activation payment transaction boundary are unchanged.

RON signatures and contexts are unchanged. The complete existing spell, permanent
entry and activation forms for Celestial Prism, Apprentice Wizard and Fire Sprites
still lower through `ron`; reusable payment behavior stays in `mage`. Static,
entry-choice, replacement, loop and delayed-binding contexts are not widened.

semantics are unchanged. No partial converter adapter is enabled: Farrelite Priest
and Initiates of the Ebon Hand still reject with the original history/planning

### Exact signatures, contexts and ownership

Engine API: `TriggeredAbilityModification(PermanentRef, *GenericTriggered)
ContinuousModification`; `HasRampage PermanentFilter`. Trigger grants reuse
`layerModification`, `capturedModification`, `composedLayerEffect`, the existing
static-grant installation service and `grantedTriggerDefinition` validation.
The outer subject keeps its resolving/static scope. The granted trigger uses an
independent permanent-source and binding scope, including when a spell supplies
the grant. Outer targets and casting facts cannot enter that body. Nil, legacy,
zone-source and unbound declarations reject before gameplay.

Each duration installation captures recipient incarnation and a separate grant
UUID. Every layer pass builds a fresh ability object with the same UUID and the
recipient's current controller. Prototypes remain immutable. Separate grants
remain separate; phasing preserves identity and suspends application; returned
objects do not receive old grants. Static use derives stable UUIDs through the
existing donor/recipient/modification identity service. Grant/removal timestamps,
pending-trigger survival, copied stack objects, target frames, APNAP and cloned
state remain owned by their shared engine services. No LKI restores an absent
recipient. No replacement or simultaneous-operation policy changes.

RON: `Rampage(n)/1`, with a bare nonnegative integer, inside
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, [AddAbility([abilities...])], duration)`
and inside `ChooseAnAbility([abilities...])/1` followed immediately by
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, [AddAbilityVariable(TheChosenAbility)],
duration)`. Existing subjects and durations retain their typed contracts.
Supported resolving contexts include spells, activations and ordinary triggers.
The choice remains lexical to its adjacent continuation. Different rampage
amounts are distinct choices; identical options reject. Other keyword grants keep
the existing Attr service. `HasAbility(AnyRampage)/1` and
`DoesntHaveAbility(AnyRampage)/1` use a bare ability-class symbol in permanent
filters. Rapid Fire checks current abilities after its first-strike instruction.
Static RON rampage grants, rampage removal and other parameterized abilities are
not added. Existing printed rampage declarations remain unchanged.

RON constructs the declared becomes-blocked pattern and shared RampageEffect;
the engine owns blocking detection, source identity, pending triggers, bonus
calculation, layer execution and duration expiry. This reuses exact rampage
behavior rather than adding a second executor. All selected records agree with

### Exact contract, reuse and remaining contexts

New engine signature:
`PreventNextDamageFromPermanent(subject PermanentRef, recipient PlayerRef,
filter PermanentFilter) ResolvingEffect`.

Installation resolves typed references in the existing frame, requires a live
matching source, and captures its incarnation and recipient. Nil, unbound and
undeclared references reject during definition validation. A zero filter permits
all permanent sources. Each damage event rechecks current source properties or
the retained departure/phase view for the exact incarnation. Missing source
information cannot fall back to a returned card. Nonmatching sources, zero
amounts and other recipients do not consume the shield. Cleanup removes it.

The existing `sourcePreventionReplacement` owns consumption and cloning.
`damageFilterSource`, typed target bindings and the shared resolution frame own
identity and retained information. The batch pipeline groups matching packets
from the captured source to the saved player as one use. Affected-player ordering
remains in the shared replacement service; another effect that prevents the whole
event leaves this shield unused. Independent installations and copied activations
keep independent consumption. Legacy `AddSourcePrevention` callers retain UUID
behavior and do not opt into captured batch grouping.

RON spelling, supported signatures and contexts are unchanged. Complete RON
source selection remains rejected. The new effect can serve typed permanent
references in resolving engine bodies; it does not select sources, install from
an absent permanent, support a spell source, follow a spell onto the battlefield,
or collect objects referred to by pending stack/replacement/delayed effects or
face-up command-zone objects. Those contracts are required before the seven
cards can be enabled. Generic filter callbacks must use the supplied permanent.
The existing engine's unpreventable-damage attribute applies to a permanent
recipient; this player-recipient slice introduces no rule for unpreventable
player damage or damage from an unpreventable source.

### Exact supported context and engine reuse

No RON spelling or compiler signature changes. Existing engine
`Activate(Costs(ManaPayment(...)), AddMana(...))` and unconditional nested mana
sequences can enter automatic planning without a tap cost. The reduced fixed
mana-only cost must consume at least the fixed output's total units. Pure fixed
mana bodies use the existing production adapters and concrete production choices.
X costs, turn activation limits, arbitrary activation conditions, targets,
non-mana costs and mixed bodies remain excluded from automatic conversion
planning. Explicit activation remains available through its existing services.

`manaSourceAbility.Repeatable` is private planning metadata. `ManaSystem` discovers
conversions on tapped or summoning-sick creatures, while tap-cost sources keep
their existing restrictions. The solver tracks tap availability separately from
repeatable use, keeps exact color payments for every activation, and uses bounded
pool states to terminate reversible cycles without an arbitrary search limit.
Its relaxation can advertise a repeated output color up to the pool's finite
bound. It compares preservation score before activation count rather than using
the old source-count weight, which could choose a worse score on a long repeated
path. Tap-only symmetry pruning remains active; conversion sources keep separate
availability so a used tap cannot hide another source's unused tap.

`ActivatePlannedManaSource` reuses current cost, controller, presence, timing,
activation restriction and captured incarnation checks. Only tap-cost execution
taps, receives tap bonuses and emits tapped-for-mana events. Conversion produces
mana immediately and fires a mana ability-activation event. The shared total-cost
transaction owns casting rollback. Hypothetical mana and X bounds do not count
conversions as new mana. Existing APIs/callers remain; no parallel payment system,
new target/choice/replacement/LKI contract, card-name branch or fallback was added.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

No new public engine API or RON spelling. Nonmodal `Activated`/supported
`ActivatedWithModifiers` contexts can compile an `ActionList` containing fixed
`AddMana(ManaProduceW|ManaProduceU|ManaProduceB|ManaProduceR|ManaProduceG|ManaProduceC)`
and `If(TimesThisAbilityHasBeenActivatedThisTurnIs(GreaterThanOrEqualTo(Integer(n))),
[CreateFutureTrigger(event, ActionList(...))])`. The threshold must be nonnegative,
branches must be nonempty, and existing delayed-step restrictions apply.
The enclosing activation supplies a fresh `ActivationHistoryBinding` per factory.
Immediate history-branch actions, conditional production, any-color production,
extra immediate actions, modal history and enclosing-history reads inside delayed
bodies remain rejected. Both real consumers use `PayMana([ManaCostGeneric(1)])`,
threshold four and a next-end-step sacrifice of `ThisPermanent`.

Engine discovery accepts fixed concrete-color production plus history branches
bound to that same ability, containing only untargeted, nonmodal `AtNext`
instructions or nonempty sequences/composites of those instructions. Deferred
bodies cannot alter current payment. The existing fixed-cost bounds, source
legality, exact payments, finite search and non-tap restrictions still apply.
X, non-mana costs, activation limits and arbitrary activation conditions remain
outside automatic non-tap conversion planning. Explicit activation retains its
existing cost/timing behavior. These restrictions do not remove current callers.

Private `manaSourceAbility.ResolveBody` selects full immediate resolution rather
than inserting production alone. Planned execution pays the saved cost, records
one activation, emits one activation event before resolution, and runs the original
body through `resolveStackObject`. Fixed output is not added twice. Tap bonuses
remain separate. The activation-event flag now reflects whether the source was
tapped, matching explicit activation; a non-tap conversion emits no tap event.

Reuse: `ActivationHistoryBinding`, `markActivatedInGame`, `IfActivationsAtLeast`,
`AtNext`, captured delayed bodies, incarnation references, the normal immediate
resolution frame, `ManaSystem`, saved activation payments, finite mana search,
`TurnTrackers.Clone`, cleanup and the total-cost transaction. Queries do not
execute bodies. Speculative payment runs in the transaction's game clone.

last-action state, game-time declaration panic or partial production registry.

### Exact supported shapes and reuse boundary

Engine constructor: `AttachedPermanentDies() creatureDiesPattern`, where the
private result implements `EventPattern` and exposes the existing death-pattern
capture methods. It matches an attached permanent of any type leaving the
battlefield for a graveyard. `AttachedCreatureDies()` keeps its creature filter.
The existing attachment-incarnation predicate, zone batch, look-back detection,
`WithController`, `WithOwner`, `WithToughness`, `WithPermanent` and `WithCard`
captures are reused. The change also gives generic patterns accurate definition
text. No existing caller or export is removed.

RON rule: `TriggerA(WhenAPermanentDies(SinglePermanent(HostPermanent)), body)`
on an Aura. Its body uses the normal resolving action-list/target declaration
service. Every factory builds its own typed binding declarations:

- `ControllerOfDeadPermanent` and `OwnerOfDeadPermanent`: event-time player facts.
- `ToughnessOfDeadPermanent`: event-time number.
- `Trigger_ThatPermanent`: departing permanent incarnation for information and
  damage-source reads; it cannot restore a departed object for actions.
- `Trigger_ThatGraveyardCard`: first graveyard visit of that host.

Callable reference symbols, malformed arities, non-Aura hosts and reads outside
this host-death body are rejected. Existing source-death and general filtered
contexts do not acquire these new bindings. Existing supported player, permanent
and graveyard actions use them through the typed reference services.

RON action: `DeadGuestPermanentDealsDamage(value, recipient)` in the host-death
resolving body. It lowers to
`DealDamageFrom(DamageSourceOf(This), recipient, value)`. The original Aura is
the source, not the dying creature. Supported instance values and existing
singular typed damage recipients are reused. The action declares no target.
It does not enable replacement operations or arbitrary graveyard Aura return.

Dependencies: phase-0 scope/instance support, typed event bindings, attachment
incarnations, look-back departure snapshots, graveyard visits, typed permanent
source damage and the shared replacement pipeline. `ron` owns spelling, scopes,
diagnostics and lowering. `mage` owns the reusable generic death-pattern API.
The implement-engine skill supplied the engine workflow. No removed card skill,
Go-card requirement, card-name branch, fallback, skipped rule, game-time declaration
panic, global action slot or partial production registry is used.

### Exact supported shapes, dependencies and engine reuse

Engine API:

The existing exact-count cost gains a source-inclusion flag. Existing

RON activation cost shapes, including nested activation-cost `And` lists:

through the existing simultaneous batch before any tap event is sent. No LKI can
restore an absent payment object. Control, filter, tap, phasing and incarnation
changes invalidate locked choices before other resources are spent.

total-cost transactions, captured incarnations and simultaneous tap events.

### Supported signatures, contexts and reuse

- `ActivatedWithModifiers(cost, actions, OtherPlayersMayActivate(AnyPlayer))`.
  One bare AnyPlayer symbol is required. The modifier is allowed in nested
  `And([...])` modifier lists, with ordinary action bodies and `Modal_ChooseOne`.
  Duplicate permissions, wrong arity, tuple/foreign/unbound player selectors,
  `OnlyPlayerMayActivate`, rule/action/cost placements and the separate
  conditional-mana context remain declaration errors.
- Each factory constructs its own action with `mage.WithAnyPlayerMay()`.
  Both players can activate; the activator pays, chooses modes/targets and
  controls the stack ability. Resolving You and target-control restrictions
  use that player. Timing, source presence/phasing, per-source limits and target
  legality still apply. No per-game last-action storage is introduced.
- Reuses ActionDefinition permissions, native transactional payment,

  the ability controller. Copies have their own controllers; clones retain
  isolated pending state. No engine API/state or replacement-order changes.

  player_filter even when the surrounding record still rejects.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Engine API: `PayOrElse(player PlayerRef, costs CostGroup, paid, unpaid
ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`. It extends the existing private
unlessPaidEffect and total-cost transaction, preserving IfPaid, UnlessPaid and
mandatory callers. One offer and one commit select exactly one branch. Failed
or declined payment selects unpaid; an absent payer selects neither. Explicit
zero costs still require acceptance. Both branches contribute effect properties.
Validation checks both bodies and keeps assignments inside each branch. No
global outcome, new payment service or legacy selector bridge is used.

RON action-sequence context:
`MayCost(PayMana([...]))` or `PlayerMayCost(typed-player, PayMana([...]))`, adjacent
to `IfElse(CostWasPaid|CostWasntPaid, [actions], [actions])`. Exact arities are
1/2 for payment and 3 for continuation. Both conditions are bare symbols; both
lists are nonempty. Each branch may contain another supported pair. Fixed
mana, including zero, is supported. X, mandatory and nonmana payments in this
three-argument continuation remain errors. Other conditions, detached result
reads, intervening actions, unbound references and malformed lists reject.
Factories build private cost/body objects and use existing instanceBindings.

RON temporary keyword collection context:
`CreateEachPermanentLayerEffectUntil(contextual-collection,
[AddAbility([temporary-keywords])], UntilEndOfTurn)`. Multiple nonempty keyword
lists use the existing temporary keyword grammar. Mixed P/T and keyword bodies
and other durations remain errors. Existing P/T lowering is preserved.
Contextual collection queries now include `IsBlockingAttacker(typed-permanent)`
and `IsBlockedByDefender(typed-permanent)` in nonempty recursive And/Or sets.
They reuse BlockersOf, BlockedAttackersOf, UnionPermanents and
IntersectPermanents. Grants reuse GrantEachKeyword and Until; membership is
captured at resolution under CR 611.2c. LKI cannot restore a combat pair.
Departure, phasing and control changes remove current combat membership
(CR 506.4). A recipient's later departure ends the grant; phase cycles preserve
captured identity and cleanup ends the grant. Source departure after installation
does not end it. No replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation service is
changed; native first-strike combat damage remains the engine's service.

### TDD and card-to-test mappings

Engine tests first failed for undefined PayOrElse. RON tests first failed at
Spitting Slug's unsupported adjacent IfElse and the same synthetic nested shape.
Implementation then passed those semantic boundaries. Test fixture corrections:
ExecuteBlockers resolves native triggers immediately, so native payment resources
must be ready before declaration; pending timing tests use saved native event
contexts instead. A control-change expectation was corrected using CR 506.4.
A shroud test initially called a nonexistent GrantKeyword signature and was
corrected to the existing base attribute API. These were fixture errors, not
source defects or environment failures.

Two old rejection boundaries now assert support: full Slug compilation and

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

RON supports one `Targeted` declaration:
`TargetAbility(And([ActivatedAbility, AbilityOfASource(IsCardtype(type))]))`.
And takes one two-member list; the two operands can appear in either order.
ActivatedAbility must be a bare symbol. AbilityOfASource and IsCardtype each take
one argument; the latter uses the existing card-type grammar. Other ability and
source filter forms remain errors. `Ref_TargetAbility` is a singular typed
reference local to the rule. `CounterAbility(Ref_TargetAbility)` takes one
argument; `ControllerOfAbility(Ref_TargetAbility)` is a typed player reference.
It can supply the payer of existing PlayerMayCost/Unless or If continuations.
Delayed, missing, malformed, incompatible and cross-rule reads are rejected.
Per-factory maps connect the immutable plan to a fresh target declaration.

Engine API:
- `AbilityRef` extends StackObjectRef with the ability role.
- `DeclareActivatedAbilityTarget(name string, sourceType core.CardType) *AbilityTargetBinding`.
- `ControllerOfAbility(ability AbilityRef) PlayerRef`.
- `CounterAbility(ability AbilityRef) ResolvingEffect`.

Native battlefield and graveyard activation paths mark stack objects as
activated. Triggered abilities and spells are excluded; mana abilities do not
supply a stack target (CR 605.3b). A final failing contract test found that the
existing graveyard activation path stacked mana abilities. It now reuses
canProduceMana and resolveStackObject for immediate resolution, preserving
nonmana stacking and the existing costs and timing restrictions. Copies and game clones retain the kind.
The target ID is the ability's stack object ID, never the source permanent ID.
Multiple activations/copies from one source therefore remain distinct.

Source type checks reuse readPermanentInformation and the existing incarnation,
phase-information and LKI services. Live characteristics can change target
legality; an absent or phased source uses retained information for its original
incarnation. A returned source cannot supply the old ability's type (CR 113.7a,
400.7 and 608.2b). Graveyard activations retain their visit and an independent
card snapshot before payment. Current cards in that visit supply current type;
self-exile and later source movement do not erase retained type. Source queries
make no choices and mutate no state.

ControllerOfAbility reads the live stack object's controller, including copied
abilities. Source control changes do not change the payer. An absent ability
supplies no player. CounterAbility uses counterReferencedEffect and
CounterStackObject, with an ability-specific text label. The original Counter
caller remains compatible. Countering leaves the source alone and does not
refund paid costs (CR 701.6a–b). Shared targets perform announcement checks,
resolution rechecks, copy retargeting and clone-isolated choices. Existing
optional payment transactions handle Ayesha's one white mana and rollback.
No replacement ordering, APNAP or simultaneous-operation contract changes.

### Exact shapes, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Supported on permanent definitions:
`TriggerA(WhenAPermanentLeavesTheBattlefield(SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)), body)`.
The event and SinglePermanent each take one argument; the source is a bare
ThisPermanent. Other event subjects, Aura hosts and arbitrary permanent filters
remain rejected. `Trigger_ThatPermanent` is a singular typed source reference
only in this rule's body. It lowers to the engine's source reference, which keeps
its captured incarnation; no new global event/result slot is introduced. It does
not grant destination-zone card access. Separate rules cannot borrow it.

The event lowers to `WhenEvent(LeavesBattlefield(This), ...)`, with a fresh
trigger per factory. Shared native leave-zone detection captures pre-movement
abilities/controller and source incarnation/LKI (CR 603.6c, 603.10a, 400.7,
608.2h). Departure after control change uses the departing controller. A later
return cannot replace retained source characteristics. Phasing supplies no
leave event (CR 702.26d). Pending events and copied triggers remain independent.

`Exile([EachPermanent(collection)], [])` now accepts existing contextual
collections in resolving actions: filters, nonempty recursive And/Or,
controller/owner selections, combat pairs and attachments. A root declared
Ref_TargetPermanents keeps its existing per-instance typed target set. Unbound
sets, invalid filters and modifiers fail compilation. The exile adapter preserves
that target-set branch locally; the shared contextual compiler and unrelated
destroy/return/layer callers are unchanged. Final review removed an initial
shared-helper extension that had also advanced Volcanic Eruption's destroy
adapter. Its unrelated gap remains unchanged in the final code.

Engine reuse: `LeavesBattlefield`, `DealDamageEach`, `PermanentDamageRecipients`,
source incarnation/LKI, `ExileEach`/`ExilePermanents`, contextual `PermanentSet`
queries, `AtNext(YourUpkeep, ...)`, live battlefield counts and `CreateTokenCopies`.
Goblin Shrine's damage uses one recipient batch and old-source damage information.
Hazezon's delayed count reads the saved player's current lands at resolution;
leaving before the entry trigger resolves does not cancel it (CR 603.7b/e).
Departure exile selects every live Sand Warrior at resolution; it is neither
linked to a creator nor limited to tokens. The engine performs one exile batch.
No new APNAP, replacement ordering, cost or zone service is added.

AnyPlayer or `SinglePlayer(You)` with a bare You and exactly one argument.
Existing action-list/target compilation supplies body support independently.
Other player selectors, malformed constructors and instant/sorcery rule contexts
remain rejected. `Trigger_ThatPlayer` is a singular typed player reference only
inside that rule's body; another ability cannot borrow it.

with EachDrawStep and fresh BindPlayer/instanceBindings for each factory.
SinglePlayer(You) adds EventPlayerIsController, exactly as the existing
intervening-if draw adapter does. The engine has no YourDrawStep export, so no
new engine API is introduced merely for that spelling. No mutable chosen state,
global result slot, card-name branch, fallback or partial production registry
is added. Existing TriggerI code remains unchanged.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

Supported RON activation modifier forms:
`OnlyPlayerMayActivate(OwnerOfPermanent(ref))` and
`OnlyPlayerMayActivate(ControllerOfPermanent(ref))`, with one bare
`ThisPermanent` or an Aura's `HostPermanent` reference. Ordinary and modal
`ActivatedWithModifiers` bodies and nested modifier `And` lists are supported.
Duplicate/conflicting permissions reject, regardless of nesting or order.

constructors, costs/actions/top-level rules, and conditional-mana activation
contexts are not added. Source owner/controller and host owner/controller
combinations all have engine gameplay tests.

New engine APIs:
`PlayerIsPermanentOwner(PermanentRef) StateCondition`;
`PlayerIsPermanentController(PermanentRef) StateCondition`.
They compare StateContext.ControllerID with live owner/controller information.
They accept This and AttachedPermanent; declaration validation rejects nil,
target and saved-binding subjects without a game-time declaration panic.
Reuse resolveStatePermanent for source presence, phasing, source incarnation
and the saved attachment incarnation. Unknown players, absent/phased sources,
and absent/phased/stale hosts fail. LKI cannot grant permission. Control and
attachment changes affect subsequent checks; returned objects do not restore
an old attachment or captured state context. Pure reads make no choices and
store no mutable state.

RON owns spelling, arity, scope and diagnostics. It combines the engine
conditions with WithAnyPlayerMay and WithActivationStateCondition. Each
factory builds a fresh ordinary/modal action and uses existing independent
target declarations. Payment, mode/target choice, stack control and resolving
You belong to the eligible activator. Timing, limits and target legality remain
in force. Copies and resolution do not recheck activation permission.
CR 602.2/2a/2b/5, 113.8, 400.7 and 702.26b/d support these contracts.
No new LKI, replacement ordering, APNAP, simultaneous-operation or mana-solver
contract is claimed; no damage/cost/zone/stack service is changed.

### Supported shapes, contexts and engine boundary

Engine APIs:
- `SkipNextUntaps(subject PermanentRef, count int) ResolvingEffect` accepts a
  nonnegative fixed count. Zero has no effect. Installation requires a live,
  phased-in original incarnation. Saved information cannot restore an absent
  subject. Control changes alter the applicable player; phasing preserves the
  count; departure clears it. Each actual controller untap consumes one step,
  even for an untapped object or overlapping prohibition. Skipped steps do not
  consume it. Other untaps remain legal and do not consume it.
- `SkipNextUntapEach(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect` resolves membership
  once, verifies live incarnations and installs one-step restrictions. Later
  membership changes cannot add recipients. It has mass/detriment metadata.

TurnSystem stores the maximum remaining count because all overlapping
restrictions count the same future steps. Repeated applications do not add
steps, and a one-step restriction cannot shorten a two-step one. Existing
SkipNextUntap callers and player-captured SkipNextUntapOf retain their behavior.
The original allocation-aware map clone helper preserves clone cost and
isolation. Departure removal, current-controller untap consumption, native
phase-in, restriction decision snapshots and simultaneous untap are reused.
No new zone, LKI, cost, damage, event or replacement system is introduced.

RON actions:
- `PermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextNumberUntaps(ref, Integer(n))/2`:
  n is a nonnegative integer literal; ref uses compilePermanentRef and fresh
  instanceBindings. Dynamic values and new binding producers remain rejected.
- `EachPermanentDoesntUntapDuringControllersNextUntap(filter)/1`: contextual
  collection queries, supported property/player/relation/attachment filters and
  nonempty nested And/Or. Unsupported collection references remain rejected.

These are resolving actions, including ordinary spell/activation/trigger bodies
and existing scoped action sequences. They are not top-level static rules,
costs or entry operations. This slice directly verifies source, target and

### Exact supported shapes and boundary

Engine:
- `PayCountersOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, counter
  core.CounterType, count int, optional bool, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect)
  ResolvingEffect`: fixed nonnegative count, optional decision or mandatory
  payment, then one branch. A nil branch has no action.
- `PayChosenCountersOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, counter
  core.CounterType, result *NumberBinding, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect)
  ResolvingEffect`: optional count from zero through available counters; result
  exists only inside the paid branch. Nested results are separate and restored
  after the branch.

These use existing RemoveCountersCost / RemoveAnyCountersCost, shared choice
locking, prepareActionPaymentTransaction and commit. Original live incarnation
and phasing are checked before payment, after the may decision and at commit.
Absent/returned objects cannot use LKI to pay. Control changes preserve the
subject and resolving actor; copies pay anew; clones have separate state.
Counter transactions retain their existing atomic removal and rollback rules.
The new private result declaration makes paid-branch dominance visible to
engine definition validation, without exporting a new authoring function.
Existing generic IfPaid and activation counter-payment restrictions remain.

RON: resolving permanent-source action lists accept
`MayCost(RemoveCounters([instruction]))`,
`PlayerMayCost(payer, RemoveCounters([instruction]))`, and
`MustCost(RemoveCounters([instruction]))`, each followed immediately by
`If(condition, [actions])` or `Unless(condition, [actions])`.
Condition is the symbol CostWasPaid or CostWasntPaid. The action list is nonempty.
Fixed instruction signatures:
- `ACounterOfTypeFromPermanent(counter, ThisPermanent)/2`.
- `NumberCountersOfTypeFromPermanent(Integer(n), counter, ThisPermanent)/3`, n >= 0.
Optional chosen instruction:
- `AnyNumberOfCountersOfTypeFromPermanent(counter, ThisPermanent)/2`.
Its paid continuation can read the symbol TheNumberOfCountersRemovedThisWay.
Each payment/factory gets a fresh typed NumberBinding. RON spelling and scope
remain in ron; transactions and identity stay in mage. Spell sources, other
subjects, mandatory chosen amounts, dynamic fixed counts, multiple instructions
and IfElse continuations remain explicit errors. This is one complete supported
payment context, not support for every RemoveCounters form.

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

`PermanentRuleEffect(subject, [CantAttackUnlessCost(cost)])` accepts a live
`ThisPermanent` on a permanent or `HostPermanent` on an Aura. Exactly one
operation is required. The cost is `PayMana(list)` with fixed mana symbols or
`SacrificeNumberPermanents(Integer(n), filter)` with positive fixed n and an
existing validated sacrifice filter. The latter permits the attacker itself to
pay when it matches. X, other costs, combined costs, malformed arities, extra
operations, unbound references and target subjects remain compile errors.
Resolving, entry, temporary and conditional attack-payment contexts are not
added. Each factory builds a fresh cost. Inventory reads its operand as `cost`,
including nested descendants under rejected parents.

RON owns spelling, scope and validation. `SourceCantAttackUnlessPays` and
`AttachedCantAttackUnlessPays` register live attack costs. `PayAttackCosts`
aggregates current costs, reserves the attacker from mana activation, prepares
choices and commits one shared payment transaction. The attacker controller
pays, independently of the Aura controller. Current attachment, ability removal,
phasing and source departure govern the tax. Casting pays only the casting cost;
Leviathan's optional upkeep payment is separate from its attack payment.

Engine prerequisite: native `doDeclareAttackers` and search `ExecuteAttackers`
now use the private `attackerAfterPayment` query after payment. Presence, original
incarnation and current declaring-player control are required by CR 508.1k.
The current pointer replaces the old pointer. A sacrificed or phased source,
a returned card, or a control-changed source cannot become an attacker or produce
attack events/history through stale information. Successful payment remains
paid if its source leaves. No new cost, zone, damage, replacement or LKI service
is introduced. This does not claim general multi-attacker declaration rollback.

### Exact supported signatures and ownership

Resolving actions:

- `CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPermanentLeavesTheBattlefield(SinglePermanent(ref)),
  ActionList(actions), UntilEndOfTurn)`.
- `CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPermanentDies(SinglePermanent(ref)),
  ActionList(actions), UntilEndOfTurn)`.

`ref` uses the existing bound singular permanent references. The nonempty body
uses existing delayed-action restrictions and outer instance bindings. Supported
spell/mode, activation, trigger and nested delayed action contexts inherit their
existing scope; this event introduces no event bindings, targets or modes.
Wrong arity, unbound/incompatible reads, other events/durations, tuple duration,
plural/filter subjects, empty bodies and new body targets remain compile errors.
RON owns spelling, validation, scope and inventory roles. The adapter lowers to
`WhenLeavesThisTurn` / `WhenDiesThisTurn` and `Sequence` with fresh bindings.

The engine keeps watched and source incarnations, installing controller, captured
outer targets and saved permanent/player/number bindings. Control and characteristic
changes preserve identity. Phasing does not trigger departure. Returned objects
cannot replace captured subjects. Source ability removal does not cancel an
installed delay. Cleanup removes subscriptions while pending triggers can resolve.
War Barge forbids regeneration for its destruction; Sandals permits regeneration.
Subscriptions install only at resolution, and absent/phased subjects install none.

Engine prerequisite: `exileInsteadOfGraveyardReplacement.Replace` previously
removed the permanent and called `ExileCard`, which sent no battlefield leave
event. It now uses the shared battlefield exile operation through private
`Game.exilePermanent(perm, exiledBy)`. `ExilePermanent` delegates to that helper
with no exile source. The replacement preserves its exile source. The normal
zone-change event and simultaneous former-battlefield snapshot now reach leave
subscriptions; death subscriptions and creature-death counts stay unchanged.
No public API change, new replacement order, parallel event service or batching
service is introduced.

replacement fixture uses destruction to exercise the replacement pipeline.
Additional synthetic fixtures needed explicit ownership and an Aura subtype;
these setup corrections did not change their behavior assertions.

branch, fallback, skipped record or partial production registry was used.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Activation modifiers:

- `ActivateOnlyIf(PlayerPassesFilter(You,
  NumCardsInHandIs(EqualTo(Integer(n)))))`, with nonnegative integer literal `n`.
- `ActivateOnlyIf(PermanentPassesFilter(subject,
  ControlledSinceBeginningOfMostRecentTurn))`, with a bare predicate and bare
  `ThisPermanent`, or `HostPermanent` in an Aura declaration.

These forms work with ordinary and modal activated bodies and existing nested
modifier `And` lists. They lower to `WithActivationStateCondition` with
`ControllerHandSizeIs(n)` and `ControlledSinceTurnStart(subject)`. Other hand
comparisons, dynamic values, player references, malformed arities, tuple predicate
spellings, target/event reads and non-Aura hosts remain declaration errors.
Resolving and static property filters do not gain these predicates.
Inventory assigns the hand predicate/comparison/value/literal roles below the
activation player filter, including descendants of unsupported parents.
RON owns spelling, role validation and lowering. The engine owns pure checks,
transactional payment, live identity, source/host presence, current controller,
mana planning and classification, stack copies, delayed capture and cloning.
Restrictions do not repeat during resolution or stack copying.

Engine prerequisite: the old `Permanent.ControlledSinceTurnStart` compared its
control-gain stamp with the current global turn, incorrectly granting permission
on the opponent's next turn. It now compares with
`TurnReader.MostRecentTurnStart(uuid.UUID) int`. `TurnSystem` owns a fixed
`[2]int` of observed starts; cloning copies it by value. Native `RunTurn` records
the active turn before step scheduling, and direct `RunStepWithPriority` records
it before step actions. Untap can be skipped without losing the start. Skipped
turns in `Run` do not execute these paths. Public setup setters save the prior
active turn before changing turn/player. The pure reader returns the current
turn for the active player, stored start for the inactive player, and zero for
unknown players or missing history. Entry and control changes reuse their
existing control-gain stamps; phase cycles retain them, and returned cards get
new incarnations and stamps. Haste does not bypass an explicit control gate.
Existing `WithControlledSinceTurnStart`, typed conditions and mana planning share
the corrected read. No new damage, payment, zone or replacement system is added.

### Exact supported contexts, dependencies and reuse boundary

The supported engine APIs are:

```go
func (g *Game) CaptureSpellDamageSource(stackID uuid.UUID) DamageSource
func DamageSourceOfSpell(spell StackObjectRef) DamageSourceRef
func SnapshotDamageSource(source DamageSourceRef, binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect
func (s DamageSource) StackID() uuid.UUID
func (s DamageSource) SameObject(other DamageSource) bool
```

Live raw capture accepts a spell's stack ID, including a permanent spell, and
rejects absent IDs, ordinary card IDs and abilities. Typed reads accept a
`*SpellTargetBinding` or `FromSpell` saved spell reference; ability references
and nil/missing declarations are invalid definitions. Information uses the
current controller, owner, effective colors and card types. A snapshot writes
an independent source value in the existing per-resolution
`DamageSourceBinding` map. Failed capture writes an empty value. Reads after
capture retain information through departure, copies and cloning without
reviving a departed live spell reference.

`ResolutionState.Begin` saves the resolving spell's exact stack ID after the
stack pop; `Clear` removes it and `Clone` copies it. Resolving source capture
uses that context and its own color override, rather than a UUID lookup that
could refer to another object. Shared damage actions, source-result bindings
and pending damage-event captures retain the value, including simultaneous
packets, amount changes, prevention and redirection. Definition inspection uses
the damage-source role for `This` and validates producer dominance and reference
kind. It does not require a battlefield source for a resolving spell snapshot.

`SameObject` compares card ID plus exact stack ID or permanent incarnation.
Unknown identities cannot match. A copied spell and a later cast remain
separate. Phasing retains a permanent incarnation; return changes it. A spell
and the permanent it becomes remain distinct under CR 400.7. A future chosen
source shield must add the special CR 609.7a link explicitly. Synthetic legacy
resolution contexts without stack IDs keep their old information behavior but
cannot prove exact spell identity.

This is an engine-contract gap, not a missing spelling adapter or data fix.
RON keeps declaration spelling and scopes; no RON shape is newly accepted.
`ChooseADamageSource`, its binding and its continuation remain strict errors.
The reusable APIs use existing spell references, source bindings, definition
validation, source snapshots, damage/replacement execution and clone services.
No second state map, global last-action result, card-name branch, factory
fallback, startup change or partial production registry is added. Permanent-only
history queries and existing UUID-based prevention callers retain their contracts.
Rules read: CR 120.7, 400.7, 609.7a-c and 615.2-9; the existing replacement
contracts cover CR 616.1 and rechecks.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

Engine APIs:

- `AttackedThisTurn PermanentFilter` and `DidntAttackThisTurn PermanentFilter`.
  They read successful declaration history for the exact permanent incarnation.
  They do not infer history from current combat status, tapped state or control.
- `TargetPlayerAttackedThisTurn() PlayerTargetOption`. It restricts the existing
  typed player target at announcement and resolution. It composes with
  `TargetOpponentOnly()` in either order and appears in definition metadata.
- Existing `HasAttackedThisTurnIncarnation(id, incarnation)` now retains every
  attacking incarnation during the turn. A later attack by a returned card
  cannot erase an earlier incarnation. Existing ID-only history and the latest
  incarnation archive for last-turn callers remain in place. Clone copies the
  additional map; final cleanup clears it with other turn history.

RON supports bare `AttackedThisTurn` and `DidntAttackThisTurn` in existing
permanent-filter contexts (including targets and battlefield collections) and
resolving `If(PermanentPassesFilter(reference, filter), [actions])`, including
nonempty `And`/`Or` and delayed bodies. References reuse `compilePermanentRef`
and `IfPermanentMatches`; current or retained information stays tied to the
original incarnation. Information cannot restore an absent/phased action target.

`TargetPlayer(AttackedThisTurn)` permits either player who declared an attack.
It keeps `Ref_TargetPlayer` in the existing per-instance environment. Bare
symbols are required; tuple/argument forms, negative player-target predicates,
unbound/incompatible references and unsupported contexts remain errors.
No new source intervening-if or static-condition context is introduced. Erg
Raiders remains rejected; accepting its first condition alone would not execute
its full record. Season of the Witch now reaches its exclusion-filter error.

The slice reuses both native attacker declaration paths, `TurnTrackers`, player
target legality, transactional casting payment, exact permanent information,
`AtNext` delayed capture, native destruction/regeneration/indestructible rules,
continuous bonuses and cleanup, spell/trigger copying, cloning and simultaneous
damage/prevention. No alternate rules service, card-name branch, global result
slot, Go fallback or partial production registry is introduced.

### Exact signatures, contexts and ownership

RON adds exactly
`PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent, [AllCreaturesMustBlockIt(filter)])` and
`PermanentRuleEffect(HostPermanent, [AllCreaturesMustBlockIt(filter)])` for a
properly declared Aura. The operation requires one argument and uses the
existing permanent-filter compiler. The subject must be the live source or
current host; unbound targets, non-Aura hosts, wrong filter/reference types,
malformed arguments and other contexts remain declaration errors.
The semantic inventory now assigns its argument the `permanent_filter` role.

Engine APIs:

- `AllCreaturesMustBlock(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter) ContinuousModification`.
  Existing `While` uses current source/host membership. Existing `Until` saves
  the recipient incarnation. The layer map resets on application and clones
  copy each filter slice. Each installation contributes an independent
  requirement. A separate Aura's rule survives host ability removal; source
  ability removal or phasing suspends its static rule. A returned host cannot
  inherit the old attachment. Nil and undeclared subjects fail validation.
- `(*Game).CompleteBlockAssignments(uuid.UUID, []BlockAssignment)
  []BlockAssignment`. Pure query; preserves legal maximum proposals and
  completes unmet requirements. Both declaration paths call the same planner
  before combat/history writes and final-pair events. Existing pairs remain
  fixed. Candidate pairs require the original attacking incarnation, a live
  untapped defending creature, existing restrictions/evasion/protection and
  landwalk legality. Duplicate pairs do not consume capacity. Normal,
  additional and unlimited capacity are shared across all requirements.
- `(*EffectManager).AddAllCreaturesMustBlock(uuid.UUID, PermanentFilter)` is
  the per-layer installation service. RON does not own assignment or storage.

The planner counts independent filtered and legacy attribute requirements,
including repeated copies. It maximizes the satisfied count under minimum
blocker restrictions, including menace. Band members share the resulting pairs
but use one declaration slot; direct declarations and indirect blocking are
separate, so an indirectly blocked member's evasion or minimum cannot forbid a
legal block of another member. The exact search has admissible bounds and lazy
subsets, with no partial-result cutoff. Complex combinations can still require
exponential work. Ordinary legal proposals with no unmet requirement avoid the
search. No new blocking-cost or player-choice service is claimed.

Reuse: existing typed references and factory bindings, `While`/`Until`, layer
capture, permanent incarnations, attachment legality, phasing, transactional
casting and targets, normal pair restrictions/protection/landwalk, band
propagation, combat damage/prevention and declaration-event snapshots. The
planner writes no history until a final declaration is committed. No new LKI
permission restores an absent object. No card-name branch, Go fallback, global
last-action slot, game-time declaration panic or partial production registry is
introduced. The former first-Lure redirection and two post-declaration helper
functions are replaced; a repository search found no remaining helper caller.

Rules: CR 400.7, 506.4, 509.1a–c/g–i, 611.3a–b, 702.22g–h, 702.26b–g and
702.111. LEA Lure and LEG Marble Priest local Oracle records agree with all
selected RON rules. No selected data correction is needed. The Gaea's Avenger
candidate mismatch is recorded above and left for its own slice. RON files are
unchanged; all twelve hashes match the vocabulary snapshot, so it is retained.

### Exact signatures, contexts and dependencies

Engine adds:

```go
func SetEachBasePowerToughness(subjects PermanentSet, power, toughness ResolutionValue) ContinuousModification
func AddEachCardType(subjects PermanentSet, kind core.CardType) ContinuousModification
```

These construct existing layer operations. `Until` captures members and values
before type application. Definition inspection rejects nil sets/values and
unsupported permanent types. Existing types, subtypes, colors and abilities
remain; Creature adds P/T identity. Layers 4 and 7b apply before bonuses, counters
and switches. The existing capture/clone/cleanup service retains incarnations;
control/subtype changes and phase cycles do not alter captured membership.
Phased-out members cannot join at resolution; later entries and returned
incarnations cannot inherit it. No separate state or executor is introduced.

RON resolving temporary contexts add:

- `CreateEachPermanentLayerEffectUntil(collection,
  [SetPT(PT(integer, integer)), AddCardtype(Creature)], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
  Exactly one fixed base pair and one Creature addition are required, in either
  order. Other/mixed operations, duplicate declarations, missing components and
  other durations remain errors. Collections reuse `compileContextualCollection`
  for typed controller/owner restrictions, intersections/unions and other
  already supported collection shapes. The existing keyword and bonus-only
  collection paths remain unchanged.
- `SetCardtypes([Artifact, Creature])` in
  `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3`, exactly those two types once each in either
  order. CR 205.1b requires preserving prior types for becoming an artifact
  creature, so this shape lowers to the shared singular type additions. Other
  type-setting lists remain errors; general type replacement is not implemented.
- `SetPowerAndToughnessBoth(value)` in the same singular temporary context.
  Uses `compileTemporaryValue`: integer, bound ValueX, subtraction, typed
  power/toughness reads with the existing information contract, and mana-value
  reads of the modified permanent. `ActionPermanent` is this subject, not a
  global result. Captured base values use the shared layer service. Unbound,
  incompatible or out-of-scope references fail compilation. Static, entry and
  cost contexts are not added.

### Exact supported shape, contexts and reuse

`Targeted([TargetPermanent(filter1), TargetPermanent(filter2), ...], actions)`
with two or more ordinary singular permanent declarations binds one-based
`Ref_TargetPermanent1`, `Ref_TargetPermanent2`, and subsequent names. Each plan
has a separate identity; each factory build maps each plan to a fresh
`PermanentTargetBinding`. Single-target callers retain their unnumbered binding.
The multiple-target body rejects the unnumbered alias, out-of-range/zero/leading
zero names, tuple references, incompatible player reads and mode-scope leaks.

Existing spell, activation, triggered and mode-local action contexts are
supported. Existing delayed bodies save numbered references independently.
Existing singular target filters/options are reused; this slice adds no new
filter spelling or dependent target relation. Empty lists, mixed declaration
kinds, plural groups, opponent choices and nested target declarations reject.
The shared singular adapter also rejects conflicting `You`/`Opponent` controller
restrictions during compilation, before they can cause a factory panic.

RON owns names, scope and lowering. Reused engine services are
`DeclarePermanentTarget`, `WithTargets`, fixed target declaration offsets,
announcement/payment transactions, resolution target legality, saved-reference
frames, `AtNext`, `PowerOfWithLKI`, temporary layers, native cleanup, stack copy
retargeting and game cloning. The same object can occur in separate groups when
it meets both filters (CR 601.2c). A partly illegal spell or ability still resolves
its legal actions; all-illegal targets prevent independent life gain too.
Return invalidates an announced incarnation; a phase cycle preserves it.
Copies retain separate target frames and can choose new targets per group.
Delayed reads preserve the exact information object's LKI after its departure;
a returned object with different power cannot replace it.

No engine rule, replacement ordering, simultaneous operation, cost service or
new LKI semantics is added. No RON action executes in the compiler. No fallback,
card-name branch, global last-action slot, partial production registry, definition
deletion, generator removal or DSL cleanup is introduced. Removal gates remain
unmet, and current callers remain intact.
