### Supported signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Both forms require two positional arguments:

- `TargetPermanentOfAPlayersChoice(permanentFilter, Opponent)`.
- `TargetPermanentOfAPlayersChoiceTheyControl(permanentFilter, Opponent)`.

The chooser is the bare `Opponent` symbol. The second form adds an opponent
control restriction; the first does not. Existing permanent target filters and
options are reused. Both work alone or with ordinary/opponent-chosen declarations
in numbered singular permanent groups. Single declarations bind
`Ref_TargetPermanent`; multiple declarations bind one-based numbered references.
Existing spell, activation, trigger and mode-local contexts remain available.
Factories create separate typed bindings per declaration and per card instance.

RON owns spelling, arity, scope, chooser validation, controller-conflict rejection
and lowering. Reuse: `DeclarePermanentTarget`, `TargetChosenByOpponent`,
`TargetOpponentControls`, `WithTargets`, declaration offsets, shared choice,
announcement/payment, resolution legality, incarnation and copy services.
Malformed arity, tuple chooser, unsupported player/event chooser, conflicting
controller filters, unbound references and incompatible scopes reject before
factory construction. `TargetPermanentOfPlayersChoice`, mixed target kinds and
plural target groups remain unsupported. Inventory classifies filter and chooser
operands below unsupported parents, including the unsupported player-choice
spelling; role reporting does not assert executable support.

Targets are chosen at announcement/trigger placement, before resolution. Their
legality uses the action controller and source, including hexproof; the chooser
does not change that context. Changed control is a resolution legality check for
`TheyControl`. A partly illegal action resolves its other legal targets; an
all-illegal action does not resolve independent life gain. Return invalidates the
saved incarnation; phasing makes it unavailable; a phase cycle preserves identity.
Separate word targets can name the same legal permanent. Copies use their own
controller's permission to change targets under CR 707.10c, without payment.

The modal activation tests exposed an existing engine gap: mode target gathering
already asks the opponent, then the ordinary announcement path asked again.
`activateAbilityByIndex` now skips the second opponent acquisition when the mode
has supplied targets. Validation and payment still run. Flat stack targets and
`ModalTargets` keep the first choice. The `implement-engine` skill was used for
this prerequisite fix; no card definition was changed. Engine API signatures are
unchanged. Rules evidence: CR 400.7, 601.2c/e/h, 602.2b, 602.3, 608.2b,
702.26b/d and 707.10c.

No LKI information query, replacement, simultaneous operation, or new cost rule
is added. Those services retain their existing contracts. No fallback, card-name
branch, global choice slot, game-time declaration panic or partial production
registry is introduced. Cutover/removal gates remain unmet; Go definitions,
generators and DSL callers are retained.

### Supported contract, dependencies and reuse

- `SinglePermanent(ref)/1`: a contextual collection operand using the existing
  scoped permanent reference plan (source, host, singular/numbered target or
  available event reference). Wrong arity, wrong type and unbound reads reject.

  tuple spelling and delayed plural reads reject.
- Nonempty `And([operands])/1` and `Or([operands])/1`: existing contextual
  intersection/union now accepts the typed reference operands alongside live
  filters, controller/owner collections, attachment sets and combat relations.
- `TapEachPermanent(collection)/1` and `UntapEachPermanent(collection)/1` now
  use `compileContextualCollection`, as do existing resolving return/destruction
  actions. Entry, cost, static and damage-set contexts are unchanged.

  existing `grantRecipientSet`; no parallel singleton evaluator is introduced.

  existing reference's current identity/legality checks. Per-factory target plans
  create separate declarations. No selected state is stored in the factory.

  relations and delayed captures own selection, deduplication and incarnation
  checks. Existing `TapEach`, `UntapEach`, return and destruction services own
  simultaneous batches and replacement behavior. Costs use existing transactions.
- Singular delayed references use the established capture service. Later shroud
  does not create a new target check. Source departure and phasing retain the
  original host relation; a returned Aura cannot redirect that relation to its
  new host. An absent/returned host cannot be restored as a live member by LKI.

### Exact supported contract and reuse boundary

New API:

- `ChooseDamageSourceFrom(player PlayerRef, sources []DamageSourceRef,
  binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
- Optional player interface
  `DamageSourceChooser.ChooseDamageSource(sources []DamageSource, g *Game) int`,
  which returns a zero-based option index.

Context: resolving actions over an explicit finite list of legal source
references. The service resolves the references at execution, removes missing
sources and exact duplicates in input order, then saves one source snapshot.
The calling rule owns legal-list enumeration and property filtering. Existing
current/LKI/saved reference semantics stay intact. Explicit referred sources can
retain departed/phased information. Separate permanent incarnations and spell
stack identities cannot be merged by card ID. Choice does not target objects.

Declarations reject empty source lists, nil references/player/binding, unnamed
bindings, undeclared target references, and reads before production. Runtime
absence clears the result without a choice. Invalid player answers choose the
first legal option, consistent with the existing required permanent choice.
Existing players use bounded numbered options with source names; typed players
receive independent snapshots. Input references are read before the output is
cleared, so valid input/output overlap works. The constructor copies the source
slice and stores no choice state. Chosen values use the existing resolution frame.

Reuses DamageSourceRef, DamageSource/SameObject, cloneDamageSource,
DamageSourceBinding/FromDamageSource, typed spell/permanent and saved references,
LKI, event capture, sequence execution, definition dominance/target validation,
player decisions, resolution frame restoration, stack copying and Game.Clone.
No alternate zone, identity, damage, replacement or cost subsystem is added.
Existing `Game.ChooseDamageSource` and its callers remain unchanged.

### Contract, signatures and ownership

Engine API:

- `DamageSourceFilter` (zero value permits any valid source), with
  `Match(DamageSource) bool`.
- `DamageSourceHasColor(core.Color) DamageSourceFilter` and
  `DamageSourceHasType(core.CardType) DamageSourceFilter`.
- `AllDamageSources(...DamageSourceFilter) DamageSourceFilter` and
  `AnyOfDamageSources(...DamageSourceFilter) DamageSourceFilter`.
- `ChooseDamageSourceMatchingFrom(PlayerRef, []DamageSourceRef,
  DamageSourceFilter, *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`.

Context: a resolving choice from an explicit complete legal list supplied by
the caller. The filter reads each reference's supplied information before the
existing required choice. Missing sources never match. Current references read
current properties, including stack color overrides and effective permanent
types. Saved/event references read saved information. No game lookup by card ID
can replace a retained source with a returned incarnation. Phasing and departure
retain the existing reference contract. Filters are pure and hold no game state.
Boolean declarations require nonempty operands and copy the caller's slice.
Definition validation rejects invalid colors/types and nested invalid filters.

The existing `ChooseDamageSourceFrom` delegates with the zero filter and keeps
its signature. Choice, exact deduplication, resolution frames, per-instance
bindings, clone snapshots, missing-player/result clearing, invalid-answer
fallback and legacy decisions reuse the existing service. No cost, damage,
replacement, zone, event or identity subsystem is duplicated or changed.

RON owns `compileChosenDamageSourceFilter` and declaration diagnostics.
`ChooseADamageSource/1` validates `AnyDamageSource` as a symbol, `IsColor/1`
(five colors), `IsCardtype/1` (existing six-type RON vocabulary), and recursive
nonempty `And([filters])/1` or `Or([filters])/1`. After filter validation, the
choice action still returns `unsupported action (ChooseADamageSource)`.
This is explicit prerequisite validation, not production execution support.
Inventory assigns nested filter/color/type roles below the unsupported action.
No partial card factory or registry is published.

and deferred; local ATQ Oracle confirms the discrepancy. Other recorded source
defects remain unchanged. RON hashes and vocabulary syntax are unchanged, so no
source-snapshot refresh is needed. No DSL function, Go card, generator or startup
caller is removed; the removal gate remains closed.

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `CombatDefendingPlayer() PlayerRef`. In combat between two players,
it resolves the current nonactive player, independent of effect controller and
whether attackers exist. Every combat step, including first-strike damage,
qualifies. Outside combat, without an active player, or without exactly two
players, it supplies no player. It has no mutable or captured state. Game clones
query their own current turn. The reference can supply a damage recipient through
the existing PlayerRef contract; no damage execution behavior changes.

`TargetControlledBy(PlayerRef) PermanentTargetOption` now accepts this reference
in addition to `You` and saved event players. Existing target enumeration and
resolution perform current control and normal protection/incarnation checks.
No new target selection, legality, combat or payment subsystem is added.

RON target-filter signatures:

- `ControlledByAPlayer(SpellDefendingPlayer)` and
  `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(SpellDefendingPlayer))`, in instant/sorcery
  `SpellActions` singular permanent targets, including modal and numbered
  singular target groups. These build `TargetControlledBy(CombatDefendingPlayer())`.
- `ControlledByAPlayer(DefendingPlayer)` and
  `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(DefendingPlayer))`, in source attack and
  unblocked-attack trigger target scopes. These use the existing per-factory
  `sourceCombatPlayerPlan`, `instanceBindings.defenders`, `WithDefendingPlayer`
  and saved event player. Each pending event has its own captured player.
- Nested `And` filters reuse the existing target-filter composition. Existing
  `ControlledByPlayer(Trigger_DefendingPlayer)`, `You`, and opponent target
  declarations are unchanged. Unsupported static, collection, resolving-player,
  activation, wrong-event and tuple-symbol contexts still reject.

The spell-target flag is lexical compiler state, not game state. Event targets
retain their saved defender after current-turn changes, source control changes,
source departure and copies. Live spell targets use the combat's nonactive
player. Ownership cannot replace control. LKI does not restore illegal or absent
targets; returned objects have a new incarnation. A phase cycle preserves the
original target identity. Copies retain their own targets/controllers and use
current ordinary targeting protection when retargeting. Costs remain in the
shared transaction; illegal targets and unpaid casting cannot spend mana.

No RON source, source hash, vocabulary syntax or card definition changes. No new
source defect was found. Avenger and the other previously recorded defects remain
separate. The vocabulary snapshot does not need a source refresh. Semantic
inventory now assigns a bare defending-player symbol beneath `ControlledByAPlayer`
the `player_reference` role. No support claim is inferred from that role.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

RON supports `TriggerI(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersUpkeep(AnyPlayer), condition,
actions)` and the same event with `SinglePlayer(You)`. Condition signatures:

- `PlayerPassesFilter(You, ControlsA(permanent_filter))` or the same with
  `Trigger_ThatPlayer`. The event player has one fresh `stepEventPlan` and
  `PlayerBinding` shared by condition and actions for each factory instance.
- `APlayerPassesFilter(Opponent,
  ControlsMorePermanentThanPlayer(You, permanent_filter))`.
- `APlayerPassesFilter(AnyPlayer, SinglePlayer(ThePlayerWithTheMostLife))`.

Filters reuse `compileStaticConditionFilter`, including its exact supported
nested conjunction/disjunction, counter and type/subtype/property forms.
The adapters add no static, resolving-action, activation, cost, entry or other
step condition context. Wrong arity, tuple symbols, empty logical filters,
unsupported player selectors and unbound/cross-rule reads remain compile errors.
Existing tapped-source upkeep conditions remain on their previous path.

Engine `PlayerControls(PlayerRef, PermanentFilter)` now accepts
`FromPlayer(binding)`, in addition to `You` and `ActivePlayer`. The private
`StateContext` player map supplies binding identity. `WithInterveningIf` reuses
`capturedTriggerTargetPlayers` to read event-pattern snapshots without executing
captures or changing the resolution frame. `IfState` reads the existing frame
populated by normal event captures. Missing bindings/players return false;
definition validation rejects missing producers. No generic game-state slot is
added. Distinct pending events, copied objects and clones retain separate frames.

New engine API: `OpponentControlsMoreThanYou(PermanentFilter) StateCondition`.
It compares current matching battlefield counts for the saved effect controller
and current opponent. Equal counts, missing controller or missing opponent return
false. It stores no state and makes no choices. Phased and departed permanents
supply no current control; ownership and LKI do not replace it.

`HasUniqueHighestLife`, `TurnStepBegins`, `EachUpkeep`/`YourUpkeep`,
`WithInterveningIf`, `PlayerControls`, existing capture/stack/copy/clone services,
and transactional casting are reused. Both condition boundaries read current
state; source departure, ability removal, control change or return cannot erase
an already pending trigger or replace its event player/controller. A tie fails
the highest-life condition. No new replacement, simultaneous-operation, cost,
targeting or zone-movement contract is introduced.

condition gap, with one clean consumer and two concrete downstream consumers.

### Exact contexts, signatures and engine reuse

RON supports these additional conditions in
`TriggerI(AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersEndStep(players), condition, actions)`:

- `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, IsUntapped)`.
- `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, DidntAttackThisTurn)`.
- `ACreatureOrPlaneswalkerDiedThisTurn(IsCardtype(Creature))`.

`players` retains the existing symbol `AnyPlayer` or `SinglePlayer(You)` shape.
The two source filters are symbols, not zero-argument tuples. Other subjects,
malformed arities, unbound references and death filters remain errors. This
slice adds no upkeep, static, activation, resolving-action, entry or cost context
for these condition signatures. Existing end-step conditions retain their path.
The semantic inventory now classifies the death condition's nested filter and
card type; role classification remains separate from support.

New engine APIs:

- `SourceAttackHistoryThisTurn(attacked bool) StateCondition` reads exact
  source-incarnation history. Without a capture it requires a live unphased
  source; with a capture it accepts original live/phased or retained departure
  identity. Unknown identity fails both variants. Departure, return, control
  changes and combat exit cannot substitute a new object's history. Direct
  insertion into combat does not record an attack declaration.
- `CreatureDiedThisTurnCondition() StateCondition` reads the shared current-turn
  creature death count, including tokens and either player's creatures.

The adapter reuses `SourceTappedStateWithLKI(false)`, `TurnStepBegins`,
`EachEndStep`/`YourEndStep`, `WithInterveningIf`, source incarnation captures,
per-instance event-player bindings, stack copy/clone frames, retained zone
information and `TurnTrackers`. Both boundaries read current state/history.
Cleanup clears history; native cleanup resolves pending stack objects before
that clear. Counter placement/removal, temporary bonuses and transactional costs
remain the existing services. Information does not permit actions on an absent
or phased source. Existing live-only source attack conditions remain unchanged.
No global action slot, parallel history system, game-time declaration panic,
card-name executor or partial production registry was introduced.

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse

Engine signatures:

- `DamageTakenThisTurn(subject PlayerRef) ResolutionValue`.
- `ArtifactDamageTakenThisTurn(subject PlayerRef) ResolutionValue`.

These pure values resolve the explicit player in the current frame and read the
existing `DamageTakenByPlayer` / `GetArtifactDamageTaken` services. Missing players
supply zero. Definition traversal checks references, including nil and unbound
bindings. Each application reads at resolution, not announcement. Life loss or
life gain does not change damage history. Actual damage after prevention and
redirection enters the shared tracker. Artifact classification uses the source's
types when damage occurs, including retained permanent and spell information.
Later control/type/departure/phasing changes cannot alter saved amounts. Clones
keep separate histories and native cleanup clears them.

RON signatures in existing resolving-value contexts:

- `DamageDealtToPlayerThisTurn(player)/1`.
- `DamageDealtToPlayerThisTurnByPermanents(player, IsCardtype(Artifact))/2`.

Both require tuples. `player` uses the existing typed player-reference compiler
and per-factory `instanceBindings`, including target, controller, action and
saved delayed references. The source filter is exactly `IsCardtype(Artifact)`;
other filters, malformed declarations and unbound/incompatible references remain
errors. Existing arithmetic supports `Twice` and compositions. No static, entry,
cost, announcement or arbitrary source-filter context is added.

Reuse includes `TurnTrackers`, actual damage execution, typed targets and player
references, stack copies/clone frames, `AtNext`, prevention/redirection ordering,
simultaneous damage and transactional casting. No new history store, zone system,
last-action slot, card-name executor, fallback or partial production registry is
introduced. Compiler spelling remains in `ron`; engine values have no RON names.

### Exact supported signatures, dependencies and reuse

Engine: `IncreaseSpellCostStatic(filter SpellPredicate, increase core.ManaCost,
controllerOnly bool) ContinuousEffect`.

The fixed mana vector supports nonnegative generic and W/U/B/R/G counts,
including zero. Declaration traversal rejects nil filters, negative counts,
X/stray XCount and hybrid declarations. The shared continuous-effect service
registers taxes per source incarnation, clears them each pass, and suppresses
printed taxes after ability removal. Payment rechecks presence/incarnation and
reads the live source controller. Phasing stops the tax; phase-in restores it.
A returned source cannot revive an old entry. Each tax applies once even when
several alternatives match; separate sources accumulate. Clone registration
slices are independent. Permanent spell copying reuses the engine's existing
separate static-source identities.

`modifySpellTotalCost` adds these mana vectors after existing increases and
before all reductions. Shared `addActionManaCost`, spell total-cost locking,
additional/alternate costs, announced X, mana planning and payment rollback
are reused. Generic reductions cannot erase colored requirements. Sacrificing
a tax source during payment does not change the locked total. A spell copied
on the stack pays nothing again. Activation and resolution-payment costs are
unchanged; this adds no replacement effect or alternate payment system.

RON permanent-definition contexts:

- `PlayerEffect(You, [IncreaseSpellCost(filter, PayMana(mana))])/2`.
- `EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer, [IncreaseSpellCost(filter, PayMana(mana))])/2`.
- `IncreaseSpellCost(filter, PayMana(mana))/2`, one operation per parent list.
- `mana` is the existing fixed generic and W/U/B/R/G symbol list; no X.
- `filter` uses `AnySpell`, nonland `IsCardtype(type)/1`, `IsColor(color)/1`
  for the five Magic colors, and nonempty nested `And(list)/1` or `Or(list)/1`.

Color lowering reuses `HasColorCardFilter`, including card color indicators.
The shared cost predicate compiler also permits that filter in the existing
static generic-reduction context. RON owns spelling, scope and diagnostics;
the engine owns registration, live source identity and total payment.
Each factory constructs fresh static effects. Other player scopes, dynamic
increases, nonmana tax payments, resolving durations, activation taxes and
other rule contexts remain rejected. Inventory assigns complete roles to the
new nested forms; it still labels gameplay support as unverified.

### Supported shapes, engine contracts and reuse

Permanent definition rule `ActivatedAbilityEffect(subject, operation)/2`:

  nonnegative integer literal. Other subjects, contexts and reduction lists
  remain errors. X increases, malformed shapes and unbound host reads reject.

Engine signatures:
`IncreaseActivationCostStatic(filter PermanentFilter, increase core.ManaCost)
ContinuousEffect`; `ReduceActivationCostStatic(subject PermanentRef, reduction,
minimum int) ContinuousEffect`.

The existing effect manager registers rules per source incarnation and clears
them each layer cycle. Queries require the live source, current filter match or
current typed attachment, and unsuppressed printed abilities. Sources and hosts
can have different controllers. Phasing, removal and return use existing exact
object services; LKI does not enable an absent static rule. Reattachment changes
the host. Each factory makes fresh static effects and independent card identities.
Rules slices are cloned independently.

The shared calculator combines mana components and announced X, adds increases
once, and then reduces generic mana. A minimum limits reductions without raising
zero costs. Colored mana remains required. Multiple sources stack. The existing
legacy reduction map/API is preserved. Ordinary ability affordability and the
locked payment transaction, native mana activation, and mana solver metadata use
the same total. Taxed native sources cannot use the free interchangeable-source
solver path. Copying stack abilities does not repeat payment. Spells and explicit
resolution-payment policies remain separate. Payment rollback, source reservation,
attachment legality and ability copying reuse existing services. No card-name
branch, fallback, parallel cost system, global result slot or partial production

### Established signatures, context and reuse

New API: `Game.CardPowerToughness(card Card) (power, toughness int)`.
A nil card returns zeroes. Live battlefield reads use current layer results;
phased objects use their retained results. Other reads evaluate inspectable count
CDAs against current nonphased battlefield membership. Spells use their current
controller, including copies with a different controller. Uncontrolled cards use
their owner in library, hand, graveyard, exile and outside zones. Queries do not
mutate printed P/T, make decisions, install effects or run layer passes.
This is a current-object query, not a saved-incarnation/LKI reference, and does
not add an announcement-time would-be-controller or general all-zone effect API.

Existing signatures are preserved:
`PTEqualsCount(PermanentFilter) ContinuousEffect`,
`PTEqualsControlledCount(PermanentFilter) ContinuousEffect`,
`ToughnessEqualsControlledCount(PermanentFilter) ContinuousEffect`.
Their count declarations are inspectable outside the battlefield. Zero filters
retain the existing match-all meaning. Copies retain expressions rather than a
frozen result. Source binding is per registration and incarnation, including
face-up registration and direct `AddContinuousEffect` callers. Bound effects are
cloned independently and cannot become active for returned sources.

The existing effect manager applies these expressions in layer 7a. The reset now
includes prior CDA values, preventing stale values after layer-6 ability removal.
Base overrides, bonuses, counters and switching retain their existing order.
Reuse: `CountBattlefield`, current permanent filters, owner/control/stack services,
printed static abilities, `CurrentPower`/`CurrentToughness`, copy definitions,
existing LKI and game cloning. Native visible hand/graveyard/exile snapshots use
the same query. No alternate zone store, rules execution in RON, card-name branch,
fallback, global result slot or partial production registry is added.

RON spelling and scope logic are unchanged. `CDA_Power(value)/1` and
`CDA_Toughness(value)/1` remain rejected in all production records. No incomplete
adapter is advertised. No cost, replacement-ordering, APNAP or simultaneous-action
rule changes are introduced; real spell regressions use their existing services.

insertion/removal and hand removal before re-entry; it exposed no engine failure.

### Exact declarations and reuse boundary

Supported only at the top level of a permanent creature's `Rules`:

- A single `CDA_Power(TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter))/1` paired
  with a single `CDA_Toughness(TheNumberOfPermanentsOnTheBattlefield(filter))/1`.
  Both values must have identical position-free ASTs. Pair order does not matter.
- A single toughness-only declaration with the same count shape and a
  `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` restriction.
- Nonempty `And/1` and `Or/1` filter lists; `IsNamed(NamedCard(string))/1` with
  a nonempty name; existing card-type, creature/land/enchantment-subtype, color
  and supertype filters, including their existing negative forms. Controller
  restrictions use only `You` and conjunctions; source-dependent disjunctions
  reject. Exclusion references, P/T/ability predicates and arbitrary values reject.

Paired declarations lower to one fresh `PTEqualsCount` or
`PTEqualsControlledCount` effect per factory call; controlled toughness-only
lowers to `ToughnessEqualsControlledCount`. RON owns declaration grouping,
position-free equality, role/context/filter validation and diagnostics.
The engine owns current nonphased membership, owner/current spell controller
queries, layer 7a, source incarnations, copies and clones. Static declarations
contain no chosen state or target binding. There is no game-time declaration
panic, fallback, card-name branch or global result slot.

Power-only, uncontrolled toughness-only, unequal count expressions, duplicate
axes, arithmetic, entry/payment results, noncreature declarations and CDA actions
inside spell/activation bodies remain errors. This is a complete supported
count context, not support for the entire CDA family. No new cost, event,
replacement or simultaneous-operation execution contract is introduced.
Existing set/modify/switch ordering remains covered by `TestCharacteristicPT*`;
real RON tests add counter/bonus/ability-removal and LKI evidence.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

New reusable engine signatures:

- `(*Game).LiveDamageSources() []DamageSource`.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromLiveObjects(player PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter,
  binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`.

The query returns current unphased battlefield permanents in battlefield order,
then live spells in stack insertion order. Lands and objects without damage
abilities qualify. Permanent spells and copies qualify; abilities do not qualify
as spells. Separate stack identities do not merge even if card IDs match.
Current layer results, controller/owner and color overrides are retained.
Shroud is irrelevant to a non-targeted choice. Each snapshot has separate card
data. Querying does not apply layers, change zones, spend resources or make a
player decision. It does not use a resolving source's LKI in place of a live
object. A returned permanent is a new selectable object.

The dynamic operation enumerates and filters at resolution. It reuses
`damageSourceChoice`, `DamageSourceFilter`, `DamageSourceChooser`, legacy
bounded numbered choices, `DamageSourceBinding`, `FromDamageSource` and the
existing resolution-frame clone service. Empty lists and absent players clear
only their output and make no choice. Invalid answers use the existing first
legal option fallback. Binding validation rejects invalid players/filters,
nil or unnamed outputs and reads before their producer. Independent bindings,
repeated choices, pending stack copies and game clones have separate results.
No compiler spelling or mutable chosen state is put in the engine declaration.

Acceptance cases were stated before implementation. Engine and RON tests first
failed because these APIs did not exist. A further face-down test failed because
the existing source snapshot exposed the underlying card name. The shared live
and LKI snapshot helper now supplies the face-down creature's visible card
characteristics, with no hidden name, color, subtype or printed keyword.
Rules: CR 120.7, 400.7, 609.7a, 702.26b, 708.2/708.2a. This does not add shield
property rechecks, replacement ordering, simultaneous-operation or payment rules.

Referred objects in stack objects, waiting replacement/prevention effects and
waiting delayed triggers, plus face-up command-zone objects, are deliberately
outside this API's declared source categories. They are missing engine
contracts, not missing RON spelling adapters. The eventual complete legal-list
service must combine those categories before the compiler accepts general
`ChooseADamageSource/1`. The RON filter adapter already exists and remains
validated in rejected records. No Go factory fallback or partial registry is
introduced. No RON sources change, so the vocabulary snapshot is not refreshed.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

New engine services:

- `BlockAnyNumber(subject PermanentRef) ContinuousModification`.
- `BlockEachAttacker(subject PermanentRef) ContinuousModification`.

Both use existing `layerModification`, captured permanent identity and `Until`.
They modify rules without adding abilities. The permission supplies unlimited
block capacity; the requirement supplies one independent requirement for each
attacking creature. Multiple installations accumulate requirements. The existing
maximum-requirement planner combines them with other requirements, capacity,
evasion, minimum blocker counts and attacking bands. Both blocker declaration
paths retain their shared planner. Layer passes reset computed rule maps; game
clones copy those maps for queries before the next pass. No parallel combat
solver or targeting service is added.

RON resolving shape:
`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(permanentRef, [operations...], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
The new list is nonempty and contains only bare `CantBeRegenerated`,
`CanBlockAnyNumberOfCreatures`, and `MustBlockEachAttacker` symbols. These lower
to the existing regeneration prohibition and new blocking rules. Source and
already declared permanent-target references use the existing lexical scope
and per-instance bindings. The adapter shares resolving action lowering;
real consumers exercise spell and activation contexts. Existing singleton
combat-rule shapes retain their restrictions. Other operation families, host
references, incompatible/unbound reads, malformed symbols, and other durations
remain rejected. Static, entry, cost and replacement contexts are not added.

Resolution captures the exact current recipient. An absent/phased or illegal
target receives no effect; no LKI enables actions on absent objects. Installed
rules retain identity through control changes and phase cycles. Source departure
and recipient ability removal do not erase them. Returned objects cannot inherit
an old installation. Copies and cloned games retain independent declarations
and resolutions. Cleanup removes the effects. Regeneration prohibition reuses
`GrantKeywordModification(..., CantRegenerate)` and the destruction replacement
check; creating shields remains legal and shields cannot replace prohibited
destruction. The slice does not add damage replacement ordering or payments;
existing targeting and atomic payment services are reused.

### Signatures, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

New engine APIs:

- `SkipUntapSteps() StaticRule`: use with `Static`. Submit a typed
  `beginUntapStepAction` through `ApplyReplacements` before starting the step.
  Replacement identity includes source incarnation and the runtime rule ID.
  The affected player selects competing replacements. Rechecks reject departed,
  phased or suppressed sources. A returned source's new ability can supply its
  own rule; it cannot restore a departed incarnation's replacement.
- `LimitUntapsDuringStepIf(filter PermanentFilter, maximum int,
  condition StateCondition) StaticRule`: extends existing `untapLimitRule` and
  `chooseStepUntaps`. Validate negative limits, nil conditions and invalid
  references at definition validation. Read current source context after phasing
  and layers and before selection; only true conditions contribute quotas.

RON permanent rule shape: `EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer, [SkipsUntapStep])`, with
one bare operation. Conditional shape:
`If(condition, [EachPlayerEffect(AnyPlayer,
[CantUntapMoreThanNumberPermanentsDuringTheirUntapStep(Integer(n), filter)])])`.
Reuse the existing static-condition grammar, typed source/Aura-host references,
nonnegative fixed limit and permanent filters. Winter Orb uses
`PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent, IsUntapped)`. Invalid/unbound/incompatible
references, malformed symbols, dynamic/negative limits, other player selectors,
mixed bodies and other conditional operations remain errors. Resolving actions,
costs and entry contexts gain no static player declaration.

Reuse `Static`, printed ability suppression, cycle replacements, affected-player
ordering/rechecks, `StateContext`, per-factory effect construction, effect clone
metadata, untap quotas, simultaneous untap, phasing, upkeep snapshots, optional
transactional mana payment and source sacrifice. No parallel turn schedule,
untap planner, zone service or global action-result state is added.

Stasis skips phasing and all untap-step actions. Stun counters, pending untap
restrictions and mana stay untouched by the skipped step. Upkeep still occurs.
Ordinary untap effects remain legal. Source control does not change either
all-player rule. Recipient ability removal does not remove a source's rule.
An Orb that starts tapped permits the complete unrestricted operation even if
it untaps during that operation. The next actual step reads its new state.
Each installation and cloned game retains its own source context.

A turn-start prerequisite was discovered during gameplay review: sickness was
cleared only inside `doUntap`. `clearTurnStartSickness` now runs in native step
execution, including skipped untap and turns that start at upkeep. It checks
current controller and `turnControlGained < CurrentTurn`, including phased
and face-down objects. New entries and current-turn control changes remain sick. Existing
turn-history setters remain read/record operations. Other existing untap callers
and legacy quota fields remain compatible. Rules consulted: CR 302.6, 500.11,
502.1–4, 503.1a, 611.3a–b, 614.10 and 614.10a.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

- `mage.IfPermanentMatchesElse(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter,
  matching, nonmatching ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `mage.UnlessPermanentMatches(subject PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter,
  body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

These are resolving effects with typed source, attachment, saved-permanent or
singular-target information references. They use the same private
`permanentInformationBranch` and `readPermanentInformation` as the existing
`IfPermanentMatches`. Existing callers retain their behavior and properties.
The predicate runs once at the instruction's position. Known information
selects exactly one alternative (or the known-nonmatch body). Missing information
runs neither body; it cannot satisfy negation. A zero filter matches known
information. Current information, phase snapshots and departure LKI retain
incarnation identity. Neither body can act on an absent or returned incarnation.
The selected body keeps the resolving controller and bindings, and propagates
errors through its surrounding sequence. New alternatives have no unconditional
AI shortcut properties.

Both alternative bodies are validated. Nil bodies, nil/unbound/unsupported
references and reads without a producer are definition errors. A producer in
one branch cannot supply another branch or a later outer instruction. A local
sequence can use its own producer. The existing definition visitor enforces
this without new global state or a separate binding service.

The compiler owns future `IfElse(PermanentPassesFilter(...), [...], [...])` and
`Unless(PermanentPassesFilter(...), [...])` spelling/scope adapters. They still
fail loading in this slice. Static conditions, combat membership, event checks,
control-history filters and optional-cost result branches do not gain support.
No rules are moved into `ron`. Existing stack legality, payment rollback,
copying, cloning, zone services and phasing are reused. No replacement order,
simultaneous operation, event or payment contract is changed.

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and reuse

- Resolving action lists accept
  `IfElse(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, propertyFilter), [matchingActions],
  [nonmatchingActions])` and
  `Unless(PermanentPassesFilter(subject, propertyFilter), [nonmatchingActions])`.
- Filters reuse `compileResolvingPropertyFilter`: existing fixed characteristic,
  keyword, counter, tapped and attack-history properties, with nonempty nested
  `And`/`Or`. Both branch bodies must be nonempty. Existing singular permanent
  references retain their source, attachment, target and event scope.
- The exact historical shape is
  `Unless(PermanentPassesFilter(subject,
  CameUnderControlOfPlayerThisTurn(playerRef)), [actions])`.
  `compilePlayerRef` supplies the typed, bound player. Other history shapes,
  static alternatives and combat-membership alternatives remain rejected.
- New engine API:
  `UnlessPermanentCameUnderControlThisTurn(subject PermanentRef,
  player PlayerRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

RON owns names, declaration checks and lowering. Reusable rules stay in mage.
Property alternatives use `IfPermanentMatchesElse` and `UnlessPermanentMatches`.
The history API uses the same `permanentInformationBranch`, information service
and definition visitor. It reads the original incarnation and selected player
once. Known nonmatches run the body; missing object or player information runs
no body. Each incarnation retains each player's latest control-acquisition turn.
Entry and actual final layer control changes record history. Haste, ability
removal and phasing do not supply or erase it. Losing control cannot erase an
earlier acquisition in the same turn. COW clones and departure/phase information
snapshots copy the history independently. A returned object starts fresh.
Existing most-recent-controller-turn permission checks retain their own field
and behavior; this query does not infer history from summoning sickness.

Each factory builds independent targets and effects. Both branches compile
through the existing action sequence service; payment continuations and their
results stay local. Nil/unbound engine references and malformed RON declarations
fail validation, before gameplay. Conditional mana activation remains rejected
until classification and solver planning support it. No game-time declaration
panic, shared last-action slot, card-name execution branch, fallback or partial
production registry was introduced.

Costs, legality, copies, targets, damage/prevention, end-step events, attack
history, cleanup and temporary layers reuse their existing engine services.
No new replacement ordering, simultaneous batch, or APNAP contract is introduced.
CR 400.7, 603.3a, 603.4–5, 608.2b/c/h/i, 611.2c and 702.26 supply identity,
controller, intervening-if, resolution information and phasing requirements.

requires current control. Local `data/ARN.json` Oracle text instead states:
“At the beginning of your end step, if this creature didn't attack this turn,
it deals 2 damage to you unless it came under your control this turn.”
The historical exception must survive loss of control after the trigger queues
(CR 603.3a, 603.5, 608.2i). A new acquisition followed by loss first failed the
new gameplay test. Both identical reprints now use the explicit
`CameUnderControlOfPlayerThisTurn(You)` predicate. Existing uses of
`NotControlledSinceBeginningOfTurn`, including Siren's Call, were not redefined.

### Exact contracts, contexts and dependencies

Engine APIs:

- `CantAttackMatchingThisTurn(filter PermanentFilter) ResolvingEffect`.
  Current matching permanents cannot be declared as attackers until cleanup.
- `MustAttackControlledThisTurn(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter)
  ResolvingEffect`. Resolve and save the player once; that player's current
  matching creatures attack if able until cleanup. Validate the typed player
  producer; nil and unbound target player declarations reject.

`turnAttackRule` uses the existing effect manager's independent source-exit,
end-of-turn and cloning services. It stores a player ID, filter and rule kind,
not current members or a global action result. Current properties and control
change membership. New and returned creatures can join. Phased-out objects
cannot attack. Source departure/control/phasing and recipient ability removal
do not remove the rule. A rule does not remove an existing attacker. Normal
and explicit declarations complete new live requirements before shared legality
and payment checks. Existing printed requirement behavior is preserved in each
path. An omitted creature with an attack cost is not added solely by this
resolving requirement; a proposed attacker uses the existing payment service.

RON supported forms in resolving action lists:

- `CreateEachPermanentRuleEffectUntil(filter, [CantAttack], UntilEndOfTurn)`;
  supported source-independent static filters, including nonempty logical

### Exact contracts and reuse boundary

Engine API: `WhenAttacksUnblockedThisTurn(subject PermanentRef,
body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`. Install only for a live, phased-in
subject. Save its incarnation, creator source and resolving controller. Match
legal unblocked-attacker events in each combat until cleanup. Subject control
changes and phase cycles retain identity; returned objects do not match. Source
phasing, departure, control and ability removal do not remove the subscription.
Pending bodies survive cleanup. Their typed information reads can use exact
LKI, while actions still require live objects. Copies use the copy controller.

`delayedPermanentEventEffect` shares the existing departure installation service;
`WhenDiesThisTurn` and `WhenLeavesThisTurn` retain their public signatures and
behavior. Matching an unblocked event requires a live creature and saved
incarnation. Explicit stale event incarnations cannot match. Unblocked events
now carry the attacker incarnation. Departure matching still uses existing LKI.

RON resolving form:
`CreateTriggerUntil(WhenACreatureAttacksAndIsntBlocked(SinglePermanent(ref)),
ActionList([actions...]), UntilEndOfTurn)`. Exactly three arguments, a bound
singular permanent subject, a nonempty action body, and the symbol duration.
Only existing supported body operations compile. No body target declaration is
created. `Trigger_ThatCreature` is body-local and resolves to the saved watched
incarnation, rather than the creator. `scope.unblockedCreature` remains separate
from the parent event, including `Trigger_ThatPermanent`. Instance construction
adds its own `PermanentBinding` while preserving parent bindings. Snapshot
and delayed frame capture retain each installation's references and X.

Reuse: `Snapshot`/`From`, `instanceBindings`, `compilePermanentRef`,
`compileActionSequence`, `capturedDelayedBody`, `TriggerSystem`,
`EvtAttacksUnblocked`, existing legal blocker commitment and event dispatch,
APNAP stack placement, stack copying, LKI, cost transactions and cleanup.
RON owns spelling, declaration checks, scopes and lowering. Engine owns event
matching and lifetime. Inventory walks delayed combat subjects and permanent
operands below unsupported bodies. No game-time declaration panic, global
last-action slot, card-name branch, Go fallback or partial production registry.
No DSL function or Go card definition is removed; runtime/removal gates remain
unmet and no deletion caller audit is claimed.

### Exact shape, engine contract and reuse

Engine API: `AssignsNoCombatDamage(subject PermanentRef)
ContinuousModification`. `Until` captures the resolved subject incarnation.
Source departure, subject control changes and ability removal do not end an
end-of-turn installation. Phasing preserves identity; returned objects do not
inherit the rule. Absent or phased subjects at installation receive no rule.
Cleanup expires it. The effect manager rebuilds an incarnation map each layer
pass and copies it for game clones.

All combat paths check assignment eligibility: ordinary/unblocked/blocked
attackers, blockers, trample with live or departed blockers, blocking bands,
and incoming/outgoing/unblocked attacking bands. Strike-step history is recorded
before suppression, including first/double strike. No suppressed packet reaches
the damage pipeline: no damage event, lifelink, shield consumption or replacement
choice results from that source. Unpreventable damage cannot bypass the rule.
Noncombat and incoming damage retain the existing behavior. Public
`Combat.DealsDamageInStep` and all existing callers remain compatible.

RON resolving form:
`CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(permanentRef, [AssignsNoCombatDamage],
UntilEndOfTurn)`. Exactly three positional arguments, one symbol operation and
one symbol duration. Bound source, target, host and supported event references
use `compilePermanentRef` and `instanceBindings`. Only this single-operation
shape is added; unknown/mixed operations and other durations reject. Engine
owns assignment, capture, identity and duration; RON owns spelling, scopes,
validation and lowering. No game-time declaration panic, global action slot,
card-name executor, fallback or partial production registry is added.

Reused services: permanent targets and snapshots, delayed captured frames,
`Until`, composed continuous effects, definition validation, effect-manager
layer passes, cloning, combat declarations, simultaneous damage, replacement
pipeline, activation/counter payment transactions and cleanup. Inventory already
walks the exact reference/operation/duration roles, so no inventory role change
is needed. No Go definitions or DSL functions are removed; the cutover/removal
gates remain unmet and no deletion caller audit is claimed.

### Exact supported shapes, contexts and reuse

Engine declarations:

- `ResolutionActionPayment` is sealed and immutable.
- `GainLifePayment(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolutionActionPayment`.
- `DamagePayment(DamageSourceRef, DamageRecipientRef, ResolutionValue) ResolutionActionPayment`.
- `DestroyPayment(PermanentRef) ResolutionActionPayment`.
- `PayActionOrElse(PlayerRef, ResolutionActionPayment, ResolvingEffect, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.

RON resolving sequences accept `MayCost(action)/1` and
`PlayerMayCost(player, action)/2`, with `GainLife(value)/1`,
`HavePermanentDealDamage(permanent, value, recipient)/3`, or
`DestroyPermanent(permanent)/1`. Recipients use the existing typed singular
permanent, player or union shapes. The adjacent continuation is `If/2`,
`Unless/2`, or `IfElse/3` with symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` and
nonempty listed bodies. Contexts use existing spell, activation, trigger,
delayed-trigger and nested branch action compilation. The adapter does not
create new bindings. The actual records use source-unblocked triggers and a
target-bound delayed-unblocked trigger. Mantle's host context remains rejected.

Preparation reads the amount once and captures the recipient's incarnation and
damage source. Recheck the recipient after choice. The paid branch uses the
accepted payment, even when prevention, life replacement or regeneration changes
the event. Absent/phased subjects and indestructible destruction cannot pay.
Zero calculated amounts still permit choice but create no damage/life event.
Each invocation stores its own preparation and result, with no global last-action
slot. The explicit payer does not replace the action player or damage source.

Reuse: typed permanent/player/recipient plans, `compileInstanceValue`,
`DamageSourceOf`, LKI, the engine's life-gain, damage-outcome and destruction
services, normal replacement ordering, existing target legality, spell/activation
transactions, delayed unblocked events and assignment suppression. Single-action
payment has no earlier resources to roll back and introduces no composite cost,
simultaneous batch, SBA or priority boundary. Collection loading stays atomic.
No Go fallback, source change, runtime cutover or DSL removal was added.

### Exact shapes and reuse boundary

`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanent_reference, [SetColor(
SimpleColorList([color_symbols...]))])` accepts a distinct fixed list of the
five Magic colors, including an empty list for colorless. It lowers to
`Until(Indefinite, SetColors(subject, colors...))`. Chosen colors, duplicate
colors, colorless symbols and malformed values are rejected before factory use.

`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(permanent_reference, [AddAbility([
fixed_keywords...])])` accepts a nonempty list through the existing fixed keyword
compiler, including fixed landwalk. It lowers each member to
`GrantKeywordModification` inside `Until(Indefinite)`. The existing single
activated-ability grant remains unchanged. Mixed activated/keyword bodies,
unknown or malformed keywords and unbound references remain rejected. Other
indefinite modification families remain partial.

RON owns spelling and validation. Existing typed source, target, combat-event
and attachment references provide each factory's independent bindings. The
engine's continuous capture service owns live subject identity, durations,
phasing, timestamps, cloning and ability layers. It captures no absent object
through LKI. Aisling's pending event survives source departure; Cocoon's saved
attachment can receive the grant after the Aura sacrifices itself. No new
engine state, global last-action slot or card-name executor was added.

No production subset registry, fallback or runtime cutover occurred. Go-card
and DSL removal gates remain unsatisfied; no functions or definitions were
removed. No engine skill was required for these compiler-only adapters.

### Exact signatures, scope and reuse

Resolving action sequences accept these adjacent pairs:

- `ChooseAColor(AnyColor)/1`, then `CreatePermanentLayerEffect(ref,
  [SetColor(TheChosenColor)])/2`.
- Bare `ChooseColors`, then `CreatePermanentLayerEffect(ref,
  [SetColor(TheChosenColors)])/2`.

The continuation must contain exactly one `SetColor/1` operation and the matching
bare result symbol. The result exists only for that continuation. Missing,
nonadjacent, preceding, escaped and wrong-kind reads remain compile errors.
Malformed tuples, restricted/invalid choice filters, wrong subjects and other
operations remain rejected. Entry choices, chosen-color filters and other
durations are not added. No target is created by either action.

RON owns declaration validation and the finite option list. Single choices offer
exactly White, Blue, Black, Red and Green. Plural choices offer all 32 subsets,
including the empty set. Each branch lowers directly to a fixed color layer.
`compilePermanentRef`, per-factory `instanceBindings`, `buildResolutionChoice`,
`ChooseAtResolution`, `Until(Indefinite)` and `SetColors` supply typed references,
resolution timing, choices and captured layer execution. The adjacent pair works
in existing resolving action-sequence contexts with their supported permanent
references. It introduces no new entry, cost, static or player-scoped context.
Only the two complete activated-card consumers gain gameplay mappings here.

Choices belong to the resolving spell/ability's controller. They are neither
announced modes nor values stored on a source permanent. Immutable fixed options
and the engine's local resolution choice preserve instance and copy isolation.
Layer capture keeps the original live incarnation; LKI does not make an absent
permanent available for an action. Existing target rechecks, saved Aura host,
source departure, phase cycles, timestamps and cloned effect state are reused.
No new engine API, parallel state store or global last-action slot is added.

### Exact shapes, contexts and engine reuse

- `Protection(FromColor(Colors([color, ...])))` is a temporary ability plan.
  At least one of White, Blue, Black, Red, Green is required. It works in
  `AddAbility/1` within `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3` and in the existing
  scoped `ChooseAnAbility/1` continuation with `AddAbilityVariable/1`.
  Existing resolving action contexts, typed permanent references and temporary
  durations retain their restrictions. The immutable bit set keeps choice plans
  comparable and gives each factory fresh engine declarations.
- `CreateEachPermanentLayerEffectUntil(Ref_TargetPermanents,
  [AddAbility([keyword, ...]), ...], UntilEndOfTurn)/3` uses the existing plural
  target declaration, including `NumberTargetPermanents(ValueX, filter)/2` and
  `OneOrMoreTargetPermanents(filter)/1`. Nonempty supported temporary keywords
  and fixed landwalk reuse one shared validator with filtered collection grants.
  All legal members are captured together at resolution. Mixed color/keyword
  operations, plural protection/rampage and delayed collection references remain
  rejected; other target kinds do not become collection bindings.
- New engine API: `GrantProtectionColors(subject PermanentRef,
  colors ...core.Color) ContinuousModification`. Copies colors, validates the
  subject and actual colors, and installs wrapped protection in layer 6 through
  existing `Until` capture, duration, identity and clone services. Layer passes
  do not accumulate runtime abilities. Normal targeting, Aura legality and
  blocking use existing protection services; no Ward exemption is added. Equipment
  and Fortification attachment checks now reject matching protection and detach
  existing illegal attachments without destroying them. Both attachment sides
  are updated through mutable permanent access.
- Protection damage prevention is now a dynamic candidate in the shared single
  and simultaneous replacement selectors. Source snapshots and the current
  recipient determine applicability after each replacement. Affected players
  can choose protection or another shield first. Legacy direct damage and
  self-fight paths no longer discard protected damage before the selector.
  Existing unpreventable-damage bypasses remain effective.

RON owns spelling, arity, lexical scope and lowering. The engine owns protection,
layer state, source information, replacement choices, batches, and capture.
No global last-action result, game-time declaration panic, fallback factory,
production subset registry or independent rules store was introduced.
Rules evidence: CR 702.14c, 702.16b-f, 611.2c, 613.1f and 616.1e-f.
Local `data/DRK.json` and `data/LEG.json` Oracle text agrees with both full records.
No source defect was corrected and no RON hash changed; vocabulary refresh was
not needed. Existing unrelated source defects remain separate blockers.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

- `PermanentLayerEffect(subject, [SetPowerAndToughnessBoth(value)])/2` supports
  exactly one modification, a singular source or declared Aura host, in an
  unconditional static rule or an existing static `If/2` body.
- `SetPowerAndToughnessBoth/1` lowers to `SetBasePowerToughness`, `While` and
  `Static`, using existing layer 7b, current-controller, attachment, incarnation,
  phasing, ability removal and clone services. This is not a CDA or a captured
  resolving bonus. The amount and condition are read on each layer pass.
- Static values add `Plus(left,right)/2`, `Minus(left,right)/2`, and
  `ManaValueOfPermanent(subject)/1` to the existing `Integer/1`, `Twice/1`, half
  rounding and restricted battlefield/attached-Aura counts. Arithmetic recurses
  through the same static validator. Mana value requires the source or declared
  Aura host and uses live `ManaValueOf`, not LKI. Arithmetic uses `AddValues` and
  `SubtractValues`. Existing static bonus adapters share these value services.
- RON owns names, shape checks, contexts and inventory roles; the engine owns
  all rules/state. No new engine contract, DSL export, card-name branch, global
  result slot, declaration panic, fallback or partial production registry.
- Collective and combined base-value modifications, announced X, P/T reads,
  targets, event references and payment-result reads remain rejected. Existing
  mixed-conditional-layer rejection remains intact.

  and `applyBecomesBasicLand`: layer 4, land-subtype replacement, printed ability

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

  `PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent,Or([AttackedThisTurn,BlockedThisTurn]))`,

  incarnation. Host history, individual history predicates, duplicate operands

  alone or in a supported nonempty `And` filter. `SinglePlayer(You)` remains

  not gain support from this change.
- Engine API:
  `CantBeTargetedBySpellsIf(PermanentRef, CardFilter, StateCondition) StaticRule`.
  A condition is required and definition validation checks its dependencies.
  It is read at each spell-target query with the live source's current controller
  and incarnation. Unconditional `CantBeTargetedBySpells` retains all callers.

  `NotCondition`, `While`, `SetBasePowerToughness`, typed permanent references,
  `OpponentsOf`, `PermanentsControlledByPlayers`, `MatchingPermanents`,

### Exact supported shapes, dependencies and engine reuse

Engine API:

- `RedirectDamageToPermanentIf(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef,
  from PermanentFilter, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`: damage from
  matching permanent sources. A zero filter means every permanent source.
- `RedirectDamageFromCardTypeToPermanentIf(player PlayerRef,
  subject PermanentRef, kind core.CardType, condition StateCondition) StaticRule`:
  includes source information outside the battlefield, including captured spells.
- `DamageSourceIsUnblocked() PermanentFilter` and
  `Combat.IsUnblockedIncarnation(id, incarnation uuid.UUID) bool`.
  `CombatGroup.Unblocked` is set in the common blocker commit before block events,
  not when attackers are declared. Added blockers clear it; removing blockers
  alone does not restore it. Explicit unblock effects set it. Combat removal
  ends it. `PermanentLKI.Unblocked` saves departure and phase information.
  Current sources use live state; absent/phased sources use their original
  information. Phase-in does not restore combat status. Clones preserve it.

Static rules require valid player/permanent references and a condition; type
validation rejects invalid card types. The rule saves its source incarnation and
checks current condition, controller, player and destination for each event.
Destinations must remain creatures or planeswalkers. Attachment references follow
current attachment identity. Phasing, departure and ability removal stop the rule;
returned sources cannot reactivate their former rule. Fresh instances work.

RON context: exactly one
`ReplaceWouldDealDamage(event,[DealToCreatureOrPlaneswalkerInstead(ref)])`
in an existing top-level permanent `If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` branch. Each branch
compiles, including inactive ones. The recipient is exactly `Player(You)`; the
destination is `ThisPermanent` or `HostPermanent` in an Aura.

- `DamageWouldBeDealtByAPermanentToRecipient(filter,Player(You))` accepts bare
  `IsUnblocked`, supported type/subtype/supertype/color predicates and nonempty
  nested `And`/`Or`. References, dynamic controller predicates and unsupported
  source predicates remain errors.
- `DamageWouldBeDealtByASourceToRecipient(IsCardtype(type),Player(You))`
  accepts exactly one valid card type. Other source-filter forms remain errors.
- Extra operations, malformed arities, empty filters, unbound/incompatible
  destinations, target recipients, resolving contexts and top-level redirection
  remain rejected. No target binding is invented.

RON owns spellings, declaration checks and semantic roles. Engine code reuses
`Static`, state conditions, typed references, continuous-effect cycle replacements,
`damageFilterSource`, `damageSourceHasCardType`, source/phase LKI, transactional
casting, native combat, stack copies, clones and cleanup. Redirection preserves
amount, combat status and full damage source; shared replacements recheck the
new recipient, protection and prevention. Shared simultaneous damage preserves
actual damage, history and lifelink. No parallel replacement/combat/damage service
is added. Existing Go helpers and callers remain compatible.

616.1/616.2 and 702.26. Local `data/LEA.json` and `data/ATQ.json` supply Oracle

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

Capability ID: `STACK-ABILITY-PERMANENT-SOURCES`.

- `Game.StackAbilityPermanentSources() []DamageSource`: original permanent
  sources of activated and triggered abilities **still on the stack**, ordered
  by stack insertion and deduplicated by exact incarnation. Missing, stale and
  unknown saved identities are excluded. The source need not have a damage
  ability. Copies refer to one source; separate visits of one card remain distinct.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackAbilities(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`: filtered non-targeted resolution choice
  from exactly that category. Per-instance output bindings use the shared
  resolution frame. Empty lists or absent players clear only their output.
- Current characteristics/controller apply to a live source. Phase information
  and departure LKI apply to absent sources. Return cannot replace the original;
  phase-in resumes current reads. Face-down snapshots hide printed information.
- This query excludes targets, other saved action/event objects, spells, pending
  triggers, waiting replacement/prevention/delayed-trigger references and command
  objects. The ability currently resolving has already left the stack and is
  excluded. These APIs explicitly describe a category, not a general legal list.

activation/trigger/stack insertion paths, copies and clones. The shared
`readPermanentIncarnationInformation` is extracted from
`readPermanentInformation` without changing existing callers. It reuses the
current permanent, pre-phase information and incarnation-keyed departure stores.
The snapshot, filter, decision and binding services remain unchanged except for
adding this enumeration mode to the shared damage-source choice.
No alternate zone, replacement, damage, targeting, payment or history service
is added. Queries do not run layers or mutate the game. Returned card data is
independent. CR 400.7, 609.7a, 702.26 and 708.2 supply the identity and information
contract. Existing API callers remain compatible.

established. Missing compiler adapters and broader source/shield contracts:

### Exact signatures, context and reuse boundary

Capability ID: `STACK-TARGET-PERMANENT-SOURCES`.

  choice from exactly that category. The existing service validates declarations,
  preserves separate bindings, clears empty/absent-player outputs and clones
  saved results. Producer-before-consumer checks still apply.
- Target legality does not erase a saved reference. Departed, returned, phased
  or newly shrouded targets remain referred objects until the final referring
  stack object leaves. Objects need no damage capability. Current characteristics
  and controller apply to live incarnations. Phase snapshots/departure LKI
  apply to absent ones; return cannot substitute a new object. Phase-in resumes
  live reads. Face-down objects hide printed characteristics.
- Copies keep the original target incarnations or their newly selected targets.
  Old map entries do not add candidates. Queries are pure and return separate
  card snapshots. Removing stack references in one clone cannot change another.
  The resolving object has already left the stack and is excluded.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

Capability ID: `STACK-TARGET-SPELL-SOURCES`.

- `Game.StackTargetSpellSources() []DamageSource`: reads exact spell targets of
  spells/abilities still on the stack. Stack insertion then target-list order;
  exact deduplication; no legality or damage-capability requirement. Permanent
  spells and spell copies qualify. Source-card, ability, player, permanent and
  unknown IDs do not. Only target-list entries with saved spell identities qualify.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackSpellTargets(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`: non-targeted filtered resolution choice
  from only that category. Shared validation, typed producer/consumer dominance,
  independent bindings, empty/absent-player clearing, fallback choices and cloned
  resolution frames apply. It does not expose a complete general source list.
- `StackObject.targetSpellSources` is private per-object saved information keyed
  by exact stack ID. `pushStack` captures spell targets. Live queries read current
  color, controller and other spell characteristics; `Stack.saveSpellInformation`
  refreshes departure data before pop, ID removal, source-ID removal and stack
  movement to ante. No global last-action slot or new unbounded history map.
- Recasts and battlefield entries cannot replace the old spell. Copying a
  referring object keeps its saved target; native retargeting captures changed
  targets. Stale map entries cannot add sources. The final referring object's
  departure ends the reference. Resolving objects have already left the stack.
- Queries return separate card snapshots, make no choices and mutate no state.
  Game clones share immutable maps; updates copy the map first. Clones can retain
  different departure characteristics. Spell objects have no phasing operation;
  permanent-target phasing retains its existing separate contract.

Reuses `CaptureSpellDamageSource` through its extracted private
`damageSourceFromSpellObject` helper, `DamageSource.SameObject`, native stack
insertion/removal/resolution, copies and retargeting, filtered decisions, binding

renamed from `saveSpellManaValue` to `saveSpellInformation`; a fresh caller audit

engine contract, not a compiler spelling adapter. No production RON context is

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

  saved in `eventDamageSourceCapture` within effects of stack objects, including
  nested sequence wrappers. Stack insertion then capture traversal order; exact
  identity deduplication. No capture execution, future result evaluation, generic

  captures and sequences supplies saved references. Current information is read

  category. Other typed references and saved delayed resolution frames remain

### Exact contract, contexts and engine reuse

Capability `STACK-DELAYED-PERMANENT-FRAMES` extends existing APIs:

- `Game.StackBoundPermanentSources() []DamageSource` now reads immutable
  `capturedDelayedBody` effects through `stackPermanentBindingReferences` and
  sequence wrappers on objects still on the stack. Supported frame fields:
  `map[*PermanentBinding]capturedPermanent`,
  `map[*targetDeclaration][]capturedPermanent` (singular/plural target groups),
  `map[*CreatedTokensBinding][]capturedPermanent`. Nil declarations and invalid
  identities cannot produce candidates. Source incarnation, player/number
  bindings and future action bodies are not treated as these permanent bindings.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackBindings(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` uses the new candidates through its
  existing shared service. No new exported API, category flag, RON spelling,
  compiler role or supported production context is added.
- Reuses `AtNext`/delayed permanent-event snapshots, existing trigger placement,
  `readPermanentIncarnationInformation`, permanent/phase/departure information,
  exact `DamageSource.SameObject` deduplication and deterministic ID/incarnation
  sorting per stack object. Live reads use current characteristics/controller;
  departed/phased reads use exact retained information. Returned objects cannot
  replace them. Query snapshots keep mutable card data separate.
- Waiting/pending delayed triggers stay excluded until placement. The resolving
  object has left the stack; another referer can retain eligibility. Copies keep
  captures and clones keep independent state. Removing/countering the final
  referer ends eligibility. No effect execution, global last-action slot, target
  declaration, RNG or player choice occurs during queries.

The missing behavior was an engine reference-enumeration contract. Existing RON
adapters and rules execution were reused exactly. No compiler/data/environment
repair was needed. Other saved binding categories and waiting-reference
categories remain separate dependencies. Existing payment, replacement ordering,
prevention and simultaneous damage services retain ownership and pass regression
checks. No new behavior is claimed for those operations.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

Capability `WAITING-DELAYED-PERMANENT-FRAMES` adds:

- `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource`: saved
  `map[*PermanentBinding]capturedPermanent`,
  `map[*targetDeclaration][]capturedPermanent`,
  `map[*CreatedTokensBinding][]capturedPermanent` in immutable
  `capturedDelayedBody` effects, nested sequence wrappers and captured modal
  bodies, plus `MatchEventID`/`matchIncarnation` event subjects, **only while the
  delayed ability is registered as waiting**.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromWaitingDelayedBindings(PlayerRef,
  DamageSourceFilter, *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`: filtered,
  non-targeted choice at resolution through the existing shared service.
- Shared private `appendPermanentReferenceSources` retains the existing stack
  reader's deterministic ID/incarnation sorting, exact deduplication, live versus
  phased/departed information reads and copied query snapshots. Waiting results
  follow trigger registration order, with sorted references within each ability.
- One-shot detection ends waiting eligibility before pending/stack placement.
  Duration-based delays continue waiting after a match until their existing
  lifecycle expires. Stack copies do not create waiting abilities. Clones retain
  independent waiting lists and immutable captured frames. Queries execute no
  effects, choices or RNG and read no global last-action slot.
- Source IDs alone, source reads inside future bodies, other typed references,
  untyped legacy IDs and unproduced future actions are outside this supported
  context. Nil bindings, invalid or unknown identities produce no candidates.
  Other CR 609.7a categories remain separate. General RON `ChooseADamageSource`
  and the complete chosen-source shields continue to reject.

RON keeps its existing spelling, scopes, per-factory targets and delayed adapters
(`compileDelayedStep`, `compileDepartureDelay`); no new production shape or
partial registry is added. TriggerSystem owns registration, pending detection,
expiry and cloning. The incarnation reader owns LKI and phasing. The shared
choice service owns output validation, producer dominance, fallback, filtering,
empty/absent-player clearing and resolution results. Existing payments, damage
batches and replacements retain ownership; no new ordering/rollback/simultaneous
contract is claimed. Runtime cutover and removal gates remain unmet. No Go card,
generator or DSL function is removed; no unused-caller audit is claimed.

`This` subjects in `Destroy`, `DestroyWithoutRegeneration`, `Sacrifice` and

modal bodies. These lower the RON `DestroyPermanent(ThisPermanent)`,
`SacrificePermanent(ThisPermanent)` and
`PutPermanentIntoItsOwnersHand(ThisPermanent)` actions in `CreateFutureTrigger`.
This is a complete supported context, not a claim of general source-body support.
Conditional wrappers and other source-reading action kinds remain separate forms.

Private `delayedSourcePermanentReference` exposes a pure typed boolean query.
The waiting reader requires the delayed ability's captured source identity and
uses the existing exact incarnation information reader, LKI/phasing services,
sorted deduplication and copied source snapshots. It executes no body, choice or
RNG and reads no global last-action slot. A source ID alone, unknown incarnation,
uncaptured source or future delayed-action producer does not qualify.

`ChooseDamageSourceFromWaitingDelayedBindings(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
*DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` consumes the new context through existing
filtering, validation, dominance, independent outputs and fallback. TriggerSystem
still owns waiting detection, APNAP placement and cloning. One-shot detection
ends waiting eligibility before pending placement. Stack copies do not create
waiting abilities. Existing action legality remains: sacrifice requires control
by the resolving ability's controller. Costs, replacements, damage ordering and
simultaneous operations retain their existing services; no new contract there

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

New native APIs:

- `ChosenPlayerOf(PermanentRef) PlayerRef`: a live exact-incarnation entry choice;
  absent/phased/returned/unchosen objects and unknown player IDs supply no player.
  It does not use LKI.
- `SetMaximumHandSizeStatic(PlayerRef, int) ContinuousEffect`: nonnegative fixed
  size, including zero. Use `WithStaticAbility`.
- `NoMaximumHandSizeStatic(PlayerRef) ContinuousEffect`: no maximum; use
  `WithStaticAbility`.

RON supports top-level permanent
`PlayerEffect(You | TheChosenPlayer, [SetMaximumHandSize(Integer(n))])` and
`PlayerEffect(You | TheChosenPlayer, [HasNoMaximumHandSize])`.
`n` is nonnegative and literal. TheChosenPlayer requires the existing same-card
`AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, [ChooseAPlayer(Opponent)])` declaration.
One operation per list is supported. Combined lists, dynamic values, resolving
contexts, event/target players and malformed/unbound references stay rejected.
The fixed amount now has the semantic inventory `value` role.

RON owns spelling, shape validation and entry-declaration checks. mage owns the
live rules and typed player reference. `Game.MaximumHandSize` evaluates active
hand-size declarations in the existing source timestamp order after object
characteristics. The last matching fixed/unlimited declaration wins. Cleanup
now uses this same service. `You` follows the current controller; an entry choice
stays fixed until a new entry. Existing direct setters retain their computed-map
behavior and supply the baseline for the typed query. Current callers stay intact.

Reuse: continuous-source registration/removal/timestamp order, printed-ability
suppression, permanent reference identity, phasing, ChooseOpponentAsEnters,
cloneEffect, definition validation, transactional casting, and native cleanup/
discard/zone/trigger services. No layer enum, parallel rule subsystem, global
last-action value or game-time declaration panic is added. The live query reads
only matching rule lifetimes; it makes no choices, consumes no RNG and mutates
no rules. No new replacement ordering or simultaneous-discard contract is
claimed. Runtime cutover/deletion gates are unmet; no Go card, generator or DSL
function is removed, and no unused-DSL audit is claimed.

  recipient PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter) ResolvingEffect`.

  Sources require exactly one permanent incarnation or spell stack identity.

  properties create no shield. Definition validation enforces typed references,

  properties. Live information overrides an earlier snapshot. Without retained
  permanent information, the exact matching packet supplies its own properties.
  The filter is checked at installation and at each damage event. Mismatching
  properties, zero damage and other recipients do not consume the shield.
- Positive matching damage consumes one shield. `capturesSourceIdentity` extends
  existing simultaneous batching to exact spell identities; all matching packets
  in one event are prevented together. Affected-player choice and replacement
  rechecks use the shared planner. Cleanup expires the shield. Clones copy source
  information and retain independent replacement consumption. Exact permanent
  subjects use the existing waiting-prevention permanent-reference contract.
- RON shape: `CreateFuturePreventDamage(NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(

  operation must be bare symbols; player references use existing typed scope.
  The lowering requires a lexical `chosenDamageSourcePlan` and a factory-local
  entry in `instanceBindings.chosenDamageSources`. The plan carries the filter.
