### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

- `Game.AddCommandObject(card Card, faceDown bool) (uuid.UUID, error)` installs
  the engine object with a new visit. The caller removes it from its former zone
  first. Nil objects, missing IDs and duplicate command IDs fail without changes.
  This service grants no casting permission and installs no command abilities
  or variant rules.
- `Game.RemoveCommandObject(visit uuid.UUID) (Card, bool)` and
  `Game.SetCommandObjectFaceDown(visit uuid.UUID, faceDown bool) bool` act only on
  the specified visit. Visibility changes retain identity; a return replaces it.
- `Game.CommandDamageSources() []DamageSource` enumerates face-up objects in
  insertion order with isolated snapshots. `DamageSource.CommandVisit()
  uuid.UUID` separates command visits from permanent incarnations and spell
  stack identities. `SameObject` requires exactly one identity kind and the
  same object ID. Command cards have no controller (CR 108.4).
- `ZoneSystem` owns live objects and departure information. Removal retains the
  exact last information, including hidden visibility; ordinary LKI clearing
  cannot erase it. Clones copy both stores independently. `FindCardAnywhere`
  reads a snapshot of live command storage. Command objects are not permanents;
  permanent destruction/phasing do not operate on them (CR 408.1).
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromCommandObjects(player PlayerRef,
  filter DamageSourceFilter, binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`
  uses the shared resolution-time choice, pure filters, result clearing,
  definition validation and per-instance bindings. RON
  `chosenDamageSourcePlan.commandChoice(instanceBindings) mage.ResolvingEffect`
  lowers validated `ChooseADamageSource(filter)` with `You` and its own binding.
  Full declarations remain strictly rejected until complete source enumeration.
- Exact and selected-source prevention plus selected-source redirection accept
  command visits through a shared exact-identity check. Property rechecks read
  current or exact departure information. Existing replacement ordering,
  simultaneous-operation and consumption services are reused (CR 609.7a–b).
  Captured delayed damage bindings retain and sort command identities, and
  existing waiting/stack damage-binding queries use the same information service.

Dependencies: existing `Card` representation, zone cloning, damage-source choice
and filters, resolution bindings, captured delayed frames, replacement pipeline,
damage services and cleanup. CR 400.7 supplies visit/return separation. The
command visibility service exposes no public characteristics while hidden; it
does not implement unrelated face-down casting or specialized variant mechanics.
Waiting command references in prevention/redirection rules need an explicit
collector before general enumeration is enabled.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

- `WhileWithSharedSubjects(condition StateCondition,
  modifications ...ContinuousModification) StaticRule` explicitly groups the
  condition and subjects for a layer pass. `While` keeps its existing live,
  separate layer-selection behavior and signature.
- `continuousRule.sharedSubjects` selects the new mode. Per-game
  `EffectManager.composedMembers` keys a rule and source, retaining each
  modification's exact permanent/incarnation subjects. Each pass clears this
  scratch state. Repeated modification declarations do not duplicate the saved
  membership. Runtime grants retain their existing per-declaration identities.
- `composedLayerEffect.continuesAcrossLayers(*Game) bool` uses the existing
  printed-ability continuation hook. Once the first part starts, later layers
  and sublayers keep their subjects even if layer 6 removes the source ability.
  A false first condition remains false for that pass. Phased/absent subjects
  are excluded, and returned objects cannot replace retained incarnations.
- Values are read in the layer that uses them through `captureMembers`; they
  are not captured with the first-layer membership. A layer-7 creature count
  can therefore include the creature type added by the same rule in layer 4.
- Type-layer dependency checks compare the condition and selected identities
  before/after an isolated shared-service probe. The layer scheduler retains
  timestamp ordering and dependency rechecks.
- `compileConditionalAnimation([]Node, mage.PermanentRef, scope)` validates
  one `SetPowerAndToughnessBoth(value)` with one or more
  `AddCardtype(Artifact | Creature)` operations, including Creature. It lowers
  through `compileConditionalStaticBody` to the new grouped engine constructor.
  This context uses `PermanentLayerEffect(ThisPermanent | HostPermanent, [...])`
  within the existing conditional grammar; HostPermanent requires an Aura.
  Existing static P/T values and typed source/host references apply. Other
  mixed rule bodies, collective base values, duplicate bases, invalid arities,
  unbound references and resolution-only values remain declaration errors.

  grants are not accepted by this adapter.
- Compiler: `compileBandsWithOtherLayer(Node, []Node) (optionFactory, error)`
  validates the declaration and builds fresh modifications inside
  `Static(While(...))`. RON owns spelling, scope and diagnostics.
- Engine: `GrantEachBandsWithOther(PermanentSet, PermanentFilter)
  ContinuousModification` installs quality grants in layer 6. Per-pass
  `EffectManager.bandsWithOther` stores immutable quality filters under exact
  permanent/incarnation keys. Clones copy the map and slices only when nonempty.
  Current subject selection controls grant availability; departure, phasing,
  controller/color/type changes and source ability removal cannot restore an
  obsolete registration. Queries do not mutate state or use LKI for absence.
- Engine: `Game.FormAttackingBand([]uuid.UUID) error` shares validation with the
  scripted `BandFormer` path. Members must be distinct current attackers with
  one controller and defender, before blocker declaration, and in no prior band.
  Ordinary formation keeps its own rules. Quality formation requires a matching
  holder and all members matching that holder's quality. Single-member bands
  are legal. Losing abilities preserves a formed band; leaving combat removes
  the member. A phase cycle or returned incarnation cannot rejoin that band.
- Damage choices use current ordinary banding or a matching holder plus another
  matching opponent for each source. Every eligible combat opponent can receive
  the damage after this condition holds. Multiple qualities do not combine into
  a broader formation predicate. Removing ordinary banding clears all current
  bands-with-other grants; later layer grants and cleanup can restore them.
- The shared combat path plans outgoing sources separately, then each distinct
  blocker once across its actual live attack/block pairs. It reuses existing
  assignment map validation, bounded choices, first-strike services, trample
  lethal checks and simultaneous damage. Ordinary bands without these qualities
  retain the existing aggregate legacy incoming distribution interface.

### Contract, dependencies and reuse

- RON: validated `ChooseADamageSource(filter)` plans have the private category
  lowering `chosenDamageSourcePlan.stackExileChoice(instanceBindings)
  mage.ResolvingEffect`. Supported filters retain their existing symbol/tuple
  validation: `AnyDamageSource`, `IsColor(color)`, `IsCardtype(type)`, and nested
  nonempty `And`/`Or` lists. It uses `You` and the instance's own source binding.
  Existing `CreateFuturePreventDamage(NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(TheChosenDamageSource, Player(You)), [PreventThatDamage])`
  lowering consumes the result. No general source list is accepted prematurely.
- Engine: `Game.CaptureExiledDamageSource(visit uuid.UUID) DamageSource` reads a
  live visit. `DamageSource.ExileVisit() uuid.UUID` is separate from permanent,
  stack and command identity. `SameObject` requires the same card and exactly one
  matching identity category. Exile cards have owners, but no controllers.
- `Game.StackBoundExileSources() []DamageSource` reads non-nil singular/plural
  payment captures and nested event-card captures from stack objects. It excludes
  other zones, wrong card IDs, absent visits and unreferenced exile objects.
  Map-derived references are sorted and duplicate visits are removed. Copies
  retain the reference; final referring departure ends category availability.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackExileBindings(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` uses shared choices and clears an empty
  result. Invalid filters, missing player/binding and premature reads reject
  during definition validation. No effect runs during source enumeration.
- Single and grouped removal retain exact departure information. Re-exile
  replaces the old entry with a fresh visit (CR 400.7, 400.8, 406.7). Returned
  objects cannot replace saved subjects. Queries and game clones own separate
  exile card and departure data with preserved physical card IDs.
- Face-down exile sources expose no characteristics, including to a player who
  may inspect the card (CR 406.3a). A hidden referred object can keep its exact
  identity, but cannot satisfy a color/type filter from private information.
- `CastableFromExilePermission.Visit uuid.UUID` binds the existing permission
  service to the current exile visit. An absent object gets no permission.
  Departure, grouped removal and re-exile end permission. A failed casting
  payment keeps the card, visit and permission. Existing signatures and legal
  callers remain; the old zone-unit fixture now installs its card before grant.
- A cast is a new spell; its battlefield entry is another object. Choosing the
  exile object for a separate shield does not grant continuation to either.
  CR 400.7h lets other parts of the casting-permission effect find the spell;
  it does not transfer an independent prevention shield. Existing CR 609.7a
  permanent-spell continuity remains intact. Permission-effect result bindings
  for additional same-effect instructions need their own future contract.

### Contract, exact signatures and reuse boundary

- `DamageSource.GraveyardVisit() uuid.UUID` is an exact identity category.
  `SameObject` requires one category, the card ID and the visit. A graveyard
  object has public characteristics and an owner, but no controller (CR 404.2).
- `Game.CaptureGraveyardDamageSource(visit uuid.UUID) DamageSource` reads only a
  live visit. Physical IDs, absent and nil visits cannot select an object.
- `Game.StackGraveyardSources() []DamageSource` reads exact graveyard targets,
  non-nil `CardBinding`/`CardsBinding` payment captures, and nested event-card
  capture sequences on stack objects. Queries are pure, sort map-derived
  references and deduplicate exact visits. Wrong zones/IDs, absent visits and
  unreferenced cards are excluded.
- Stack insertion saves target visits. Copies keep original visits; native
  retargeting captures the new target. Illegal targets still refer to the old
  object (CR 609.7a); unused copied snapshots do not supply references. Final
  referring stack departure ends availability.
- `BasePlayer.RemoveFromGraveyard`, `ClearGraveyard` and `SetGraveyard` retain
  departure information. The whole-zone setter retains its existing fresh-visit
  behavior. Return cannot replace a saved source (CR 400.7). Immutable history
  maps use copy-on-write; queries and clones keep separate mutable card facts
  with physical IDs intact. Wrapped-player extraction retains history.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackGraveyardReferences(PlayerRef,
  DamageSourceFilter, *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` uses the shared
  resolution decision service. Invalid declarations and premature reads reject;
  an empty result clears the binding.
- RON `chosenDamageSourcePlan.stackGraveyardChoice(instanceBindings)
  mage.ResolvingEffect` lowers validated `ChooseADamageSource(filter)` with `You`
  and its separate instance binding. Existing `CreateFuturePreventDamage(
  NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(TheChosenDamageSource,
  Player(You)), [PreventThatDamage])` consumes the choice.

contexts. General source choice remains unsupported; no partial production
registry or Go-card fallback is added.

### Exact signatures, dependencies and reuse boundary

- `chosenDamageSourcePlan.stackGraveyardChoice(instanceBindings)
  mage.ResolvingEffect` reuses validated `ChooseADamageSource(filter)` lowering
  with `You` and that plan's per-instance `DamageSourceBinding`.
- `ChooseDamageSourceFromStackGraveyardReferences(player PlayerRef,
  filter DamageSourceFilter, binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`
  retains its existing signature, definition validation and resolution timing.
- `Game.StackGraveyardSources() []DamageSource` now reads stack and resolving
  frames, retaining exact graveyard target visits, singular/plural payment
  bindings, nested event captures and placed delayed card frames.
- `Stack.referenceObjects() []*StackObject` and
  `Stack.resolvingReferenceObjects []*StackObject` generalize the existing
  hand/exile frame service. Resolution saves/restores frame depth; cloning
  copies frames with the existing `cloneStackObject` implementation.

RON owns spelling, filter/arity/scope validation and instance lowering. Mage
owns lifetime, identity, departure information, deterministic ordering,
deduplication and choice execution. This fixes missing engine query mechanics,
not missing RON spelling. Reused contracts include graveyard visit/departure
readers, card/event/delayed binding collectors, transactional payment rollback,
copy/clone isolation and selected-source shield installation/consumption.
There is no new history store or resolution-global last-action slot.

References remain available during nested resolution and in a clone of the
resolving game, then leave with the last referring frame. Returned visits cannot
replace saved visits. Public facts use current/departure information; returned
characteristic changes cannot alter the old visit. Queries cannot mutate retained
facts. Nil bindings, wrong visits, other zones and unreferenced history supply
no choices. Copies choose independently. Source phasing/departure does not undo
a paid activation. Graveyard cards do not phase. Failed payment publishes no
reference or choice. Installed shields keep independent selected sources after
resolution and consume normally.

Rules evidence: local CR 400.7, 608.2 and 609.7a–b. General source choice remains
rejected. No source defect was found; RON source and vocabulary are unchanged.
Removal gates remain unmet; Go card definitions and DSL services remain.
API/rules docs describe only the established graveyard context.

### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse boundary

- Existing `CreateFutureTrigger(AtTheBeginningOfTheNextEndStep,
  ActionList([PermanentDealsDamage(ThisPermanent, value, recipient)]))`

  and `DamageSourceOf(This)` reads through the existing typed waiting-reference
  interface. Other source bindings do not imply a self source. Amount and
  recipient are not resolved during enumeration. A zero amount still refers
  to the source; CR 609.7a does not require that it can deal damage.

reference enumeration, exact source capture, live/phasing/departure information,
registration lifetime, deduplication, choice, cloning, damage and shields.

multi-recipient damage bodies. It does not claim to finish the entire reference
audit or enable general production choice. Estimated and actual compilation

subrule scenarios; full-card gameplay coverage remains unchanged. The actual
result matches the estimate because general aggregation remains rejected.

### Exact shapes, dependencies and reuse boundary

The existing AST adapters already lower delayed damage instructions. The missing
contract was native waiting-reference declaration. This slice makes permanent
self-source lowering explicit and shared rather than introducing another source
chooser or an identity store.

- `compileSelfDamageSource(Node, scope, bool) (damageSourceFactory, error)`
  validates the scoped self source. `damageSourceFactory` is
  `func(instanceBindings) mage.DamageSourceRef`. Permanent sources lower to
  `mage.DamageSourceOf(permanentReferencePlan.build(instanceBindings))`;
  spell self sources retain `mage.This`. Self aliases use existing lexical
  scope, including `Trigger_ThatPermanent` for a source-tapped trigger.
  Target, attachment and unrelated event reads do not enter this helper.
- `compilePlayerRecipientDamage(Node, scope, damageSourceFactory)
  (effectFactory, error)` receives the validated source plan from its sole
  compiler caller. A fresh whole-repository search confirmed that caller.
  Collection and packet adapters share the same source lowering. Existing
  single-recipient referenced-permanent adapters stay separate.
- Inside `CreateFutureTrigger(event, ActionList([...]))`, supported bodies include
  `PermanentDealsDamage(ThisPermanent, amount, EachPermanent(filter))`,
  `EachPlayer(AnyPlayer|Opponent)`, the existing mixed `MultipleRecipients`, and
  `PermanentDealsMultipleDamage(ThisPermanent,
  [DamageToRecipients(amount, recipient), ...])`. Their existing amount,
  recipient, target and filter restrictions still apply.
- `(*damageEachEffect).refersToSourcePermanent() bool`,
  `(*playerDamageEachEffect).refersToSourcePermanent() bool` and
  `(*damagePacketsEffect).refersToSourcePermanent() bool` use the shared
  `damageReadsSourcePermanent(DamageSourceRef) bool` reader. The existing
  single-recipient declaration also uses this reader. Direct `This` and
  `DamageSourceOf(This)` qualify. Bound sources do not imply self.
- `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource` and
  `ChooseDamageSourceFromWaitingDelayedBindings(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` keep their signatures. The existing
  `chosenDamageSourcePlan.waitingDelayedPermanentChoice(instanceBindings)`
  supplies each real protection record's filter and per-instance binding.

RON owns spelling, declaration validation, scope and lowering. Mage owns pure
enumeration, exact source capture, current/phasing/departure information,
registration lifetime, deduplication, cloning, choice, simultaneous damage and
prevention. Enumeration runs no callback, amount, recipient or filter query.
Empty collections and zero damage keep the reference. Nested future bodies do
not imply an outer self read. Saved sequences and modes keep their declaration.

Creation occurs at resolution; one-shot detection ends waiting availability.
Departure and phasing retain the original incarnation. A returned card cannot
replace it. Query facts can reflect current color/control, while execution keeps
the saved ability controller. Queries and game clones keep separate facts and
waiting frames. Duplicate packets combine before prevention; one shield covers
the complete matching batch, and a copied delay creates another batch. Rules:
local CR 400.7, 603.7a–e and 609.7a–b. Recipient self reads, conditional wrappers,
other damage implementations and opaque references remain separate audit work.

### Exact shapes, signatures and ownership

RON reuses existing AST lowering rather than adding a duplicate adapter:

- `compileDelayedStep(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` lowers supported
  `CreateFutureTrigger(event, ActionList([...]))` declarations.
- `compileResolvingPermanentBranch(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` lowers
  `If(PermanentPassesFilter(permanent, IsAttacking), [actions])` and the
  `IsBlocking` form through `compilePermanentRef` and fresh instance bindings to
  `IfPermanentAttacking(PermanentRef, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` and
  `IfPermanentBlocking(PermanentRef, ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- New private `(*combatStateBranch).refersToSourcePermanent() bool` reads its
  typed self subject or the body's explicit self declaration.
- `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource` and
  `ChooseDamageSourceFromWaitingDelayedBindings(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter,
  *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` retain their signatures.

Supported subjects use existing self/target/attachment/event lexical scopes.
RON owns spelling, arity, scope, diagnostics and factory isolation. Mage owns
pure declaration traversal, saved incarnation capture, information snapshots,
deduplication, waiting lifetime, choices and execution. Sequences, captured
bodies, nested supported branches and modes propagate declarations. A false or
unknown combat condition still refers to its subject/body objects. Queries do
not resolve subjects, check combat, run amounts/actions or consume RNG.
Bound and attached conditions do not imply self. Nested future producers retain
separate lifetime boundaries. Missing subjects/bodies, unbound scopes, tuple
combat filters, empty bodies and alternative combat branches remain errors.

Existing delayed and exact-object services retain current color/control and
LKI after departure. Phasing retains a reference; return cannot replace it.
One-shot detection ends waiting availability before pending placement. Resolution
checks current combat membership, excludes absent/phased subjects and uses the
saved ability controller. A phase cycle removes combat membership without a
new incarnation. Payment rollback, prevention consumption, damage batching and
replacement ordering use existing services. Local CR 400.7, 603.7a–e,
609.7a–b and 702.26b apply. No source-data defect or environment failure was found.

  producer identity. Native constructor signatures remain unchanged.

reference declarations and runtime execution. Queries do not evaluate values,
conditions or filters, run bodies, offer payments, choose modes, flip coins or

service. Trigger detection ends waiting eligibility. False intervening-if
conditions retain the wait; successful detection consumes it and resolution
rechecks the condition. Scoped coin execution occurs at resolution and consumes
one outcome. Source-controller reads follow their existing LKI policy.

captured subjects, layers, phase expiry, phasing, targets, costs, damage,
prevention and delayed destruction. No Go-card requirements, fallback registry,
new source syntax, removed skills or delegation were used.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

- Existing AST shape:
  `CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil(subject, [modifications...], UntilEndOfCombat)`.
  The duration is a bare symbol. Existing singular permanent reference and
  modification validation remains in force.
- `compileTemporaryDuration(Node, scope)
  (func([]mage.ContinuousModification) mage.Effect, error)` now accepts that
  duration in every supported resolving layer body, including spells, upkeep
  triggers and nested delayed bodies. Activation, source-attack and combat-start
  bodies remain supported. There is no event-specific duration permission.
- `compileTemporaryLayer(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` remains the only
  caller. Collection layers, rule effects, costs and installed event
  subscriptions retain their separate adapters and supported contexts.
- Engine reuse: `Until(Duration, ...ContinuousModification) ResolvingEffect`,
  `ModifyPT`, `GrantKeywordModification`, per-instance targets, `composedLayerEffect`,
  `EffectManager.RemoveEndOfCombat` and `Game.RunStepWithPriority(EndCombat)`.
  No missing engine mechanics or new public signature was needed.
- Subjects and values are captured at resolution. Returned incarnations cannot
  inherit the modification. A phase cycle retains identity; application is
  suspended while phased out. Removal from combat and source departure do not
  end the resolved effect. Clones keep separate expiry state.
- End-of-combat triggers and priority run before combat-duration expiry. Layers
  installed during that step expire at the same phase boundary. The next combat
  cannot inherit them. Independent end-of-turn prevention and next-end-step
  destruction retain their own lifetimes.

Rules evidence: local CR 400.7, 511.2–3, 611.2a/c/d and 702.26b. This is a missing
compiler adapter, not a missing engine contract, source defect or environment
failure. RON source is unchanged; the vocabulary source snapshot needs no refresh.

failed at the expected `unsupported duration (UntilEndOfCombat)` diagnostic

synthetic delayed fixture also needed Artifact metadata instead of a Creature
without CardPT. Native tests prove the reused engine boundary rather than
requiring an artificial new engine API.

Fixture corrections after lowering preserved behavior: phasing removes a Wall
from combat, so the pre-resolution phase-cycle case assigns it to block again;
turn-long prevention ends through native cleanup, not continuous-layer removal;
queries after copy-on-write cloning use the current permanent object; direct
phase-in after expiry requires the same explicit layer refresh as native step
execution before priority.

  ContinuousModification` reuses `layerModification`, exact captured subjects,

  producer bindings and targets. A token's This refers to the token even when

  token entry, payment transactions, stack copies, game clones, native layer

The selected shared prerequisite has concrete downstream multi-card value.
The audit found `millSubjectEffect` carries typed PlayerRef and ResolutionValue
operands but has no `refersToSourcePermanent` contract. The RON action adapter
also accepts only fixed integers despite the engine's existing typed mill amount.
These are separate engine declaration and compiler adapter gaps, not data defects.

library inspection/shuffle players. Combat-exit operands also need the remaining
audit. This run does not claim the audit or general aggregation is complete.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse

- Existing engine `Mill(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` now declares
  source reads in both operands to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources()`.
  Private `(*millSubjectEffect).refersToSourcePermanent() bool` uses the shared
  typed player/value walkers. It runs no operand, modifier or player choice.
- `MillNumberCards(value)` in resolving player scopes lowers through existing
  `compileInstanceValue(Node, scope) (valueFactory, error)`, with per-instance
  bindings. Bare actions, PlayerAction and PlayerActions can use scoped values,
  including source/target power or mana value, arithmetic and saved numbers.
  Delayed bodies retain their existing lexical context and exact captures.
- `compileMillAction(Node, scope) ([]effectFactory, error)` checks arity and
  preserves fixed-integer validation before lowering. Optional mill costs still
  require positive fixed integers through `compileMillCount`; dynamic costs
  and all-player milling remain rejected.
- Native mill definition validation rejects a negative direct Fixed declaration,
  as well as missing player/amount declarations. Computed nonpositive amounts
  use the existing no-operation behavior.
- Queries retain source declarations even for zero amounts; departure, return,
  phasing, control changes and game clones use existing captured incarnations,
  retained facts, snapshot copies and delayed trigger lifetimes. Trigger detection
  ends waiting availability. Implicit attachments, opaque callbacks and future
  nested delays do not infer a source reference.
- Resolution reads the amount once, then uses the existing mill modifier and
  owner-order batch service. Copies and distinct factories keep separate target
  bindings. Current or exact LKI reads do not follow a returned target. A saved
  delayed body does not choose new targets when its former target gains shroud.

### Established signatures, context and reuse

  reorder bool) ResolvingEffect` evaluates its count once at resolution after
  both players are available. The existing `LookAtLibraryTop(..., count int, ...)`
  delegates with Fixed and preserves callers. Nil or negative direct Fixed counts
  fail definition validation; computed nonpositive counts inspect nothing.
- `libraryInspectionEffect.refersToSourcePermanent()` declares viewer, library
  and count reads. `mayShuffleLibraryEffect.refersToSourcePermanent()` declares
  chooser and library reads, using the existing typed operand walkers.
- `LookAtTheTopNumberCardsOfPlayersLibrary(player, value, [operation])` lowers
  through `compileInstanceValue` with fresh per-instance bindings in existing
  resolving spell, activation, trigger and delayed scopes. The only operations
  remain bare LeaveRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInSameOrder or
  PutTheRemainingCardsOnTopOfLibraryInAnyOrder. Direct Integer counts must be
  nonnegative. Unbound/wrong-role values, unsupported ordering, costs and entry
  declarations remain errors. Existing `MayHavePlayerAction(player, Shuffle)`
  retains its spelling and player scope.
- Waiting queries read no operand, inspect no cards and make no choices. Zero
  counts retain declarations. Exact delayed captures and retained departure facts
  survive phasing, return and clones until trigger detection. Implicit attachments,
  opaque values and future delayed producers infer no source read.
- Existing private card snapshots, top-order validation, optional shuffle choices,
  delayed capture, target legality, stack copying and game cloning services are
  reused. No parallel state, card-name executor or production fallback was added.

### Contract, signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

### Exact contracts, dependencies and reuse

- Engine: `(*Game).DamageSourcesFor(playerID uuid.UUID) []DamageSource` is a pure
  aggregate query; `ChooseDamageSource(player PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter,
  binding *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect` makes the non-targeted choice
  at resolution using the shared chooser and resolution-frame binding service.
- The shared `damageSourceChoice.candidates(*Game, uuid.UUID) []DamageSource`
  retains bounded callers. General enumeration includes live permanents and
  spells; face-up command objects; stack/resolving ability sources, permanent
  and spell targets, permanent/card/damage/spell bindings; waiting counter,
  draw-step life, regeneration, redirection, exile, discard, untap, persistent,
  empty-library and modifier references; waiting permanent/spell/hand/exile/
  command prevention references; and waiting delayed permanent, spell, damage
  and hand/graveyard/exile card references. Existing readers own exact facts
  and active lifetimes. The aggregate also reads the saved graveyard visit of
  graveyard activated ability sources through graveyardVisitInformation.
  Opaque callbacks do not invent references.
- Exact identities deduplicate one object across categories but retain distinct
  casts, copies, incarnations and zone visits. Phasing removes live membership
  while an explicit reference can remain available. Departure information and
  old visits cannot follow a returned card. Queries and chooser options have
  separate mutable card data. Querying does not choose, evaluate delayed
  operands, install rules or extend availability.
- Every hand source is normalized through the existing viewer-aware information
  service before deduplication and filtering. This also covers a visit supplied
  only by a captured damage-source binding. Private inspection does not reveal
  the hand or make unreferred cards available.
- RON: `compileGeneralDamageSource(Node, []Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)`
  validates ChooseADamageSource/1 and lowers its remaining action sequence.
  AnyDamageSource is a symbol; IsColor/1 and IsCardtype/1 are tuples; And/1 and
  Or/1 take nonempty filter lists. Existing exact filter validation is reused.
- The producer declares TheChosenDamageSource only in its continuation. Nested
  branch choices cannot export bindings. Subsequent choices allocate separate
  bindings and shadow the prior declaration in their own continuation. Each
  factory call clones the compiler binding map and creates a fresh typed engine
  binding. Direct effect contexts without an action sequence reject.
- The six Circles and Greater Realm use the existing
  PreventNextDamageFromSelectedSource service. Jade uses
  RedirectNextDamageFromSelectedSource with its exact creature target and saved
  ability controller. The engine retains property rechecks, one-use event
  consumption, simultaneous packets, replacement ordering, cleanup and exact
  permanent-spell continuation before entry effects. Payments and legality stay
  in existing shared services. No Go-card fallback or partial registry is added.
- Rules read locally: CR 120.7, 400.7a–c, 603.7a–e, 609.7a–c, 615.9 and

### Exact signatures, supported contexts and reuse

- Engine: `MayEntryOperations(operations ...AsEntersBattlefieldAbility)
  AsEntersBattlefieldAbility` copies the child declaration slice. It stores no
  decision. The entry controller uses Player.ChooseMayAbility before the
  permanent is registered. Decline allows entry. Acceptance invokes children
  in order; false stops the sequence and preserves existing failed-entry handling.
- Engine: `EnterTappedAsEnters() AsEntersBattlefieldAbility` writes tapped
  status for an optional sequence. Decline cannot undo another required tapped
  entry effect. Existing ChooseBasicLandTypeAsEnters and ChooseOpponentAsEnters
  services own the corresponding per-permanent choice data.
- RON: `compileOptionalEntry(Node) (entryAbilityFactory, error)` and
  `compileOptionalEntryOperation(Node) (entryAbilityFactory, error)` lower
  `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, [MayActions([operations])])`.
  MayActions/1 must take a nonempty list. Children are bare EntersTapped,
  bare ChooseABasicLandType, ChooseAPlayer/1 with bare Opponent, or a nested
  MayActions/1 with the same grammar. The outer entry rule still requires one
  operation and a bare ThisPermanent source on a permanent card.
- Every factory call constructs fresh wrapper and child abilities. Decisions
  and results stay on each entering permanent. Nested decisions stay local;
  an optional choice does not declare TheChosenPlayer or TheChosenLandType
  for another rule. Empty bodies, wrong kinds/arity, incompatible references,
  nonpermanent sources, resolution actions and unsupported bodies reject.
- Definition validation traverses all children, including typed nils and nested
  empty declarations. No new global result slot, Go-card fallback, partial
  registry, target declaration, cost mechanism or alternative entry pipeline
  is introduced. Existing prepareBattlefieldEntry, permanent choice storage,

### Exact signatures, contexts, dependencies and engine reuse

- New engine API: `HighestManaValue(subjects PermanentSet) PermanentSet`.
  Read the subject collection once per use. Keep all maximum-mana-value members
  in collection order. Empty stays empty; face-down mana value is zero, and X
  contributes zero on the battlefield. Counters and P/T do not alter the value.
  Definition validation traverses its subject, including target/binding reads.
- Reuse `ChoosePermanent(PlayerRef, PermanentSet, *PermanentBinding)`,
  `BindPermanent` and `From`. Multiple candidates use the specified player;
  a sole candidate needs no choice. Invalid/nil answers use the first candidate.
  No candidates or an absent player clears the result. The exact incarnation
  survives controller changes and a phase cycle, and cannot follow a returned
  card. Resolution frames, saved delayed bindings and clones remain separate.
- RON: `compilePermanentChoice(Node, []Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)`
  lowers `ChooseAPermanent/1` in resolution ActionList sequences, including
  spell, activation and delayed bodies. The argument uses the existing typed
  contextual collection grammar. `APermanentWithTheHighestManaValue/1` wraps
  that grammar; bare IsUnblocked reuses DamageSourceIsUnblocked.
- Bare TheChosenPermanent is a permanent reference dominated by its producer.
  Each producer allocates its own typed declaration per factory call. Remaining
  instructions use that declaration; a later producer gets a different one.
  Wrong arity/kind, empty boolean collections, unbound reads, tuple references
  and reads outside the producing ability/branch/player action reject.
- `PlayerAction(player, ChooseAPermanent(collection))` makes that player's
  terminal choice without exporting its binding or changing an outer choice.
  ThePermanentChosenByPlayerThisWay, PlayerMustCost and exchange remain explicit
  unsupported contracts. The choice is not an announcement target or a cost.
- Integration: HighestManaValue preserves explicit source reads in collection
  operands. ChoosePermanent now declares explicit source reads in its typed
  player and subjects to waiting delayed queries. Queries do not select members,
  read mana values, execute filters, resolve players or make choices. Saved
  source incarnations and delay detection lifetimes use existing services.
  Implicit attachments and opaque filters infer no explicit source reference.
- No new global action slot, game-time declaration panic, reflection dispatcher,
  card-name execution branch, Go factory fallback or partial registry is added.
  Existing targeting, payments, combat unblocked status, phasing, LKI, registry
  validation and all-or-nothing loading remain in their existing services.
- Rules read locally: CR 115.10, 202.3/202.3a/202.3e, 400.7, 608.2c–d and
  702.26b. API and rules-contract docs describe only the established behavior.

and restore its printed rules after departure. Implementing early scheduling

### Contract, exact contexts and reuse

- `mage.BuildEntryCopy(original mage.Card, values *mage.CopiableValues)
  (mage.Card, error)` is a pure pre-entry prototype builder. It builds fresh
  effective declarations and fresh physical departure declarations, preserving
  original ID, owner and token status. It changes neither input nor snapshot.
- `mage.WithPrintedCardDefinitionPlan(*mage.CardDefinitionPlan) mage.CardOption`
  lowers printed origin alongside effective provenance in every accepted RON
  `Card(...)` factory. Native plan Build supplies the same origin. There is no
  new RON spelling, target scope or choice binding. No declaration executes or
  makes a game-time choice in this builder.
- Copied characteristics, keywords, targets, costs and rules use validated
  snapshot builders. Printed physical entry abilities do not execute. Acquired
  entry abilities execute through normal entry, with independent counters,
  choices and per-instance bindings. Source counters, attachments and saved
  target/entry choices do not transfer. Standard face-down values produce a
  face-up nameless 2/2; physical token status stays separate.
- Repeated building for the same physical card keeps its own printed origin.
  Copying another copy's values uses the new physical card's origin. Card.Copy,
  SetID and SetOwner isolate the retained departure card and keep its identity
  consistent. Phasing preserves effective rules. Game clones retain both plans
  through existing immutable card sharing and zone cloning.
- Audited all native permanent-card departure captures. Destroy, sacrifice,
  direct graveyard placement, bounce, exile, ante, gathered bounce, return-to-hand
  costs and rejected entry use a shared physical-card accessor. LKI capture and
  queued/departed abilities continue to use effective battlefield rules. No
  replacement or event ordering is changed. Zone replacements still use the
  shared pipeline before physical destination movement.
- Nil/legacy/mismatched physical provenance, untracked effective metadata,
  nil IDs, nonpermanent inputs, invalid snapshots and builder drift return
  errors before entry. Declaration plans continue to reject unsupported rules.
- Reuses CardDefinitionPlan, CopiableValues, entry services, target/payment
  legality, counter replacements, LKI, delayed triggers and game cloning.
  No card-name dispatch, Go fallback, global action result or partial registry.
- Local CR 400.7, 603.6c, 614.12, 707.2–7 and 708.2 support these boundaries.
  Entry permission, source selection, early copy replacement scheduling,
  competing copy replacements, copy exceptions, copied Aura attachment and

### Exact contract, dependencies and reuse boundary

- Engine API: `mage.MayCopyAsEnters(filter mage.PermanentFilter) mage.Ability`,
  installed by WithAbility on a permanent with a validated physical plan.
- RON shape: `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
  [MayActions([EnterAsACopyOfAPermanent(filter, NoCopyEffects)])])`.
  The outer optional body has exactly one copy operation. Filter lowering uses
  the existing context-free permanent filter compiler. No lexical target,
  resolution, entry-choice or action-result binding is introduced.
- NoCopyEffects must be a symbol. Wrong arities, copy modifications, required
  copy operations, mixed or nested copy sequences, and wrong source contexts
  reject during compilation. Instant/sorcery declarations reject through native
  battlefield-source validation. Existing ordinary optional sequences remain.
- Battlefield preparation exposes the entering permanent and supplies an
  event-local battlefieldEntryAction to EffectManager before tapped entry,
  counters and ordinary entry operations. Its copy candidates join registered
  replacement candidates, using existing priority tiers and affected-player
  choices. Applicability is recomputed after each replacement.
- Each retained definition plan and ability position identifies one declaration
  within the event. Reconstructed rules retain that replacement object, so fresh
  ability UUIDs cannot repeat a used effect. Removed rules disappear; an acquired
  declaration from a different plan gets its own opportunity. Later entries
  create new event-local state. No global last-action slot or persistent cache.
- The entry controller chooses from present matching permanents without targeting.
  Phased donors are excluded. Invalid/null required-choice output uses the first
  offered candidate. A chosen incarnation is rechecked for presence, identity
  and its current filter. Empty sets and decline preserve ordinary entry.
- CaptureCopiableValues and BuildEntryCopy supply accurate values and fresh rules
  for supported validated sources, including RON tokens, copied entries and
  standard face-down creatures. Untracked legacy copy provenance remains rejected;
  there is no approximation. Builder/capture failure rejects the entry through
  the existing failed-entry path rather than running an incomplete copy.
- Physical identity, owner, token status, incarnation, entry controller and
  supplied entry state remain. Source counters, ordinary layers and saved choices
  do not transfer. Construction stays in card.go; copy scheduling owns no Layer 2
  controller writes. Fresh copied entry counters/choices precede ETB observers.
- Reuses the existing replacement loop and applied set, native choice interfaces,
  immutable definition plans, token provenance, physical copy/departure services,
  counter replacement pipeline, simultaneous entry batch, costs, LKI, phasing,
  triggers and game cloning. No card-name branches, registry fallback or panics.
- Does not migrate all legacy entry replacements to the proposed entry action.
  External copy grants, exceptions, live copy layers, back faces and nonstandard
  face-down shapes remain separate contracts. Current Go callers are retained.

### Supported contract and ownership

- Native `CopyAddCardTypes(types ...core.CardType) CopyModification` is an
  immutable type addition. Creature, Artifact, Enchantment, Land and Planeswalker
  are supported. Empty lists, nil modifications, invalid types, Instant and
  Sorcery additions reject during definition validation.
- `(*CopiableValues).WithModifications(...CopyModification)
  (*CopiableValues, error)` builds a new validated definition plan and snapshot.
  Each build creates independent abilities, targets and costs. Existing types
  and abilities remain; duplicates are removed. The source snapshot and input
  slices cannot change the resulting declaration. Missing snapshots return errors.
- `MayCopyAsEntersWithModifications(PermanentFilter, ...CopyModification) Ability`
  integrates those values before BuildEntryCopy in the existing copy-priority
  replacement pipeline. MayCopyAsEnters remains compatible.
- RON accepts `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
  [MayActions([EnterAsACopyOfAPermanent(filter,
  CopyEffects([AddCardtypes([type, ...]), ...]))])])`. The copy must be the sole
  optional operation. Both lists are nonempty. Multiple additions run in order.
  RON reuses its existing type vocabulary: Creature, Artifact, Enchantment, Land.
  NoCopyEffects remains a symbol. Malformed lists/arities, unknown types, mixed
  unsupported modifications, KeepColor and AddAbility remain compilation errors.
- RON owns syntax validation and context. Mage owns snapshot construction,
  immutable modifications and replacement identity. Type-only derived plans
  retain declarationOrigin, because adding types does not create a new ability.
  The event key uses the original plan and ability position. Rebuilt rules cannot
  repeat within one entry; later entries use new applied sets (CR 614.5).
- Types become copiable values (CR 707.9b), including in subsequent copies
  (CR 707.3). Existing characteristic-defining abilities remain (CR 707.9d).
  Ordinary Layer 4/5/7 changes do not enter the snapshot. There is no later layer
  that reasserts added types; modified base values precede ordinary layers
  (CR 613.1a/d, 613.2c).

  preparation/replacement ordering, simultaneous batches, counters, source
  choice, cost transactions, phasing, LKI, departure and game-clone services.
  No parallel lifecycle, global last-action slot, card-name branch, fallback,
  game-time declaration panic or partial production registry is introduced.

### Exact supported shapes and reusable engine contract

- `PreventNextCombatDamageFromPermanentExcept(subject PermanentRef,
  recipient PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` saves the exact
  creature incarnation, player and amount at resolution. Installation requires
  a present, unphased creature and an existing player. Definition validation
  rejects nil/unbound/undeclared references, nil amounts and negative fixed
  amounts. Dynamic negative values become zero; later power changes do not
  recalculate the allowance.
- It matches positive combat damage from that exact creature to that player.
  Creature properties use current or exact retained information. Noncombat,
  zero damage, a different recipient or a returned object cannot consume it.
  A saved shield survives phasing and control changes; cleanup expires it.
- Matching simultaneous packets share one allowance. Actual prevention consumes
  the rule; if no damage is prevented, it remains available (CR 609.7b). In
  particular, a one-point Forcefield event does not consume its shield. Two
  independent shields can therefore protect successive events. Replacement
  order and rechecks belong to the existing affected-player pipeline.
- RON accepts `CreateFuturePreventDamage(
  NextTimeCombatDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnByCreatureToRecipient(permanentRef,
  Player(playerRef)), [PreventAllButSomeOfThatDamage(value)])` in resolving action
  contexts. Exactly one operation is required. The adapters retain their
  existing typed reference/value scopes and per-instance binding construction.
  Permanent recipients, other operations/events and malformed declarations
  reject. Inventory classifies the event source as permanent_reference and the
  operation amount as value.
- Forcefield's preceding ChooseAPermanent owns unblocked membership at resolution,
  with nontarget choice and existing shroud behavior. Activation before blocker
  declaration is legal; an empty choice installs nothing. Later blocked status
  does not rewrite the saved subject; damage to a blocker cannot use a player
  shield. RON owns spelling/context; mage owns rules and runtime state.
- Reuses sourcePreventionReplacement, damage-source identity/current/LKI services,
  affected-player replacement choices, simultaneous damage batches, actual damage
  notifications/lifelink, duration cleanup, source queries, transactional mana
  costs, scoped permanent choices and game/stack cloning. Existing APIs retain
  prior behavior. No card-name branch, Go fallback, declaration panic, global
  result slot or partial production registry is added.
- Active rules supply the exact subject through WaitingPreventionPermanentSources.
  Explicit source reads in subject/player/amount also qualify in waiting delayed
  bodies without evaluating amounts or installing a rule. This adds no general
  unpreventable-damage or new source-category contract.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reusable contract

- `ProposedDamageValue` is a sealed, immutable event value.
  `ProposedDamageAmount() ProposedDamageValue` reads the matching proposed
  amount; `HalfProposedDamageRoundedDown() ProposedDamageValue` reads half,
  rounded down. These values do not read resolution bindings or retain game state.
- `PreventProposedDamage(amount ProposedDamageValue) SourcePreventionOperation`
  specifies one prevention operation.
  `GainLifeFromPreventedDamage(player PlayerRef) SourcePreventionOperation`
  specifies its optional additional life gain to a separately saved player.
- `PreventNextDamageFromSelectedSourceWithOperations(source DamageSourceRef,
  recipient PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter, operations
  ...SourcePreventionOperation) ResolvingEffect` requires one prevention
  operation and at most one following life-gain operation. Definition validation
  rejects empty, nil, reversed or repeated operations, nil amounts/players,
  invalid filters and unbound references. Source and player declarations retain
  existing scope validation. Prior public APIs and callers are preserved.
- Installation saves the exact chosen source, protected player and gain player.
  The amount is read when prevention applies, after earlier replacements.
  Matching simultaneous packets from that source to that player share one
  amount. Half is rounded once across those packets, then removed from them.
  Other sources and recipients do not contribute. Zero damage cannot consume
  the rule; one-point half prevention prevents zero and keeps it for a later
  event (CR 609.7b). Each packet still records the rule as applied.
- Actual prevention consumes the rule before the additional gain. The original
  single or simultaneous damage event finishes before its life gain (CR 615.5).
  Private replacement preparation returns local typed gain outcomes to the damage
  service. No result lives in a game-wide slot. The gain uses this rule's actual
  prevention once per event; shared life modifiers, replacements, Lich, history
  and actual-gain triggers apply. Damage during a gain replacement cannot reuse
  the consumed shield. Prevented damage supplies no damage history or lifelink.
- Current/exact retained source properties, spell identity, selected permanent
  spell continuation before entry, returned-incarnation exclusion, phasing,
  cleanup and cloning reuse existing services. Active shields retain waiting
  source references. Explicit source reads in a gain player qualify in delayed
  bodies without evaluating that player. No general unpreventable-damage or
  arbitrary replacement-body execution contract is added.
- RON accepts `CreateFuturePreventDamage(
  NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(TheChosenDamageSource,
  Player(playerRef)), operations)` in resolving actions after a dominating
  damage-source choice. The list starts with bare `PreventThatDamage` or
  `PreventSomeOfThatDamage(proposedValue)`. Supported proposed values are bare
  `WouldDealDamage_ThatMuchDamage` and
  `HalfRoundedDown(WouldDealDamage_ThatMuchDamage)`. The optional next operation
  is `GainLife(TheAmountOfDamagePreventedThisWay)`. Implicit gain uses the saved
  action controller, independently of the event recipient. Proposed amounts and
  actual results cannot escape the operation list. Wrong kinds/arities, unbound
  choices, wrong recipients, reversed/duplicate operations and other value forms
  reject during compilation. Inventory supplies `proposed_damage_value`,
  `prevention_result` and `damage_source_reference` roles.
- RON owns spelling and lexical scopes; mage owns mechanics and runtime state.
  Reuses sourcePreventionReplacement, affected-player replacement choices and
  rechecks, exact damage information/LKI, shared single and simultaneous damage,
  life services, waiting references, transactional mana/tap/sacrifice costs,
  resolution choices and game/stack/definition cloning. No card-name branch,
  Go fallback, declaration panic, skipped rule or partial registry is added.

### Supported contracts and reuse boundary

New mage services:

- `ReplaceTappedManaTypeForPlayerThisTurn(player PlayerRef,
  filter PermanentFilter, to Color) ResolvingEffect` saves the player at
  resolution and replaces all types from matching permanents controlled by that
  player when that player taps them for mana. Membership/control stay live;
  later entries qualify. Source departure does not end it; cleanup does.
- `ReplaceTappedManaTypeUntilLeaves(subject PermanentRef,
  from, to Color) ResolvingEffect` captures a present exact incarnation and
  changes only the specified type from its tap-symbol mana abilities. Later
  subtype/control changes do not remove the rule. Phasing keeps the rule;
  departure ends it permanently. No returned incarnation can inherit it.
- `(*Game).ManaTypesAbilityCouldProduce(ability Ability,
  sourceID uuid.UUID) []Color` reads every possible resulting type without
  checking payment/tapped status, making choices or changing state. The existing
  opponent-land color service uses it. Raw production metadata APIs stay intact.
- `(*Game).WaitingManaReplacementPermanentSources() []DamageSource` supplies
  exact subjects of active indefinite mana rules to general damage-source
  choices. Phasing keeps those references; departure ends them. Player/filter
  rules do not infer permanent references. Typed installation effects also
  declare explicit source reads through the existing delayed-body contract.

RON accepts `CreateReplaceWouldProduceManaUntil/3` in resolving action lists:

1. `PlayerTappingAPermanentWouldProduceMana(You, controlledFilter)`, one
   `WouldProduceMana_ReplaceType(concreteType)` operation, `UntilEndOfTurn`.
   The filter must include `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))`, use existing
   independent permanent filters, and omit source exclusion.
2. `TappingPermanentWouldProduceMana(permanentRef)`, one
   `WouldProduceMana_ReplaceTypeOfType(fromType, toType)` operation,
   `UntilPermanentLeavesBattlefield(theSamePermanentRef)`. References use current
   lexical declarations and fresh per-instance bindings.

Both preserve amounts and spending restrictions. Other shapes, nonconcrete
colors, unbound references, multiple operations, incompatible contexts and
mismatched durations reject at compilation or native definition validation.
Inventory reports `mana_replacement_event`, `mana_replacement_operation`,
`mana_type` and typed duration references.

RON owns syntax, scope checks and lowering. Mage owns the proposed event,
replacement state, identity and execution. The new internal manaProductionAction
uses shared replacement candidates, priorities, affected-player choices,
rechecks and once-per-event execution. Manual/direct/typed mana abilities replace
production before pool addition. Actual types feed bonuses and tapped-for-mana
facts. Separate typed add instructions remain separate production events.
Non-tap conversions, spells and triggered bonus mana do not acquire tap context.

Automatic payment projects pure type transformations through the same candidate
and priority checks. Conditional replacements consider concrete color choices;
projection deduplicates equivalent states and repeated operations. Queries do
not make choices, tap, spend or add mana. Execution checks current outputs,
restrictions, costs, source incarnation and bonuses before payment, then uses
its selected order. Stable per-rule IDs work with cloned registrations. Existing
transactional casting/activation rollback, pool restrictions, mana solver,
resolution frames, delayed bodies, target legality, LKI, phasing, copies and

### Supported shape, contract and reuse boundary

Exact RON shape: one top-level
`DeckConstruction(RemoveFromDeckIfNotPlayingForAnte)` in any card's `Rules` list,
including instant and sorcery records. The operation is a bare symbol.
Wrong arity, duplicate declarations, unknown operations and action, cost, entry
or static nesting reject. RON owns this spelling and declaration context.
The semantic inventory assigns its operand `deck_construction_operation`.

Engine signatures:

- `WithAnteDeckRestriction() CardOption`
- `(*BaseCard).RequiresAnte() bool`
- `PrepareCardsForAnte(cards []Card, enabled bool) (retained, excluded []Card)`

The pure engine service supplies deck and sideboard preparation. It preserves
card IDs, owners and order, and returns separate slice storage without input
mutation. `NewGame` removes marked cards from both initial libraries before
zone binding or drawing; excluded cards enter no game zone. `NewGameWithAnte`
keeps them eligible for initial ante selection. No sideboard zone exists;
sideboard callers use the explicit service. Existing supplied scenario hands
and other zones are not treated as pregame decks.

Physical `BaseCard.Copy` retains the metadata. `CloneFrom` cannot replace
physical deck eligibility. `BuildEntryCopy` takes eligibility from the physical
printed definition, not from the copied prototype. Existing printed-definition
plans rebuild the RON declaration with fresh card identities. Existing game
cloning keeps prepared libraries and the ante flag. No global choice state,
new event pipeline, production partial registry, Go-card fallback, card-name
branch or runtime declaration panic is introduced.

pregame sentence for all seven names. No source defect was found or corrected.

### Exact contracts and reuse boundary

RON supports bare `AnteTopCardOfLibrary` in ordinary resolving action lists,
`PlayerAction(playerRef, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`, scoped
`PlayerActions(playerRef, [AnteTopCardOfLibrary, ...])`, and
`EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`. Existing resolving trigger,
modal, conditional and delayed bodies share the ordinary action adapter.
The player reference uses existing scope and per-factory bindings. The all-player
form requires bare `AnyPlayer` and creates no loop binding. Wrong arities,
tuple spellings, unbound player references, cost, entry and static contexts reject.
Bare ordinary `DiscardHand` now routes to the existing hand-operation adapter.

Engine signatures:

- `AnteTopFor(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`
- `AnteTopEach(subjects PlayerSet) ResolvingEffect`
- `(*Game).AnteLibraryTops(players []uuid.UUID)`

The engine owns library-to-ante movement. It selects current tops at resolution,
preserves physical card IDs, owners and remaining library order, and commits all
eligible moves before sending zone-change events. Duplicate player IDs contribute
once. Missing players, empty libraries, tokens and tops owned by another player
cannot contribute. Disabled or settled ante games move no cards. An ineligible
player cannot prevent another player's action or later independent instructions.
The action creates no draw, choice, payment, ownership change or random result.

Legacy `AnteLibraryTop` retains its public signature and selector behavior and
now uses this same batch service. Existing `MoveToAnte` contracts for other zones
remain. Typed single-player sets reuse `libraryRecyclePlayer`, with existing
player bindings, definition validation and explicit waiting-source declarations.
Queries do not select a top or move cards. Source-controller reads keep exact
incarnations and existing LKI; departure, phasing and return cannot replace the
saved delayed source. Spell copies read their own players and current tops.
Clones and pending frames keep separate mutable state. No global last action,
card-name branch, fallback registry or declaration-time runtime panic is added.

Rules evidence: CR 101.4 requires simultaneous actions; 407.2 establishes public
ante; 407.4 permits only the owner to ante an object; 608.2c orders instructions;
609.3 permits other instructions when one is impossible. Complete Oracle text
in local `data/LEA.json` matches both selected RON cards. No source defect was
found or corrected. All twelve complete RON records were inspected. Rebirth,
Jeweled Bird, Nebuchadnezzar and Petra Sphinx were inspected for comparison.
No RON source changed, so the vocabulary source snapshot is unchanged.
Its loader examples remain historic evidence.

### Exact contracts, dependencies and reuse

Engine APIs:

- `AnteTopCost() Cost`
- `PayPermanentAnteOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`
- `AntePermanentOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`

The first permanent constructor offers optional payment; the second performs a mandatory payment without an offer. Typed references capture the exact
subject before the optional choice. The payer must own a nontoken, present, unphased permanent; control is not required. Departure and return cannot
substitute a new incarnation. Missing players execute no branch. Nil individual branches do nothing; two nil branches reject. Each invocation keeps
its own result.

The shared transaction locks each successive library top on its validation game. Ante costs participate in commit preflight, including selected
`EitherCost` alternatives. A stale top, stale permanent or impossible combined cost fails before live mana, taps or other payment resources are spent.
Queries do not move cards or make decisions. `AnteLibraryTops` and `MoveToAnte` retain movement, physical identity, owners, departure LKI and event
behavior. No destruction, sacrifice or new replacement ordering is introduced. Multiple sequential costs are sequential; this slice does not implement
simultaneous all-player payments.

RON supports `MayCost(AnteTopCardOfLibrary)` and `PlayerMayCost(playerRef, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`. `MayCost`, `PlayerMayCost` and `MustCost` support
`AnteAPermanent(SinglePermanent(permanentRef))`. Each payment requires an adjacent `If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` with bare `CostWasPaid` or
`CostWasntPaid` and nonempty action-list branches. Ordinary resolving spells, activations, triggers and delayed bodies share the adapter. Per-factory
typed bindings preserve target identity and payer scope. Results cannot escape their continuation. Activation costs, entry/static operations,
mandatory top payments, arbitrary permanent collections and `EachPlayerMayCost` remain rejected.

Explicit source operands and branch bodies supply waiting delayed references. Queries do not resolve subjects or pay costs. Delayed bodies keep
original incarnations through departure, phasing and return; actual payment still requires presence. Pending copies use their own payer; clones retain
separate zones and delayed lifetimes. There is no name-specific executor, global last-action state, Go-card fallback or partial production registry.

Rules evidence: CR 118.3 and 118.10–12 establish complete payment and local resolution results; 400.7 establishes new zone-change objects; 407.4
limits ante to the owner; 608.2c/f establishes ordered resolution and its payment choices. Local `data/ARN.json` and `data/LEG.json` match the
selected payment instructions. No RON source was changed, so vocabulary source hashes remain unchanged.

### Exact contracts, dependencies and reuse

Engine API: `DeclareAnteCardTarget(name string) *CardTargetBinding`.
The declaration supplies existing `TargetBinding` and `CardRef` interfaces.
It targets exactly one card in the shared ante zone, regardless of owner.
Disabled or settled ante games supply no candidates. Typed reads require the
original visit to remain present; they return current card information and
current ownership. No LKI can make an absent card available.

`BasePlayer` ante storage now assigns visits on all arrivals, including initial
ante, `MoveToAnte`, library-top batches and payments. `SetAnte` preserves visits
for cards still in that zone, so copy-on-write `ChangeOwner` does not change
identity. Removal ends a visit; return creates a new visit. Clone extraction
and ordinary player cloning retain these visits with separate future mutations.

Casting from hand, alternate casting and activation capture ante targets before
payment. Existing stack capture, legality, resolution frames, spell/ability
copies and legal retarget choices retain the saved zone and visit. Copies keep
an old visit unless a legal new choice selects a current visit, including one
with the same physical card ID. A payment that moves or returns the target
cannot replace its announced identity. Ante captures do not become hand or
exile captures after departure. Later spell casts have separate stack identities.

RON supports `TargetAnteCard(AnyCard)` in existing singular `Targeted` spell,
activation and trigger contexts. It declares local `Ref_TargetAnteCard` through
`cardReferencePlan` and a fresh per-factory `CardTargetBinding`. Other filters,
wrong kind/arity and unbound or incompatible reads reject during compilation.
Graveyard return and exile reject ante operands explicitly. No new plural
ante targets, movement actions, source-payment result bindings, ownership
operations or delayed ante consumers are claimed. Inventory assigns the target
filter and still-unsupported exchange operands their actual semantic roles.

CR 407.2 establishes public shared ante cards; CR 115.1 establishes announcement
and trigger-placement targeting; CR 400.7 and 608.2b establish new zone objects
and target rechecks. Local `data/LEA.json` confirms Darkpact can target an
opponent-owned ante card before it acquires ownership. Its legacy own-card
restriction is not reused. No replacement, simultaneous-movement, cost rollback
or phasing rule is added. Existing payment validation and rollback remain in
force. Ante cards cannot phase; source phasing does not change their visits.
There is no card-name executor, global action result, Go-card fallback or
partial production registry.

### Exact signatures, contexts and engine reuse

Engine API:

- `AnteCardSet`: sealed typed selection of exact shared-ante visits.
- `AnteCardsOwnedBy(owner PlayerRef) AnteCardSet`: pure current-owner selection
  across both players' storage.
- `OtherAnteCards(subjects AnteCardSet) AnteCardSet`: physical source exclusion
  after its payment moves it to ante.
- `PutAnteCardsInGraveyards(subjects AnteCardSet) ResolvingEffect`: saves visits,
  deduplicates subjects, offers each owner's graveyard order in APNAP order,
  then moves all available cards before any zone-change event.

Private `Game.removeAnteVisit(capturedCard) (Card, bool)` checks exact ante
identity and removes without event delivery, so future atomic operations can
complete their destination state before observers run. This replaces no legacy
caller. It rejects absent, returned, disabled and settled subjects. Movement
uses current ownership, preserves prior graveyard order and creates new visits
through existing player storage. All choices use card snapshots and precede
movement; invalid answers select the first remaining candidate. Saved visits
and owners are rechecked after choices. Ownership changes preserve the visit;
departure and return do not. Clones retain separate zones and visit mutations.

`Game.orderCardsForGraveyard` extracts existing mill ordering without changing
mill semantics. Ante movement does not call mill modifiers, cause a death, or
use battlefield-departure replacements. No general zone replacement behavior
is added. Owner references retain existing explicit-source waiting declarations;
queries do not execute selections or choices. Physical source exclusion is not
an implicit permanent-information read. No global result, card-name executor,
Go fallback, game-time declaration panic or partial registry is introduced.

RON action shape:
`PutEachCardFromAnteInGraveyard(OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(playerRef)))`.
Existing typed player references and local target bindings are reused in
resolving spell, activation and trigger action contexts. Explicit source
exclusion is `Other(OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(playerRef)))`, available only
in the paid branch of an adjacent source-permanent ante payment and its
immediate nested actions. Unpaid, out-of-continuation and delayed reads reject.
Cost, entry and static roles reject, as do malformed filters and unbound or
incompatible references. Inventory records ante-card-filter, player-filter and
player-reference roles and descends into unsupported forms.

Rules evidence: local CR 407.2–4 (shared ante and ante movement), 400.7/400.7j
(new visits and finding a payment's publicly moved card), 400.5/404.3 (graveyard
order) and 101.4 (APNAP choices before simultaneous actions). Source phasing or
return cannot pay the existing exact-permanent payment. Ante cards do not phase.
LKI cannot enable an action on an absent selected visit. Existing transaction
rollback and payment-result scopes are preserved and regression-tested.

### Contract, supported contexts and reuse boundary

Engine signatures:

- `AcquireCardOwnership(card CardRef, owner PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`:
  requires a current nontoken typed card and an existing player in an enabled,
  unsettled ante game. Reuses `Game.ChangeOwner`, copy-on-write card replacement
  and original-owner settlement history. No zone move, controller change or
  visit change occurs. Hand, graveyard, visible exile and ante references work.
- `ExchangeAnteCardWithLibraryTop(card CardRef, player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`:
  checks a current exact ante visit and current player. Both subjects must belong
  to that player. A token or foreign-owned library top prevents the entire
  exchange. An empty library receives the ante card. The top is read at
  resolution; the tail keeps its order. Uses `removeAnteVisit`, player storage,
  fresh ante arrivals and the shared zone-event service. Both moves precede events.

The exchange does not acquire ownership. Ownership precedes exchange in the
corrected RON sequence and remains when exchange cannot proceed. Neither action
uses a global last-action result, registry fallback, card-name branch, runtime
declaration panic or parallel zone/replacement system. Ante/library movement has
no applicable battlefield, draw or mill replacement operation. No general zone
replacement service is introduced. No choices or APNAP decisions are needed.

`Game.ChangeOwner` exposed a missing engine contract: its graveyard replacement
used `SetGraveyard`, which gives every card a new visit. New private
`BasePlayer.replaceGraveyardCard(id uuid.UUID, replacement Card) bool` replaces
only the card through copied slice storage. `replaceCardReference` uses it for
players with modeled graveyard storage. Existing `SetGraveyard` semantics and
legacy callers remain. The selected card and its neighbors keep visits; clones
keep independent cards, visits and original-owner history.

RON shapes:
`AcquireOwnershipOfCard(anteCardRef, playerRef)` and
`ExchangeAnteCardWithTopCardOfPlayersLibrary(anteCardRef, playerRef)`.
The card operand is exactly the bound `Ref_TargetAnteCard` from
`TargetAnteCard(AnyCard)`. Resolving spell, activation and trigger action contexts
are supported. Player operands reuse typed player plans and instance bindings.
Wrong kinds/arities, unbound/incompatible references, graveyard operands and
cost/entry/static roles reject before gameplay. Inventory gives card/player
reference roles to both operands and still descends into unsupported forms.

Typed player source reads are declared to waiting delayed queries. Queries do
not resolve cards/players or change ownership/zones. Departure and phasing retain
the saved source; a returned source cannot replace it. Detection ends the waiting
category, and clones keep independent lifetimes. The card action itself requires
a live exact visit; LKI cannot move an absent or returned target. Pending abilities
survive source departure/return and phasing through existing stack services.

Rules evidence: local CR 407.3/4 (ante ownership and eligible ante subjects),
701.12a/d (complete cross-zone exchange, same owner and empty-zone permission),
400.7 (new objects on zone changes), and 608.2b/c (target legality and ordered
instructions). The official 2024 rulebook's 701.10d has the same empty-zone
permission: https://media.wizards.com/2024/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020240308.pdf.

### Contract, exact signatures and reuse boundary

RON supports exactly `ChooseACardName(AnyOracleCard)` in resolving spells,
activations and triggers, directly or under explicit `PlayerAction`/
`PlayerActions`. `AnyOracleCard` is a symbol. Wrong kinds/arities, other name
filters and cost/entry/static roles reject before gameplay. Inventory descends
with `card_name_catalog` for both action and player-action arguments.

RON owns syntax validation, the current typed player plan and fresh factory
construction. `compileCardNameCatalog(Node)` lowers the exact name-set symbol;
`compileCardNameChoice(Node, scope)` builds a fresh engine binding for each
instance. No Go-card lookup, name-specific card branch, skipped rule, global
last-choice slot, runtime declaration panic or partial registry is introduced.

Engine contracts:

- `OracleCardNameCatalog() *CardNameCatalog`: retained immutable catalog.
- `(*CardNameCatalog).Names() []string`: separate sorted list storage.
- `(*CardNameCatalog).Contains(string) bool`: exact English membership.
- `BindCardName(string) *CardNameBinding`: separate typed declaration.
- `(*CardNameBinding).Resolve(*EffectContext) (string, bool)`: current-frame read.
- `ChooseCardName(PlayerRef, *CardNameCatalog, *CardNameBinding) ResolvingEffect`:
  required non-targeting resolution choice. An absent chooser clears the result;
  an invalid decision index selects the first legal name.

Reuse: existing PlayerRef resolution, `Player.ChooseMode`, definition inspection,
per-instance construction, stack resolution/copy, game clone, resolution frames,
loop frames, typed source reads and waiting delayed-source/LKI services. The
engine adds a typed name-result map to ResolutionState, Clear/Clone, nested effect
frames and permanent/card/damage-result loop frames. Decision list storage cannot
change the catalog. No zone, payment, replacement or simultaneous-operation
service is changed. Failed payment makes no choice; choice occurs only when the
pending action resolves. Existing callers remain.

The embedded asset has 35,919 distinct sorted names derived from all 35,137
entries in https://api.scryfall.com/catalog/card-names. Source documentation:
https://scryfall.com/docs/api/catalogs/card-names (all nontoken English names).
Retrieval time, source hash, transformation and final asset hash are retained in
`pkg/mage/oracle_card_names_source.json`. Combined names are split on ` // `,
then exact English names are deduplicated and sorted. CR 201.4/201.4b–f requires
Oracle names, excludes token-only names and permits individual split, flip,
double-faced, meld and adventure names. Choices include names outside the game's
format and executable collection. The snapshot is deterministic, embedded and
requires neither runtime network access nor a working-directory path. It must
be refreshed when new card data is adopted.

### Supported signatures, contexts and dependencies

- `mage.RevealRandomHandCardInto(PlayerRef, *CardBinding) ResolvingEffect`:
  selects one current hand card with Game.RandomCardFromHand, saves its exact
  hand visit and records public reveal history. No move or player choice occurs.
  An absent player or empty hand clears the result without consuming randomness.
  A present card without engine hand-visit identity returns an explicit error;
  it cannot silently skip the operation or publish an unbound reveal.
- `mage.DiscardCardFromHandFor(PlayerRef, CardRef) ResolvingEffect`:
  requires current membership in the explicit player's hand before the existing
  PlayerDiscardByEffect service. The saved visit cannot follow a returned card.
  Prevention and library redirection retain the shared discard/event behavior.
- RON `PlayerAction(player, RevealACardFromHandAtRandom)` in resolving action
  sequences; the producer operation is a bare symbol. The producer compiles its
  remaining continuation with a lexical handRevealPlan and creates a fresh
  CardBinding per factory build. Later producers shadow locally, without mutable
  state in the plan or a global last-action slot.
- `ron.compileRevealedHandCardRef(Node, scope)
  (func(instanceBindings) mage.CardRef, error)` accepts only the bound symbol
  `TheCardRevealedFromHandThisWay`. Current RON consumer:
  `PlayerAction(player, DiscardTheCardRevealedThisWay)`, also a bare symbol.
  Unbound/incompatible references, malformed producers/consumers, wrong players,
  use before production and optional-branch result escape reject.
- The adapter uses resolving spell/mode/activation/trigger/delayed sequences.
  Direct PlayerActions production/export, cost/static/entry/replacement contexts,
  drawn/library/plural producers, reveal predicates, saved mana-value reads,
  ownership exchange and movement consumers remain unsupported.

### Exact contracts, signatures and contexts

- `RevealedCardMatcher` is a native pure matcher with private snapshot access.
- `RevealedCardHasType(core.CardType) RevealedCardMatcher` and
  `RevealedCardLacksType(core.CardType) RevealedCardMatcher` check saved types.
- `RevealedCardNamed(CardNameMatcher) RevealedCardMatcher` checks the saved name
  through the shared interchangeable-name service and current lexical name result.
- `IfRevealedCardMatches(*CardBinding, RevealedCardMatcher, ResolvingEffect,
  ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` evaluates once and selects one body. A nil
  native body makes no change; at least one body is required. Missing/empty or
  non-reveal captures select unmatched, including for negative type filters.
- `RevealRandomHandCardInto` now saves a private immutable name/type snapshot
  alongside the exact hand visit in `capturedCard`. No signature or prior
  movement behavior changed. Exact-card actions still use `FromCard` visit checks.
- Private `ron.compileRevealResultMatcher(Node, scope)
  (func(instanceBindings) mage.RevealedCardMatcher, error)` accepts exact tuples
  `IsCardtype(type)`, `IsNonCardtype(type)` and `IsNamed(TheChosenName)`.
  Types use existing Creature/Artifact/Land/Enchantment/Instant/Sorcery lowering.
- Private `ron.compileRevealResultBranch(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)`
  accepts `If(condition, actions)`, `Unless(condition, actions)` and
  `IfElse(condition, matchedActions, unmatchedActions)`, where the condition is
  exactly `ACardWasRevealedThisWay(filter)` and a singular hand result dominates.
  Explicit branch lists must be nonempty. `Unless` reverses the selected body,
  not the existence requirement inside the negative-type filter.
