### Contract, boundaries and dependencies

Native signature:
`RevealHandCardInto(card CardRef, result *CardBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
It resolves the input visit, clears the result, and reveals only a card currently
in a hand. It saves a separate exact visit and immutable name/type facts, records
public history and makes no move, choice or RNG call. Absent/returned/outside-
hand inputs leave no reveal result. Historical predicates retain facts after
movement; actions still require the original current visit. Definition checks
validate input/result declarations and producer dominance. Clone and nested
resolution storage stay separate through the existing card maps.

RON supports the symbol `DrawACard`, also `PlayerAction(player, DrawACard)`, as
a lexical singular result producer in resolving action-list continuations.
The symbol `RevealTheCardDrawnThisWay` consumes that result and produces a
separate reveal binding for `ACardWasRevealedThisWay` predicates.
`DiscardTheCardDrawnThisWay`, also in `PlayerAction`, consumes the draw binding
and checks the explicit player's hand. Spell, activation, trigger and delayed
resolving action lists share the adapter. Each factory instance builds fresh
bindings. Later producers shadow only their own continuations; conditional
producers cannot export results. PlayerActions does not export draw results.
Explicit-player reveal wrappers, plural draws, cost/static/entry/replacement
contexts and library production remain rejected rather than inferred.

Reuse: `DrawFor(player, Fixed(1), DrawCardInto(binding))`, `FromCard`, existing
hand visits, public reveal snapshots, `IfRevealedCardMatches`, shared discard
replacement/events, Sequence, native definition validation, clone/frame/delayed
maps, target/player bindings and existing source/LKI lifecycle. CR 121.6c is
retained: replacement-drawn cards cannot supply the original draw result.
There is no global last-drawn read. RON owns spelling, scope and lowering;
mage owns the reveal result and exact identity. No new replacement-order,
simultaneous-operation or payment subsystem is needed. Source phasing/departure
cannot cancel a pending stack action. Card absence never gains action permission
through LKI. Existing Go callers and production registry behavior are preserved.

Rules evidence: local CR 121.1–6 (especially 121.6c), 400.7 and 701.20a–c;
retained `data/ARN.json` Oracle text matches the complete Sindbad RON record.
No source defect was found or corrected. No RON source changed, so the syntax
vocabulary snapshot needs no source/hash refresh. API/reference and rules-contract
documentation describe only the behavior established here.

### Supported contract and reuse boundary

Native APIs:

- `ExtraTurnFor(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`: one present selected player
  gets one extra turn after the current turn, at resolution. Missing players do
  nothing. Definition inspection validates the typed player and its bindings.
  Waiting delayed-source queries retain explicit player source reads without
  granting turns. Legacy `ExtraTurn() Effect` keeps its controller behavior.
- `(*Game).AdvanceToNextTurn()`: after the caller finishes the current turn,
  select the newest pending extra turn and increment the turn number. Retain the
  next normal player through extra turns and nested grants, then resume normal
  order. This operation does not execute steps, cleanup or begin-turn replacements.
- Existing GrantExtraTurn, PopExtraTurn and turn-state signatures stay available.
  TurnSystem owns the ordered pending list and nextNormalPlayer; clones copy both.
  GrantExtraTurn now inserts before pending turns, as required by CR 500.7.

lists. Default player scope, `PlayerAction(player, TakeAnExtraTurn)` and

references. Spell, activation, trigger and delayed bodies share the adapter.
Tuple spelling, unbound players, payment costs, static/entry operations and
all-player grants remain unsupported. The compiler owns spelling/context checks;
the engine owns player execution and turn state. No card-name dispatch, fallback,

### Exact shapes, engine mechanics and boundaries

- New `PutLibraryTopInHand(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` and
  `PutLibraryTopInGraveyard(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` share a private
  libraryTopMoveEffect. The typed player and current top are read at execution.
  Owner validation precedes removal. SetLibrary ends the departed visit;
  AddToHand/AddToGraveyard create the destination visit. One EvtZoneChange follows
  both moves and supplies the physical ID, owner and library/destination zones.
- Empty libraries and absent player bindings do nothing. A missing destination
  owner returns an error before mutation. Nil player definitions reject.
  Retained library suffix visits survive. No saved reveal is required or consumed.
- RON lowering accepts only bare `PutTopOfLibraryInHand` and
  `PutTopOfLibraryInGraveyard` in resolving lists, explicit PlayerAction and nested
  PlayerActions. Spell, activation, trigger and delayed contexts share the adapter.
  Tuple/argument forms, unbound players, costs, static effects, entry operations
  and replacement bodies reject. Each factory builds fresh typed operands.
- Neither operation is draw or mill. The first implementation proposal reused
  Mill for graveyard transport. Local Petra Oracle text in data/LEG.json and
  Wizards' Ravnica Remastered release notes established that this was wrong:
  mill modifiers require the mill keyword. A failing-first native test now proves
  that a doubling mill rule cannot add a second card. The shared mill service
  remains unchanged. CR 121.5 likewise excludes draw replacements, draw events,
  last-drawn state and empty-library draw loss from the hand operation.
- Rules evidence: local CR 400.3, 400.7, 401, 121.5, 608.2c and 701.17;
  [Wizards release notes](https://media.wizards.com/2023/downloads/RVR_Release_Notes_XrN0zlJaFn/EN_MTGRVR_ReleaseNotes_20231120.pdf).
  No source defect or RON change was needed. Source hashes and vocabulary are
  unchanged. The RON instructions read current tops; Petra's native ordered
  reveal/predicate/branch sequence has no intervening resolving action.
- Explicit source reads participate in waiting delayed queries without reading
  players or libraries. Existing exact LKI retains source control after departure;
  a returned source cannot replace it. Clones and delayed/stack frames use the
  existing independent state. Target legality and failed payment use the existing
  announcement and cost transaction services. These single-card movements add
  no simultaneous multi-card operation or new replacement-ordering contract.
  General library-zone replacement declarations remain a separate capability.

### Contract, contexts and engine boundary

- New engine APIs:
  `RevealRandomHandAndDiscardMatchingName(player PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue,
  matcher CardNameMatcher) ResolvingEffect` and
  `RevealHandAndDiscardRandomMatching(player PlayerRef, filter CardFilter)
  ResolvingEffect`.
- Partial form reads the current hand and amount at resolution, selects distinct
  cards uniformly without replacement, reveals them, and discards only selected
  cards matching the saved name. Unrevealed matching cards remain in hand.
  Full-hand form reveals every current hand card and discards one randomly
  selected matching card. No matching card means no discard or RNG use.
- Both share private `Game.selectRandomCards([]Card, int) []Card` with the existing
  `DiscardAtRandom` executor. Its input storage is preserved. Each selection uses
  one random value, including the last candidate; short hands clamp the amount.
  Nonpositive amounts, empty selections and absent players use no randomness.
- Public reveal snapshots precede shared effect-caused discard replacements.
  All replacement preparation precedes movement; all movement precedes events.
  Prevention does not select a replacement card. Library redirection remains
  a discard. The shared discard pipeline retains replacement ordering and rechecks.
  CR 404.3 requires owner choices for simultaneous graveyard arrivals. A new
  failing native test established that the existing discard batch omitted them.
  The batch now uses existing orderCardsForGraveyard after replacements, in
  active-player order, before any movement. Hidden destinations do not offer
  graveyard-order choices; prevention changes the set before ordering.
- RON supports tuple
  `RevealNumberCardsFromHandAtRandomAndDiscardEachCardOfType(value,
  IsNamed(TheChosenName))` and tuple
  `RevealHandAndDiscardACardOfTypeAtRandom(handCardFilter)`.
  The partial form retains existing typed resolution-value grammar and X scope;
  fixed integers must be nonnegative. The full-hand form retains existing type,
  color, negative and nonempty And/Or hand-card filters. Other partial filters
  and full-hand chosen-name filters remain explicit unsupported shapes.
- Resolving spell, activated, triggered and delayed lists share the adapters.
  Bare actions, explicit PlayerAction and nested PlayerActions use typed players.
  Wrong arity/shape, unbound players/names/X, read-before-producer and unsupported
  cost/static/entry/replacement-operation contexts reject at declaration time.
- These compound operations expose no singular or plural card result. Selection
  is local to one synchronous operation; it does not extend a hand visit or keep
  a global last-action slot. Cards are not hand targets. Source departure,
  return, control changes and phasing keep the already-announced ability's player.
- A failing delayed-context test exposed omitted chosen-name capture in existing
  `capturedDelayedBody`. Step and permanent-event delay creation now clone
  cardNameBindings. Body execution clones the saved map and restores the outer
  map with defer. Saved names remain independent of later choices and game clones.
  This is an engine prerequisite for the accepted resolving shape, not RON state.
- Typed player and amount source reads participate in waiting delayed queries.
  Queries do not inspect hands, choose names, reveal, discard or consume RNG.

Engine reuse: chosen-name equivalence matching, lexical per-instance bindings,
announced X, opponent targets, native cast/activation/trigger resolution,
transactional mana/tap payments, exact source LKI and phasing, immutable reveal

### Exact established shapes, services and reuse boundary

Engine signatures:

- `NewExileLink() *ExileLink`: immutable identity for one group of declarations.
- `ExilePermanentLinked(subject PermanentRef, link *ExileLink) ResolvingEffect`.
- `ExileLibraryTopLinked(player PlayerRef, link *ExileLink, faceDown bool) ResolvingEffect`.
- `CardsExiledWith(link *ExileLink, source PermanentRef) ExiledCardSet`.
- `CountExiledCards(subjects ExiledCardSet) ResolutionValue`.

Exile visits carry a private link declaration and captured source incarnation.
The link is saved before the zone event. Current membership requires both the
same declaration and source incarnation. Repeated instructions with a shared
native link accumulate cards; another declaration on the same permanent or a
legacy ExiledBy value cannot add members. Departure and re-exile end that visit.
Source departure, cleanup, phasing and control changes keep an announced source;
a returned source cannot inherit earlier links. Tokens leave through the existing
service and supply no linked card. Clone storage preserves immutable declaration
identity and exact visits, while copying cards and visibility permissions.

RON lowering adds `Exile([TheTopCardOfLibrary], [])` and
`Exile([TheTopCardOfLibrary], [ExilesFaceDown])` in resolving permanent-source
bodies. Activated, triggered and delayed contexts are covered. Singular
`Exile([Permanent(ref)], [])` in permanent bodies uses the same linked transport.
Each constructed producer gets a fresh declaration. Ordinary spell permanent
exile, collection exile, graveyard exile and exile costs retain existing services.
Library-top exile reads the current top at resolution, makes no draw/reveal/mill,
and gives no player permission to inspect face-down cards. Empty libraries do
nothing. Invalid symbols, arity, modifiers, unbound subjects and unsupported
cost/static/entry/spell-source contexts reject during declaration.

RON owns spelling and context. The engine owns links, source/visit identity,
movement, visibility and cloning. The native query returns exact typed exile visit references for transport,

### Established signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

New native signatures:

- `IfRequiredSacrificePaid(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`
- `UnlessRequiredSacrificePaid(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`

RON adds `MustCost(SacrificePermanent(ref))` immediately followed by
`If` or `Unless` with symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` and a nonempty action
list. The existing typed permanent scope supplies source, target, event, chosen
permanent or Aura host where declared. Activated, triggered and delayed resolving
bodies are exercised. No new reference lifetime or spell-source permission is
introduced. Invalid arity/symbols, unbound/incompatible refs, separated or missing
continuations, empty bodies and unsupported entry/static contexts reject at
compile time. Two-branch IfElse remains rejected.

RON owns spelling, lexical scope, declaration errors and lowering. The engine
extends sacrificePaymentEffect with mandatory mode. It reads the exact subject
once and constructs the existing incarnation filter and matching sacrifice cost.
The existing unlessPaidEffect supplies mandatory payment without an optional
offer; the action-payment transaction handles affordability, selection,
validation and commit. The payer must control the present unphased subject;
ownership determines destination. Departure and return cannot supply the saved
subject. Phase cycles retain it. An absent payer runs no body. Each invocation
uses a local payment result; nested payment, stack copies and game clones share
no result state. Invalid selection leaves both subject and other permanents
unchanged.

Existing sacrifice replacements, affected-controller ordering, rechecks, zone
movement, LKI triggers and CR 118.11–12 payment success remain authoritative.
A replacement that changes or prevents movement after payment starts does not
undo success. Regeneration and indestructible do not prevent sacrifice. Waiting
delayed queries reuse the existing typed sacrifice source-read declaration;
they do not resolve operands, query affordability or make payment.

No card-name branches, Go-card fallbacks, game-time declaration panics, partial
production registries, global action results or parallel cost/zone systems were
added. Existing optional typed sacrifice and mandatory matching-sacrifice callers

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

New native signatures:

RON adds `ReturnEachExiledCardToOwnersHand(WasExiledWithPermanent(ref))` and
`PutExiledCardsIntoOwnersGraveyards(WasExiledWithPermanent(ref))` in resolving
activated, triggered and delayed permanent-source bodies. The supported declaration
has exactly one library-top or singular permanent exile instruction. A definition
preflight associates that producer with source-local consumers. Missing or multiple
producers reject instead of inferring a link. `ThisPermanent` and the source-departure
`Trigger_ThatPermanent` use the existing typed source reference. Other object
references, malformed arity/set expressions and cost/static/entry contexts reject.
Multiple linked producer groups and battlefield consumers remain unsupported.

The link is an immutable declaration retained by the compiled definition. It has
no chosen state or game state. Each producer saves its exact source incarnation
on the new exile visit; each consumer selects by that declaration and source.
Factory instances and pending effects use the existing per-instance targets,
source captures and resolution frames. Different physical sources and returned
sources cannot inherit one another's linked visits. Copies and clones retain
immutable declarations and separate mutable zones and frames.

RON owns syntax, declaration association, scope checks and lowering. The engine
owns transport. Existing `CardsExiledWith`, `ExiledCardSet`, exact exile visits,
`RemoveFromExile`, owner hand/graveyard insertion, graveyard ordering, source LKI,
stack copies and clone services are reused. Transport saves membership once,
deduplicates physical visits and checks each saved visit and owner again after
choices. Current owners supply destinations. Graveyard choices occur in active-
player order before movement; all moves finish before zone-change events.
Face-down exile needs no inspection permission for transport. A public graveyard
arrival permits its owner to order the arriving cards (CR 400.6). This operation
is neither a draw, discard, mill nor death. Destination services create new visits.

Waiting delayed queries retain direct source reads through the selected set.
They do not select cards, make choices or execute transport. Source departure
and phasing keep saved identity; a later incarnation cannot replace it. Native
nil sets, links and references fail definition validation before execution.

### Supported signatures, scope and engine boundary

Native APIs:

- `PermanentExileGroup{Subjects PermanentSet, Result *CardsBinding}`.
- `ExilePermanentGroupsInto(groups ...PermanentExileGroup) ResolvingEffect`.
- `ExiledCardsFrom(binding *CardsBinding) ExiledCardSet`.
- `SingleExiledCardFrom(binding *CardsBinding) CardRef`.

RON supports direct resolving action-sequence `Exile([Permanent(ref), ...
EachPermanent(filter) ...], [])` with two or more groups. Existing spell,
activated, triggered, conditional and delayed sequence contexts reuse this plan.
`AttachedToPermanent(ref)` lowers through singleton/attachment selection and
existing intersection/Aura filtering. All groups select before movement.

Two singular declarations supply symbol `TheFirstCardExiledThisWay` and
`TheSecondCardExiledThisWay` in declaration order. One singular plus one
collection supplies `TheSinglePermanentExiledThisWay` and
`TheOtherPermanentsExiledThisWay`. One explicit source group supplies
`ThisExiledCard`. Failed movement cannot promote a later group. Producers must
dominate reads; conditional producers cannot supply outer results. Fresh factories
build distinct group bindings. RON owns spelling, scope and shape checks.

`PutExiledCardIntoOwnersGraveyard(ref)` lowers singular groups through the shared
exile transport service. Existing plural hand/graveyard/owner-entry consumers
accept the other group; owner entry still permits only `[EntersUnderOwnersControl]`.
Typed singular card operands lower to `SingleExiledCardFrom` for later consumers.
Graveyard and ante consumers reject incompatible exile operands. Unknown
modifiers, wrong arities/symbol spellings, mixed card/library/spell groups,
unbound/ambiguous references, cost/static/entry producers and unsupported return
options remain errors. Existing singular/link producers retain their callers.

The engine reuses `Game.ExilePermanents`, `withZoneChangeBatch`, existing departure,
LKI, printed-card restoration, exile-history and zone-visit storage. Overlapping
subjects move once and supply the same visit to each declared group. Current,
unphased incarnations qualify. Tokens leave and emit the existing event/history,
but supply no retained exile card. Empty production clears results. All writes
precede batch events. No new replacement priority or exile replacement rule is
introduced. Existing cost transactions and target legality supply announcement,
rollback and fizzle behavior without changes to payment mechanics.

Readers require saved current visits; departure or re-exile ends them. The singular
reader also requires public visibility and exactly one original result; a plural
result cannot become singular after one member leaves. Transport uses current
owners. Existing frame, delayed/stack capture and clone services copy maps/slices.
Nested execution restores outer results. Waiting queries retain explicit source
reads in all groups without selecting, filtering, choosing or moving objects.

### Contract, signatures, dependencies and reuse

Engine: `ExchangeCardOwnership(first CardRef, second CardRef) ResolvingEffect`.
It resolves both present nontoken cards and validates both current owners before
changing either. Active unsettled ante is required. Same card/owner pairs make
no change. Missing/returned visits, tokens or missing owners prevent both changes.
It reads current owners at resolution, preserves physical IDs, zones, visits,
controllers and attachments, and emits no zone events. It reuses `Game.ChangeOwner`
copy-on-write replacement and original-owner settlement history. No choices,
replacement callbacks or events run between the two checked updates.

RON: `ExchangeOwnershipOfTwoCards(cardRef, cardRef)` in resolving spell,
activation, trigger, conditional and delayed action sequences. Supported operands
are bound singular grouped-exile results, `TheCardRevealedFromHandThisWay`,
graveyard targets/death results and ante targets. Existing per-instance builders
and definition validation enforce lexical binding and dominance. RON owns spelling,
arity, role diagnostics and lowering; the engine owns all ownership mutations.
No new state slots, target mechanism, fallback registry or card-name branch exists.

Existing exact-visit references reject departure/return and hidden exile inspection.
LKI does not authorize absent actions. Grouped producers select current unphased
incarnations. Frame/delay/clone services retain separate saved bindings; waiting
queries do not resolve card operands or infer a permanent source. Shared activation
payment and target legality provide rollback, announcement timing and fizzle.
Explicit destinations and physical-source references remain unsupported.

Rules evidence: local CR 108.3, 400.7, 407.3 and 701.12a; local `data/ATQ.json`
and `data/LEG.json` supplied the Oracle text. Bronze Tablet's unpaid RON branch
swaps owners, whereas Oracle assigns the other card to the ability controller.

record. This defect remains explicit for the independent assignment adapter and
complete-card test; this slice does not correct RON or claim Tablet Oracle fidelity.
RON assets and vocabulary source hashes are unchanged. Runtime cutover, Go-card
removal and DSL deletion gates remain unmet; no functions were removed.

### Exact supported contract and boundaries

RON `ControllersSacrificeEachPermanent(collection)` is a tuple with exactly one
positional operand in supported resolving action contexts. It uses
`compileContextualCollection(Node, scope) (permanentSetFactory, error)` and lowers
to **`mage.ControllersSacrificeEach(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect`**.
Supported operands retain the existing filters, unions/intersections, singleton
references, plural targets, owner/controller sets and attachment/combat sets.
Inventory assigns the operand the contextual permanent-collection role; simple
filter operands retain their existing permanent-filter classification.

The private engine service is
`(*Game).controllersSacrificePermanents(subjects []*Permanent)` with
`(*Game).orderSacrificeGraveyards(actions []*SacrificePermanentAction)`.
Selection reads the current collection once at resolution. Each selected
permanent's current controller sacrifices it regardless of the effect controller
or owner. Current exact incarnations are checked; departed/returned or phased
subjects cannot move. Duplicate subjects move once. No selection choice is
needed for an instruction that selects all its subjects.

All replacement proposals are prepared in active-player order before any move.
This retains a replacement whose source leaves in the same instruction. Each
owner orders their nontoken graveyard arrivals in active-player order before
movement. Exile replacements and tokens do not contribute graveyard-order
choices. The shared batch moves all successful proposals before events and state
checks. Sacrifice events retain sacrificing controllers; destinations use owners.
Indestructible and regeneration do not stop sacrifice. Token movement supplies
no retained graveyard card. Source leave abilities and the former battlefield
remain available to trigger checks.

Reuse: `PermanentSet`, exact incarnations, target declarations and lexical
instance bindings, `prepareSacrifice`, `SacrificePermanentAction`,
`effects.ApplyReplacements`, `orderCardsForGraveyard`,
`cardForBattlefieldDeparture`, `performSacrifice`, `withZoneChangeBatch`, LKI,
and delayed resolution frames. `refersToSourcePermanent` delegates to
`permanentSetReadsSourcePermanent`; queries do not select subjects, apply
replacements, move objects or offer choices. Native rules evidence: CR 101.4,
400.3, 400.6–7, 404.3, 701.21a; target legality remains CR 608.2b.

RON owns spelling, arity, role and scope checks. Engine owns sacrifice, ordering,
identity, replacements, movement and events. This establishes an effect, not a
cost or static modification. It creates no new result binding or mutable shared
factory state. There is no card-name branch, Go-card fallback, partial registry,
game-time declaration panic or global result slot.

`Trigger_ThosePermanents` stays unbound until its state-event producer is
implemented. Both original-printing filters stay rejected. Enclosing unsupported
rules remain errors. No existing callers, Go definitions, generator or DSL
function was removed: runtime cutover and removal gates are not met.

### Exact signatures, contexts and reuse boundary

RON `SharesANameOriginallyPrintedInAntiquities` and
`SharesANameOriginallyPrintedInArabianNights` are symbols with no arguments.
`compileFilter(Node) (mage.PermanentFilter, error)` lowers them through:

- `mage.OriginalPrintingNameCatalog(setCode string) (*mage.CardNameCatalog, error)`.
- `mage.HasNameIn(catalog *mage.CardNameCatalog) mage.PermanentFilter`.
- `(*mage.CardNameCatalog).Matches(names []string) bool`.

The catalog supports exactly ARN and ATQ. Unknown codes return errors before
execution. Embedded assets contain the entire CR 206.3a/b name lists, with
77 ARN and 85 ATQ names. Typographic apostrophes become ASCII English-name
apostrophes; accents remain. The local lists exactly match the current official
rules effective 2026-09-25, retrieved from
https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260925.txt.
`original_printing_names_source.json` records provenance, counts and SHA-256
hashes. Membership does not depend on physical printing, runtime registry,
filesystem layout or mutable catalog initialization.

`CardNameCatalog.Matches` reads supplied names and the existing interchangeable
English-name groups under CR 201.2a/201.3. Nil catalogs and absent names cannot
match. `Names()` keeps separate sorted storage. The engine models one current
name per permanent; the pure catalog matcher also accepts supplied multiple-name
lists without claiming a new object-name model. `HasNameIn` reads current names,
excludes face-down objects under CR 708.2 and deliberately leaves token status
separate. Sylex's exact `IsNonToken` conjunction excludes token copies.

Supported consumers: permanent targets, resolving collections, matching
sacrifice payments, static permanent selections and resolving property
conditions. `compileResolvingPropertyFilter` explicitly admits both symbols.
Invalid tuple forms, action/cost/player roles and unsupported enclosing
spell/land restriction declarations still reject atomically. Inventory retains
its existing permanent-filter role; no reporting adapter or fabricated binding
is needed. The prior controller-sacrifice rejection fixture now checks a
malformed tuple rather than the newly supported valid symbol.

A failing static recheck established a required engine integration fix:
face-down subjects retained a former name-based P/T bonus because their layer
reset was skipped. `(*mage.Permanent).resetComputedPT()` now resets computed
P/T bonuses, CDAs and switching in every pass, including face-down subjects.
Base overrides remain fixed. Copy-on-write preserves clone isolation. This is
part of the shared filter's layer contract, not a separate migration slice.

Reuse: immutable `CardNameCatalog`, its sorted membership and copy-on-read names,
Oracle interchangeable-name groups, permanent characteristic names, definition
plans, entry copying/printed restoration, target declarations and exact
incarnations, phasing, current collection selection, LKI information branches,
transactional mana/sacrifice payment, cloned frames, controller-sacrifice
replacement preparation, owner ordering and simultaneous zone batches.
RON owns syntax, arity, roles and supported-context admission. Engine owns name
membership and execution contracts. No new result slot, movement pipeline,
card-name branch, Go factory fallback or partial registry was added.

No RON source defect was established or changed. RON asset hashes remain
unchanged; vocabulary refresh is not required. Existing legacy set filters and
casting blocks retain their callers. Go definitions, generators and DSL exports
remain because runtime loading, test migration and removal gates are unmet.

### Exact shape, contracts and reuse boundary

RON supports one
`XIs(TheTotalNumberOfCountersOfTypeAmongPermanents(counter,
SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)))` in `ActivatedWithModifiers`, including inside
`And([...])`, with `PayManaX` and one or more X mana symbols. The compiler checks
arity, counter kind, exact source spelling, an X mana payment and uniqueness.
Wrong roles, plural subjects, other references, arithmetic and target-derived
values remain errors. Bodies/targets containing `ValueX` reject: CR 107.3c can
make defined X change while pending, and a fixed announcement must not silently
implement a dynamic resolving-X or dynamic target-legality contract.

Engine API: `WithActivationManaXFromSourceCounters(core.CounterType) ActionOption`.
It stores an immutable declaration on each `ActionDefinition`. Validation requires
an activated action, exactly one declaration, a valid counter kind and an X mana
cost. `CanActivate(controller, game)` reads the live source count for pure mana
affordability without changing the resolution frame. Activation scopes this X
before target checks, costs and stack construction, then restores the outer X on
all returns. Disabled, absent or phased sources cannot activate.

CR 107.3a/c/k and 602.1b/602.2b distinguish a defined payment X from a player
choice and prohibit changing the locked announcement/payment. All X symbols
share the same count. The existing transaction substitutes X before activation
cost reductions, locks the amount before counter removal or sacrifice, and
commits through the existing mana and zone/counter payment services. Stack
copies save the payment X and pay nothing. Separate sources and cloned games
retain independent counter state and pending objects. Resolution uses the
existing `CountersOnWithLKI` for live or exact-departure counts. A returned source
cannot replace the original. Phasing information remains available to pending
source-information reads; it does not grant a new activation.

Reuse: `ActionDefinition`, source identity/incarnations, scoped resolution X,
`ManaCostPayment`, combined X mana costs, activation cost modification, target
validation, transactional counter/sacrifice payment, stack copies and clone
services, source counter LKI, damage/prevention, regeneration/destruction,
upkeep and intervening-if end-step triggers. RON owns spelling, shape, context
and semantic role; mage owns announcement and payment. No game-time declaration
panic, card-name branch, global result slot, fallback registry, parallel payment
service or new Go card definition was added.

Inventory now assigns `XIs` operands to `activation_x_value` and source-counter
children to the existing counter-type and permanent-subject roles. Unsupported
nested forms remain visible. Existing accepted cards continue to compile.
Obsolete Doll rejection assertions became positive compilation/validation tests;
its previous end-step condition probe remains. Exact collection assertions and
supported-card regression checks now include the new accepted record.

### Exact supported shapes and engine boundary

RON supports, in resolving spell, activation and trigger bodies:

`CreatePlayerEffectUntil(playerRef,
[MayPayManaAnyTimeTheyCouldCastAnInstant(manaList, actionList), ...], UntilEndOfTurn)`.

Mana is fixed, nonnegative ordinary mana. Operation and body lists are nonempty.
Each operation installs a separate repeatable permission. Existing supported
resolving actions and typed references can appear in the body. Outer lexical
bindings must dominate installation; body results cannot escape its scope.
Invalid kinds, arity, player bindings, mana, X, empty lists, unsupported nested
operations and other durations reject before publishing a registry. Spell,
activation and trigger gameplay contexts have explicit tests. Static, cost,
entry and replacement adapters are not added.

Native APIs:

- `PlayerManaPaymentThisTurn(player PlayerRef, mana core.ManaCost, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`.
- `Game.GetPlayerPayments(player uuid.UUID) []PlayerPaymentInfo`, with stable ID,
  SourceID and Description.
- `Game.TakePlayerPayment(player, id uuid.UUID) error`.
- `PriorityTakePlayerPayment` and `PriorityAction.PlayerPaymentID`.

The selected player is saved at installation. The original controller, exact
source incarnation, target visits, X, event context and typed bindings remain in
an immutable snapshot. Each payment copies the saved frame, executes its body
immediately, then restores the ambient frame. Payment does not announce another
target, create a permanent or stack object, or fire an activation event.

The shared action payment transaction supplies automatic mana production,
affordability and rollback. Activation modifiers do not apply. Queries do not
make choices, tap, pay or execute bodies. Direct callers supply an instant-timing
opportunity; both APIs reject stack-resolution use. Source departure, phasing,
control change and ability removal do not revoke the permission. Cleanup removes
it. Clones keep separate permission lists and immutable snapshots; each execution
gets independent mutable frames and resources. Returned subjects cannot replace
saved visits, and source information uses exact LKI.

A failing opponent-payment priority test exposed the coordinator's unconditional
active-player restart. It now retains the successful actor (CR 116.3, 117.3c)
and returns priority to the active player after stack resolution (CR 117.3b).
Existing priority regression tests pass. This is the required shared timing
integration, not a separate card capability.

Reuse: typed references and per-factory bindings, definition validation with
isolated bindings, ResolutionState.Clone, exact source/target identity and LKI,
shared action cost transactions and mana solver, clone services, priority loop,
cleanup lifecycle, existing finite prevention, damage and replacement ordering.
RON owns spelling, context, lexical scope and lowering; mage owns permission
state, payment and execution. No Go-card fallback, card-name branch, game-time
declaration panic, global last-action slot or partial production registry exists.

were corrected before confirming the missing signatures alone. The inventory

the coordinator fix. An ambient-frame test explicitly seeds its outer binding

ability's producer/consumers. Branches and delayed bodies retain lexical scope.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

Supported RON producers are exactly the symbols `ChooseTwoColorWords` and
`ChooseTwoBasicLandTypes` in resolving action sequences and player bodies.
Tuple, cost, entry and static uses reject. The action player chooses at resolution;
announcement and failed payment do not choose. Each first list contains the five
legal values. The second list excludes the first because Oracle says “with
another.” Invalid responses select the first remaining legal option. Missing
choosers clear prior results; both decisions finish before publication.

Native signatures:

- `BindColorWordPair(string) *ColorWordPairBinding` and
  `BindBasicLandWordPair(string) *BasicLandWordPairBinding`.
- `ChooseColorWordPair(PlayerRef, *ColorWordPairBinding) ResolvingEffect` and
  `ChooseBasicLandWordPair(PlayerRef, *BasicLandWordPairBinding) ResolvingEffect`.
- `FirstColorWord` / `SecondColorWord` accept the color binding and return
  `ColorWordRef`, with `Resolve(*EffectContext) (core.Color, bool)`.
- `FirstBasicLandWord` / `SecondBasicLandWord` accept the land binding and return
  `BasicLandWordRef`, with `Resolve(*EffectContext) (core.BasicLandType, bool)`.

RON `compileColorWordRef` and `compileLandWordRef` lower the exact symbols
`TheFirstChosenColorWord`, `TheSecondChosenColorWord`,
`TheFirstChosenLandType`, `TheSecondChosenLandType` from matching lexical plans.
Typed domains cannot substitute for one another or for amounts/names. Factory
maps give each producer and its operands one independent declaration. Producers
in branches/modes stay local; a player body's producer is not exported to the
outer sequence. Actual text consumers stay rejected until their own slice.

Mage owns legal domains, decisions, result storage, definition checks and frame
lifecycle. RON owns spelling, contexts, scope and lowering. Reuse: typed player
references and LKI, `Player.ChooseMode`, resolution state, clone/clear, nested
application, existing permanent/card/damage-result loops, delayed frame capture
and restore, source waiting queries, stack copies, target legality and existing
payment rollback. A dedicated immutable-pair map follows all existing frame
boundaries. No global last-action slot, Go-card fallback, card-name branch,
game-time declaration panic or partial production registry is introduced.
No movement, replacement ordering, simultaneous zone action or text layer is
part of the choice operation.

### Exact shapes, signatures and boundaries

RON supports `SpellActions(Targeted_Modal([Targeted([TargetSpell(AnySpell)],
ActionList(actions)), Targeted([TargetPermanent(AnyPermanent)],
ActionList(actions))]))` on nonpermanent spells. Branch order is free. Exactly
one unfiltered target per category is required. Each body uses the existing
resolving action compiler, with its category's lexical reference. Cross-category

### Contract, lowering and reuse boundary

- `WithDefinitionAbilityGroup(group int, option CardOption) CardOption` assigns
  definition-local group/member keys to added abilities. Groups must be distinct
  and nonnegative; nil declarations, duplicate membership and stale keys reject.
  Ordinary validation preserves existing callers that add ungrouped abilities.
- `BuildTextDefinitionRevision(card Card, changes ...TextChange)
  (*TextDefinitionRevision, error)` builds an independent changed prototype and
  checks exact group/member sets and ability categories. Any ungrouped ability
  rejects revision construction rather than silently becoming printed text.
- `TextDefinitionRevision.Definition() Card` returns the fresh prototype.
  `ReplacementAbility(id uuid.UUID) (Ability, bool)` maps the original definition
  UUID to the fresh declaration. Unknown IDs and nil revision lookup have no result.
- RON lowers every existing compiled top-level rule option with its rule index
  plus one. Zero identifies the combined count CDA option. Empty options retain
  their group. This mapping is not based on card names or source line numbers.
  Existing spelling, scopes and unsupported-expression errors remain unchanged.

  timestamps do not change when text changes (CR 613.7a).
- Registration saves its declaration and source incarnation. Membership and
  controller use the existing layer-7c callbacks on each pass (CR 611.3a/c,
  613.4c). Clones have separate effect lists and runtime replacement. No choice,
  target or result state is introduced.
- Phasing suspends the rule without discarding the revision. Layer-6 removal
  suspends its layer-7c registration. Subsequent restoration uses the retained
  revised holder, so ending removal restores revised rules. Departure removes
  registrations and retains normal P/T LKI; return uses printed origin (CR 400.7).
- Unknown IDs, IDs from another source, granted, removed, unmarked, absent,
  phased, returned and face-down declarations reject before mutation. Invalid
  substitutions, failed builders, incomplete registrations, lost groups and
  changed contracts also reject without modifying runtime rules or registrations.

RON owns syntax, filter validation and opt-in lowering. Mage owns declaration
eligibility, checked installation, registration identity/order and restoration.

### Supported shapes and engine boundary

RON opts in the existing `TriggerA` two-argument pair path:

- `WhenACreatureBlocksACreature(SinglePermanent(subject), filter)`.
- `WhenACreatureBecomesBlockedByACreature(SinglePermanent(subject), filter)`.
- A two-member `Or` of those directions with identical subject and filter,
  including the existing reversed order.

`subject` is `ThisPermanent` or `HostPermanent`. Existing validated creature,
subtype, color and fixed toughness filter contexts remain unchanged. The existing
body adapter supplies resolving actions, targets and exact opponent bindings.
Grouped events, `TriggerI` and temporary granted pair rules do not opt in.
No RON spelling or scope policy moves into the engine.

Engine signatures:

- `(*GenericTriggered).WithCombatPairTextRevision() *GenericTriggered`.
- `(*Game).RevisePrintedCombatPairTrigger(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID,
  changes ...TextChange) error`.

Marked declarations require `filteredCombatPairPattern`, one supported matching
event kind, battlefield source, no extra zones, no state trigger and a checked
source/attachment subject. The fresh replacement must preserve its event direction
and opt-in marker. Reuse `revisePrintedTrigger`, `BuildTextDefinitionRevision`,
printed group correspondence and `revisedPrintedTriggers` restoration. The checked
installer preserves active ID/position/source/current controller with fresh event
filters, targets, actions and bindings. Each declaration retains its own ordered
prototype; immutable prior triggers remain separate.

Pending triggers, stack copies and future bodies retain earlier text and captured
opponents (CR 603.2–3). Departed/returned opponents cannot supply an old action.
Information reads use existing LKI; present-object actions retain legality checks.
Phasing suspends detection and keeps revisions. Ability removal suspends the
rule; restoration uses the revised declaration. Clones and sibling declarations
keep separate later changes. A returned source uses its printed definition.
Granted abilities reject (CR 612.3). Source mana, name, printed colors and copiable
origin stay separate from semantic word roles (CR 612.2).

This is a complete checked declaration bridge, not full live layer installation.
The caller still supplies layer-3 order, duration and original-text restoration.
No payment, replacement-ordering or simultaneous-action service is replaced.
Existing shared combat-pair tests retain regeneration, indestructibility, attachment,
multiple pair events and delayed identity contracts. No Go fallback or partial
registry is introduced. Runtime cutover and DSL removal gates remain unmet.

### Exact contract and reuse boundary

RON opts in `If(APlayerPassesFilter(Opponent, ControlsA(filter)), [body])`:

- `filter = IsLandType(Plains|Island|Swamp|Mountain|Forest)` with source body.
- `filter = And([IsNonToken, IsColor(White|Blue|Black|Red|Green)])` with either body.
- Source body: `PermanentLayerEffect(ThisPermanent, [AdjustPT(integer, integer)])`.
- Named body: `EachPermanentLayerEffect(And([IsCardtype(Creature), IsNamed(NamedCard(nonempty_string))]), [AdjustPT(integer, integer)])`.

Both two-member conjunctions permit either order. Native signatures:

- `SourcePTWhileOpponentControlsBasicLand(landType string, power, toughness int) ContinuousEffect`.
- `SourcePTWhileOpponentControlsNontokenColor(color core.Color, power, toughness int) ContinuousEffect`.
- `NamedCreaturesPTWhileOpponentControlsNontokenColor(name string, color core.Color, power, toughness int) ContinuousEffect`.
- Existing `(*StaticAbilityHolder).WithPTTextRevision() *StaticAbilityHolder`.
- Existing `(*Game).RevisePrintedStaticPTAbility(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID, changes ...TextChange) error`.

The native private `opponentPTEffect` retains one typed condition/recipient
context, immutable land/color/name metadata and a cloned composed effect.
Definition validation rejects invalid basic types, colors, empty named recipients
and mixed/multiple conditional effects. Checked revision now compares typed P/T
contexts and fixed recipient names: global, controller-land source, opponent-land
source, opponent-color source and opponent-color named collection cannot switch

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

RON opts in exactly:

```ron
If(PermanentPassesFilter(HostPermanent,
    And([IsSupertype(Basic), IsLandType(basic_type)])), [
    EachPermanentLayerEffect(And([IsCreatureType(creature_type),
        IsCardtype(Creature)]), [AdjustPT(integer, integer)])
])
```

Both two-member conjunctions permit either order. The type arguments are fixed
symbols; basic_type must be Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain or Forest.
HostPermanent requires Aura scope. There must be one body rule with one fixed
adjustment. Unless, IfElse, nonbasic land subtypes, missing Basic, general
collections and multiple adjustments keep existing execution without revision
opt-in. Malformed syntax and unbound references remain declaration errors.

Native signatures:

- `CreaturesPTWhileAttachedToBasicLand(landType, creatureType string, power, toughness int) ContinuousEffect`.
- Existing `(*StaticAbilityHolder).WithPTTextRevision() *StaticAbilityHolder`.
- Existing `(*Game).RevisePrintedStaticPTAbility(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID, changes ...TextChange) error`.

Private `hostPTEffect` retains immutable land/creature type metadata and a cloned
composed P/T effect. Definition validation checks the basic type and creature
subtype family. A revision-marked declaration must contain exactly one typed
effect. Context correspondence retains the host-Basic condition and creature
collection recipient kind plus the fixed recipient subtype. All transitions to
other P/T contexts or a different recipient subtype reject before mutation.

RON owns spelling, shape checks and opt-in. The engine reuses
PermanentMatchesFilter, AttachedPermanent, While, MatchingPermanents, IsCreature,
HasSubType, ModifyEachPT and Fixed. Its Basic filter uses the same supertype read
as existing RON filters. The exact current host supplies the condition; no LKI
can substitute an absent host. Earlier type layers supply land and creature
subtypes. Recipients remain live under either player, including tokens and later
entries. Control and ownership do not restrict the host or recipients.

The shared revision service retains active IDs, printed groups, source visits
and registration positions. Reattachment still gives the Aura its normal new
timestamp. Independent declarations, sibling factories and clones keep separate
histories. Phasing retains revisions; ability removal suspends the rule;
restoration uses the revised rule. Recipient departure saves current P/T in LKI.
A returned host cannot inherit an old attachment; returned sources use printed
rules. Mana costs and Goblin Shrine's separate departure trigger remain separate.
Layer-3 ordering, lifetime and original-text restoration belong to the caller.
No card-name branches, fallback definitions, global result slots, declaration
panics or partial production registry were added.

Cutover/removal gates remain unmet. No Go card definitions, generators or DSL
functions were removed. This run does not establish a caller audit that permits
removal. API/rules-contract docs describe only this bounded installed rule.

### Contract, signatures and reuse boundary

RON supports exactly:

```ron
TriggerA(WhenAPermanentIsTappedForMana(IsLandType(land_type)),
  ActionList([PlayerAction(ControllerOfPermanent(Trigger_ThatPermanent),
    AddMana(fixed_mana_type))]))

CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPlayerTapsAPermanentForMana(AnyPlayer,
  IsLandType(land_type)), ActionList([AddMana(fixed_mana_type)]), UntilEndOfTurn)
```

The permanent declaration has one controller-directed action. The temporary
operation has one implicit future-activator action, in a resolving action list.
Both require one known land subtype, one concrete mana unit and exact arities.
Unknown/wrong-family subtypes, malformed symbols, other recipients/durations,
extra body actions, dynamic amounts and incompatible result references reject
at compilation. General filtered non-mana events remain unsupported.

Native signatures:

- `LandManaBonusThisTurn(filter PermanentFilter, color core.Color) ResolvingEffect`.
- `NewControllerManaBonusAbility(filter PermanentFilter, bonusMana Color) *ManaBonusAbility`.
- Existing `ManaSystem.ManaBonuses(g *Game, permanentID uuid.UUID) []ManaBonusColor`.
- Existing `Game.RevisePrintedManaTapTrigger(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID, changes ...TextChange) error`.

RON owns spelling, declaration checks and lowering. It combines IsLand with
HasSubType and uses the existing known-subtype event validation. Persistent
lowering uses the new explicit controller-recipient option on the existing
ManaBonusAbility. Old constructors retain their activating-player semantics.
Checked revision retains recipient context, active identity and registration
position. Land-word substitutions change the filter; mana symbols remain fixed.
Factories retain independent ability identities and immutable filter plans.

The temporary resolving effect installs a private continuous rule in the shared
EffectManager. It uses EndOfTurn expiry and the existing survivesSourceExit
contract. It does not grant an ability to each land. Current lands under either
player, including nonbasic, later and returned lands, can match; phasing suspends
subject availability. Source departure, phasing and removal do not end it.
Clones copy registrations; cleanup in one clone cannot change another.

ManaSystem uses one internal bonus-entry query for both solver colors and actual
production, retaining controller/activator recipient metadata. Planning uses
controlled sources. A tap-symbol mana activation with positive production gets
one bonus per declaration, even if its original production has several units or
colors (CR 106.12, 605.4a). Ordinary taps, zero production and mana activations
without a tap symbol do not qualify. Actual mana-type replacement changes the
original production; the fixed bonus keeps its type. Existing transactions keep
failed payments atomic. Multiple persistent and temporary bonuses accumulate.
No target/LKI permissions, damage batches, replacement ordering or new
simultaneous-operation behavior were introduced.

Selected the shared source-filter restriction: one complete card and a concrete
second-card prerequisite for less effort than the coin process. Its subject
contract reuses existing typed source/attachment readers. Its engine boundary is
live target legality for abilities whose sources match a card filter. RON owns
spelling, filter validation, source/host scope and combined static declarations.
Acceptance cases were stated before edits: invalid declarations, real RON
casting and all Artifact Ward rules, selection/resolution legality, cost
rollback, LKI, returned identities, phasing, reattachment, ability removal and
restoration, current types/colors, triggered abilities, copies and clones.

### Signatures, contexts and dependencies

New engine API:

- `CantBeTargetedByAbilities(subject PermanentRef, filter CardFilter) StaticRule`.

RON supports:

- `PermanentRuleEffect(ThisPermanent|HostPermanent, [CantBeTheTargetOfAbilities(AbilityOfASource(filter))])`.
- `filter = IsCardtype(type) | IsColor(color) | And([filter, ...]) | Or([filter, ...])`.
- Card types use existing validated enums; colors are the five colors.
  Colorless is not a color and is rejected in this context.
- Nonempty filter compositions; one operation or two distinct operations with
  `CantBeTheTargetOfSpells` in either order. The existing Aura restriction
  spell/attachment composition remains available; duplicate operations and an
  ability/attachment pair remain errors.
- ThisPermanent requires a permanent definition. HostPermanent requires an Aura.
  Target, event, unbound and malformed references remain compile errors.
  AnyAbility, CanTargetOnly, unsupported source filters, conditional bodies and
  resolving installations remain unsupported.

The rule registers through Static, EffectManager and printed-ability lifecycle
wrappers. The shared Permanent.CanBeTargetedBy query applies it at target
selection and resolution, including copied abilities and triggered targets.
SpellTargetSource keeps spell targeting separate. Nontargeted operations and
direct attachments are unaffected. Legacy callers and attributes remain.
No Go-card fallback, card-name execution branch or partial registry was added.

The granting source must remain present, unphased and able to supply the rule.
Its current attachment determines the subject. Removing host abilities does not
remove a separate Aura's restriction. Reattachment, source departure, source
return without attachment, host departure/return, control changes, clone
isolation, phase restoration and ability restoration have tests.

Current ability source types/colors use existing permanent characteristic and
card-filter services. The shared resolutionTargetSource now supplies current
card types as well as colors for live incarnations. Trigger target selection
and modal eligibility now use the same exact-incarnation source view as
resolution and retargeting. Pending source departure uses retained information;
returned cards cannot substitute their new characteristics. Sources without a
battlefield incarnation keep the supplied card snapshot without following a
later battlefield object. CR 113.7a, 115.1c–d and 608.2b supply the contracts.

Costs, bindings, target legality, mixed-target resolution, copies, retained LKI,
static registration and cloning reuse existing services. Failed activation
checks spend no mana; later illegal targets do not refund paid costs. No new
payment, replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation service was introduced.
Artifact Ward's existing prevention still uses the shared replacement pipeline.
Its prevention batch, ordering and damage-source tests remain passing.

panic or partial production registry was added. No Go definitions, generators,

### Exact contract, lowering and dependencies

RON lowers top-level `Landwalk(IsLandType(Plains|Island|Swamp|Mountain|Forest))`
to `mage.WithLayeredPrintedBasicLandwalk(keyword core.Attr) CardOption`.
Desert/legendary landwalk, keyword filters and granted landwalk keep their prior
representations. Arity, invalid subtypes and unbound variable declarations reject.
No RON spelling or source record changed; no vocabulary refresh is required.

`(*mage.Game).AddPrintedBasicLandwalkTextEffect(source *mage.Permanent,
abilityID uuid.UUID, duration core.Duration, changes ...mage.TextChange) error`
installs one printed declaration in layer 3. The source must be the original
present face-up incarnation with an active opted-in declaration. Changes must
be a nonempty sequence of validated basic-land substitutions. Only EndOfTurn
and Indefinite are supported. An isolated definition probe verifies the retained
builder, declaration groups, replacement type and eligibility before installation.
Invalid requests install no effect and change no characteristic or declaration.

Each pass restores that declaration's baseline before layer 1, then uses the
existing layer manager and timestamp order to apply the active text changes.
An earlier temporary substitution can feed a later indefinite substitution.
After expiry, remaining changes run against the baseline again; a later change
cannot retain a word that only the expired effect supplied. Layer 6 removal can
remove the revised keyword. Grants, separate base contributions and duplicate
printed declarations keep independent contributions and lifetimes.

Baseline maps use copy-on-write. Restored ability instances are separate in each
game, including after controller changes. Phasing keeps identity and suspended
state; the normal present layer pass after phase-in recomputes current text,
including expiry while absent. Departure LKI keeps the final result; a return
or independent printed copy cannot inherit the effect. Copiable information
stays printed. Copy-layer replacement of declaration IDs is outside this bounded
API; it does not rebind to an unrelated new declaration.

The existing direct `RevisePrintedBasicLandwalk` caller path remains available.
A direct revision can establish the baseline before layering. A direct revision
of that same declaration is rejected while its layered result is present, so it
cannot bypass layer order; unrelated declarations retain direct revision.

Reuse: BuildTextDefinitionRevision/BuildTextChangedDefinition, semantic RON AST
transformation, definition validation/groups, retained copy information, exact
capturedPermanent identities, EffectManager layers/expiry, attribute counts,
ability removal/restoration, phasing, LKI and Game.Clone. No new zone, payment,
trigger or replacement system was added. This slice makes no decisions or
payments; payment rollback and simultaneous operations retain their existing
services and tests. No Go-card fallback, card-name branch, global last-action
slot, runtime declaration panic or partial production registry was introduced.
CR 612.1–3, 613.1c/f, 613.3/5/7b, 400.7 and 702.26 support this bounded contract.
API and rules-contract docs describe only the established context.

### Exact supported context and engine boundary

RON lowers top-level `Protection(FromColor(Colors([...])))` with a nonempty
Magic-color list to `ProtectionAbility.WithLayeredColorTextRevision()
*ProtectionAbility`. Existing malformed/empty/colorless declarations remain
errors. Nested grants do not receive the marker.

`Game.AddPrintedProtectionTextEffect(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID,
duration core.Duration, changes ...TextChange) error` accepts one active printed
color-protection declaration, validated color changes and Indefinite or EndOfTurn.
It requires the original present face-up incarnation, definition provenance,
semantic builder and correspondence to an eligible fresh replacement. An
isolated probe validates before registration, with no live mutation on failure.

Engine ownership: the shared effect manager installs layer-3 effects in timestamp
order. Each pass restores a separate baseline before applying all ordered text
changes. Cleanup/expiry recomputes surviving changes; a later change cannot retain
an expired earlier substitution. Each declaration keeps its active UUID and
position. Earlier direct revisions can supply the baseline. Direct revision
cannot bypass a currently installed layered result. Printed copy information,
siblings and granted rules remain separate.

Layer-6 ability removal suppresses protection. Restoration keeps an independently
owned declaration and the next pass reapplies text. Phasing preserves incarnation
and suspends application; the next present layer pass handles expiry. Departure
LKI keeps the last result; returned objects use printed rules. Clone effects,
baselines and changed controller contexts stay separate, including clones made
after expiry. Copy-layer replacement of declaration IDs and whole-object/spell
text need separate services.

Reuse: BuildTextDefinitionRevision/BuildTextChangedDefinition, retained RON AST,
validated definition groups, capturedPermanent, EffectManager ordering/cleanup,
printed ability restoration, Game.Clone and existing protection targeting,
damage, blocking and attachment services. No new zone/payment/replacement system.
No payment or decision occurs; cost rollback and simultaneous damage keep their
existing contracts. No Go-card fallback, card-name branch, runtime declaration
panic, global last-action state or partial production registry was added.
